knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exterior and exact penalty formulation families
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), \(h:X\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(g:X\to\mathbb R^r\). The constrained problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\), where \(F=\{x\in X:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic nonlinear programming; the definition classifies exterior and finite-parameter exact formulations, without asserting exactness for every violation function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty formulation is a family \(\Phi_\rho:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) of the form \(\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x)\), where \(\rho>0\), \(V:X\to[0,+\infty]\), and \(V(x)=0\iff x\in F\). It is an exterior penalty family when minimization is allowed over all of \(X\) and infeasibility is discouraged only through \(V\). It is asymptotic when constrained solutions are recovered from minimizers or approximate minimizers along \(\rho_k\to+\infty\). It is globally exact if there is \(\bar\rho<+\infty\) such that \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\Phi_\rho(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\) for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\). It is locally exact at a constrained local minimizer \(x^*\) if some neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) and \(\bar\rho<+\infty\) satisfy \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in U\cap X}\Phi_\rho(x)\) for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a constrained problem on X, a penalty formulation adds a positive parameter times a nonnegative violation function that vanishes exactly on the feasible set. The family is exterior when infeasible points remain in its domain, asymptotic when recovery requires the parameter to diverge, globally exact when all global penalized minimizers coincide with constrained global minimizers above one finite threshold, and locally exact at a constrained local minimizer when that point minimizes every sufficiently highly penalized problem in a fixed neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho>0\); any asserted exactness threshold is finite and uniform for all \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_\rho=f+\rho V\) is classified by whether feasibility is recovered only as \(\rho\to+\infty\) or already for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho<+\infty\), globally or locally.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Global exactness is equivalently \(\inf_{x\in X}\Phi_\rho(x)=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) together with \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{X}\Phi_\rho\subseteq F\) and equality of the minimizer sets, for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\).
special_cases_latex: The quadratic exterior family uses \(V(x)=\tfrac12\|h(x)\|_2^2\) for equality constraints.
A standard nonsmooth exact family uses \(V(x)=\max\{0,g_1(x),\ldots,g_r(x),|h_1(x)|,\ldots,|h_m(x)|\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If global exactness holds, one penalized problem with any \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\) has precisely the constrained global solution set.
The condition \(V^{-1}(0)=F\) separates a genuine feasibility penalty from a regularizer that may remain positive at feasible points.
boundary_notes: An augmented Lagrangian depending on multiplier variables is not represented by the scalar form unless those variables are included in the ambient domain.
Finite exactness is an additional property; it is not implied merely by nonnegativity and zero-set agreement of the violation function.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(h:X\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable, and consider \(\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ h(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained problems; this is the classical smooth, generally nonexact quadratic exterior penalty regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c>0\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\tfrac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2\) on \(X\). A smooth exterior penalty sequence consists of bounded \(\{\lambda_k\}\subset\mathbb R^m\), parameters \(0<c_k<c_{k+1}\) with \(c_k\to+\infty\), and subproblems \(\min_{x\in X}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k)\). The classical quadratic penalty method is the special case \(\lambda_k=0\) for every \(k\). Smoothness means that \(L_c(\cdot,\lambda)\) inherits the chosen differentiability class from \(f\) and \(h\); exterior means that points with \(h(x)\neq0\) remain admissible. The family is generally asymptotic rather than exact: feasibility is enforced through \(c_k\to+\infty\), not through an asserted finite parameter threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth quadratic exterior penalty adds one half of a positive parameter times the squared Euclidean equality residual, optionally with a bounded linear multiplier term. The penalty subproblems are minimized over the original simple set X, so infeasible points remain admissible. In the classical method the multiplier term is zero, the positive parameters increase strictly to infinity, and constrained solutions are sought as limits of solutions of the smooth penalized subproblems. This definition does not claim finite exactness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{L_{c_k}(\cdot,\lambda_k)\}\) is a smooth exterior penalty family whose feasibility pressure grows without bound.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\lambda_k=0\), the subproblem is \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)+\tfrac{c_k}{2}\|h(x)\|_2^2\).
special_cases_latex: For one equality \(h(x)=0\), the penalty term is \(\tfrac c2 h(x)^2\).
If \(f,h\in C^2\), then each finite-parameter objective is twice continuously differentiable.
immediate_consequences_latex: For every fixed infeasible \(x\) and bounded \(\lambda_k\), \(\lambda_k^Th(x)+\tfrac{c_k}{2}\|h(x)\|_2^2\to+\infty\).
For feasible \(x\), the added term is zero for every \(k\).
boundary_notes: The squared positive-part penalty for inequalities is continuously differentiable but may fail to be twice continuously differentiable at an active constraint.
Increasing \(c_k\) can produce ill-conditioned subproblems; that numerical property is not part of the definition.

notation.meaning: Quadratically penalized objective with an optional multiplier term.

children.title: Quadratic Penalty Family
children.top_down_role: Classical smooth exterior penalization for equality, inequality, and mixed constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity for Convex Programs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic exterior penalization preserves convexity for affine equalities and convex inequalities, including strong convexity supplied by the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is convex, every equality constraint is affine, every inequality function \(g_i\) is convex, and \(\rho\ge0\), then \[Q_\rho(x)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left(\|h(x)\|_2^2+\sum_i[g_i(x)]_+^2\right)\] is convex. If \(f\) is strongly convex, then \(Q_\rho\) is strongly convex with at least the same modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_\rho\text{ is convex}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity inheritance of the quadratic exterior objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalized Stationarity as a Lagrangian Equation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic-penalty gradient is a Lagrangian gradient with multipliers equal to the parameter times residuals; stationarity alone is not a KKT certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[Q_\rho(x)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left(\|h(x)\|^2+\|[g(x)]_+\|^2\right),\] define \(\lambda_\rho(x)=\rho h(x)\) and \(\mu_\rho(x)=\rho[g(x)]_+\). Then \[\nabla Q_\rho(x)=\nabla f(x)+J_h(x)^\top\lambda_\rho(x)+J_g(x)^\top\mu_\rho(x).\] Here \(\mu_\rho(x)\ge0\) and \(\mu_{\rho,i}(x)=0\) when \(g_i(x)\le0\). Thus quadratic-penalty stationarity is a Lagrangian stationarity equation with residual-scaled multiplier estimates, but it does not by itself imply primal feasibility or complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla Q_\rho(x)=\nabla_xL(x,\lambda_\rho(x),\mu_\rho(x)).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-scaled multiplier representation of the quadratic-penalty gradient.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Penalty Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic exterior family augments the objective by one-half the penalty parameter times the squared equality residuals and squared positive inequality violations. It is continuously differentiable for continuously differentiable problem data but is generally not exact at a finite parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,\qquad g(x)\le 0,\]
where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), the quadratic exterior penalty family is
\[Q_\rho(x)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left(\lVert h(x)\rVert_2^2+\lVert[g(x)]_+\rVert_2^2\right),\qquad \rho>0.\]
Here the positive part is applied componentwise. If \(f\), \(h\), and \(g\) are continuously differentiable, then every \(Q_\rho\) is continuously differentiable. This family is generally not exact at a finite penalty parameter; convergence of minimizers or approximate minimizers as \(\rho\to\infty\) requires additional hypotheses.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_\rho(x)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}(\lVert h(x)\rVert_2^2+\lVert[g(x)]_+\rVert_2^2)\) is a continuously differentiable exterior penalty for every \(\rho>0\), but finite-parameter exactness is not generally guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard exterior quadratic penalty for finite smooth equality and inequality systems.

notation.meaning: Componentwise positive part, with component max(v_i,0).

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Power Penalties Are Not Generally Finitely Exact
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable residual power is flat to first order at feasibility and therefore cannot generally reproduce a nonzero constraint multiplier at a finite parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), and let \(x^*\) be feasible. For \(q>1\), define \[P_ho(x)=f(x)+ho\sum_j|h_j(x)|^q.\] The penalty contribution has zero gradient at \(x^*\), so \(
abla P_ho(x^*)=
abla f(x^*)\). Consequently, if \(
abla f(x^*)
e0\), then \(x^*\) is not stationary for any finite \(ho\), even when it is a regular constrained minimizer with a nonzero KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla P_\rho(x^*)\ne0\quad\text{for every finite }\rho.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-parameter stationarity obstruction for residual powers with exponent greater than one.

knowledge_statements.title: Power-Kernel Curvature Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subquadratic smooth powers have unbounded curvature near feasibility, while superquadratic powers become flat there.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\psi_q(t)=|t|^q\) with \(q>1\), \(\psi_q\) is continuously differentiable and \[\psi_q'(t)=q|t|^{q-1}\operatorname{sgn}(t).\] For \(t\ne0\), \(\psi_q''(t)=q(q-1)|t|^{q-2}\). Thus curvature diverges as \(t\to0\) when \(1<q<2\), equals \(2\) when \(q=2\), and tends to zero when \(q>2\). In particular, the subquadratic kernel is not twice differentiable at zero, whereas the superquadratic kernel is flat to second order there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{t\to0,\,t\ne0}\psi_q''(t)=\begin{cases}+\infty,&1<q<2,\\2,&q=2,\\0,&q>2.\end{cases}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity and local curvature of nonquadratic smooth residual powers.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonquadratic Smooth Exterior Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth exterior family applies differentiable nonquadratic kernels to equality residuals and positive inequality violations, with the kernels vanishing precisely on feasible residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) and \(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) be continuously differentiable, with \(\psi(t)=0\) exactly when \(t=0\), and \(\phi(t)=0\) for \(t\le0\) while \(\phi(t)>0\) for \(t>0\). A nonquadratic smooth exterior penalty family is
\[P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\left(\sum_{j=1}^{p}\psi(h_j(x))+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\phi(g_i(x))\right),\qquad \rho>0,\]
where at least one kernel is not a quadratic residual kernel. For example, \(\psi(t)=|t|^q\) and \(\phi(t)=[t]_+^q\) are continuously differentiable when \(q>1\), and are nonquadratic when \(q\ne2\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(h\), and \(g\) are continuously differentiable on \(\mathbb R^n\).
The kernels \(\psi\) and \(\phi\) satisfy the displayed zero-set conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\rho\) is continuously differentiable and its added term vanishes exactly at feasible points.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable smooth exterior penalties whose residual growth is not quadratic.

notation.meaning: Residual-growth exponent in the power-kernel example.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f,h_i,g_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(F=\{x:h_i(x)=0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ g_j(x)\leq0\ (j=1,\ldots,r)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonlinear programs using a nonsmooth feasibility measure; local and global exactness are distinguished explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(P(x)=\max\{0,g_1(x),\ldots,g_r(x),|h_1(x)|,\ldots,|h_m(x)|\}\) and \(\Phi_c(x)=f(x)+cP(x)\) for \(c>0\). Then \(P(x)\geq0\) and \(P(x)=0\iff x\in F\). The family is globally exact when a finite \(\bar c\) exists such that \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\Phi_c(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\) for every \(c\geq\bar c\). It is locally exact at a constrained local minimizer \(x^*\) when there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) and finite \(\bar c\) such that \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in U}\Phi_c(x)\) for all \(c\geq\bar c\). The adjective nonsmooth records that the maximum, absolute-value, and positive-part operations can make \(P\) nondifferentiable where active residuals tie or vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical nonsmooth exact penalty adds a finite positive multiple of the largest equality or inequality violation to the objective. Its violation term is nonnegative and vanishes exactly at feasible points. Global exactness means that, above one finite threshold, the unconstrained and constrained global minimizer sets coincide. Local exactness at a constrained local minimizer means that the same point minimizes every sufficiently highly penalized objective in one fixed neighborhood. Nonsmoothness arises from maximum and absolute-value operations.
assumptions_latex: The functions are finite-valued on \(\mathbb R^n\); regularity required for a particular exactness result is separate from this definition.
The exactness threshold, when asserted, is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_c=f+cP\) is a nonsmooth penalty representation, and it is exact precisely when constrained minimizers are recovered for every finite \(c\) above a common threshold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P(x)=\|(h(x),[g(x)]_+)\|_\infty\), where \([g(x)]_+\) is taken componentwise.
special_cases_latex: With equalities only, \(P(x)=\|h(x)\|_\infty\).
With inequalities only, \(P(x)=\|[g(x)]_+\|_\infty\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every feasible point satisfies \(\Phi_c(x)=f(x)\).
Finite exactness avoids the defining requirement \(c_k\to+\infty\) of a classical quadratic exterior sequence.
boundary_notes: The definition does not guarantee that a finite threshold exists.
Stationary points of the penalized objective need not all be feasible unless additional hypotheses are imposed.

knowledge_statements.title: Ell-One Exact Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ell-one family adds the sum of absolute equality residuals and positive inequality violations; exactness means a finite parameter threshold preserves a constrained local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For equality constraints \(h_j(x)=0\) and inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), the ell-one penalty family is
\[P^{(1)}_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\left(\sum_{j=1}^{p}|h_j(x)|+\sum_{i=1}^{m}[g_i(x)]_+\right),\qquad \rho>0.\]
It is locally exact at a feasible local minimizer \(x^*\) if there exist \(\bar\rho<\infty\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) such that \(x^*\) minimizes \(P^{(1)}_\rho\) over \(U\) for every \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\). The absolute-value and positive-part terms generally make this exact family nonsmooth at feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are defined near \(x^*\).
\(x^*\) is feasible and is a local minimizer of the constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local exactness holds precisely when a finite \(\bar\rho\) and neighborhood \(U\) satisfy \(P^{(1)}_\rho(x^*)\le P^{(1)}_\rho(x)\) for all \(x\in U\) and \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonsmooth exact penalty for finite equality and inequality constraints.

children.title: Maximum-Violation Exact Penalty Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Maximum-violation and finite minimax exact penalty families.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For residual vector \(R(x)=(|h_1(x)|,\ldots,|h_m(x)|,[g_1(x)]_+,\ldots,[g_r(x)]_+)\in\mathbb R_+^{m+r}\), let \(v_\infty(x)=\|R(x)\|_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite constraint systems; the equivalence concerns algebraic minimax representations of the same maximum-violation penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The maximum-violation exact-penalty family is \(\Phi_c(x)=f(x)+c\,v_\infty(x)\), where \(v_\infty(x)=\max\{0,g_1(x),\ldots,g_r(x),|h_1(x)|,\ldots,|h_m(x)|\}\). Its finite minimax epigraph representation is \(\min_{x,t}\ f(x)+ct\) subject to \(t\geq0\), \(t\geq g_j(x)\) for every \(j\), and \(-t\leq h_i(x)\leq t\) for every \(i\). For each fixed \(x\), the least admissible epigraph variable is \(t=v_\infty(x)\); hence the two formulations have the same optimal values and their minimizers correspond by \(t=v_\infty(x)\). Exactness means that a finite \(\bar c\) exists for which the \(x\)-components of global minimizers equal the constrained global minimizer set for all \(c\geq\bar c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum-violation penalty uses the infinity norm of the vector containing absolute equality residuals and positive inequality residuals. It has an equivalent finite minimax epigraph form with one scalar t constrained to dominate every violation. At any fixed x, the smallest feasible t equals the maximum violation, so minimizing either formulation gives the same x solutions. The family is exact only if those solutions coincide with the constrained solutions above a finite parameter threshold.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many scalar equality and inequality residuals.
Exactness, when claimed, uses one finite threshold valid for every larger \(c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)+c\|R(x)\|_\infty\) and its scalar-epigraph minimax formulation are equivalent penalty models, with \(t=\|R(x)\|_\infty\) at every minimizing pair.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(v_\infty(x)=\min\{t\geq0:g(x)\leq t\mathbf1,\ -t\mathbf1\leq h(x)\leq t\mathbf1\}\).
special_cases_latex: For inequalities only, the epigraph conditions are \(t\geq0\) and \(g_j(x)\leq t\).
For equalities only, they are \(|h_i(x)|\leq t\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The epigraph form replaces a nonsmooth outer maximum by finitely many inequalities in one additional variable.
Any exactness threshold for one representation is an exactness threshold for the other.
boundary_notes: Algebraic equivalence does not itself establish finite exactness.
For infinitely many constraints, the finite epigraph representation requires modification.

notation.meaning: Vector of nonnegative equality and inequality violations.
Scalar epigraph variable dominating all violations.

knowledge_statements.title: Ell-Infinity Exact Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ell-infinity family penalizes only the largest absolute equality residual or positive inequality violation and is exact when a finite parameter threshold preserves local optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the maximum violation
\[V_\infty(x)=\max\left\{|h_1(x)|,\ldots,|h_p(x)|,[g_1(x)]_+,\ldots,[g_m(x)]_+\right\}.\]
The ell-infinity penalty family is
\[P^{(\infty)}_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V_\infty(x),\qquad \rho>0.\]
It is locally exact at a feasible local minimizer \(x^*\) when some finite \(\bar\rho\) and neighborhood \(U\) satisfy \(P^{(\infty)}_\rho(x^*)\le P^{(\infty)}_\rho(x)\) for every \(x\in U\) and every \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\).
assumptions_latex: The constraint system has finitely many equality and inequality residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^{(\infty)}_\rho=f+\rho V_\infty\) is a maximum-violation penalty, with local exactness characterized by the displayed finite-threshold inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum-residual nonsmooth exact penalty for finite constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Form of a Finite Minimax Penalty
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite minimax penalty is equivalently optimized with one epigraph variable constrained to dominate every branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\phi_k(x)=f(x)+\rho r_k(x)\), \(k=1,\ldots,q\),
\[\min_{x\in X}\max_{1\le k\le q}\phi_k(x)=\min_{x\in X,\,t\in\mathbb R}\{t:t\ge\phi_k(x)\ \forall k\}.\]
The two problems have the same minimizing \(x\)-components.
assumptions_latex: All branches have common domain \(X\), objective \(f\), and coefficient \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimax and epigraph problems have equal optimal values and identical minimizing \(x\)-components.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph representation of the finite maximum of objective-plus-residual branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Minimax Exact Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking the maximum of finitely many objective-plus-residual branches equals the objective plus the largest violation, so the minimax and ell-infinity penalties have identical exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the nonnegative violation components be \(r_j(x)=|h_j(x)|\) for \(1\le j\le p\) and \(r_{p+i}(x)=[g_i(x)]_+\) for \(1\le i\le m\). Then the finite minimax penalty has the representation
\[M_\rho(x)=\max_{1\le k\le p+m}\{f(x)+\rho r_k(x)\}=f(x)+\rho\max_{1\le k\le p+m}r_k(x).\]
Thus it is exactly the ell-infinity maximum-violation penalty. Local or global exactness of either representation at a parameter value is therefore equivalent to exactness of the other at the same value.
assumptions_latex: There is at least one constraint and the residual family is finite.
All branches share the same objective \(f\) and penalty parameter \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V_\infty(x)=P^{(\infty)}_\rho(x)\) for every \(x\) and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite maximum representation of componentwise exact penalties.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Violation Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many constraints, sum and maximum violations differ by at most the number of residuals, so exactness transfers between them with a possible parameter scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q=p+m\ge1\), and collect the nonnegative violations in \(r(x)\in\mathbb R_+^q\). Then
\[\lVert r(x)\rVert_\infty\le\lVert r(x)\rVert_1\le q\lVert r(x)\rVert_\infty.\]
Consequently, if \(x^*\) locally or globally minimizes \(f+\rho\lVert r\rVert_\infty\), it also minimizes \(f+\rho\lVert r\rVert_1\). If it minimizes \(f+\rho\lVert r\rVert_1\), it minimizes \(f+q\rho\lVert r\rVert_\infty\). Hence finite-parameter exactness is invariant under choosing sum or maximum violation, although sufficient exactness thresholds may scale by \(q\).
assumptions_latex: \(r(x)\in\mathbb R_+^q\) contains all absolute equality and positive inequality residuals.
The comparison uses the same feasible point \(x^*\), where \(r(x^*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness of \(f+\rho\lVert r\rVert_\infty\) implies exactness of \(f+\rho\lVert r\rVert_1\), while the reverse implication holds with parameter \(q\rho\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional transfer of exactness between sum and maximum violation penalties.

notation.meaning: Total number of equality and inequality residuals.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm-, gauge-, and distance-induced exact penalties
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(R:X\to Y\) map into a finite-dimensional vector space \(Y\), and let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a nonempty closed constraint set. Feasibility is \(R(x)\in K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional residual-space formulation; exactness is defined independently of the particular norm, gauge, or distance construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma:Y\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfy \(\gamma(0)=0\), \(\gamma(y)>0\) for \(y\neq0\), and positive homogeneity \(\gamma(ty)=t\gamma(y)\) for \(t\geq0\). Define the gauge distance \(d_\gamma(y,K)=\inf_{z\in K}\gamma(y-z)\) and the penalty \(\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho d_\gamma(R(x),K)\). When \(\gamma\) is a norm, this is the ordinary norm-distance penalty. The family is globally exact if some finite \(\bar\rho\) satisfies \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\Phi_\rho(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x):x\in X,\ R(x)\in K\}\) for all \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\). Local exactness at \(x^*\) is defined by the same equality restricted to a fixed neighborhood of \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm-gauge-distance penalty measures how far the residual mapping R(x) lies from its admissible set K using a positive homogeneous gauge. The penalized objective adds a positive multiple of this distance to f. Norm distance is the symmetric special case. The family is globally exact when its global minimizers coincide with the constrained global minimizers for every parameter above one finite threshold, and locally exact when the same correspondence holds in a fixed neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma\) is positive homogeneous, vanishes at zero, and is positive away from zero.
The feasible set \(\{x\in X:R(x)\in K\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_\rho=f+\rho d_\gamma(R(\cdot),K)\) is the gauge-distance penalty family, with exactness characterized by finite-threshold minimizer correspondence.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(K=\{0\}\), then \(d_\gamma(R(x),K)=\gamma(R(x))\).
If \(\gamma=\|\cdot\|\), then \(d_\gamma(y,K)=\operatorname{dist}_{\|\cdot\|}(y,K)\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(Y=\mathbb R^{m+r}\), \(K=\{0\}^m\times\mathbb R_-^r\), and an infinity norm produces a maximum-violation penalty.
A weighted norm produces component-scaled constraint violation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every feasible point has zero penalty term.
Different gauges encode different relative geometries without changing the feasible zero set when the gauge is positive definite.
boundary_notes: A nonclosed set \(K\) can have zero distance at points outside \(K\), so closedness is material.
Positive homogeneity alone does not ensure convexity, symmetry, or finite exactness.

notation.meaning: Infimal gauge displacement from y to K.

review_flags: No inspected local source was found that supports the full norm–gauge–distance scope and finite-threshold exactness definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Norm-, gauge-, and distance-induced exact penalties
Dual-Norm Support Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm penalty is the maximum of linear residual scalarizations over the scaled dual-norm ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\|\cdot\|_*\) is dual to \(\|\cdot\|\), then
\[\|r(x)\|=\max_{\|y\|_*\le1}\langle y,r(x)\rangle,\qquad f(x)+\rho\|r(x)\|=\max_{\|y\|_*\le\rho}\{f(x)+\langle y,r(x)\rangle\}.\]
The maxima are attained in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\rho,\|\cdot\|}(x)=\max_{\|y\|_*\le\rho}(f(x)+\langle y,r(x)\rangle)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function representation of a finite-dimensional norm penalty.

knowledge_statements.title: General Norm Exact Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any norm of the combined equality and positive inequality residual vector defines a penalty; finite-dimensional norm equivalence preserves exactness up to scaling the parameter threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the residual vector
\[r(x)=\bigl(h(x),[g(x)]_+\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{p+m},\]
and any norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) on \(\mathbb R^{p+m}\), the associated norm penalty is
\[P_{\rho,\lVert\cdot\rVert}(x)=f(x)+\rho\lVert r(x)\rVert,\qquad \rho>0.\]
It is locally exact at a feasible local minimizer \(x^*\) if some finite \(\bar\rho\) and neighborhood \(U\) make \(x^*\) a minimizer of \(P_{\rho,\lVert\cdot\rVert}\) over \(U\) for every \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\). In finite dimensions, equivalence of norms transfers exactness between norm choices after rescaling the threshold.
assumptions_latex: The constraint system is finite dimensional and has finitely many residual components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\rho,\lVert\cdot\rVert}=f+\rho\lVert r\rVert\) is a general norm penalty, and finite exactness does not depend on the norm choice except through threshold constants.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-vector exact penalties induced by an arbitrary finite-dimensional norm.

notation.meaning: Combined equality and positive inequality residual vector.
An arbitrary norm on the finite residual space.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without a Gauge-Residual Error Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the gauge residual is only quadratic in distance while the objective decreases linearly, every finite penalty coefficient fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{0\}\), \(r(x)=x^2\), \(\gamma(y)=|y|\), and \(f(x)=-|x|\). Then \(0\) is the constrained minimizer, but for every finite \(\rho>0\),
\[f(x)+\rho\gamma(r(x))=-|x|+\rho x^2<0\]
for all sufficiently small nonzero \(x\). Thus the gauge penalty is not locally exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite \(\rho\) makes \(0\) a local minimizer of \(-|x|+\rho x^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A residual gauge vanishing too rapidly may not support finite exactness.

knowledge_statements.title: Minkowski-Gauge Residual Penalty
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex body's Minkowski gauge measures residual size and yields a possibly asymmetric penalty; central symmetry makes it a norm penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^q\) be compact and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\), and define
\[\gamma_C(y)=\inf\{t\ge0:y\in tC\}.\]
For a residual map \(r\) with \(r^{-1}(0)=F\), the gauge penalty is
\[P_{\rho,C}(x)=f(x)+\rho\gamma_C(r(x)).\]
The gauge is finite, nonnegative, positive definite, positively homogeneous, and subadditive. It is a norm exactly when \(C=-C\).
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^q\) is compact and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\rho,C}=f+\rho\gamma_C\circ r\) is a positive-definite, positively homogeneous gauge penalty and is norm-based iff \(C=-C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Possibly asymmetric residual penalty generated by a convex gauge body.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Support Representation of a Gauge
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Minkowski gauge is the support function of the polar body, so the gauge penalty is a maximum of linear residual scalarizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With
\[C^\circ=\{z\in\mathbb R^q:\langle z,c\rangle\le1\ \forall c\in C\},\]
the gauge satisfies
\[\gamma_C(y)=\max_{z\in C^\circ}\langle z,y\rangle.\]
Consequently,
\[P_{\rho,C}(x)=\max_{z\in C^\circ}\{f(x)+\rho\langle z,r(x)\rangle\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^q\) is compact and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C=\sigma_{C^\circ}\) and \(P_{\rho,C}(x)=\max_{z\in C^\circ}(f(x)+\rho\langle z,r(x)\rangle)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-space polar representation of the Minkowski gauge.

notation.meaning: Support function of the polar body.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Residual Exactness Under an Error Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge penalty is locally exact when its residual gauge bounds distance to feasibility strongly enough; exactness can fail without that error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(x^*\in F\) locally minimizes \(f\) over \(F\), \(f\) is locally \(L\)-Lipschitz, and for some \(\alpha>0\),
\[\gamma_C(r(x))\ge\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\]
near \(x^*\). Then every \(\rho>L/\alpha\) makes \(x^*\) a local minimizer of \(f+\rho\gamma_C\circ r\). Without such residual-to-distance control, finite exactness need not hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\rho>L/\alpha\) is a sufficient local exactness coefficient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-threshold local exactness when gauge residual controls distance to feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Exact Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Possibly asymmetric exact penalties generated by Minkowski gauges of residual-space convex bodies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^q\) be a compact convex set with \(0\) in its interior. Its Minkowski gauge is
\[\gamma_C(y)=\inf\{t\ge0:y\in tC\}.\]
For a residual mapping \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) satisfying \(r(x)=0\) exactly at feasible points, the gauge penalty family is
\[P_{\rho,C}(x)=f(x)+\rho\gamma_C(r(x)),\qquad \rho>0.\]
The family is exact at a constrained minimizer when the usual finite-threshold local or global minimizer property holds. The gauge is positively homogeneous and positive definite, but need not be symmetric unless \(C=-C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex body's Minkowski gauge measures residual size and yields a possibly asymmetric exact penalty; it becomes norm-based when the body is centrally symmetric.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^q\) is compact and convex, with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\).
The residual mapping satisfies \(r^{-1}(0)=F\), where \(F\) is the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\rho,C}=f+\rho\gamma_C\circ r\) is a positive-homogeneous gauge penalty, symmetric precisely when the chosen gauge body is centrally symmetric.

notation.meaning: Convex gauge body in residual space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Minkowski-gauge construction is mathematically coherent, but no source is supplied for its placement as an exact-penalty family or for the conditions under which finite-threshold exactness holds. A specific source locator addressing gauge penalties and their exactness hypotheses is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without Lipschitz Control
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without suitable Lipschitz control, objective improvement can dominate the linear distance penalty, so no finite coefficient is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{0\}\subset\mathbb R\) and \(f(x)=-\sqrt{|x|}\). The point \(0\) is the constrained minimizer, but for every finite \(\rho>0\),
\[f(x)+\rho\operatorname{dist}(x,F)=-\sqrt{|x|}+\rho|x|<0=P_\rho(0)\]
for all sufficiently small nonzero \(x\). Hence no finite distance-penalty coefficient is locally exact at \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No \(\rho<\infty\) makes \(0\) a local minimizer of \(f(x)+\rho\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exactness can fail when objective decrease dominates distance linearly near feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Exactness of the Feasible-Set Distance Penalty
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a closed feasible set is an exact local penalty when its coefficient exceeds a local Lipschitz constant of the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, let \(x^*\in F\) locally minimize \(f\) over \(F\), and suppose \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on a neighborhood of \(x^*\). Define
\[P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\operatorname{dist}(x,F).\]
Then, after restricting to a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(x^*\), every \(\rho>L\) makes \(x^*\) a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)=0\) exactly when \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\rho>L\), \(x^*\) locally minimizes \(f+\rho\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,F)\), and the distance term vanishes exactly on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision-space distance penalization for a closed feasible set and locally Lipschitz objective.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from x to F.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance-Based Exact Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact penalization by distance to a closed feasible set under local Lipschitz continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(x^*\in F\) be a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(F\), and suppose \(f\) is Lipschitz with constant \(L\) on a neighborhood containing nearby points and their nearest feasible points. Define
\[P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\operatorname{dist}(x,F).\]
Then for every \(\rho>L\), after possibly shrinking the neighborhood, \(x^*\) is a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\). Thus distance to feasibility is an exact penalty under the stated local Lipschitz and neighborhood-projection conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the objective is locally Lipschitz and feasible projections stay in the local-optimality neighborhood, adding distance to the feasible set is exact for any parameter above the Lipschitz constant.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and closed, and \(x^*\) locally minimizes \(f\) on \(F\).
\(f\) is locally \(L\)-Lipschitz on the required neighborhood.
Nearest feasible points of sufficiently nearby points remain in the constrained local-optimality neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\rho>L\), \(x^*\) locally minimizes \(f(x)+\rho\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from x to F.
Local Lipschitz constant of the objective.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record states a sufficient exactness theorem rather than a generic property, so theorem is the more accurate content kind. Although the finite-dimensional distance argument is plausible, no source is supplied for the precise local Lipschitz and projection-neighborhood hypotheses. A specific theorem, proposition, or page locator is required before choosing a reliable replacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Only Differentiable Exact Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-only differentiable exact penalty is a smooth objective in the original variable whose finite parameter threshold preserves each targeted constrained local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set of a constrained problem. A primal-only differentiable penalty family is a collection \(E_\rho:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), indexed by \(\rho>0\), with each \(E_\rho\) continuously differentiable and containing no multiplier or auxiliary optimization variable. It is locally exact at a constrained local minimizer \(x^*\in F\) if there exist \(\bar\rho<\infty\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) such that
\[E_\rho(x^*)\le E_\rho(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U\text{ and }\rho\ge\bar\rho.\]
Exactness is a property of the constructed family, not a consequence of differentiability alone.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) is the feasible set and \(x^*\in F\) is a constrained local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is primal-only and locally exact exactly when the displayed finite-threshold local-minimizer condition holds without additional optimization variables.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness class for smooth penalty functions involving only the original decision variable.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT-Residual Minimization Does Not Select Constrained Minima
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared KKT residuals also minimize at KKT maxima and saddles, so additional structure is required for primal–dual differentiable exact penalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min_{u,v}(u^2-1)^2 subject to v=0. The feasible point (u,v)=(0,0) with multiplier \lambda=0 is a KKT point but a strict constrained local maximizer in the u direction. Nevertheless R(u,v,\lambda)=\tfrac12[4u(u^2-1)]^2+\tfrac12\lambda^2+\tfrac12v^2 has global minimum value zero at (0,0,0). Hence a smooth function whose zeros are all KKT pairs need not be an exact penalty whose local minimizers project only to constrained local minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(0,0,0)=0\quad\text{but}\quad(0,0)\text{ is not a constrained local minimizer}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating smooth primal–dual residual minimization from exact preservation of constrained minimizers.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f,h\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained finite-dimensional problems with multiplier variables retained as optimization variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For parameters \(c>0\) and \(\alpha>0\), define \(P_{c,\alpha}:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) by \(P_{c,\alpha}(x,\lambda)=L(x,\lambda)+\tfrac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2+\tfrac\alpha2\|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\|_2^2\). This is a primal–dual differentiable penalty because both \(x\) and the multiplier estimate \(\lambda\) are decision variables and the objective is continuously differentiable under the stated smoothness. It is exact on a specified region \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\) when finite admissible parameter thresholds exist such that the selected local or global minimizers of \(P_{c,\alpha}\) in \(D\) correspond exactly to KKT pairs \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) of \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\). At every KKT pair, \(h(x^*)=0\) and \(\nabla_xL(x^*,\lambda^*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal–dual differentiable exact penalty optimizes jointly over the primal vector and multiplier vector. It combines the Lagrangian with squared feasibility and Lagrangian-stationarity residuals. Under twice continuous differentiability it is smooth. Exactness is the additional finite-parameter property that its relevant minimizers in a stated region are precisely KKT pairs of the equality-constrained problem.
assumptions_latex: Any exactness assertion specifies a region and parameter range under which spurious minimizers are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{c,\alpha}\) is a differentiable penalty on \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\), and primal–dual exactness means finite-parameter minimizer correspondence with constrained KKT pairs.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The residual-only function \(\tfrac12\|h(x)\|_2^2+\tfrac12\|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\|_2^2\) has value zero exactly at KKT pairs, but it does not retain the objective-curvature preference encoded by \(L\).

A matrix-weighted stationarity term replaces the scalar \(\alpha\) by a suitable linear operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Differentiable Exact Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth exact penalty class whose optimization variables include primal and multiplier estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a constrained problem with primal variable \(x\) and multiplier vector \(y\), a primal–dual differentiable penalty family consists of continuously differentiable functions \(E_\rho(x,y)\). It is locally exact at a KKT pair \((x^*,y^*)\) if some finite \(\bar\rho\) and neighborhoods \(U\) of \(x^*\) and \(V\) of \(y^*\) satisfy
\[E_\rho(x^*,y^*)\le E_\rho(x,y)\qquad\text{for all }(x,y)\in U\times V\text{ and }\rho\ge\bar\rho,\]
and every minimizing pair in the designated neighborhood has a feasible primal component satisfying the intended KKT system. The multiplier variables are part of the smooth exact formulation rather than externally fixed parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal–dual differentiable exact penalty is smooth in both decisions and multipliers and, above a finite threshold, locally minimizes at KKT pairs with feasible primal components.
assumptions_latex: The constrained problem admits a KKT pair \((x^*,y^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local exactness means that a finite threshold makes \((x^*,y^*)\) a local minimizer and excludes locally minimizing pairs with non-KKT primal components in the designated neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Differentiable Exact Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth dimension-augmented penalty is exact when nearby minimizers above a finite threshold project precisely to constrained local solutions in the original variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set, and introduce an auxiliary variable \(z\in\mathbb R^s\). An auxiliary-variable differentiable penalty family consists of continuously differentiable functions \(E_\rho:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^s\to\mathbb R\). It is locally exact at a constrained local minimizer \(x^*\) if there exist \(z^*\), a finite \(\bar\rho\), and a neighborhood \(W\) of \((x^*,z^*)\) such that \((x^*,z^*)\) minimizes \(E_\rho\) over \(W\) for every \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\), and the primal projection of every designated nearby minimizing pair belongs to \(F\) and solves the original local problem.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) is the feasible set and \(x^*\) is a constrained local minimizer.
Each \(E_\rho\) is continuously differentiable in \((x,z)\) near a representing pair \((x^*,z^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness requires both local minimization of \(E_\rho\) at \((x^*,z^*)\) for all \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\) and correct projection of nearby minimizing pairs onto constrained solutions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth exact penalty class obtained by augmenting the decision space with nonmultiplier variables.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set of a nonlinear program and let \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be an auxiliary-variable space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional lifted formulations; the definition concerns exactness after projection from a smooth extended-space problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An auxiliary-variable differentiable penalty is a family \(P_\rho:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) with \(P_\rho\in C^1(X\times Y)\) such that the lifted unconstrained problem is \(\min_{(x,y)\in X\times Y}P_\rho(x,y)\). It is globally exact for the original constrained problem when there is a finite \(\bar\rho\) for which, for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\), \(\operatorname{proj}_X\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in X\times Y}P_\rho(x,y)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\), and every constrained global minimizer admits at least one minimizing lift \(y\). It is locally exact at \(x^*\) when some lift \(y^*\), neighborhood \(U\) of \((x^*,y^*)\), and finite threshold give the analogous local correspondence. The auxiliary variables may encode slacks, smoothing variables, or residual factorizations; exactness is always assessed after projection to \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An auxiliary-variable differentiable exact penalty replaces the original constrained problem by a smooth unconstrained problem on a higher-dimensional space. Above a finite threshold, projecting the lifted minimizers onto the original variables must give exactly the constrained minimizers, and each constrained minimizer must possess a minimizing lift. Local exactness uses the same condition near one lifted solution. The auxiliary coordinates can encode slacks or smooth representations, but they are not themselves original decision variables.
assumptions_latex: Any asserted exactness threshold is finite and uniform for all larger parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Auxiliary-variable exactness is the equality between projected lifted minimizers and original constrained minimizers for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Global exactness can be written as two inclusions: every lifted minimizer projects to a constrained minimizer, and every constrained minimizer has a minimizing lift.
special_cases_latex: Slack variables satisfying \(g(x)+s^2=0\) can convert inequalities into smooth equalities in an extended space.
A scalar smoothing variable can replace a nonsmooth residual expression when the lifted function remains exact after projection.
immediate_consequences_latex: Uniqueness of the primal constrained minimizer does not require uniqueness of its auxiliary lift.
Dimension augmentation distinguishes this family from primal-only smooth penalties.
boundary_notes: A smooth approximation whose projected minimizers converge only as a smoothing parameter vanishes is asymptotic, not finitely exact under this definition.
Eliminating auxiliary variables may recover a nonsmooth reduced objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual aggregation architecture for penalty models
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(r:X\to\mathbb R_+^q\) collect nonnegative residual components with \(r(x)=0\iff x\in F\), and let \(A:\mathbb R_+^q\to[0,+\infty]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite heterogeneous residual systems; aggregation specifies how component violations form one scalar penalty term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty aggregation architecture is a pair \((r,A)\) defining \(V(x)=A(r(x))\) and \(\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x)\), where \(A(0)=0\), \(A(u)>0\) for every \(u\in r(X)\setminus\{0\}\), and \(A\) is nondecreasing on \(\mathbb R_+^q\) in the componentwise order. A single-parameter architecture uses one \(\rho>0\). A weighted architecture has \(A_w(u)=A(w_1u_1,\ldots,w_qu_q)\) with \(w_i>0\). A grouped or decomposable architecture partitions \(\{1,…,q\}\) into blocks \(I_b\), forms block penalties \(A_b(r_{I_b}(x))\), and combines them through an outer aggregator \(B\). The zero-set requirement \(V^{-1}(0)=F\) is mandatory; exactness or asymptotic recovery is a separate property of the resulting family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty aggregation architecture consists of a vector of nonnegative residuals and a scalar aggregation map. The aggregator must vanish at zero, remain positive on every nonzero attainable residual vector, and be monotone componentwise. One parameter may scale the whole aggregate, positive weights may rescale individual residuals, and grouped systems may use inner block aggregators followed by an outer aggregator. The construction must preserve the feasible zero set; it does not automatically guarantee finite exactness.
assumptions_latex: \(r_i(x)\geq0\) for every component and \(r(x)=0\iff x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V=A\circ r\) is a scalar feasibility measure, and \(\Phi_\rho=f+\rho V\) is the penalty model induced by the chosen aggregation architecture.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Maximum aggregation is \(A(u)=\|u\|_\infty\).
Additive aggregation is \(A_w(u)=\sum_{i=1}^q w_i u_i\) with \(w_i>0\).
special_cases_latex: Equality and inequality residuals may be collected as \(r(x)=(|h(x)|,[g(x)]_+)\).
Block maxima followed by a weighted sum define a two-level grouped architecture.
immediate_consequences_latex: Strictly positive weights preserve the residual zero set.
Changing the aggregator can change smoothness and exactness while leaving feasibility unchanged.
boundary_notes: Zero weights can erase constraints and violate zero-set preservation.
Monotonicity and zero-set preservation do not by themselves establish an exactness threshold.

children.title: Single-Parameter Penalty Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Common penalty strength across aggregated residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Scale Reparameterization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescaling the aggregate and inversely rescaling the common parameter leaves the penalized objective unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(a>0\), \[f(x)+\rho\Phi(r(x))=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{a}(a\Phi)(r(x)).\] Thus the numerical value of the common parameter is meaningful only relative to a fixed normalization of \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\rho,\Phi)\text{ and }(\rho/a,a\Phi)\text{ define the same penalized objective}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization ambiguity between the common parameter and residual aggregate.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Parameter Penalty Aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single positive scalar multiplies one aggregate of all constraint residuals; the aggregation rule, rather than separate penalty parameters, determines their relative influence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and let residuals \(r_i:X\to[0,\infty)\) vanish exactly when constraint \(i\) is satisfied. A single-parameter aggregate penalty is a family \[P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\,\Phi(r_1(x),\ldots,r_m(x)),\qquad \rho>0,\] where \(\Phi:[0,\infty)^m\to[0,\infty)\) satisfies \(\Phi(z)=0\) if and only if \(z=0\). The same scalar \(\rho\) therefore controls the strength of every residual, while their relative influence is determined solely by \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\Phi(r_1(x),\ldots,r_m(x))\) uses one common penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar penalty strength applied uniformly to an aggregate constraint-violation measure.

children.title: Weighted Penalty Families
children.top_down_role: Constraint-specific weights and residual scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Weight Detection Loss
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-weight residuals are detected exactly, while a zero-weight constraint becomes invisible and can enlarge the penalty zero set when it is not redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(V_w(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\phi_i(r_i(x))\), suppose \(w_i\ge0\), \(\phi_i(t)\ge0\), and \(\phi_i(t)=0\iff t=0\). Then \[V_w(x)=0\iff r_i(x)=0\quad\text{for every }i\text{ with }w_i>0.\] A constraint with \(w_j=0\) is therefore not detected by this penalty term; if the residual system admits a point satisfying all positive-weight constraints but violating constraint \(j\), the penalty zero set strictly contains the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V_w(x)=0\iff r_i(x)=0\text{ for all }i\text{ such that }w_i>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for preservation of the residual zero set by additive weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Scale Nonidentifiability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common scale can be shifted between the overall penalty parameter and all component weights; only their products affect the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[P_{\rho,w}(x)=f(x)+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\phi_i(r_i(x)),\] only the products \(\rho w_i\) determine the penalized objective. For every \(a>0\), \[P_{\rho,w}=P_{\rho/a,aw}.\] Consequently, one positive normalization of \(w\) may be imposed without changing the represented family.
assumptions_latex: The weighted penalty has the displayed additive form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{\rho,w}=P_{\rho/a,aw}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between overall scale and proportional rescaling of all component weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Penalty Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive constraint-specific weights scale residuals before aggregation, allowing normalization or unequal enforcement without changing which points have zero total violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_i:X\to[0,\infty)\) be constraint residuals and let \(w_i>0\). A weighted penalty family has the form \[P_{\rho,w}(x)=f(x)+\rho\,\Phi(w_1r_1(x),\ldots,w_mr_m(x)),\qquad \rho>0,\] or, in the fully separable case, \[P_w(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\phi_i(r_i(x)).\] Positive weights preserve the common zero set of the residuals and permit constraint-specific normalization or penalty strength.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted penalty has zero violation term exactly when \(r_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-specific scaling within an additive or norm-based penalty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary for preservation of the common residual zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(V_w(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\phi_i(r_i(x))\), suppose \(w_i\ge0\) and \(\phi_i(t)=0\iff t=0\). Then
\[V_w(x)=0\iff r_i(x)=0\quad\text{for every }i\text{ with }w_i>0.\]
Hence if some \(w_j=0\), violation of constraint \(j\) is invisible to \(V_w\), and the zero set can strictly contain the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity of every component weight is necessary for an additive weighted penalty to detect every constraint violation.

children.title: Decomposable Penalty Structures

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let the constraint residuals be partitioned into nonempty blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_B\), and write \(r_b(x)=r_{I_b}(x)\in\mathbb R_+^{|I_b|}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite grouped constraint systems; decomposability refers to additive or nested block structure, not to separability of the objective itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty \(V:X\to[0,+\infty]\) is block decomposable with respect to \(I_1,\ldots,I_B\) if there are block functions \(V_b:X\to[0,+\infty]\) depending on \(x\) only through \(r_b(x)\), positive weights \(\omega_b>0\), and \(V(x)=\sum_{b=1}^B\omega_bV_b(x)\), with \(V_b(x)=0\iff r_b(x)=0\). More generally, a nested decomposable penalty has \(V(x)=A(V_1(x),\ldots,V_B(x))\), where \(A\) is nonnegative, componentwise nondecreasing, and vanishes only when all its arguments vanish. The associated family is \(\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x)\), or \(\Phi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(x)=f(x)+\sum_b\rho_bV_b(x)\) for block parameters \(\rho_b>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-decomposable penalty partitions residuals into groups, assigns each group a nonnegative penalty that vanishes exactly when that group is satisfied, and combines the group penalties additively with positive weights or through a zero-preserving monotone outer aggregator. A scalar parameter can scale the total penalty, or each block can have its own positive parameter. Decomposability concerns the violation model and does not require the objective or variables to be separable.
assumptions_latex: \(I_1,\ldots,I_B\) form a partition of the residual indices.
All additive weights or block penalty parameters are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate penalty vanishes exactly when every residual block vanishes and admits explicit blockwise evaluation or weighting.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For additive aggregation, \(V(x)=0\iff V_b(x)=0\) for every \(b\).
A nested representation is \(V=A\circ(V_1,\ldots,V_B)\).
special_cases_latex: One residual per block gives a componentwise separable penalty.
One block containing all residuals recovers a nondecomposed aggregate penalty.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive block weights preserve the feasible zero set.
Block parameters permit heterogeneous scaling without changing which points have zero violation.
boundary_notes: Penalty decomposability does not imply that minimization decomposes across variable blocks.
Overlapping groups require a cover formulation rather than the partition definition used here.

notation.meaning: Index set of residual block b.
Penalty contribution of residual block b.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-decomposable penalty structure
Block-Additive Penalty Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residuals are partitioned into disjoint blocks, each block is aggregated independently, and the resulting block terms are added.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[\{1,\ldots,m\}=I_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_B\]
and let \(r_{I_b}(x)=(r_i(x))_{i\in I_b}\). A block-structured penalty has the form
\[P(x)=f(x)+\sum_{b=1}^B\rho_b\Phi_b(r_{I_b}(x)),\qquad \rho_b>0,\]
where \(\Phi_b(z)\ge0\) and \(\Phi_b(z)=0\iff z=0\). It permits arbitrary within-block aggregation but contains no term jointly depending on distinct blocks. Its total penalty term is zero exactly when every residual block is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P-f=\sum_b\rho_b\Phi_b(r_{I_b})\), and \(P(x)-f(x)=0\iff r_{I_b}(x)=0\) for every \(b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty decomposition over a fixed disjoint partition of residual indices.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty decomposition over a fixed partition of the constraint residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the constraint indices as \(\{1,\ldots,m\}=I_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_B\), and write \(r_{I_b}(x)=(r_i(x))_{i\in I_b}\). A block-structured penalty admits the representation \[P(x)=f(x)+\sum_{b=1}^{B}\rho_b\,\Phi_b(r_{I_b}(x)),\qquad \rho_b>0,\] where each \(\Phi_b\) is nonnegative and vanishes only at the zero block. Thus interactions may occur among residuals inside a block, but no penalty term jointly depends on residuals from distinct blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint residuals are partitioned into blocks; each block has its own aggregate penalty, and the total penalty is the sum of those block terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P-f\) decomposes as \(\sum_{b=1}^{B}\rho_b\Phi_b(r_{I_b})\), with no cross-block term.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At smooth points, each residual contributes an independent summand to the gradient and Hessian of a constraintwise separable penalty.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The derivatives of \(P\) decompose into the displayed componentwise sums.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative structure inherited from constraintwise additivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity Inheritance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex nondecreasing component kernels preserve convexity when composed with convex residuals and summed with nonnegative weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a convex domain, if \(f\) and every \(r_i\) are convex, each \(\phi_i:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) is convex and nondecreasing, and \(\rho_i\ge0\), then \[P(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i\phi_i(r_i(x))\] is convex.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\phi_i\) is convex and nondecreasing, and \(\rho_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for convexity of a constraintwise additive penalty.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraintwise Separable Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The violation penalty is a sum of one-residual terms. With positive-definite component penalties, its zero set is exactly the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For residuals \(r_i:X\to[0,\infty)\), a constraintwise separable penalty is represented by \[P(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\rho_i\,\phi_i(r_i(x)),\] where \(\rho_i>0\) and each \(\phi_i:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) satisfies \(\phi_i(0)=0\). If additionally \(\phi_i(t)>0\) for \(t>0\), then the penalty contribution vanishes exactly when every constraint is satisfied. Each summand depends on only one residual, so changing \(r_i\) directly changes only its corresponding summand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(x)-f(x)=\sum_i\rho_i\phi_i(r_i(x))\), and this quantity is zero exactly at feasible points under positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive decomposition into terms depending on individual constraint residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular-Difference Separability Criterion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate is additively separable across prescribed residual blocks exactly when every two-block rectangular mixed difference vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\prod_{b=1}^B D_b\) and \(F:D\to\mathbb R\). A representation \(F(z)=c+\sum_{b=1}^B F_b(z_b)\) exists if and only if, for every pair \(b\ne c\), every fixed choice of the other blocks, and all \(u_b,u_b'\in D_b\), \(u_c,u_c'\in D_c\), the rectangular mixed difference vanishes: \[F(u_b,u_c)-F(u_b',u_c)-F(u_b,u_c')+F(u_b',u_c')=0.\]
assumptions_latex: The attainable residual domain is the product set \(D=\prod_{b=1}^B D_b\).
The displayed differences are evaluated with all unlisted blocks fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(z)=c+\sum_{b=1}^B F_b(z_b)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{all displayed rectangular mixed differences vanish}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact test for additive decomposition across a prescribed product partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Residual Coupling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Euclidean norm couples two residuals and cannot be written as a sum of one-residual penalties on a nontrivial product neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(r_1,r_2)=\sqrt{r_1^2+r_2^2}\) on \([0,\infty)^2\), the rectangular mixed difference at \((0,0),(a,0),(0,b),(a,b)\) is \[\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b\ne0\qquad(a,b>0).\] Hence no functions \(F_1,F_2\) and constant \(c\) satisfy \(F(r_1,r_2)=c+F_1(r_1)+F_2(r_2)\) throughout any product neighborhood containing those points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(r_1,r_2)\ne c+F_1(r_1)+F_2(r_2)\text{ on the stated product domain}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical coupled aggregate that is not constraintwise additive.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Decomposition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-residual coupling prevents additive decomposition over prescribed blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two nonnegative residuals be penalized by \(V(x)=\sqrt{r_1(x)^2+r_2(x)^2}\). There do not exist functions \(v_1,v_2:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(V(x)=v_1(r_1(x))+v_2(r_2(x))\) for all attainable residual pairs containing a neighborhood of \((0,0)\). Indeed, additive separability would force every rectangular mixed difference to vanish, whereas the Euclidean norm has nonzero mixed differences away from the axes. Consequently, a block boundary is valid only when no penalty term couples residuals lying in different blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled norm such as the Euclidean norm cannot generally be written as a sum of individual-residual penalties; decomposition boundaries must respect all residual couplings.
assumptions_latex: The attainable residual set contains a neighborhood of \((0,0)\) in \([0,infty)^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No representation \(V(r_1,r_2)=v_1(r_1)+v_2(r_2)\) holds throughout that neighborhood.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Euclidean-norm example is a suitable failure boundary, but the record has no cited evidence and includes proof-style justification beginning with “Indeed,” contrary to the no-proof requirement. The assumption also contains malformed \([0,infty)^2\) notation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_\rho=f+\rho V\) on \(X\), where \(V\geq0\) and \(V^{-1}(0)=F\), and let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic penalty families; the hierarchy distinguishes finite exactness, minimizing sequences, local paths, approximate stationarity, and numerical parameter growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The penalty asymptotic regime of \(\{\Phi_\rho\}_{\rho>0}\) is classified by the strongest recovery relation established: (i) finite exactness, if \(\operatorname*{argmin}_X\Phi_\rho=S\) for all \(\rho\geq\bar\rho<+\infty\); (ii) global-minimizer limit recovery, if every cluster point of every selected \(x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_X\Phi_{\rho_k}\), \(\rho_k\to+\infty\), lies in \(S\); (iii) local-minimizer path recovery, if local minimizers \(x_k\) of \(\Phi_{\rho_k}\) exist with \(x_k\to x^*\in F\); (iv) inexact-stationarity recovery, if residual tolerances tend to zero and every regular cluster point satisfies constrained first-order stationarity; and (v) numerical-boundary behavior, which records conditioning or solvability loss as \(\rho\) grows. These labels are properties of a formulation together with its quantified solution selection and assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty family is placed in the strongest recovery regime it satisfies. Finite exactness recovers constrained minimizers above a finite threshold. Global-minimizer recovery concerns cluster points of exact global penalized minimizers as the parameter diverges. Local-path recovery concerns branches of local penalized minimizers. Inexact-stationarity recovery concerns approximately stationary subproblem solutions whose limiting regular points satisfy constrained stationarity. Numerical-boundary behavior records the loss of conditioning or solvability at large parameters and is not itself a solution correspondence.
assumptions_latex: Every regime states whether selected subproblem points are global minimizers, local minimizers, or approximate stationary points.
Cluster-point conclusions are conditional on the existence of cluster points unless compactness is separately assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hierarchy orders penalty claims by finite exact recovery, asymptotic minimizer recovery, local path recovery, inexact stationarity recovery, and numerical limiting behavior.
special_cases_latex: Quadratic exterior penalties typically belong to an asymptotic regime.
Nonsmooth exact penalties may belong to the finite-exactness regime under suitable regularity.
immediate_consequences_latex: A finite-exactness claim is stronger than recovery only along one diverging parameter sequence.
A stationarity-limit claim does not imply local or global optimality.
boundary_notes: The regimes are not automatically nested without matching quantifiers and solution concepts.
Numerical ill-conditioning is not a failure of mathematical convergence by definition.
review_flags: The inspected source separately supports several listed regimes, but no single locator supports this complete formal hierarchy.

children.title: Penalty-Sequence Convergence Principle
children.top_down_role: Limit regimes for exact and approximate solutions of increasingly restrictive penalty subproblems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(F=\{x\in X:h(x)=0\}\neq\varnothing\), and \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\tfrac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic equality-penalty sequences with exact or approximate subproblem solutions; the definition separates the convergence property from hypotheses establishing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \((x_k,\lambda_k,c_k,\varepsilon_k)\) is a penalty-solution sequence when \(\{\lambda_k\}\) is bounded, \(0<c_k<c_{k+1}\), \(c_k\to+\infty\), \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), and either \(x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k)\) or \(L_{c_k}(x_k,\lambda_k)\leq\inf_{x\in X}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k)+\varepsilon_k\). The global penalty-sequence convergence property holds when every cluster point of every such sequence is feasible and globally minimizes \(f\) over \(F\). A stationarity version replaces objective-value accuracy by \(\|\nabla_xL_{c_k}(x_k,\lambda_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_k\) and requires every regular cluster point to satisfy constrained first-order stationarity with an associated limiting multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty-solution sequence uses bounded multiplier estimates, strictly increasing penalty parameters tending to infinity, vanishing subproblem tolerances, and exact or objective-value approximate solutions of each quadratic penalty subproblem. The global convergence property means that every cluster point of every such sequence is feasible and globally optimal. A weaker stationarity version uses vanishing gradient residuals and requires regular cluster points to satisfy the constrained first-order conditions with limiting multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Penalty-sequence convergence is the quantified requirement that all cluster points of the specified subproblem-solution sequences possess the stated constrained solution property.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The exact global-minimizer case is obtained by setting \(\varepsilon_k=0\).
special_cases_latex: With \(\lambda_k=0\), this is the classical quadratic penalty sequence.
For gradient-residual accuracy, regularity means \(\nabla h(x^*)\) has full column rank.
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition is conditional on cluster points unless boundedness is separately available.
Objective-value accuracy and stationarity accuracy define different convergence principles.
boundary_notes: Approximate global minimization is stronger than approximate stationarity.
A divergent sequence can satisfy all subproblem conditions while having no cluster point.

children.title: Global-Minimizer Limit Regime
children.top_down_role: Global penalized solution sequences and constrained limit points.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Global-Minimizer Limit Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing global penalized-subproblem value errors preserve feasibility, constrained global optimality of cluster points, and optimal-value convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be compact, let \(f,V:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, let \(V\ge0\), and suppose \(F=\{x\in X:V(x)=0\}\ne\varnothing\). If \(\rho_k\to\infty\), \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), and \[f(x_k)+\rho_kV(x_k)\le\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho_kV(x)\}+\varepsilon_k,\] then \(V(x_k)\to0\), every cluster point of \((x_k)\) globally minimizes \(f\) over \(F\), and \(f(x_k)+\rho_kV(x_k)\to\min_{x\in F}f(x)\).
assumptions_latex: The displayed penalized-subproblem objective-gap bound holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x_k)\to0\), every cluster point belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\), and the penalized values converge to \(\min_F f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global penalty convergence under vanishing penalized-subproblem objective gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Minimizer Limit Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain, global minimizers of increasingly severe continuous penalties become feasible, and every cluster point globally solves the constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact, let \(f,V:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous, suppose \(V\ge0\), and let \(F=\{x\in X:V(x)=0\}\ne\varnothing\). If \(\rho_k\to\infty\) and \[x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho_kV(x)\},\] then every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \((x_k)\) belongs to \(F\) and satisfies \[f(\bar x)=\min_{x\in F}f(x).\] Moreover, \(V(x_k)\to0\) and the penalized optimal values converge to the constrained optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\) lies in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\), and \(V(x_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of global minimizers for increasing nonnegative penalty parameters.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and closed \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Define \(F=\{x\in X:h(x)=0\}\neq\varnothing\) and \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\tfrac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global solutions of quadratic penalty subproblems; the regime gives cluster-point recovery and does not assert existence or convergence of the entire sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The global-minimizer limit regime consists of sequences \(x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L_{c_k}(x,\lambda_k)\), where \(\{\lambda_k\}\) is bounded, \(0<c_k<c_{k+1}\), and \(c_k\to+\infty\). The regime has constrained global recovery when every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \(\{x_k\}\) belongs to \(F\) and satisfies \(f(\bar x)=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Under continuity of \(f,h\), closedness of \(X\), existence of each global penalized minimizer, and nonemptiness of \(F\), this cluster-point property is the classical quadratic-penalty global convergence conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the global-minimizer limit regime, each iterate is a global minimizer of a quadratic penalty subproblem, multiplier estimates remain bounded, and the positive penalty parameters increase to infinity. Constrained global recovery means that every cluster point is feasible and attains the constrained global optimum. The regime does not require the complete sequence to converge and does not itself guarantee that penalized global minimizers or cluster points exist.
assumptions_latex: Each \(x_k\) is a global minimizer of \(L_{c_k}(\cdot,\lambda_k)\) over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(\bar x\in F\) and \(f(\bar x)=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every convergent subsequence \(x_{k_j}\to\bar x\), \(h(\bar x)=0\) and \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\).
special_cases_latex: The classical quadratic penalty method has \(\lambda_k=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If the sequence is bounded and the constrained global minimizer is unique, then every cluster point equals that minimizer.
The conclusion concerns global, not merely local, constrained optimality.
boundary_notes: Closedness and continuity do not ensure that every penalized subproblem attains its infimum.
Without boundedness, the sequence may have no cluster point.

notation.meaning: Cluster point of global penalized minimizers.
