knowledge_statements.title: Regular Large-Penalty Local Path and Rates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ and positive reduced Lagrangian curvature produce a locally unique large-penalty minimizer path; primal, multiplier, and feasibility errors are all of inverse-penalty order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), and use the KKT convention \(
abla f(x^*)+J_c(x^*)^{\mathsf T}\lambda^*=0\). Suppose \(f,c\in C^2\), \(J_c(x^*)\) has full row rank, and \(d^{\mathsf T}
abla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*)d>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker J_c(x^*)\), where \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\). Then for all sufficiently small \(t\ge0\) there is a locally unique \(C^1\) solution \((x(t),\lambda(t))\) near \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) of \[
abla f(x)+J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0,\qquad c(x)-t\lambda=0.\] For \(t>0\), setting \(ho=1/t\) makes \(x(t)\) a strict local minimizer of \(f(x)+ rac{ho}{2}\lVert c(x)Vert^2\) and \(\lambda(t)=ho c(x(t))\). Moreover, \(x(t)-x^*=O(t)\), \(\lambda(t)-\lambda^*=O(t)\), and \(c(x(t))=O(t)\).
assumptions_latex: The Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on \(\ker J_c(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all sufficiently large \(\rho\), a locally unique strict local minimizer \(x(1/\rho)\) exists with \(x(1/\rho)-x^*=O(\rho^{-1})\), \(\rho c(x(1/\rho))-\lambda^*=O(\rho^{-1})\), and \(c(x(1/\rho))=O(\rho^{-1})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic-penalty branch obtained as a smooth perturbation of the equality-constrained KKT system.

notation.meaning: Equality-constrained Lagrangian under the stated plus-sign convention.
Effective multiplier, equal to \(\rho c(x(t))\) for positive t.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local penalized-minimizer path approaching a constrained minimizer
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(L_c(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\tfrac c2\|h(x)\|_2^2\) on a closed set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(X^*\) be an isolated compact set of constrained local minimizers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic-penalty solutions near an isolated constrained local-minimizer set; the path may be a sequence or subsequence rather than a smooth parameterized curve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local-minimizer path regime toward \(X^*\) is a diverging parameter sequence \(c_k\to+\infty\), a bounded multiplier sequence \(\lambda_k\), and local minimizers \(x_k\) of \(L_{c_k}(\cdot,\lambda_k)\) over \(X\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X^*)\to0\). For a singleton \(X^*=\{x^*\}\), this is \(x_k\to x^*\). The set \(X^*\) is isolated when every point of it is a constrained local minimizer and some fixed neighborhood contains no other constrained local minimizers. The term path denotes the selected branch of local penalized solutions; it does not require uniqueness, differentiability with respect to \(c\), or global minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local-minimizer path is a sequence of local solutions of increasingly severe quadratic penalty subproblems that approaches an isolated compact set of constrained local minimizers. If the set consists of one point, the penalized local minimizers converge to that point. The selected branch need not be unique or smooth in the parameter and need not contain global penalized minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(X^*\) is a nonempty compact isolated set of constrained local minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a selected sequence or subsequence of local penalized minimizers satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X^*)\to0\); for \(X^*=\{x^*\}\), \(x_k\to x^*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For compact \(X^*\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X^*)\to0\) means every cluster point of a bounded selected branch lies in \(X^*\).
special_cases_latex: A strict constrained local minimizer is an isolated set containing one point.
immediate_consequences_latex: Local-path recovery is weaker than global-minimizer recovery.
Different local branches may approach different members of a non-singleton isolated set.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert a continuously differentiable path \(x(c)\).
A local penalized minimizer can exist far from every constrained local minimizer; the regime concerns the selected approaching branch.

notation.meaning: Compact isolated set of constrained local minimizers.
Euclidean distance from x to the set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(f\) and \(c\) twice continuously differentiable. knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Stationarity Limit Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If quadratic-penalty stationarity errors vanish and scaled residuals converge, the limiting point is feasible and satisfies the equality-constrained KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable, let \(\rho_k\to\infty\), and define \(P_k(x)=f(x)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\). Suppose \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(\lVert\nabla P_k(x_k)\rVert\to0\), and \(\lambda_k=\rho_kc(x_k)\) converges to \(\bar\lambda\). Then \(c(\bar x)=0\) and \[\nabla f(\bar x)+J_c(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda=0.\] Hence \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) satisfies the equality-constrained KKT conditions despite inexact subproblem stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(\bar x)=0\) and \(\nabla f(\bar x)+J_c(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT limits from approximately stationary quadratic-penalty subproblems.

The multiplier estimate is the bounded input multiplier plus the penalty parameter times the equality residual. If a subsequence converges to a point where the constraint Jacobian has full column rank, constrained stationary recovery means that the shifted multipliers converge and the limit satisfies feasibility and the equality-constrained first-order stationarity equation.

abla_xL_{c_k}(x_k,\lambda_k)=
abla f(x_k)+
abla h(x_k)\widetilde\lambda_k\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\), let \(V:\mathbb R^n\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfy \(V^{-1}(0)=F\), and define \(\Phi_c(x)=f(x)+cV(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonlinear programming; global, local, and stationary exactness are distinct correspondences and must not be conflated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exact penalty principle is the finite-threshold correspondence between the constrained problem and \(\Phi_c\). Global exactness means that some \(\bar c<+\infty\) satisfies \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\Phi_c(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\) for every \(c\geq\bar c\). Local exactness at a constrained local minimizer \(x^*\) means that some neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) and finite \(\bar c\) satisfy \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in U}\Phi_c(x)\) for every \(c\geq\bar c\); strong local correspondence additionally requires every local penalized minimizer in \(U\) to be feasible and locally solve the constrained problem. Stationary exactness requires a separately stated correspondence between penalized stationary points and constrained KKT points. For the maximum-violation function \(V=P\), a strict constrained local minimizer satisfying the source's second-order regularity assumptions is locally exact for every \(c\) exceeding the sum of the absolute equality multipliers and nonnegative inequality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact penalty principle says that constrained solution structure is reproduced by penalized problems after one finite threshold, rather than only in the limit as the parameter tends to infinity. Global exactness equates global minimizer sets. Local exactness preserves a specified constrained local minimizer in one neighborhood, while strong local correspondence also excludes infeasible local penalized minimizers there. Stationary exactness is a different property relating penalized stationary points to KKT points. For the maximum-violation penalty, a multiplier-based finite local threshold is available under the cited regularity assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The exactness threshold \(\bar c\) is finite and independent of the particular \(c\geq\bar c\).
For the multiplier threshold specialization, \(x^*\) is a strict constrained local minimizer satisfying the source's stated second-order sufficiency and regularity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness is finite-parameter equality or correspondence of the specified constrained and penalized solution sets; for maximum violation, local exactness holds when \(c>\sum_i|\lambda_i^*|+\sum_j\mu_j^*\) under the cited hypotheses.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Global exactness is equivalent to equality of optimal values plus equality of global minimizer sets for all \(c\geq\bar c\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, the cited sufficient local threshold is \(c>\|\lambda^*\|_1\).
For inequality constraints only, it is \(c>\sum_j\mu_j^*\) in the cited maximum-violation formulation.
immediate_consequences_latex: A single sufficiently large finite parameter can represent the constrained local solution.
Finite exactness is categorically stronger than recovery asserted only along \(c_k\to+\infty\).
boundary_notes: Local exactness does not imply global exactness.
Preservation of minimizers does not automatically imply correspondence of all stationary points.
The multiplier bound is sufficient under the cited assumptions, not a universal minimal threshold.

notation.meaning: Equality and inequality multiplier vectors at the constrained solution.

children.title: Local Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness near constrained local solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Local Exactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise local exactness preserves one specified constrained local minimizer for all sufficiently large finite parameters but does not classify every nearby penalized minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x^*\in F be a local minimizer of f over F and P_\rho=f+\rho V, with V\ge0 and F=\{V=0\}. The penalty is pointwise locally exact at x^* if there exist \bar\rho<\infty and a neighborhood U of x^* such that x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X\cap U}P_\rho(x) for every \rho>\bar\rho. This alone does not imply that every other penalized local minimizer in U is feasible or constrained-optimal.
assumptions_latex: x^*\in F=\{V=0\} is a constrained local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U,\bar\rho<\infty\;\forall\rho>\bar\rho:\ x^*\in\arg\min_{X\cap U}P_\rho.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of a selected constrained local solution rather than equality of all nearby solution sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Local Exactness under a Local Error Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict constrained local minimum remains strict when the penalty coefficient exceeds the local Lipschitz constant times the error-bound modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the local Lipschitz, nearest-feasible-point, and error-bound assumptions of the seed theorem, suppose additionally that x^* is a strict local minimizer of f over F. Then every \rho>L\kappa makes x^* a strict local minimizer of P_\rho=f+\rho V.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of the immutable local-exactness theorem hold near x^*.
x^* is a strict local minimizer of f over F.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni x^*\;\forall x\in(X\cap U)\setminus\{x^*\}:\ P_\rho(x)>P_\rho(x^*).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict variant of the immutable local-exactness theorem.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Exactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the objective is locally Lipschitz and violation controls distance to the feasible set near a constrained local minimizer, then every penalty coefficient larger than the Lipschitz constant times the error-bound modulus makes that point a local minimizer of the penalized problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(V:X\to[0,\infty)\), and define \(F=\{x\in X:V(x)=0\}\). Let \(x^*\in F\) be a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(F\). Suppose there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) such that \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(U\), \[\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le \kappa V(x)\qquad(x\in U),\] and each \(x\in U\) sufficiently near \(x^*\) has a nearest point \(y_x\in F\cap U\) lying in a neighborhood on which \(f(y_x)\ge f(x^*)\). Then every \(\rho>L\kappa\) makes \(x^*\) a local minimizer of \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x)\) over \(X\).
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\in F\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(F\), and \(f\) is locally \(L\)-Lipschitz.
Locally, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa V(x)\), and suitable nearest feasible points remain in the constrained-minimizing and Lipschitz neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\rho>L\kappa\), \(x^*\) is a local minimizer of \(P_\rho=f+\rho V\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness derived from Lipschitz continuity and a local error bound.

notation.meaning: local Lipschitz constant of the objective
feasible set defined by zero violation

children.title: Global Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness for global solution sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Finite Global Exactness for a Quadratic Violation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic violation can drive solutions toward feasibility without reproducing the constrained global solution at any finite parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On X=[-1,1], consider \min\{-|x|:x=0\} and V(x)=x^2. The constrained value is 0. For \rho\ge1/2, P_\rho(1/(2\rho))=-1/(4\rho)<0; for 0<\rho<1/2, P_\rho(1)=-1+\rho<0. Hence no finite \rho is globally exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_XP_\rho<0=\min_Ff\quad\text{for every finite }\rho>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact example separating asymptotic feasibility from finite global exactness.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Exactness of a Penalty Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global exactness means that every sufficiently large finite penalty parameter reproduces the complete constrained global minimizer set and value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=\{x\in X:V(x)=0\} and P_\rho=f+\rho V, where V\ge0. The family is globally exact if there exists \bar\rho<\infty such that, for every \rho>\bar\rho, \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}P_\rho(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\ne\varnothing. Consequently, \min_XP_\rho=\min_Ff.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar\rho<\infty\;\forall\rho>\bar\rho:\ \arg\min_XP_\rho=\arg\min_Ff\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attained global-value and complete minimizer-set exactness.

knowledge_statements.title: Upward Closure of Global Exactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once a nonnegative violation penalty is globally exact, every larger parameter is globally exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose V\ge0, F=\{V=0\}, and \operatorname*{argmin}_X(f+\rho_0V)=\operatorname*{argmin}_Ff\ne\varnothing. Then for every \rho>\rho_0, \operatorname*{argmin}_X(f+\rho V)=\operatorname*{argmin}_Ff. Thus the globally exact parameters form an upper interval, possibly containing its lower endpoint.
assumptions_latex: The penalized minimizers at \rho_0 equal the nonempty constrained minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho>\rho_0\Longrightarrow\arg\min_X(f+\rho V)=\arg\min_Ff.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter monotonicity for a nonnegative violation penalty.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Exactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a global error bound and a globally Lipschitz objective, a sufficiently large linear penalty has exactly the constrained global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(F=\{x\in X:V(x)=0\}\ne\varnothing\), and suppose \(V\ge0\). Assume \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(X\), every \(x\in X\) has a nearest point in \(F\), and \[\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa V(x)\qquad(x\in X).\] If the relevant minima are attained, then for every \(\rho>L\kappa\), \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho V(x)\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x).\] Thus the penalized and constrained global optimal values and solution sets coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa V(x)\) globally and the minima are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\rho>L\kappa\), \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{X}(f+\rho V)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{F}f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global equality of constrained and penalized minimizer sets under a global error bound.

children.title: Exact-Penalty Parameter Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Threshold families connected with multiplier and sensitivity information.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Penalty Parameter Thresholds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the standard L1 exact penalty, any coefficient strictly larger than the largest KKT multiplier magnitude is locally sufficient under LICQ and second-order sufficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\), with twice continuously differentiable data. Let \(x^*\) be a KKT point with multipliers \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\), where \(\mu^*\ge0\). If LICQ and the second-order sufficient condition hold at \(x^*\), then \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer of \[P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\left(\lVert c(x)\rVert_1+\sum_j\max\{0,g_j(x)\}\right)\] for every \(\rho>\max\{\lVert\lambda^*\rVert_\infty,\lVert\mu^*\rVert_\infty\}\). Equality at the threshold is not generally sufficient.
assumptions_latex: The problem data are twice continuously differentiable.
\(x^*\) satisfies KKT with multipliers \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\), and LICQ holds.
The second-order sufficient condition holds at \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\rho>\max\{\lVert\lambda^*\rVert_\infty,\lVert\mu^*\rVert_\infty\}\) is a sufficient local exact-penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-based threshold for the standard nonsmooth exact penalty.

children.title: Exactness-Regularity-Error-Bound Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationships between exact penalization and local constraint error bounds.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz, and let \(\Omega=\{x\in X:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\). Let \(v:X\to\mathbb R_+\) be a continuous violation function with \(v^{-1}(0)=\Omega\), and define \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho v(x)\). Fix \(\bar x\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local definition for a Lipschitz objective and a scalar exact penalty; it packages, rather than proves, the three properties commonly compared near one feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The tuple \((\bar x,U,\kappa,L,\bar\rho)\) is an exactness–regularity–error-bound certificate if \(U\) is a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), \(\kappa,L>0\), \(\bar\rho\geq0\), and
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)\leq\kappa v(x)\quad(x\in U\cap X),\]
\[|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\|x-y\|\quad(x,y\in U\cap X),\]
and, for every \(\rho>\bar\rho\),
\[\bar x\in\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in U\cap X}P_\rho(x)\iff \bar x\in\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in U\cap\Omega}f(x).\]
When the certificate additionally satisfies \(\bar\rho\leq L\kappa\), the numerical threshold is said to be compatible with the local error-bound modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactness–regularity–error-bound certificate at \(\bar x\) consists of a neighborhood and constants for which distance to the feasible set is bounded by constraint violation, the objective is locally Lipschitz, and every penalty parameter strictly above \(\bar\rho\) gives the same local-minimizer status at \(\bar x\) as the constrained problem. Compatibility records the bound \(\bar\rho\leq L\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\bar x,U,\kappa,L,\bar\rho)\text{ is a certificate}\iff\text{the displayed error bound, Lipschitz bound, and local exactness equivalence all hold}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The error-bound component is equivalently \(\sup_{x\in(U\cap X)\setminus\Omega}\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)/v(x)\leq\kappa\), with the supremum over an empty set interpreted as \(0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(v(x)=\|h(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\), the definition specializes to the standard nonsmooth \(\ell_1\) penalty.
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition separates the geometric modulus \(\kappa\), objective modulus \(L\), and exactness threshold \(\bar\rho\); it does not identify any of them with a smallest possible constant.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert that an error bound alone implies exactness, nor that exactness implies an error bound without additional regularity.
Global exactness and quadratic exterior penalties are outside this local certificate.

notation.meaning: local Lipschitz modulus of the objective

review_flags: No inspected source was available that supports this packaged definition and its exact quantifiers; a precise authoritative locator is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Local exactness–regularity–error-bound certificate
Pointwise Local Exactness Need Not Exclude Nearby Infeasible Minimizers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty can preserve the targeted feasible local minimizer while possessing infeasible local minimizers arbitrarily close to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(F=\{0\}\), \(V(x)=x^2\), and fix \(\rho>0\). Define \(P_\rho(0)=0\), \(P_\rho(x)=x^2(1+\sin(1/x))\) for \(x\neq0\), and \(f=P_\rho-\rho V\). Then \(0\) is the unique feasible point and a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\). For \(x_j=(3\pi/2+2\pi j)^{-1}\), however, \(P_\rho(x_j)=0\), so every infeasible \(x_j\) is also a local minimizer and \(x_j\to0\).
assumptions_latex: Pointwise local exactness at a coefficient means that the specified constrained local minimizer is a local minimizer of the corresponding penalized objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_j\notin F,\qquad x_j\to0,\qquad x_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}P_\rho.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between preservation of one constrained local minimizer and equality of nearby local-minimizer sets.

notation.meaning: infeasible penalized minimizers converging to the feasible point

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Penalization Outcomes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global exactness preserves the attained constrained optimal value and global minimizer set. Pointwise local exactness ensures that the specified constrained local minimizer is also a penalized local minimizer with the same objective value, but it does not automatically identify every nearby local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(V:X\to[0,\infty)\), define \(F=\{x\in X:V(x)=0\}\), and let \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x)\) for \(\rho>0\). If \(P_\rho\) is globally exact in the sense that its global minimizers coincide with the global minimizers of \(f\) over \(F\), then, whenever these minimizers exist, \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}P_\rho(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\] and \[\min_{x\in X}P_\rho(x)=\min_{x\in F}f(x).\] Hence every penalized global minimizer is feasible and constrained-optimal, and every constrained global minimizer is penalized-optimal. If instead \(P_\rho\) is locally exact at a constrained local minimizer \(x^*\in F\), the corresponding pointwise outcome is that \(x^*\) is a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\) and \(P_\rho(x^*)=f(x^*)\); equality of all nearby local-minimizer sets requires a stronger definition or additional assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(P_\rho=f+\rho V\) is exact in the stated global or pointwise local sense.
For global solution-set and minimum equalities, the relevant minima are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global exactness yields equality of the attained constrained and penalized global minimum values and minimizer sets; pointwise local exactness makes the specified constrained local minimizer a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\) with unchanged value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-value and solution consequences of global or pointwise local exact penalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictness and Nonnecessity in the LICQ–MFCQ–Error-Bound Chain
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent active inequalities can satisfy MFCQ, and redundant equalities can violate MFCQ while retaining an exact local violation error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F_1=\{x\in\mathbb R:x\leq0,\ 2x\leq0\}\) at \(\bar x=0\), LICQ fails because the active gradients \(1\) and \(2\) are dependent, while MFCQ holds with \(d=-1\). For \(F_2=\{x\in\mathbb R:x=0,\ 2x=0\}=\{0\}\), equality-gradient independence and hence MFCQ fail, yet with \(v(x)=|x|+|2x|\), \[\operatorname{dist}(x,F_2)=|x|=\tfrac13v(x).\] Thus neither converse in \(\mathrm{LICQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{MFCQ}\Rightarrow\) local error bound holds in general.
assumptions_latex: All displayed constraints are affine and hence continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{MFCQ}\not\Rightarrow\mathrm{LICQ},\qquad \text{local error bound}\not\Rightarrow\mathrm{MFCQ}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary smooth systems separating LICQ, MFCQ, and the local violation error bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Rank Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CRCQ requires each family formed from all equality gradients and any subset of active-inequality gradients to retain constant rank locally; unlike LICQ, it permits redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For F=\{x:c(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\} and \bar x\in F, CRCQ holds at \bar x if, for every subset J\subseteq A(\bar x), the family \{\nabla c_i(x)\}_{i=1}^m\cup\{\nabla g_j(x)\}_{j\in J} has constant rank throughout some common neighborhood of \bar x. LICQ implies CRCQ, while CRCQ permits redundant active gradients.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{LICQ}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{CRCQ},\qquad \mathrm{CRCQ}\not\Longrightarrow\mathrm{LICQ}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A weaker smooth regularity regime for mixed equality and inequality systems.

notation.meaning: Arbitrary subset of active inequality indices.

knowledge_statements.title: Constant Positive Linear Dependence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CPLD requires every positively dependent selection of equality and active-inequality gradients to remain linearly dependent locally.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{CPLD}(\bar x)\iff\text{positive dependence at }\bar x\text{ persists locally as linear dependence}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CPLD for finite-dimensional continuously differentiable mixed equality and inequality constraints.

notation.meaning: Selected equality and active-inequality index sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Constant Positive Linear Dependence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RCPLD fixes a basis for the equality-gradient span and requires positive dependence involving that basis and active inequalities to persist locally as linear dependence.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in F\).
The equality-gradient family has constant rank near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{RCPLD}(\bar x)\iff\text{the stated basis-reduced positive-dependence persistence holds}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: RCPLD for finite-dimensional continuously differentiable mixed equality and inequality constraints.

notation.meaning: Index set selecting a basis of the equality-gradient span at the reference point.
Arbitrary subset of active inequality indices.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Constraint-Qualification Implication Map
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ implies both MFCQ and CRCQ; each branch leads through CPLD to RCPLD, while MFCQ and CRCQ are generally incomparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-dimensional C^1 mixed constraint system, \[\mathrm{LICQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{MFCQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{CPLD}\Rightarrow\mathrm{RCPLD},\qquad \mathrm{LICQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{CRCQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{CPLD}.\] MFCQ and CRCQ are not comparable in general.
assumptions_latex: The finite constraint functions are continuously differentiable near the feasible reference point.
CPLD and RCPLD use the stated sign convention g\le0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{LICQ}\Rightarrow\{\mathrm{MFCQ},\mathrm{CRCQ}\}\Rightarrow\mathrm{CPLD}\Rightarrow\mathrm{RCPLD},\quad \mathrm{MFCQ}\not\Leftrightarrow\mathrm{CRCQ}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Principal implication branches among the regularity regimes represented in this leaf.

knowledge_statements.title: CRCQ Local Violation Error Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CRCQ is sufficient for a local residual error bound controlling distance to the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let c and g be continuously differentiable near \bar x\in F and suppose CRCQ holds at \bar x. Then there exist \kappa,\delta>0 such that every x with \|x-\bar x\|<\delta satisfies \operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa\bigl(\|c(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\bigr).
assumptions_latex: \(c\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\kappa,\delta>0:\ \|x-\bar x\|<\delta\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa\left(\|c(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\right).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error-bound consequence of constant-rank regularity for finite-dimensional smooth constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: RCPLD Local Violation Error Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RCPLD yields a local residual error bound; all stronger represented qualifications inherit that conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let c and g be continuously differentiable near \bar x\in F and suppose RCPLD holds at \bar x. Then there exist \kappa,\delta>0 such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa\bigl(\|c(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\bigr)\qquad\text{whenever }\|x-\bar x\|<\delta.\] Consequently the same implication holds under CPLD, CRCQ, MFCQ, or LICQ.
assumptions_latex: c and g are continuously differentiable near \bar x\in F.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\kappa,\delta>0:\ \|x-\bar x\|<\delta\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa\left(\|c(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\right).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local metric error bound supplied by the weakest represented persistent-dependence qualification.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Regularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite-dimensional continuously differentiable constraints, LICQ implies MFCQ, and MFCQ yields a local bound controlling distance to the feasible set by aggregate constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{LICQ}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{MFCQ}\Longrightarrow\bigl(\exists\kappa,\delta>0\;\forall x:\|x-\bar x\|<\delta\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa v(x)\bigr).\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional continuously differentiable constraints near a feasible point.

notation.meaning: Index set of inequalities active at the reference point.
Componentwise positive part of the inequality residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Error-Bound Penalty Threshold
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The product of the objective Lipschitz modulus and error-bound modulus is worst-case sharp from below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{0\}\subset\mathbb R\), \(v(x)=|x|\), and \(f(x)=-L|x|\) with \(L>0\). Then \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)=v(x)\), so \(\kappa=1\). The penalized objective is \(P_\rho(x)=(\rho-L)|x|\). For every \(\rho<L=L\kappa\), \(0\) is not a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\); at \(\rho=L\), the penalty is locally constant. Thus the two moduli alone provide no universal sufficient coefficient smaller than \(L\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho<L\kappa\Longrightarrow 0\notin\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\text{ near }0}P_\rho(x)\quad\text{in this example}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case necessity of the modulus-product threshold below its boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Does Not Alone Imply a Linear Error Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty may be exact because the objective already favors feasibility even though its violation function has no linear local error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{0\}\), \(v(x)=x^2\), and \(f(x)=x^2\). For every \(\rho>0\), \(P_\rho(x)=(1+\rho)x^2\) has the unique minimizer \(0\), so the penalty is globally exact for this objective. Nevertheless, no \(\kappa,\delta>0\) satisfy \(|x|\leq\kappa x^2\) for every \(0<|x|<\delta\). Hence exact penalization of a particular objective does not imply the linear local error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\leq\kappa v(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R}P_\rho=F=\{0\},\qquad \nexists\kappa,\delta>0:\ |x|\leq\kappa x^2\ \forall\,0<|x|<\delta.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Error-Bound Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local error bound converts objective Lipschitz continuity into exact penalization: every penalty parameter exceeding the product of the two moduli is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(\bar x\in F\) be a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(F\), and let \(v\ge0\) vanish exactly on \(F\) locally. Suppose \(f\) is locally Lipschitz with constant \(L\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa v(x)\) near \(\bar x\). Then, for every \(\rho>L\kappa\), \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho v(x)\). Thus the local error-bound modulus supplies an explicit sufficient exact-penalty threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) on the closed set \(F\).\)
\(f\) is locally \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\le\kappa v(x)\) near \(\bar x\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho>L\kappa\Longrightarrow \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\text{ near }\bar x}\{f(x)+\rho v(x)\}.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness obtained by combining an error bound with objective Lipschitz continuity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalty solution trajectory and its graph
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(I\subseteq(0,\infty)\) be an interval of penalty parameters, and let \(P:I\times X\to\mathbb R\), \(P(\rho,x)=P_\rho(x)\), be a parameterized penalty family. For a neighborhood \(U\), write \(S_U(\rho)=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in U\cap X}P_\rho(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic trajectory of local minimizers; stationary-point trajectories may be defined by replacing the local-minimizer solution map with a generalized stationarity map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A penalty solution trajectory on \(I\) is a continuous map \(x:I\to X\) for which there exists an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) containing \(x(I)\) such that
\[x(\rho)\in S_U(\rho)\quad\text{for every }\rho\in I.\]
Its graph is \(\Gamma_x=\{(\rho,x(\rho)):\rho\in I\}\subseteq I\times X\). It is locally isolated at \(\rho_0\in I\) if there are neighborhoods \(J\) of \(\rho_0\) and \(V\) of \(x(\rho_0)\) such that
\[\operatorname{gph}S_U\cap(J\times V)=\Gamma_x\cap(J\times V).\]
Trajectory analysis means the study of this graph under parameter variation, including its continuity, differentiability, limiting points, isolation, and maximal continuation interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty solution trajectory is a continuous selection \(x(\rho)\) from a local-minimizer solution map of the penalized subproblem over an interval of penalty parameters. Its graph records parameter–solution pairs. The trajectory is locally isolated when, near a selected pair, that graph is the entire nearby local solution graph rather than one of several indistinguishable branches.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\text{ is a penalty solution trajectory on }I\iff x\in C(I,X)\text{ and }x(\rho)\in S_U(\rho)\text{ for every }\rho\in I\text{ for some common }U.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The selection condition is equivalently \(\Gamma_x\subseteq\operatorname{gph}S_U\) together with single-valued parameterization of \(\Gamma_x\) over \(I\).
special_cases_latex: If \(P\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(x(\rho)\) is an unconstrained strict local minimizer, then the trajectory lies in \(\{(\rho,z):\nabla_xP(\rho,z)=0\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A maximal trajectory has a maximal connected parameter interval on which the same continuous selection remains defined.
boundary_notes: A sequence of unrelated subproblem solutions is not a trajectory unless it belongs to a continuous selection.
The definition does not guarantee uniqueness, differentiability, or convergence as \(\rho\to\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isolated penalty trajectory is the unique stationary branch in a product neighborhood of a reference stationary point and parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the seed theorem, if \nabla_{xx}^2P(\bar x,\bar\rho)\succ0, then after shrinking the parameter interval, \nabla_{xx}^2P(x(\rho),\rho)\succ0 for every nearby \rho, so each x(\rho) is a strict isolated local minimizer. More generally, the inertia of a continuous symmetric Hessian is constant on each connected nonsingular branch.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists I\ni\bar\rho\;\forall\rho\in I:\ \nabla_{xx}^2P(x(\rho),\rho)\succ0.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Predictor–Newton Corrector Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a regular smooth branch, tangent prediction has second-order local error and sufficiently small parameter steps place it in the Newton corrector's quadratic-convergence region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x,\rho)=\nabla_xP(x,\rho)\) be \(C^2\) near a stationary branch \(x(\rho)\), and suppose \(D_xF(x(\rho),\rho)\) is uniformly nonsingular there. For sufficiently small \(h\), the tangent predictor \(y_0=x(\rho)+hx'(\rho)\) satisfies \(\lVert y_0-x(\rho+h)\rVert=O(h^2)\). If \(D_xF\) is locally Lipschitz and its inverses are uniformly bounded, Newton correction applied to \(F(\cdot,\rho+h)=0\) is well defined from \(y_0\) and converges quadratically to \(x(\rho+h)\).
assumptions_latex: \(D_xF\) is uniformly nonsingular along the local branch.
\(D_xF\) is locally Lipschitz with uniformly bounded inverse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert y_0-x(\rho+h)\rVert=O(h^2)\), and Newton correction converges quadratically for all sufficiently small \(|h|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local accuracy and convergence of tangent prediction followed by Newton correction on a regular stationary branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Trajectory Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predict the next stationary point using the branch tangent, then apply Newton corrections at the new parameter; return the corrected iterate that satisfies a stopping test or report failure after the prescribed iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a stationary pair \((x_k,ho_k)\in\mathbb R^n	imes\mathbb R\), a target parameter \(ho_{k+1}\in\mathbb R\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_N>0\), and an integer \(J_{\max}\ge1\), let \(P(x,ho)=f(x)+ho q(x)\). Solve \(
abla_{xx}^2P(x_k,ho_k)s_k=-
abla q(x_k)\) and set \(y_0=x_k+(ho_{k+1}-ho_k)s_k\). For \(j=0,\ldots,J_{\max}-1\), first return \(x_{k+1}=y_j\) if \(\|
abla_xP(y_j,ho_{k+1})\|\le\varepsilon_s\). Otherwise solve \(
abla_{xx}^2P(y_j,ho_{k+1})d_j=-
abla_xP(y_j,ho_{k+1})\) and set \(y_{j+1}=y_j+d_j\). If \(\|d_j\|\le\varepsilon_N\), return \(x_{k+1}=y_{j+1}\). If neither test holds after \(J_{\max}\) corrector steps, report corrector nonconvergence and retain \(y_{J_{\max}}\) only as an unsuccessful trial point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consistent extrapolator for a penalty trajectory
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x:I\to\mathbb R^n\) be a penalty trajectory, and let \(\rho_{k-1}<\rho_k<\rho_{k+1}\) belong to \(I\). An extrapolator uses previously computed pairs \((\rho_j,x_j)\), with \(x_j\approx x(\rho_j)\), to produce a predictor for \(x(\rho_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic local prediction along one identified branch; the definition concerns predictor consistency and does not prescribe the corrector used to solve the next penalty subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An order-\(p\) penalty-trajectory extrapolator is a family of maps \(E_k\) producing
\[x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{pred}}=E_k\big((\rho_{k-j},x_{k-j})_{j=0}^{q-1},\rho_{k+1}\big)\]
for some memory length \(q\geq1\), such that, whenever the inputs are exact samples from every trajectory \(x\in C^p(I,\mathbb R^n)\) in the stated class and \(h_k=\max_{0\leq j<q}|\rho_{k+1}-\rho_{k-j}|\to0\),
\[\|x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{pred}}-x(\rho_{k+1})\|=O(h_k^p).\]
The secant extrapolator is the case \(q=2\) defined by
\[x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{pred}}=x_k+\frac{\rho_{k+1}-\rho_k}{\rho_k-\rho_{k-1}}(x_k-x_{k-1}),\]
provided \(\rho_k\ne\rho_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty-trajectory extrapolator maps earlier parameter–solution samples and a new parameter to a predicted point on the same branch. It has order \(p\) when exact data from a sufficiently smooth branch produce prediction error \(O(h_k^p)\) as the parameter mesh shrinks. The two-point secant formula is a canonical instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[E_k\text{ has order }p\iff\|E_k(\text{exact branch samples},\rho_{k+1})-x(\rho_{k+1})\|=O(h_k^p).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Consistency is the order-one condition \(\|x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{pred}}-x(\rho_{k+1})\|\to0\) whenever \(h_k\to0\).
special_cases_latex: If a derivative \(x'(\rho_k)\) is available, tangent prediction takes the form \(x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{pred}}=x_k+(\rho_{k+1}-\rho_k)x'(\rho_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The prediction belongs to the ambient space but need not be stationary, locally minimizing, or feasible; those properties are delegated to a corrector.
boundary_notes: The definition is branch-specific and does not resolve branch switching or bifurcation.
A large parameter step is not covered by the asymptotic order condition.
review_flags: No inspected authoritative source locator was found for this formal order definition in the penalty-path setting.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local continuation-failure boundary of a penalty branch
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S:I\rightrightarrows X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a localized solution or stationary-point map for a penalty family, and let \(\Gamma\) be a connected component of \(\operatorname{gph}S\). Denote the parameter projection by \(\pi_\rho(\rho,x)=\rho\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological definition for a locally followed finite-dimensional branch; it covers ambiguity and disappearance without asserting a particular analytic cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A point \((\rho_*,x_*)\in\overline\Gamma\) is a finite penalty-branch failure boundary point if \(\rho_*\in\overline{\pi_\rho(\Gamma)}\), \(x_*\in X\), and there do not exist neighborhoods \(J\) of \(\rho_*\), \(V\) of \(x_*\), and a continuous single-valued map \(s:J\to V\) such that
\[\operatorname{gph}S\cap(J\times V)=\{(\rho,s(\rho)):\rho\in J\}\]
and
\[\Gamma\cap(J\times V)\subseteq\operatorname{gph}s.\]
The branch failure boundary is the set \(\mathcal B(\Gamma)\) of all such points. Failure is called ambiguous when every neighborhood contains two distinct solution selections at a common parameter, and terminal when one side of \(\rho_*\) contains no nearby point of \(\operatorname{gph}S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branch-failure boundary is a closure point of a connected penalty solution branch at which the nearby solution graph can no longer be represented by one continuous local selection that extends the followed branch. Ambiguous failure means competing nearby selections; terminal failure means nearby solutions disappear on one side of the parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\rho_*,x_*)\in\mathcal B(\Gamma)\iff\text{no local continuous single-valued graph representation extends }\Gamma\text{ through }(\rho_*,x_*).\]
special_cases_latex: For a smooth stationarity equation \(F(\rho,x)=0\), loss of invertibility of \(\nabla_xF(\rho_*,x_*)\) is a common candidate boundary mechanism, but singularity is not built into the definition.
immediate_consequences_latex: Ordinary continuation based on a unique local solution map is not defined at points of \(\mathcal B(\Gamma)\).
boundary_notes: Divergence \(\|x(\rho)\|\to\infty\) has no finite state-space boundary point unless the state space is compactified.
Failure of a particular numerical corrector is not branch failure when the mathematical branch remains locally single-valued and continuous.
review_flags: The topological failure-boundary terminology requires an authoritative source matching these continuation and ambiguity clauses.

Generic Scalar Fold Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple scalar singularity with nonzero parameter and second-state derivatives is a fold at which two stationary branches coalesce.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^2	o\mathbb R\) be \(C^2\), with \(F( ar x, arho)=0\), \(F_x( ar x, arho)=0\), \(F_{xx}( ar x, arho)
e0\), and \(F_ho( ar x, arho)
e0\). Then the solution set near \(( ar x, arho)\) is a \(C^2\) curve \(ho=\psi(x)\), where \(\psi'( ar x)=0\) and \(\psi''( ar x)=-F_{xx}( ar x, arho)/F_ho( ar x, arho)
e0\). In a sufficiently small neighborhood, one side of \( arho\) has two stationary solutions and the other has none, with the two branches coalescing at the fold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho-\bar\rho=\tfrac12\psi''(\bar x)(x-\bar x)^2+o((x-\bar x)^2)\), with two nearby solutions on one parameter side and none on the other.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local fold of a scalar stationary penalty equation under standard nondegeneracy conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Path Bifurcation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-Jacobian boundary for locally unique stationary penalty paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x,\rho)=\nabla_xP(x,\rho)\) be continuously differentiable and satisfy \(F(\bar x,\bar\rho)=0\). If \(D_xF(\bar x,\bar\rho)\) is nonsingular, the stationary set is locally one continuously differentiable graph \(x=x(\rho)\). Consequently, a local bifurcation at which stationary branches merge, split, turn, or cease to be representable uniquely as a function of \(\rho\) can occur only where \(D_xF\) is singular. For a twice differentiable penalty objective, candidate bifurcation points therefore satisfy \(\det\nabla_{xx}^2P(\bar x,\bar\rho)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth stationary penalty path cannot bifurcate while its Hessian is nonsingular; singularity is a necessary boundary for branch multiplicity or turning.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is twice continuously differentiable near \((\bar x,\bar\rho)\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Local stationary-path bifurcation at }(\bar x,\bar\rho)\Longrightarrow\det\nabla_{xx}^2P(\bar x,\bar\rho)=0.\)

notation.meaning: Jacobian with respect to the decision variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Penalty Branch Disappearance at a Finite Parameter
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a genuine quadratic-penalty family, two infeasible local-minimum branches terminate at the finite parameter one, leaving only the feasible branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min_x f(x) subject to c(x)=x=0, where f(x)=\tfrac14x^4-\tfrac12x^2, and its quadratic penalty P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\tfrac\rho2c(x)^2=\tfrac14x^4+\tfrac{\rho-1}{2}x^2. Stationarity is x(x^2+\rho-1)=0. For 0\le\rho<1, x_\pm(\rho)=\pm\sqrt{1-\rho} are strict infeasible local minimizers and x=0 is a local maximizer. At \rho=1 the three branches meet at the degenerate stationary point x=0. For \rho>1, x=0 is the sole stationary point, so both followed infeasible minimizing branches have disappeared at a finite penalty parameter.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic exterior penalty is \(\rho c(x)^2/2\) for the equality constraint \(c(x)=x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho>1\Longrightarrow\{x:\partial_xP_\rho(x)=0\}=\{0\},\qquad x_\pm(\rho)\text{ exist only for }0\le\rho<1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit exterior quadratic-penalty family whose infeasible local-minimum branches terminate.

knowledge_statements.title: Necessary Alternatives at a Finite Branch Endpoint
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded smooth stationary branch cannot disappear at an interior finite parameter while its limiting Hessian remains nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F(x,\rho)=\nabla_xP(x,\rho) be continuously differentiable. Suppose F(x(\rho),\rho)=0 for \rho<\rho_* and x(\rho_k)\to x_* along some \rho_k\uparrow\rho_*. If (x_*,\rho_*) is an interior point of the domain, then continuity gives F(x_*,\rho_*)=0. If D_xF(x_*,\rho_*) is nonsingular, the implicit-function theorem extends the locally unique stationary branch through \rho_*. Therefore finite disappearance requires Hessian singularity, absence of a finite accumulation point, encounter with a domain boundary, or loss of the required smoothness.
assumptions_latex: F=\nabla_xP is continuously differentiable near the proposed finite endpoint.
The branch has a finite accumulation point x_* as \rho\uparrow\rho_*.
(x_*,\rho_*) is interior to the domain for the extension conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \det D_xF(x_*,\rho_*)\ne0\Longrightarrow\text{the stationary branch extends locally through }\rho_*.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General continuation boundary distinct from the immutable deferred saddle-node example.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Branch Disappearance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Saddle-node normal form showing finite-parameter branch termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\rho_*>0\) and consider \(P(x,\rho)=x^3/3+(\rho-\rho_*)x\) on \(\mathbb R\). Its stationarity equation is \(x^2+\rho-\rho_*=0\). For \(\rho<\rho_*\), it has two stationary branches \(x_\pm(\rho)=\pm\sqrt{\rho_*-\rho}\), with \(x_+\) locally minimizing and \(x_-\) locally maximizing. At \(\rho=\rho_*\), the branches coalesce at \(x=0\) and \(\partial_{xx}P=0\). For \(\rho>\rho_*\), no real stationary point remains; continuation in increasing \(\rho\) therefore cannot preserve either branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A saddle-node family has two stationary penalty branches before a critical parameter, one degenerate point at it, and no stationary branch afterward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho>\rho_*\Longrightarrow\{x:\partial_xP(x,\rho)=0\}=\varnothing.\)

notation.meaning: The two stationary branches below the critical parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quartic Penalty Branch Ending at a Fold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit smooth family in which a locally minimizing stationary branch terminates at a finite parameter while another branch survives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P_\rho(x)=\tfrac14x^4-\tfrac12x^2+\rho x and \rho_*=2/(3\sqrt3). Stationarity is x^3-x+\rho=0 and P_\rho''(x)=3x^2-1. For \rho<\rho_* sufficiently close to \rho_*, there is a positive local-minimum branch x_+(\rho)>1/\sqrt3 and an adjacent local-maximum branch in (0,1/\sqrt3). They coalesce at (x,\rho)=(1/\sqrt3,\rho_*), where P_\rho'=P_\rho''=0. For \rho>\rho_* the positive locally minimizing branch no longer exists, although a negative stationary branch remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quartic family has a positive local-minimum branch that collides with a local-maximum branch and disappears at a finite parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho>\rho_*\Longrightarrow\nexists x>0:\ \partial_xP_\rho(x)=0,\qquad \rho_*=\frac{2}{3\sqrt3}.

notation.meaning: Positive locally minimizing stationary branch below the fold.

Transverse Value-Crossing Criterion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transverse crossing of the values of two regular local-minimizer branches forces their objective ranking to reverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_1(\rho)\) and \(x_2(\rho)\) be distinct continuous local-minimizer branches of \(P(\cdot,\rho)\) near \(\rho_*\), and let \(\Delta(\rho)=P(x_1(\rho),\rho)-P(x_2(\rho),\rho)\). If \(\Delta\) is differentiable, \(\Delta(\rho_*)=0\), and \(\Delta'(\rho_*)\ne0\), then \(\Delta\) has opposite signs on the two sides of \(\rho_*\). Hence the lower-valued branch switches at \(\rho_*\), although both local branches may remain regular and locally minimizing.
assumptions_latex: \(x_1(\rho)\) and \(x_2(\rho)\) are distinct continuous local-minimizer branches near \(\rho_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{sign}\Delta(\rho)\text{ reverses at }\rho_*,\text{ so the lower-valued branch switches}.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local criterion for switching the preferred member of two regular minimizing branches.

notation.meaning: Difference between the objective values along the two branches.
Parameter at which the branch values coincide.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Branch Switching Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Competing local minima whose objective ordering reverses along the parameter path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\rho_*>0\) and define \(P(x,\rho)=(x^2-1)^2+(\rho-\rho_*)x\). At \(\rho=\rho_*\), both \(x=-1\) and \(x=1\) are strict local and global minimizers with equal value. By nonsingularity of \(\partial_{xx}P(\pm1,\rho_*)=8\), each extends to a smooth local-minimizer branch near \(\rho_*\). For sufficiently small nonzero \(t=\rho-\rho_*\), the branch near \(-1\) has lower value when \(t>0\), whereas the branch near \(1\) has lower value when \(t<0\). Thus global branch selection switches at \(\rho_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two smooth minimizing branches can coexist while their objective ranking reverses, making continuation of a locally chosen branch different from global branch selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{sign}(\rho-\rho_*)\text{ determines which of the two nearby minimizing branches has lower objective value}.\)

notation.meaning: Signed displacement of the penalty parameter from the switching value.
Parameter at which the competing branches tie.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P_\rho:X\to\mathbb R\) be a penalty family and let \(x(\rho)\) be a selected subproblem solution. Fix finite tolerances \(K_{\max}\geq1\), \(D_{\max}\geq1\), and \(\eta_{\max}\geq0\). Let \(K(\rho)\), \(D(\rho)\), and \(\eta(\rho)\) quantify conditioning, residual-scale disparity, and unresolved stationarity, respectively.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational finite-precision definition relative to explicitly chosen diagnostics and tolerances; it does not assign universal numerical limits to a penalty formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The numerically admissible parameter set is
\[\mathcal A=\{\rho>0:K(\rho)\leq K_{\max},\ D(\rho)\leq D_{\max},\ \eta(\rho)\leq\eta_{\max}\}.\]
The penalty numerical boundary is the relative boundary
\[\mathcal N=\partial_{(0,\infty)}\mathcal A.\]
A sequence \(\rho_k\) reaches an ill-conditioning boundary if \(K(\rho_k)\uparrow K_{\max}\), a scaling boundary if \(D(\rho_k)\uparrow D_{\max}\), and a stationarity-resolution boundary if \(\eta(\rho_k)\uparrow\eta_{\max}\), while the remaining diagnostics stay admissible. The tuple \((K,D,\eta;K_{\max},D_{\max},\eta_{\max})\) is part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty numerical boundaries are the boundary points of the set of penalty parameters for which chosen conditioning, scaling-disparity, and stationarity-resolution diagnostics remain within specified finite tolerances. Because the diagnostics and tolerances are included in the object, the boundary is machine-, solver-, and scaling-dependent rather than intrinsic to the constrained problem alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal N=\partial_{(0,\infty)}\{\rho:K(\rho)\leq K_{\max},\ D(\rho)\leq D_{\max},\ \eta(\rho)\leq\eta_{\max}\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If all diagnostics are continuous, \(\mathcal N\subseteq\{\rho:\max(K/K_{\max},D/D_{\max},\eta/\eta_{\max})=1\}\), omitting ratios whose denominator is zero.
special_cases_latex: For a smooth unconstrained penalty subproblem, one may take \(K(\rho)=\kappa_2(\nabla^2P_\rho(x(\rho)))\) when the Hessian is positive definite.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing variable scaling or inner-solver accuracy can change \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal N\) without changing the exact penalty function.
boundary_notes: This definition does not claim that crossing \(\mathcal N\) makes computation impossible.
Nonsmoothness requires diagnostics other than an ordinary Hessian condition number.
review_flags: This diagnostic boundary is a formalized taxonomy object; no inspected source was available for its exact definition.

children.title: Penalty Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Deteriorating curvature and linear-system conditioning along penalty sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Curvature Cannot Repair a Defective Tangent Hessian
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger quadratic penalty stiffens directions detected by the constraint Jacobian but cannot repair nonpositive tangent curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every d\in\ker J, d^T(\rho J^TJ)d=0. Consequently, if the reduced objective Hessian has a nonzero tangent direction d with d^T\nabla^2f(x^*)d\le0, then \nabla^2f(x^*)+\rho J^TJ is not positive definite for any \rho. Increasing the quadratic penalty cannot create uniform positive curvature in a defective tangent direction.
assumptions_latex: J is the constraint Jacobian at a feasible point x^*.
There exists 0\ne d\in\ker J with d^T\nabla^2f(x^*)d\le0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^T(\nabla^2f(x^*)+\rho J^TJ)d\le0\quad\text{for every }\rho>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where increasing the penalty supplies no curvature in Jacobian-null directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal–Tangent Curvature Separation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When both normal and tangent directions are present, quadratic penalization adds order-rho normal curvature but only order-one tangent curvature, causing linear condition-number growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For P_ho(x)=f(x)+ racho2\|c(x)\|^2, 
abla^2P_ho(x)=
abla^2f(x)+ho J(x)^TJ(x)+ho\sum_i c_i(x)

Then the large eigenvalues associated with \operatorname{range}J(x^*)^T are \Theta(ho), while the remaining eigenvalues stay bounded above and away from zero; hence \kappa_2(

assumptions_latex: f and c are twice continuously differentiable near a feasible x^*.
The reduced objective Hessian is positive definite on \ker J(x^*).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{\max}(\nabla^2P_\rho(x^*))=\Theta(\rho),\qquad \kappa_2(\nabla^2P_\rho(x^*))=\Theta(\rho).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General local Hessian structure behind quadratic-penalty ill-conditioning.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian at the feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a basic quadratic penalty model, normal curvature grows with the penalty parameter while tangent curvature stays fixed, so the Hessian condition number grows linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(u,v)\in\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s\), let \(H\) be symmetric positive definite, and consider the equality constraint \(v=0\) with quadratic penalty \(P_\rho(u,v)=\tfrac12u^THu+\tfrac\rho2\|v\|^2\). Then \(\nabla^2P_\rho=\operatorname{diag}(H,\rho I_s)\). If \(\rho\ge\lambda_{\max}(H)\), its spectral condition number is \(\kappa_2(\nabla^2P_\rho)=\rho/\lambda_{\min}(H)\). Hence increasing the exterior penalty parameter makes normal curvature grow while tangent curvature remains fixed, producing unbounded linear-system ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(\nabla^2P_\rho)=\rho/\lambda_{\min}(H)\to\infty\text{ as }\rho\to\infty.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic model exhibiting linear growth of the Hessian condition number.

notation.meaning: Tangent variables unaffected by the constraint penalty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curvature ill-conditioning along a penalty sequence
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P_{\rho_k}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable near points \(x_k\), with \(\rho_k\to\infty\). Let \(H_k=\nabla^2P_{\rho_k}(x_k)\), or let \(H_k\) be the symmetric matrix defining the local quadratic model actually solved.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional curvature definition; singular or indefinite models are treated through singular values, while nonsmooth exact penalties require a different generalized-curvature notion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The penalty sequence is curvature ill-conditioned along \((x_k)\) if
\[\kappa_2(H_k)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(H_k)}{\sigma_{\min}(H_k)}\longrightarrow\infty,\]
where \(\kappa_2(H_k)=\infty\) when \(H_k\) is singular. It is asymptotically penalty-ill-conditioned if there exist nonzero directions \(u_k,v_k\) with
\[\frac{\|H_ku_k\|/\|u_k\|}{\|H_kv_k\|/\|v_k\|}\longrightarrow\infty.\]
For positive-definite \(H_k\), this is equivalently \(\lambda_{\max}(H_k)/\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\to\infty\). A rate statement \(\kappa_2(H_k)=\Theta(q(\rho_k))\) records the deterioration law when \(q(\rho)\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty ill-conditioning is unbounded disparity between the largest and smallest curvature scales of the penalized subproblem along a parameter sequence. It is measured by the spectral condition number of the Hessian or quadratic-model matrix. For positive-definite matrices, this is the ratio of extreme eigenvalues; singularity gives infinite condition number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{penalty ill-conditioning along }(x_k,\rho_k)\iff\kappa_2(H_k)\to\infty.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For symmetric positive-definite \(H_k\), \(\kappa_2(H_k)=\lambda_{\max}(H_k)/\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+(\rho/2)\|h(x)\|^2\), \(H=\nabla^2f+\rho J_h^TJ_h+\rho\sum_i h_i\nabla^2h_i\); the definition measures the conditioning of this complete matrix, not only \(J_h^TJ_h\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition is invariant under multiplying \(H_k\) by a nonzero scalar but generally not under a nonorthogonal change of variables.
boundary_notes: A large gradient norm is not itself ill-conditioning.
An indefinite nonsingular Hessian can have a moderate singular-value condition number despite being unsuitable for a minimization Newton step.
review_flags: The mathematical condition-number definition is standard, but no inspected source locator was established for its penalty-sequence specialization.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature ill-conditioning along a penalty sequence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where increasing the penalty cannot regularize tangent or Jacobian-null directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(d^TJ^TJd=\|Jd\|^2\), increasing \(\rho\) adds no curvature in any direction \(d\in\ker J\). Consequently, a singular or indefinite reduced Hessian on \(\ker J\) is not repaired by the quadratic Gram term \(\rho J^TJ\), even while nonzero singular directions become increasingly stiff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger quadratic penalty stiffens only directions seen by the constraint Jacobian; it cannot repair singular or negative tangent curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is the constraint Jacobian at the point under consideration.
The quadratic-penalty Hessian contains the Gram term \(\rho J^TJ\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in\ker J\Longrightarrow d^T(\rho J^TJ)d=0\) for every \(\rho\).

children.title: Constraint-Scaling Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Distortion caused by heterogeneous residual scales.

knowledge_statements.title: A Single Global Weight Cannot Correct Heterogeneous Scaling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One scalar penalty parameter cannot undo unequal constraint rescalings; constraint-specific weights are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose two nonzero residual components can vary independently and are rescaled by \alpha_1 and \alpha_2. A scalar replacement \widetilde\rho preserves \frac\rho2(c_1^2+c_2^2) for all residual values only if \widetilde\rho\alpha_1^2=\widetilde\rho\alpha_2^2=\rho. For the L1 penalty it requires \widetilde\rho|\alpha_1|=\widetilde\rho|\alpha_2|=\rho. Thus either preservation requires |\alpha_1|=|\alpha_2|.
assumptions_latex: The two residual components can vary independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\alpha_1|\ne|\alpha_2|\Longrightarrow\nexists\widetilde\rho>0\text{ preserving either penalty for all residual values}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of scalar-parameter normalization for independently rescaled residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Compensated Penalty Weights
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse-square weights compensate quadratic residual scaling, while inverse-absolute weights compensate L1 residual scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let w_i>0 and \widetilde c_i=\alpha_i c_i with \alpha_i\ne0. The weighted quadratic penalty \frac\rho2\sum_iw_ic_i^2 is unchanged by \widetilde w_i=w_i/\alpha_i^2. The weighted absolute penalty \rho\sum_iw_i|c_i| is unchanged by \widetilde w_i=w_i/|\alpha_i|.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_i\widetilde w_i\widetilde c_i^2=\sum_iw_ic_i^2,\qquad \sum_i\widetilde w_i|\widetilde c_i|=\sum_iw_i|c_i|.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraintwise weights making quadratic and absolute penalties invariant under residual rescaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Scaling Imbalance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescaling an equivalent constraint changes its effective quadratic or exact penalty weight, so heterogeneous residual units can distort steps, stationarity, and conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For residuals \(c_i(x)\), define \(Q_\rho(x)=f(x)+\tfrac\rho2\sum_i c_i(x)^2\) and \(E_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\sum_i|c_i(x)|\). Replacing each constraint by \(\widetilde c_i=\alpha_i c_i\), where \(\alpha_i\ne0\), changes its quadratic-penalty weight from \(\rho\) to \(\rho\alpha_i^2\) and its exact-penalty weight from \(\rho\) to \(\rho|\alpha_i|\). Thus algebraically equivalent constraint systems generally generate different penalized objectives, stationary points, and conditioning unless individual weights compensate for the scaling factors.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are defined on a common domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_i\mapsto\alpha_i c_i\Longrightarrow \tfrac\rho2c_i^2\mapsto\tfrac{\rho\alpha_i^2}{2}c_i^2\text{ and }\rho|c_i|\mapsto\rho|\alpha_i||c_i|.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of penalty curvature and influence on residual units.

notation.meaning: Nonzero scaling factor for constraint i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-scale imbalance in a weighted penalty
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_m):X\to\mathbb R^m\) collect constraint residuals and let \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\). Consider \(P_{\rho,w}(x)=f(x)+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\phi_i(r_i(x))\), where each \(\phi_i\geq0\) vanishes at an admissible residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional componentwise residual scaling; the definition distinguishes representation-dependent imbalance from the scalar strength of the entire penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x\), define active penalty sensitivities
\[s_i(x;w)=w_i\,\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial(\phi_i\circ r_i)(x)\bigr),\]
and let \(I(x)=\{i:s_i(x;w)>0\}\). The local constraint-scaling imbalance is
\[\mathfrak D(x;w)=\frac{\max_{i\in I(x)}s_i(x;w)}{\min_{i\in I(x)}s_i(x;w)},\]
with \(\mathfrak D(x;w)=1\) when \(|I(x)|\leq1\). A penalty model is \(D\)-imbalanced on \(U\subseteq X\) if \(\sup_{x\in U}\mathfrak D(x;w)>D\). Two equivalent constraint representations \(r\) and \(Ar\), with nonsingular diagonal \(A\), exhibit representation distortion when their imbalance indices differ under unchanged weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-scaling imbalance measures the ratio between the largest and smallest nonzero componentwise penalty sensitivities at a point. A model is \(D\)-imbalanced on a region when this ratio exceeds \(D\) somewhere. Equivalent diagonal rescaling of the residual equations can alter the index unless the penalty weights are transformed correspondingly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak D(x;w)=\max_{i\in I(x)}s_i(x;w)/\min_{i\in I(x)}s_i(x;w),\quad \sup_{x\in U}\mathfrak D(x;w)>D\text{ defines }D\text{-imbalance}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For differentiable \(\phi_i\circ r_i\), \(s_i(x;w)=w_i\|\nabla(\phi_i\circ r_i)(x)\|\).
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic equality penalty, \(\phi_i(t)=t^2/2\) gives \(s_i(x;w)=w_i|r_i(x)|\|\nabla r_i(x)\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Multiplying every weight by the same positive scalar leaves \(\mathfrak D\) unchanged.
Replacing \(r_i\) by \(a_ir_i\) and transforming its weight to compensate can preserve the weighted penalty, whereas leaving the weight fixed generally changes the imbalance.
boundary_notes: Zero component sensitivity is excluded from the ratio and may instead indicate degeneracy.
The index is norm-dependent and does not by itself measure Hessian conditioning.
review_flags: The proposed sensitivity-ratio formalization lacks an inspected authoritative source with matching definitions.

children.title: Spurious Penalized Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Penalized stationary structures not corresponding to desired constrained solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Row Rank Excludes Spurious Stationarity for Pure Feasibility Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a pure feasibility penalty, full row rank of the constraint Jacobian rules out infeasible stationary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For P_\rho(x)=\frac\rho2\|c(x)\|^2, if J(x) has full row rank at a stationary point, then J(x)^Tc(x)=0 implies c(x)=0. Thus every stationary point in a region of full row rank is feasible. In the general model, a nonzero objective gradient can instead cancel J(x)^T\rho c(x).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla P_\rho(x)=0\Longrightarrow c(x)=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient boundary for the objective-free squared-residual model.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Penalty Stationarity as an Incomplete KKT System
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-parameter quadratic stationarity gives a Lagrangian-gradient equation with multiplier estimate rho times the residual but does not certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality constraints c(x)=0 and P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\frac\rho2\|c(x)\|^2, define \lambda_\rho=\rho c(x). Then \nabla P_\rho(x)=0 if and only if \nabla f(x)+J(x)^T\lambda_\rho=0. This is the Lagrangian stationarity equation, but it supplies neither c(x)=0 nor boundedness of \lambda_\rho as \rho varies.
assumptions_latex: f and c are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla P_\rho(x)=0\iff\nabla_xL(x,\lambda_\rho)=0,\qquad \lambda_\rho=\rho c(x),
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies which constrained condition fixed-parameter stationarity supplies and which it omits.

knowledge_statements.title: Spurious Penalized Stationarity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic penalty may retain infeasible stationary points for every parameter, so solving only its stationarity equations does not ensure convergence to feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the feasibility problem \(\min 0\) subject to \(c(x)=x^2-1=0\) on \(\mathbb R\), and its quadratic penalty \(P_\rho(x)=\tfrac\rho2(x^2-1)^2\) for \(\rho>0\). The feasible solutions are \(x=\pm1\), but \(P_\rho'(x)=2\rho x(x^2-1)\), so \(x=0\) is also stationary for every \(\rho\). Because \(c(0)=-1\), this stationary point is infeasible and does not approach a constrained solution as \(\rho\to\infty\). Penalized first-order stationarity alone therefore does not certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\rho'(0)=0\text{ and }c(0)\ne0\text{ for every }\rho>0.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An infeasible stationary point persisting for every quadratic penalty parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spurious stationary point of a penalized problem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(\Omega=\{x\in X:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\), and let \(P_\rho=f+\rho v\) be locally Lipschitz. Write \(N_X(x)\) for a chosen limiting normal cone and \(\partial P_\rho(x)\) for the corresponding limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonsmooth stationarity relative to a specified normal cone and subdifferential; spuriousness is judged against feasibility and the constrained first-order target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A point \(x_\rho\in X\) is penalty-stationary when
\[0\in\partial P_\rho(x_\rho)+N_X(x_\rho).\]
It is a spurious penalized stationary point if it is penalty-stationary and at least one of the following holds:
\[x_\rho\notin\Omega,\]
or \(x_\rho\in\Omega\) but there exist no multipliers \((\lambda,\mu)\), with \(\mu\geq0\) and \(\mu_i g_i(x_\rho)=0\), satisfying
\[0\in\partial f(x_\rho)+J_h(x_\rho)^T\lambda+J_g(x_\rho)^T\mu+N_X(x_\rho).\]
Relative to a solution set \(S_*\subseteq\Omega\), one may use the stronger designation solution-spurious when additionally \(x_\rho\notin S_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spurious penalized stationary point satisfies the first-order stationarity inclusion for the unconstrained or simply constrained penalty subproblem but is either infeasible or fails the chosen constrained multiplier stationarity system. If a target solution set is specified, the stronger term solution-spurious also requires exclusion from that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_\rho\text{ is spurious}\iff 0\in\partial P_\rho(x_\rho)+N_X(x_\rho)\text{ and }(x_\rho\notin\Omega\text{ or constrained multiplier stationarity fails}).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(X=\mathbb R^n\) and \(P_\rho\) is differentiable at \(x_\rho\), penalty stationarity reduces to \(\nabla P_\rho(x_\rho)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For an infeasible smooth stationary point of a quadratic exterior penalty, spuriousness follows directly from \(v(x_\rho)>0\), independently of whether it is a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Penalty stationarity alone is not a certificate of feasibility or constrained stationarity.
boundary_notes: A feasible constrained stationary point that is not globally optimal is not spurious under the basic definition unless a target solution set is explicitly imposed.
The definition depends on the selected generalized derivative and constraint qualification conventions.

children.title: Nonsmoothness as a Cost of Exactness
children.top_down_role: Solver and local-model consequences of nonsmooth exact penalties.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Rounding Can Destroy Exactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding an absolute-value kink can eliminate finite exactness even when the original nonsmooth penalty is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min\{-x:x=0\}. For \rho>1, the exact penalty -x+\rho|x| is uniquely minimized at x=0. For every \varepsilon>0, the smooth rounding P_{\rho,\varepsilon}(x)=-x+\rho\sqrt{x^2+\varepsilon^2} satisfies P'_{\rho,\varepsilon}(0)=-1, so the feasible point is not stationary and cannot be a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \arg\min_x(-x+\rho|x|)=\{0\},\qquad P'_{\rho,\varepsilon}(0)=-1\ne0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar example showing that smoothing the exact-penalty kink is not innocuous.

knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Subdifferential of the Finite L1 Penalty
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, equality kinks contribute interval coefficients and active inequality kinks contribute one-sided interval coefficients to the Clarke subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
