knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kink set of a nonsmooth exact penalty
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f,h_i,g_j\) be continuously differentiable on an open subset of \(\mathbb R^n\), and define
\[P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\left(\sum_{i=1}^m|h_i(x)|+\sum_{j=1}^q[g_j(x)]_+\right),\quad\rho>0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-dimensional nonsmooth exact penalty; the definition records the loss of ordinary differentiability at residual kinks and its consequence for smooth local models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The exact-penalty kink set is
\[\mathcal K=\{x:\exists i,\ h_i(x)=0,\ \nabla h_i(x)\ne0\}\cup\{x:\exists j,\ g_j(x)=0,\ \nabla g_j(x)\ne0\}.\]
Nonsmoothness is called a cost of exactness at \(\bar x\) when \(P_\rho\) is locally exact at \(\bar x\) for finite \(\rho\) and
\[\partial P_\rho(\bar x)\text{ is not a singleton}.\]
At such a point, an ordinary gradient and Hessian of \(P_\rho\) do not define a unique smooth first- or second-order Taylor model. A local model is penalty-compatible only if it uses a generalized derivative, an explicit piecewise representation, or an equivalent smooth reformulation with auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the standard finite-parameter \(\ell_1\) exact penalty, the kink set contains points where an equality residual or active inequality residual is zero with nonzero gradient. Nonsmoothness is a cost of exactness at a locally exact solution when the penalty subdifferential there is not a singleton, so a unique classical gradient and Hessian model is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{nonsmoothness is a cost of exactness at }\bar x\iff P_\rho\text{ is locally exact there and }|\partial P_\rho(\bar x)|>1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a locally Lipschitz function, singleton failure of the Clarke subdifferential is a standard certificate of failure of strict differentiability, provided the Clarke convention is used consistently.
special_cases_latex: The scalar term \(|h_i(x)|\) has generalized gradient \(\alpha\nabla h_i(x)\) with \(\alpha\in[-1,1]\) when \(h_i(x)=0\).
The term \([g_j(x)]_+\) has generalized gradient \(\alpha\nabla g_j(x)\) with \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) when \(g_j(x)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A smooth Newton method applied without reformulation or generalized derivatives is not directly defined at a point where the relevant penalty subdifferential is non-singleton.
boundary_notes: Degenerate residuals with zero gradients may require higher-order analysis and are not included in \(\mathcal K\) by the displayed regular-kink criterion.
Smooth exact penalties constructed with auxiliary variables are outside this particular definition.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a simple closed set, let \(P_\rho:X\to\mathbb R\) be a penalty family, and let \(R_\rho(x)\geq0\) measure inner-subproblem stationarity. Let \(v(x)\geq0\) measure constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic outer–inner architecture; it specifies interfaces and state transitions without fixing an inner solver or asserting convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A sequential penalty algorithm architecture is a tuple
\[\mathfrak A=(P,\mathcal S,\mathcal U,\mathcal T,\mathcal W)\]
that generates states \(z_k=(x_k,\rho_k,\varepsilon_k,\omega_k)\) as follows. The inner-solver interface returns
\[x_{k+1}\in\mathcal S(P_{\rho_k},x_k,\varepsilon_k),\qquad R_{\rho_k}(x_{k+1})\leq\varepsilon_k.\]
The parameter policy sets
\[\rho_{k+1}=\mathcal U(z_k,x_{k+1},v(x_{k+1})),\]
the stopping test is \(\mathcal T(z_k,x_{k+1})\in\{\mathrm{continue},\mathrm{stop}\}\), and the work state satisfies
\[\omega_{k+1}=\mathcal W(\omega_k,\operatorname{work}_{k+1}).\]
Warm starts, derivative data, and preconditioners may be components of \(\omega_k\). The outer index advances only after the inner interface returns or an explicitly represented failure state is produced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequential penalty architecture is a formal outer–inner state machine. At each outer iteration an inner solver approximately solves the current penalty subproblem to a stated residual tolerance; a policy updates the penalty parameter; a stopping map decides whether to continue; and a work-state map records reusable information and computational effort.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak A\text{ is a sequential penalty architecture}\iff\text{its generated states satisfy the displayed inner, update, stopping, and work interfaces}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The architecture may equivalently be represented as a transition map \(z_{k+1}\in\mathcal F(z_k)\) whose components obey the four displayed interfaces.
special_cases_latex: A cold-start architecture sets the reusable portion of \(\omega_{k+1}\) independently of \(\omega_k\); a warm-start architecture transfers at least the previous primal iterate.
immediate_consequences_latex: The architecture distinguishes outer iterations from the inner work required to produce each accepted subproblem point.
boundary_notes: This definition does not require \(\rho_k\to\infty\); finite exact-penalty reductions are included.
A single merit-function line search without an outer penalty state is not automatically a sequential penalty architecture.
review_flags: The state-machine packaging is precise but lacks an inspected scholarly source using the same architecture definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Outer–inner sequential penalty architecture

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P_\rho:X\to\mathbb R\) be a penalty family and let \(S_\varepsilon(\rho)=\{x\in X:R_\rho(x)\leq\varepsilon\}\) denote acceptable approximate solutions of its subproblem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Taxonomic definition separating an unbounded repeated-subproblem organization from a finite-parameter exact-reduction organization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A sequential penalty architecture is of repeated-subproblem type if it generates an infinite or potentially infinite sequence
\[(\rho_k,\varepsilon_k,x_{k+1})_{k\geq0},\qquad x_{k+1}\in S_{\varepsilon_k}(\rho_k),\]
with distinct outer stages and a parameter rule intended to strengthen constraint enforcement. It is of finite-reduction type if there is a finite index \(K\) and a finite parameter \(\hat\rho=\rho_K\) such that all subsequent optimization work targets the single subproblem \(P_{\hat\rho}\), with no required limit \(\rho_k\to\infty\). The architecture class is
\[\mathscr A_{\mathrm{seq}}=\mathscr A_{\mathrm{repeat}}\cup\mathscr A_{\mathrm{finite}},\]
where membership is determined by the organization of outer subproblems rather than the algebraic form of \(P_\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential penalty architectures comprise repeated-subproblem organizations, which solve a succession of increasingly restrictive penalty problems, and finite-reduction organizations, which eventually select one finite-parameter exact subproblem and direct all remaining optimization work to it. Classification depends on the outer organization, not merely on the penalty formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathscr A_{\mathrm{seq}}=\mathscr A_{\mathrm{repeat}}\cup\mathscr A_{\mathrm{finite}}.\]
special_cases_latex: Classical quadratic exterior-penalty methods with \(\rho_k\uparrow\infty\) are repeated-subproblem architectures.
An \(\ell_1\) exact-penalty method that fixes a certified finite \(\hat\rho\) is a finite-reduction architecture.
immediate_consequences_latex: A method may begin with several parameter-adjustment stages and still be finite-reduction type if the parameter is eventually fixed after finitely many outer stages.
boundary_notes: Finite termination of the inner solver is not required by finite-reduction type; only the number of distinct penalty-parameter stages is finite.
Augmented-Lagrangian architectures with independent multiplier states are not classified here unless explicitly represented as penalty architectures.

notation.meaning: acceptable approximate-solution set for a subproblem

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Exterior-Point Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequential exterior-point method approximately solves each smooth quadratic-penalty subproblem, tightens the inner stationarity tolerance, and increases the penalty weight until explicit feasibility and penalized-stationarity tests are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) be continuously differentiable. Given \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\rho_0>0\), inner tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), growth factors \(\gamma_k>1\), and stopping tolerances \(\eta_F,\eta_P>0\), define \(v_2(x)=\|c(x)\|_2^2+\|[g(x)]_+\|_2^2\). At outer iteration \(k\), approximately minimize \(P_k(x)=f(x)+\tfrac{\rho_k}{2}v_2(x)\) from the current warm start, obtaining \(x_{k+1}\) such that \(\|\nabla P_k(x_{k+1})\|_2\le\varepsilon_k\). Return \(x_{k+1}\) if \(v_2(x_{k+1})^{1/2}\le\eta_F\) and \(\|\nabla P_k(x_{k+1})\|_2\le\eta_P\). Otherwise set \(\rho_{k+1}=\gamma_k\rho_k\) and solve the next exterior-penalty subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are continuously differentiable.
Each inner solver returns an iterate satisfying \(\|\nabla P_k(x_{k+1})\|_2\le\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) is returned when \(v_2(x_{k+1})^{1/2}\le\eta_F\) and \(\|\nabla P_k(x_{k+1})\|_2\le\eta_P\); otherwise \(\rho_{k+1}=\gamma_k\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer iteration for increasingly weighted smooth exterior-penalty subproblems.

notation.meaning: Exterior-penalty subproblem at outer iteration k.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(v:X\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfy \(v(x)=0\iff x\in\Omega\). Let \(\psi:\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R_+\) be increasing with \(\psi(0)=0\), and set \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\psi(v(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic exterior method whose iterates may remain infeasible and whose constraint enforcement is strengthened through an unbounded scalar penalty sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A sequential exterior-point method generates \((\rho_k,\varepsilon_k,x_{k+1})\) satisfying
\[0<\rho_k<\rho_{k+1},\qquad \rho_k\to\infty,\]
and
\[P_{\rho_k}(x_{k+1})\leq\inf_{x\in X}P_{\rho_k}(x)+\varepsilon_k\]
for global subproblem accuracy, or a stated local stationarity condition \(R_{\rho_k}(x_{k+1})\leq\varepsilon_k\). The method is asymptotically accurate when \(\varepsilon_k/\rho_k\to0\). It is exterior because every subproblem is defined on \(X\), not on \(\Omega\), so infeasible points with \(v(x)>0\) remain admissible at every finite \(\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequential exterior-point method solves penalty subproblems on a domain that still admits infeasible points, while the positive penalty parameter increases without bound. Each subproblem is solved to either an explicit objective-gap tolerance or an explicit local stationarity tolerance. Relative accuracy requires \(\varepsilon_k/\rho_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{sequential exterior method}\iff \rho_k\uparrow\infty\text{ and each }x_{k+1}\text{ satisfies the stated }P_{\rho_k}\text{-subproblem criterion on }X.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(t_k=1/\rho_k\), the parameter condition is equivalently \(t_k\downarrow0\).
special_cases_latex: The quadratic exterior penalty uses \(\psi(v)=v^2/2\), commonly with \(v(x)^2=\|h(x)\|^2+\|[g(x)]_+\|^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: No finite outer stage is required by the definition to produce a feasible point.
boundary_notes: An interior barrier method is not an exterior-point method because its finite-parameter domain excludes the constraint boundary or exterior.
An exact penalty held at a finite parameter belongs to the finite-reduction class, not this unbounded-sequence definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Exterior-Penalty Violation Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global objective lower bound converts approximate global penalty minimization into an inverse-penalty bound on constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in X:V(x)=0\}\neq\varnothing\), let \(x^*\in F\) minimize \(f\) over \(F\), and suppose \(f(x)\geq m> -\infty\) on \(X\). If \(\rho_k>0\), \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), and \[ f(x_k)+\rho_kV(x_k)\leq \inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho_kV(x)\}+\varepsilon_k, \] then \[ 0\leq V(x_k)\leq \frac{f(x^*)-m+\varepsilon_k}{\rho_k}. \] Consequently, if \(\rho_k\to\infty\) and \((\varepsilon_k)\) is bounded, then \(V(x_k)=O(\rho_k^{-1})\) and \(V(x_k)\to0\).
assumptions_latex: \(V:X\to[0,+\infty]\), and a feasible global minimizer \(x^*\) exists.
\(x_k\) satisfies the stated global objective-gap inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V(x_k)\leq\frac{f(x^*)-m+\varepsilon_k}{\rho_k}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative feasibility estimate for globally inexact generalized exterior-penalty subproblems.

notation.meaning: global lower bound for the objective on X

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Exterior-Penalty Sequences
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing-error minimizers of increasingly severe exterior penalties have feasible, globally optimal accumulation points, provided the relevant sublevel sets remain bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(V:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous, and define \(F=\{x\in X:V(x)=0\}\). Assume \(F\neq\varnothing\), the constrained optimum \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) is finite and attained, and the relevant penalty sublevel sets are bounded. If \(\rho_k\uparrow+\infty\), \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), and
\[
f(x_k)+\rho_kV(x_k)\leq\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho_kV(x)\}+\varepsilon_k,
\]
then every accumulation point \(\bar x\) of \((x_k)\) belongs to \(F\) and satisfies \(f(\bar x)=f^*\). Thus an unbounded generalized exterior-penalty hierarchy globalizes feasibility while preserving global optimality at cluster points.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\) and the constrained minimum is finite and attained.
\(f\) and \(V\) are lower semicontinuous on closed \(X\).
\(\rho_k\to+\infty\), \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), and the generated sequence is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in F\) and \(f(\bar x)=f^*\) for every accumulation point \(\bar x\) of \((x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global accumulation result for abstract exterior penalties solved with vanishing objective error.

notation.meaning: exterior-penalty parameter at outer iteration k

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(v_i:X\to\mathbb R_+\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be violation components with \(\Omega=\{x\in X:v_i(x)=0\ \forall i\}\). Let \(\phi_{k,i}:\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R_+\) be increasing and satisfy \(\phi_{k,i}(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized or hierarchical exterior penalties with component-dependent shapes and strengths; scalar quadratic continuation is a strict special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A generalized exterior-penalty sequence is a family
\[P_k(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_{k,i}\phi_{k,i}(v_i(x)),\qquad \rho_{k,i}>0,\]
together with approximate subproblem points \(x_{k+1}\), such that for every \(\delta>0\),
\[\inf_{x\in X:\,\max_i v_i(x)\geq\delta}\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_{k,i}\phi_{k,i}(v_i(x))\longrightarrow\infty.\]
This uniform separation condition is called exterior enforcement. The sequence is hierarchical when the index set has ordered levels \(I_1,\ldots,I_s\) and
\[\frac{\min_{i\in I_\ell}\rho_{k,i}}{\max_{j\in I_{\ell+1}}\rho_{k,j}}\to\infty\quad(\ell=1,\ldots,s-1),\]
so violations at earlier levels dominate later ones asymptotically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized exterior-penalty sequence permits separate parameter sequences and penalty shapes for different violation components. Its defining enforcement condition requires the total penalty to diverge uniformly on every set whose violation stays at least \(\delta>0\). A hierarchical sequence additionally imposes asymptotically dominant parameter scales between ordered constraint levels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\{P_k\}\text{ is generalized exterior-enforcing}\iff\forall\delta>0,\ \inf_{\max_i v_i\geq\delta}(P_k-f)\to\infty.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(\rho_{k,i}=\rho_k\), \(\phi_{k,i}(t)=t^2/2\), and \(\rho_k\to\infty\), the family reduces to a classical quadratic exterior-penalty sequence.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exterior enforcement is a property of the complete weighted family and need not require every component weight to diverge when the violation components are redundant.
boundary_notes: The definition does not specify how accurately each \(P_k\) is solved.
Lexicographic feasibility is represented only when an explicit hierarchy of levels is supplied.

children.top_down_role: Finite-parameter reductions intended to avoid an unbounded outer sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Exact-Penalty Threshold Can Be Necessary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing the penalty exactly equal to an optimal multiplier magnitude can leave infeasible global minimizers, so the usual strict threshold is sharp without additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[ \min_{0\leq x\leq1}-x\quad\text{subject to}\quad x=0. \] The unique feasible and constrained-optimal point is \(x^*=0\), and, under \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda x\), an optimal equality multiplier is \(\lambda^*=1\). The \(\ell_1\) penalty is \[ P_\rho(x)=-x+\rho|x|=(\rho-1)x\qquad(0\leq x\leq1). \] At \(\rho=|\lambda^*|=1\), every \(x\in[0,1]\) minimizes \(P_\rho\), including infeasible points. For every \(\rho>1\), its unique minimizer is \(x=0\).
assumptions_latex: The equality constraint is \(x=0\), the objective is \(f(x)=-x\), and the Lagrangian convention is \(L=f+\lambda x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in[0,1]}P_1(x)=[0,1]\not\subseteq\{0\},\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in[0,1]}P_\rho(x)=\{0\}\ \text{for }\rho>1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary example showing that equality with an optimal multiplier norm need not produce an exact single subproblem.

notation.meaning: optimal equality multiplier under the convention L=f+lambda x

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Subproblem Exact Reductions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a convex problem with strong duality, one sufficiently large finite ell-one penalty yields exactly the constrained global solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_{x\in X} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,\quad g(x)\leq0,
\]
where \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed and convex, \(f\) and every component of \(g\) are convex, and \(h\) is affine. Suppose strong duality holds and an optimal multiplier pair \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\), with \(\mu^*\geq0\), exists. For any finite
\[
\rho>\max\{\|\lambda^*\|_\infty,\|\mu^*\|_\infty\},
\]
every minimizer over \(X\) of
\[
P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\bigl(\|h(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\bigr)
\]
is feasible and solves the constrained problem. Hence one unconstrained or simply constrained subproblem is an exact reduction; no divergent penalty sequence is required.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is closed and convex; \(f,g_i\) are convex and \(h\) is affine.
Strong duality holds and an optimal multiplier pair \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}P_\rho(x)\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x):x\in X,\ h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex global exactness of one finite-parameter ell-one penalty subproblem.

notation.meaning: componentwise positive part of the inequality residual

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\Omega\subseteq X\) be the feasible set, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(P_\rho:X\to\mathbb R\) be a parameterized penalty function. Write \(S=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in\Omega}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global finite-parameter reduction of a constrained problem to one penalty subproblem; local exact reductions use localized argmin sets instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite parameter \(\hat\rho>0\) defines a single-subproblem exact reduction when
\[\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in X}P_{\hat\rho}(x)=S\]
and
\[\inf_{x\in X}P_{\hat\rho}(x)=\inf_{x\in\Omega}f(x).\]
An architecture realizes the reduction after outer index \(K<\infty\) if \(\rho_K=\hat\rho\), \(\rho_k=\hat\rho\) for all \(k\geq K\), and every subsequent inner iteration is directed at minimizing the same function \(P_{\hat\rho}\). The least exact threshold, when it exists, is
\[\rho_* =\inf\{\rho>0:\operatorname{argmin}_X P_\tau=S\text{ and }\inf_XP_\tau=\inf_\Omega f\ \forall\tau>\rho\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-subproblem exact reduction selects one finite penalty parameter for which the penalized problem has exactly the constrained solution set and constrained optimal value. An algorithm realizes the reduction when, after finitely many parameter adjustments, all remaining inner work minimizes that one fixed penalized objective. The definition also records an infimum exactness threshold when exactness persists for all larger parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_{\hat\rho}\text{ is a single-subproblem exact reduction}\iff\operatorname{argmin}_X P_{\hat\rho}=\operatorname{argmin}_\Omega f\text{ and }\inf_XP_{\hat\rho}=\inf_\Omega f.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(P_\rho=f\) on \(\Omega\), equality of nonempty global argmin sets implies equality of the attained optimal values.
special_cases_latex: For an exact \(\ell_1\) penalty, a parameter above a valid multiplier-based threshold may furnish such a reduction under appropriate regularity and existence assumptions.
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduction avoids an outer sequence with \(\rho_k\to\infty\), though solving the fixed subproblem may still require infinitely many inner iterations.
boundary_notes: Local exactness at one constrained minimizer is weaker than the displayed global reduction.
Equality of optimal values alone is insufficient because infeasible penalized minimizers may remain.
review_flags: An inspected source locator is required for the exact argmin-set reduction and persistent-threshold convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-parameter single-subproblem exact reduction

children.title: Penalty-Parameter Management
children.top_down_role: Families governing penalty strength across outer iterations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Z\) be an outer-algorithm state space. A state \(z_k\in Z\) contains at least a primal point \(x_k\), penalty parameter \(\rho_k>0\), violation value \(v_k\geq0\), inner residual \(r_k\geq0\), and any stored history \(H_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic management policy for scalar penalty strength; vector-valued penalties replace the scalar codomain with a positive cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A penalty-parameter management policy is a map
\[\mathcal U:Z\to(0,\infty)\times\mathcal E\]
that returns \((\rho_{k+1},e_k)=\mathcal U(z_k)\), where \(e_k\) is an update event, and satisfies declared invariants such as
\[\rho_{\min}\leq\rho_{k+1}\leq\rho_{\max},\qquad \rho_{k+1}\geq\rho_k\]
when monotone exterior enforcement is intended. It is prescribed if \(\rho_{k+1}\) depends only on \(k\) and fixed data, adaptive if it depends on observed components of \(z_k\), and steering if it compares predicted or achieved objective and feasibility effects before selecting \(\rho_{k+1}\). The policy includes its initialization, admissible parameter set, update triggers, safeguarding bounds, and termination or freeze rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty-parameter management is a state-to-parameter policy together with explicit events and invariants. It specifies initialization, admissible values, update triggers, safeguards, and when the parameter is frozen or updating stops. Prescribed, adaptive, and steering policies are distinguished by whether they use only the outer index, observed algorithm state, or predicted and achieved objective–feasibility effects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal U\text{ is a parameter-management policy}\iff\mathcal U(z_k)=(\rho_{k+1},e_k)\text{ lies in its declared admissible set and satisfies its stated invariants}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A set-valued policy \(\mathcal U:Z\rightrightarrows(0,\infty)\times\mathcal E\) represents nondeterministic admissible updates.
special_cases_latex: A geometric exterior update uses \(\rho_{k+1}=\tau\rho_k\) with fixed \(\tau>1\).
A safeguarded adaptive update may restrict \(\rho_{k+1}\in[\rho_k,\tau_{\max}\rho_k]\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The same penalty formulation can support different management families because \(P_\rho\) and \(\mathcal U\) are distinct objects.
boundary_notes: Parameter management alone does not specify inner-subproblem accuracy.
Nonmonotone reductions are allowed unless monotonicity is declared as an invariant.
review_flags: No inspected source defines the full policy object with the same state, event, safeguard, and freeze components.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-parameter management policy

children.title: Prescribed Penalty Continuation
children.top_down_role: Predetermined monotone penalty schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Prescribed Penalty Continuation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve successive penalized problems using parameter and inner-accuracy schedules fixed before execution, warm-starting each solve and stopping when the specified feasibility and optimality tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(V:X\to[0,+\infty)\), and let \(R_k:X\to[0,+\infty)\) be a specified optimality residual for the \(k\)-th penalty subproblem. Choose \(x_0\in X\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}>0\), and, before execution, sequences \(0<\rho_0\leq\rho_1\leq\cdots\) and \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), approximately solve
\[
\min_{x\in X}P_k(x),\qquad P_k(x)=f(x)+\rho_kV(x),
\]
starting from \(x_k\), and return an iterate \(x_{k+1}\) satisfying the selected inner termination test with tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\). Stop if
\[
V(x_{k+1})\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
R_k(x_{k+1})\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}};
\]
otherwise advance to the next predetermined parameter. Neither \(\rho_k\) nor \(\varepsilon_k\) is changed in response to observed progress.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed, and \(f\), \(V\), and each residual \(R_k\) are defined on \(X\).
The sequences \((\rho_k)\) and \((\varepsilon_k)\) are fixed before execution, with \(0<\rho_k\leq\rho_{k+1}\) and \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the algorithm terminates at outer iteration \(k\), its output \(x_{k+1}\) satisfies \(V(x_{k+1})\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) and \(R_k(x_{k+1})\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exterior-penalty continuation with predetermined monotone parameter and inner-accuracy schedules.

notation.meaning: penalized objective at outer iteration k
specified optimality residual for the kth penalty subproblem

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Classes of Penalty Functions and Corresponding Methods of Multipliers p. 302

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P_\rho:X\to\mathbb R\) be a penalty family. Fix an initial parameter \(\rho_0>0\) and a deterministic schedule generator \(G:\mathbb N\times(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Open-loop scalar continuation: the parameter schedule is fixed independently of computed iterates, violations, inner residuals, or acceptance outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A prescribed penalty continuation is a sequence \((\rho_k)_{k\geq0}\) satisfying
\[\rho_{k+1}=G(k,\rho_k),\qquad \rho_{k+1}\geq\rho_k,\]
where \(G\) and \(\rho_0\) are fixed before subproblem solutions are computed and
\[\rho_{k+1}\perp(x_0,\ldots,x_{k+1},v(x_0),\ldots,v(x_{k+1}),r_0,\ldots,r_k)\]
in the algorithmic sense that none of these observed quantities is an argument of \(G\). The continuation is exterior-divergent if \(\rho_k\to\infty\), finite-target if \(\rho_k\uparrow\bar\rho<\infty\), and strictly monotone if \(\rho_{k+1}>\rho_k\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prescribed penalty continuation fixes a monotone parameter recurrence and its initial value before any subproblem results are observed. The next parameter cannot depend on iterates, violations, residuals, or acceptance outcomes. The schedule may diverge for an exterior penalty or approach a finite target, and it may be nondecreasing or strictly increasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\rho_k)\text{ is prescribed continuation}\iff\rho_{k+1}=G(k,\rho_k)\geq\rho_k\text{ for a preassigned state-independent }G.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The schedule is open-loop: there exists a preassigned sequence \((\widehat\rho_k)\) such that \(\rho_k=\widehat\rho_k\) for every possible realization of the inner solves.
special_cases_latex: Geometric continuation is \(\rho_k=\rho_0\tau^k\) with \(\tau>1\).
Additive continuation is \(\rho_k=\rho_0+k\Delta\) with \(\Delta>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Two runs using the same prescribed data have identical parameter sequences even if their inner iterates differ.
boundary_notes: A rule that increases \(\rho_k\) only after insufficient feasibility progress is adaptive, not prescribed.
A predetermined schedule does not by itself determine inner stopping tolerances or guarantee convergence.
review_flags: A precise inspected source locator for the open-loop independence condition was not available.
knowledge_statements.title: Predetermined monotone penalty continuation schedule

children.title: Adaptive Penalty Updates
children.top_down_role: Parameter changes based on observed subproblem and feasibility progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Penalty Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain the penalty after adequate violation reduction; otherwise multiply it by a fixed factor, while separately enforcing inner-solve quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(0<\theta<1\), \(\gamma>1\), \(\rho_0>0\), and \(x_0\in X\). At iteration \(k\), approximately minimize \(P_k(x)=f(x)+\rho_kV(x)\) over \(X\), warm-started at \(x_k\), to obtain \(x_{k+1}\). Update
\[
\rho_{k+1}=
\begin{cases}
\rho_k,&V(x_{k+1})\leq\theta V(x_k),\\
\gamma\rho_k,&V(x_{k+1})>\theta V(x_k).
\end{cases}
\]
If the inner solver fails its prescribed stationarity or objective-reduction test, tighten its tolerance before assessing the violation ratio. Stop only when \(V(x_{k+1})\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) and the chosen optimality residual is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\). Thus parameter growth is triggered by insufficient observed feasibility progress.
assumptions_latex: Each subproblem solver supplies a checkable inner-accuracy measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{k+1}\geq\rho_k\), with strict increase exactly when the prescribed feasibility-progress test fails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Violation-ratio update for an exterior-penalty sequence.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The selected algorithmic role fits adaptive penalty management, but the exact violation-ratio rule, the instruction to tighten inner tolerances before ratio assessment, and the stopping protocol are more specific than the cited general section can presently support. The statement also uses X, f, and the optimality tolerances and residual without fully introducing them. An authoritative algorithm or theorem locator supporting this precise update is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptive update rule for a sequential penalty method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Let \(P(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu V(x)\), or \(P(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu V(x)^2/2\), where \(V(x)\geq0\) measures constraint violation. At outer iteration \(k\), an inner solver returns \(x_k\) and observable data \(z_k\), such as stationarity residual, constraint violation, and inner work.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic sequential penalty methods. The definition covers feedback-based parameter changes and does not require a particular penalty function or convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive penalty update is a family of maps \[U_k:(0,\infty)\times\mathcal Z\to(0,\infty),\qquad \mu_{k+1}=U_k(\mu_k,z_k),\] for which the value of \(\mu_{k+1}\) depends on data obtained while approximately minimizing \(P(\cdot;\mu_k)\). A standard monotone instance chooses constants \(1<\gamma_{\min}\leq\gamma_{\max}\) and sets \[\mu_{k+1}=\gamma_k\mu_k,\qquad \gamma_k\in[\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}],\] with \(\gamma_k\) selected from observed subproblem cost or feasibility progress; safeguards may force an increase when \(V(x_k)\) fails a prescribed progress test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive penalty update is a positive-valued feedback rule \(\mu_{k+1}=U_k(\mu_k,z_k)\), where \(z_k\) contains information observed during the current penalty-subproblem solve. In a monotone multiplicative version, \(\mu_{k+1}=\gamma_k\mu_k\), and the multiplier \(\gamma_k>1\) is chosen according to inner cost or achieved feasibility reduction. Thus the parameter sequence is not fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mu_{k+1}=U_k(\mu_k,z_k)>0,\quad z_k\text{ contains iteration-}k\text{ feedback.}\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update is adaptive precisely when the sequence \(\{\mu_k\}\) is generated recursively from the algorithmic history rather than prescribed independently of that history.
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic penalty method, a modest increase such as \(\mu_{k+1}=1.5\mu_k\) may follow an expensive inner solve, whereas a larger increase such as \(\mu_{k+1}=10\mu_k\) may follow a cheap solve.
A feasibility safeguard may increase \(\mu_k\) and restore an earlier starting point when violation does not decrease sufficiently.
immediate_consequences_latex: If every accepted update satisfies \(\mu_{k+1}\geq\gamma_{\min}\mu_k\) with \(\gamma_{\min}>1\), then \(\mu_k\to\infty\).
Allowing \(\gamma_k\) to depend on inner cost explicitly couples outer parameter growth to subproblem work.
boundary_notes: This definition is distinct from prescribed continuation, where the entire parameter sequence is fixed before observing iterates.
For an inverse penalty convention, in which smaller parameters impose stronger penalties, the corresponding monotonicity direction is reversed.

notation.meaning: positive penalty parameter at outer iteration k
observed subproblem, feasibility, and work data

children.top_down_role: Penalty choices coordinated with predicted feasibility and optimality progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Steering Exact-Penalty Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the exact-penalty weight so the model step achieves a fixed fraction of the best predicted feasibility improvement, then globalize by merit reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iterate \(x_k\), let \(m_k^f(d)\) model the objective change and let \(m_k^V(d)\geq0\) model violation over a step set \(D_k\). First compute a feasibility step \(d_k^V\in D_k\) and its predicted reduction \(\Delta_k^V=m_k^V(0)-m_k^V(d_k^V)\). Choose \(\rho_k>0\) and compute
\[
d_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in D_k}\{m_k^f(d)+\rho_km_k^V(d)\}
\]
so that
\[
m_k^V(0)-m_k^V(d_k)\geq\sigma\Delta_k^V,
\]
where \(0<\sigma<1\). Accept or reject \(d_k\) using actual versus predicted reduction of \(f+\rho_kV\); enlarge \(\rho_k\) and recompute when the steering inequality fails. Stop at the prescribed feasibility and stationarity tolerances.
assumptions_latex: Local objective and violation models are available on \(D_k\).
The feasibility-model subproblem has a computed step \(d_k^V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted trial step satisfies \(m_k^V(0)-m_k^V(d_k)\geq\sigma\Delta_k^V\) and the chosen merit acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-based penalty selection balancing predicted feasibility and objective progress.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and predicted-feasibility steering idea match the container, but no citation is supplied for the particular steering inequality, penalty-enlargement direction, or merit acceptance mechanism. Different steering exact-penalty methods use materially different parameter conventions and acceptance rules, so the mathematical version cannot be confirmed without an authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a nonlinear program, let \(m_k(p)\) be a piecewise-linear model of total constraint violation at \(x_k\), let \(q_\mu(p)=f_k+\nabla f_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp+\mu m_k(p)\), and restrict \(p\) to a nonempty step set \(\mathcal P_k\), such as a trust region with elastic linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonsmooth exact-penalty SQP, sequential linear-quadratic programming, or related model-based methods. Steering concerns the joint selection of the penalty weight and step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A steering exact-penalty iteration computes \(p_k=p_k(\mu_k)\) and \(\mu_k\geq\mu_{k-1}>0\) so that the feasibility-model reduction is compared with the best feasibility reduction available in the same step set. If \[p_k^F\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathcal P_k}m_k(p),\] then for a prescribed \(\epsilon_F\in(0,1)\) the steering condition is \[m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\geq\epsilon_F\bigl(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k^F)\bigr).\] A model-balance condition may additionally require, for \(\epsilon_Q\in(0,1)\), \[q_{\mu_k}(0)-q_{\mu_k}(p_k)\geq\epsilon_Q\mu_k\bigl(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A steering exact-penalty method chooses the penalty parameter together with the trial step. The chosen step must recover a fixed fraction \(\epsilon_F\) of the maximum feasible reduction in the linearized violation model, and it may also be required to produce penalized-model reduction commensurate with that feasibility improvement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Delta m_k(p_k)\geq\epsilon_F\Delta m_k(p_k^F),\qquad \Delta q_{\mu_k}(p_k)\geq\epsilon_Q\mu_k\Delta m_k(p_k).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The first condition compares the computed step with the limiting feasibility step obtained by suppressing the objective terms, conventionally described as using an infinite penalty weight.
special_cases_latex: If \(m_k(p_k(\mu_{k-1}))=0\), the previous parameter is retained.
If the best feasibility step has positive residual, \(\mu_k\) is increased until the computed step achieves the required fraction of its reduction.
immediate_consequences_latex: The penalty weight is large enough to enforce quantified linearized-feasibility progress but need not be made unnecessarily large.
The step and parameter cannot generally be selected independently because \(p_k\) solves a model containing \(\mu_k\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert that steering conditions alone imply convergence.
This is more specific than an update triggered only by the current nonlinear violation; it uses a reference feasibility subproblem.

notation.meaning: best feasibility-model step in the current step set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Solver family induced by penalty-subproblem structure
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the constraints retained explicitly and let \(P_k:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the penalty objective at outer iteration \(k\). An inner method returns \(x_k\in X\) satisfying a stated approximate-stationarity or model-reduction condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A structural taxonomy rather than a convergence claim. It distinguishes solver interfaces by smoothness of \(P_k\) and by the geometry of retained constraints \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty-subproblem solution family is a class \(\mathfrak S(\mathcal C,\mathcal X,\mathcal R)\) of inner algorithms applicable whenever \(P_k\in\mathcal C\), \(X\in\mathcal X\), and termination is certified by \(R_k(x_k)\leq\eta_k\) for a residual \(R_k\in\mathcal R\). Canonical classes are \[\begin{aligned}\mathfrak S_{\rm sm}&:\ P_k\in C^1\text{ or }C^2,\ X=\mathbb R^n;\\\mathfrak S_{\rm ns}&:\ P_k\text{ is locally Lipschitz or piecewise smooth};\\\mathfrak S_X&:\ X\neq\mathbb R^n\text{ is retained and admits tractable projection or constrained steps}.\end{aligned}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty-subproblem solution family groups inner algorithms by three pieces of data: the regularity class of the penalized objective, the explicitly retained feasible set, and the residual used to stop. Smooth unconstrained, nonsmooth model-based, and simple-constraint methods are the principal distinct families.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_k\in\mathcal C,\ X\in\mathcal X,\ R_k(x_k)\leq\eta_k\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \text{the inner solve belongs to }\mathfrak S(\mathcal C,\mathcal X,\mathcal R).\]
special_cases_latex: For smooth equality quadratic penalties, Newton, quasi-Newton, and other unconstrained smooth methods form \(\mathfrak S_{\rm sm}\).
For a max-type exact penalty, linearization or quadratic-model subproblems form \(\mathfrak S_{\rm ns}\).
If bounds remain explicit, projected, active-set, or bound-constrained solvers form \(\mathfrak S_X\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A change in penalty smoothness can change the admissible inner family even when the original nonlinear program is unchanged.
Retaining a simple set \(X\) changes the stationarity residual from \(\|\nabla P_k(x)\|\) to a constrained residual such as a projected-gradient mapping.
boundary_notes: The three classes can overlap; they are interfaces, not mutually exclusive complexity categories.
No single cited source was found that states this complete three-axis taxonomy as one formal definition.
review_flags: The mathematical taxonomy is standard-field synthesis, but the supplied sources support its component families rather than this exact unified definition.
A precise authoritative locator for the complete taxonomy is required.

children.title: Smooth Penalty Subproblem Solvers
children.top_down_role: Newton, quasi-Newton, and related interfaces for smooth penalized objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Penalty Subproblem Solvers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply safeguarded line-search Newton or quasi-Newton iterations to an unconstrained smooth penalty objective, returning the first iterate whose gradient residual meets the prescribed inner tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(\rho>0\), let \(P_\rho:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable on an open set containing the iterates. Starting from \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), at inner iteration \(j\) select a symmetric matrix \(B_j\). For a Newton step take \(B_j=\nabla^2P_\rho(x_j)\) when the Hessian exists; for a quasi-Newton step take a positive-definite secant approximation. Compute
\[
B_jd_j=-\nabla P_\rho(x_j).
\]
If necessary, modify \(B_j\) or replace \(d_j\) so that \(\nabla P_\rho(x_j)^\mathsf{T}d_j<0\). Choose \(\alpha_j>0\) by a sufficient-decrease line search, set \(x_{j+1}=x_j+\alpha_jd_j\), and perform the prescribed matrix update. Terminate at the first index \(j\) for which \(\|\nabla P_\rho(x_j)\|\leq\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon>0\), and return that iterate to the outer penalty method.
assumptions_latex: \(P_\rho:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable near the generated iterates.
For a Newton step, \(P_\rho\) is twice differentiable at the current iterate; otherwise a symmetric quasi-Newton approximation is used.
A descent direction and a sufficient-decrease line-search step can be computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the inner algorithm terminates at index \(j\), the returned iterate satisfies \(\|\nabla P_\rho(x_j)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded line-search Newton or quasi-Newton solution of an unconstrained smooth penalized subproblem.

notation.meaning: smooth penalized objective at a fixed penalty parameter
Newton Hessian or symmetric quasi-Newton approximation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth solver interface for a penalty subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P_\mu:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, and twice continuously differentiable when Hessian models are used. At an inner iterate \(y_j\), let \(g_j=\nabla P_\mu(y_j)\) and let \(B_j\) approximate \(\nabla^2P_\mu(y_j)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth unconstrained penalty subproblems. Inequality penalties that are only once differentiable or nonsmooth at activity changes require modified interfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A smooth penalty-subproblem solver generates \[B_js_j=-g_j+r_j,\qquad y_{j+1}=y_j+\alpha_js_j,\] or an equivalent trust-region step, where \(B_j\) is the exact Hessian, a quasi-Newton approximation, or another smooth model matrix; \(r_j\) is an optional inexact linear-solve residual; and \(\alpha_j\in(0,1]\) is chosen by a smooth globalization rule. The solve terminates at \(x_k=y_j\) when \[\|\nabla P_{\mu_k}(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth penalty-subproblem solver treats the penalized objective as an unconstrained differentiable function. It computes Newton, quasi-Newton, or related model steps and returns a point whose gradient residual is below a prescribed inner tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_k\text{ is an accepted inner solution when }\|\nabla P_{\mu_k}(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: An inexact Newton interface may use \(\|B_js_j+g_j\|\leq\xi_j\|g_j\|\) instead of an exact Newton equation.
A trust-region implementation minimizes \(g_j^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_js\) over \(\|s\|\leq\Delta_j\).
special_cases_latex: For an equality quadratic penalty, \(P_\mu(x)=f(x)+\mu\|c(x)\|^2/2\) is smooth whenever \(f\) and \(c\) are smooth.
Differentiable exact penalties involving the Lagrangian and squared stationarity or feasibility terms may likewise be minimized by derivative-based algorithms.
immediate_consequences_latex: Increasing a quadratic-penalty parameter can make the Hessian ill-conditioned, so solver choice and linear-system formulation affect inner work.
A quasi-Newton realization replaces exact second derivatives by updates built from gradient differences.
boundary_notes: The definition excludes a raw \(\ell_1\) exact penalty at its kink points.
It defines a solver interface, not local superlinear or quadratic convergence.

notation.meaning: exact or approximate Hessian of the smooth penalty objective

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Ell-One Model Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global optimality of the convex linearized penalty model is certified by compatible residual subgradients and a normal-cone multiplier for the polyhedral step set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_*\in D_k\) minimize the immutable seed's convex model and put \(z=h(x_k)+J_h(x_k)d_*\) and \(w=g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)d_*\). Then \(d_*\) is globally model-optimal if and only if there exist \(u\in\partial\|z\|_1\), \(v\in\partial\|[w]_+\|_1\), and \(n\in N_{D_k}(d_*)\) such that \[0=\nabla f(x_k)+B_kd_*+\rho J_h(x_k)^\mathsf Tu+\rho J_g(x_k)^\mathsf Tv+n.\] Componentwise, \(u_i=\operatorname{sign}(z_i)\) for \(z_i\ne0\) and \(u_i\in[-1,1]\) for \(z_i=0\); likewise \(v_j=1\) for \(w_j>0\), \(v_j=0\) for \(w_j<0\), and \(v_j\in[0,1]\) for \(w_j=0\).
assumptions_latex: The model objective is finite at \(d_*\in D_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\nabla f(x_k)+B_kd_*+\rho J_h(x_k)^\mathsf T\partial\|z\|_1+\rho J_g(x_k)^\mathsf T\partial\|[w]_+\|_1+N_{D_k}(d_*).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient and normal-cone certificate for the convex LP/QP local model.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional derivative combines signed derivatives for nonzero equality residuals, absolute directional residuals at satisfied equalities, and positive-part directional derivatives for inequalities.

For \(P_ho(x)=f(x)+ho\sum_i|h_i(x)|+ho\sum_j[g_j(x)]_+\) with differentiable data, \[P_ho'(x;d)=

e0,\|

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Minimax Linearization Subproblem
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearizing finitely many smooth branches and introducing one epigraph variable produces an LP or convex QP minimax subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(x)=\max_{1\leq\ell\leq L}\phi_\ell(x)\), where every \(\phi_\ell\) is differentiable. At \(x_k\), with \(B_k\succeq0\) and a nonempty polyhedral step set \(D_k\), the minimax linearization model is \[\min_{d\in D_k,t}\ t+\tfrac12d^\mathsf TB_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad \phi_\ell(x_k)+\nabla\phi_\ell(x_k)^\mathsf Td\leq t,\ \ell=1,\ldots,L.\] It is an LP when \(B_k=0\) and a convex QP when \(B_k\succeq0\).
assumptions_latex: The number of branches \(L\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_k=0\Rightarrow\text{LP},\qquad B_k\succeq0\Rightarrow\text{convex QP}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph local model for a maximum of finitely many smooth penalty branches.

notation.meaning: epigraph variable for the maximum of linearized branches

knowledge_statements.title: Linearization Methods for Nonsmooth Exact Penalties
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize the constraint residuals over a polyhedral step set, represent absolute values and positive parts with epigraph variables, and solve the resulting LP or convex QP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{m_E}\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{m_I}\) be continuously differentiable, and define
\[
P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\bigl(\|h(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\bigr),
\qquad \rho>0.
\]
At \(x_k\), choose a symmetric matrix \(B_k\succeq0\) and construct
\[
M_k(d)=f(x_k)+\nabla f(x_k)^\mathsf{T}d+\tfrac12d^\mathsf{T}B_kd+\rho\bigl(\|h(x_k)+J_h(x_k)d\|_1+\|[g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)d]_+\|_1\bigr).
\]
Approximately minimize \(M_k\) over a nonempty polyhedral step set \(D_k\), which may include retained linear constraints and an infinity-norm trust region. Introduce epigraph variables for the absolute-value and positive-part terms. The resulting model subproblem is an LP when \(B_k=0\) and a convex QP when \(B_k\succeq0\). Use actual versus predicted reduction in \(P_\rho\) to accept or reject the trial step and to update the step set or trust-region radius.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(h\), and \(g\) are continuously differentiable near the iterates.
The step set \(D_k\) is nonempty and polyhedral.
An actual-versus-predicted-reduction acceptance rule is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The epigraph representation of the local model over \(D_k\) is an LP when \(B_k=0\) and a convex QP when \(B_k\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral-step linearization of an ell-one exact-penalty objective, producing LP or convex-QP subproblems.

notation.meaning: Jacobians of the equality and inequality constraint maps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linearization step for a max-type exact penalty
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F_c(x)=f(x)+cP(x)\), where \(c>0\), \(P(x)=\max_{0\leq j\leq r}g_j(x)\), \(g_0\equiv0\), and every \(g_j\) is continuously differentiable. Let \(J(x)=\{j:g_j(x)=P(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional locally nonsmooth max penalties. Sum-of-absolute-values penalties can be represented by equivalent epigraph or elastic-variable models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linearization method for \(F_c\) chooses \(H_k\succ0\) and an index set \(J_k\supseteq J(x_k)\), then computes the unique primal step component of \[\min_{d\in\mathbb R^n,\,\xi\in\mathbb R}\ \nabla f(x_k)^Td+\tfrac12d^TH_kd+c\xi\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_j(x_k)+\nabla g_j(x_k)^Td\leq\xi\quad(j\in J_k).\] A line search or trust-region rule subsequently selects an accepted displacement from this local piecewise-linear penalty model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearization method replaces each active smooth branch of a nonsmooth exact penalty by its affine model, introduces an epigraph variable \(\xi\), and adds a positive-definite quadratic regularizer. The computed step minimizes this convex local model before globalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(d_k,\xi_k)\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{\nabla f(x_k)^Td+\tfrac12d^TH_kd+c\xi:g_j(x_k)+\nabla g_j(x_k)^Td\leq\xi\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an \(\ell_1\) penalty, positive and negative elastic variables yield a linear or quadratic program representing the same piecewise-linearized violation model.
special_cases_latex: Taking \(J_k=\{0,1,\ldots,r\}\) retains every branch.
Taking \(H_k\) as a quasi-Newton matrix gives a sequential quadratic programming realization.
immediate_consequences_latex: Because \(H_k\succ0\), the step component is uniquely determined when the model is feasible.
The step model remains tractable even though \(F_c\) is nondifferentiable where several branches attain the maximum.
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover arbitrary nonsmooth penalties lacking a finite smooth-branch representation without additional generalized-derivative machinery.
Positive definiteness of \(H_k\) is part of this canonical convex-model version.

notation.meaning: active set of maximal penalty branches
epigraph variable for the linearized maximum

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Stationarity Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth penalty objective over a closed convex retained set, the projected-gradient residual vanishes exactly at first-order stationary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(P_ho\) be differentiable at \(x\in X\). Define \[G_X(x)=x-\Pi_X(x-
abla P_ho(x)).\] Then \[G_X(x)=0\iff 0\in
abla P_ho(x)+N_X(x)\iff 
abla P_ho(x)^\mathsf T(y-x)\geq0\quad orall y\in X.\] Thus \(\|G_X(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) is a computable approximate stationarity test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_X(x)=0\iff0\in\nabla P_\rho(x)+N_X(x).

knowledge_statements.title: Retained-Set Penalty Subproblem
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep bounds or another tractable set explicit and penalize only the remaining constraints, so every subproblem iterate respects the retained set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed. For \[\min f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\in X,\ h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0,\] a retained-set penalty subproblem has the form \[\min_{x\in X}P_\rho(x),\qquad P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\bigl(\|h(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\bigr),\quad\rho>0.\] Every subproblem point satisfies the retained constraint. For a box \(X=[\ell,u]\), Euclidean projection is componentwise clipping. The penalty term vanishes exactly when \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\).
assumptions_latex: The inner solver can enforce \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}P_\rho(x)\subseteq X,\qquad \|h(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1=0\iff h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty reduction that keeps an easily enforced constraint set explicit.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalty reduction retaining a simple feasible set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Partition the original constraints into a set represented by \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and constraints represented by a nonnegative violation map \(V:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty]\). Let \(P_\mu(x)=f(x)+\mu V(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional penalty methods that penalize selected difficult constraints while enforcing bounds, boxes, affine sets, or another tractable set exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simple-constraint penalty subproblem is \[\min_{x\in X}P_\mu(x)=f(x)+\mu V(x),\] where membership in \(X\) is imposed exactly at every inner iterate and admits a designated tractable operation, such as projection \(\Pi_X\), a linear minimization oracle, or an active-set step. An approximate solution \(x_k\in X\) is certified by a constrained stationarity residual; for differentiable \(P_{\mu_k}\), one canonical residual is \[R_k(x_k)=\bigl\|x_k-\Pi_X(x_k-\nabla P_{\mu_k}(x_k))\bigr\|\leq\eta_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple-constraint penalty subproblem penalizes some constraints but retains a tractable set \(X\) explicitly. Inner iterates must remain in \(X\), and termination uses a constrained residual such as the projected-gradient mapping rather than the ordinary gradient norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_k\in X,\qquad \|x_k-\Pi_X(x_k-\nabla P_{\mu_k}(x_k))\|\leq\eta_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For closed convex \(X\), exact first-order stationarity is equivalent to \(0\in\nabla P_\mu(x)+N_X(x)\).
special_cases_latex: For box constraints, \(X=[\ell,u]\) and \(\Pi_X\) is componentwise clipping.
For affine constraints, \(X=\{x:Ax=b\}\) and projected or null-space methods can enforce membership exactly.
immediate_consequences_latex: The penalized constraints may be violated during inner minimization, but the retained constraints cannot.
When \(X=\mathbb R^n\), the projected-gradient residual reduces to the ordinary gradient residual.
boundary_notes: The supplied locator hints did not expose a passage defining this exact selective-penalization interface.
Nonconvex retained sets require a different stationarity mapping and are outside the displayed projection formulation.

notation.meaning: normal cone to a closed convex set X at x

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty reduction retaining a simple feasible set
Simple-Constraint Penalty Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty reduction that retains an easily enforceable closed constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty closed set onto which projection or exact constrained steps are computationally available. For the problem
\[
\min f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\in X,\quad h(x)=0,\quad g(x)\leq0,
\]
a simple-constraint penalty subproblem retains \(X\) and penalizes only the remaining constraints:
\[
\min_{x\in X}P_\rho(x),\qquad P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\bigl(\|h(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\bigr).
\]
For bound constraints, \(X=[\ell,u]\) and projection is componentwise clipping. Any feasible point of the original problem has zero penalty term, while every minimizer of the displayed subproblem automatically satisfies the retained constraints, independently of \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep bounds or another tractable set explicit and penalize only the difficult constraints; every subproblem iterate then respects the retained set.
assumptions_latex: The retained constraint \(x\in X\) can be enforced by the inner solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}P_\rho(x)\subseteq X\), and the penalty term vanishes exactly when \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accuracy schedule and induced inner-work profile
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), let \(P_k\) be a penalty subproblem, let \(R_k(x)\geq0\) be its stationarity residual, and let \(W_k(\eta)\) denote the inner work required to obtain \(R_k(x)\leq\eta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic outer–inner penalty architectures. Work may count inner iterations, linear solves, objective evaluations, or derivative evaluations, but the unit must be stated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty accuracy–work specification is a tolerance schedule \(\{\eta_k\}_{k\geq0}\) together with an accounting function \(W_k:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}\) such that the returned point satisfies \[R_k(x_k)\leq\eta_k\quad\text{after at most}\quad W_k(\eta_k)\text{ declared work units}.\] The associated cumulative work through outer iteration \(K\) is \[W^{\rm tot}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K}W_k(\eta_k).\] The tradeoff is the dependence of this cumulative quantity and the outer progress conditions on the chosen tolerance schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The penalty accuracy–work tradeoff is the formal pairing of an inner stopping tolerance \(\eta_k\) with the work needed to meet it. Tighter tolerances strengthen the quality of each subproblem solution but can increase \(W_k\); looser tolerances reduce inner work but must still support the outer method's progress requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[R_k(x_k)\leq\eta_k,\qquad W^{\rm tot}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K}W_k(\eta_k).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A budget formulation prescribes \(b_k\) and defines the smallest achieved residual \(\eta_k^{\rm ach}=\inf\{R_k(x):x\text{ is produced within }b_k\text{ units}\}\).
special_cases_latex: Asymptotically exact solves use \(\eta_k\to0\).
Controlled inexact solves tie \(\eta_k\) to feasibility or outer progress rather than requiring a uniformly tiny tolerance.
immediate_consequences_latex: Comparisons of two schedules are meaningful only under the same work unit and residual definition.
The number of outer iterations alone is not a complete cost measure when inner effort varies with \(k\).
boundary_notes: The cited source motivates the tradeoff through progressively tightened tolerances and variable subproblem difficulty, but it does not name the abstract work function \(W_k\).

notation.meaning: work required at outer iteration k to attain residual eta

children.title: Asymptotically Exact Inner Solves
children.top_down_role: Outer convergence with progressively more accurate penalty subproblem solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Exterior-Penalty Limit Under Asymptotically Exact Solves
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain, asymptotically globally accurate exterior-penalty solves with diverging weights have only globally optimal feasible accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(f,V:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous with \(V\geq0\), and suppose \(F=\{x\in X:V(x)=0\}\neq\varnothing\). Let \(\rho_k\to\infty\), \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), and \[f(x_k)+\rho_kV(x_k)\leq\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho_kV(x)\}+\varepsilon_k.\] Then every accumulation point \(\bar x\) of \(\{x_k\}\) belongs to \(F\) and minimizes \(f\) over \(F\).
assumptions_latex: The displayed global objective-gap inequality holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\quad\text{for every accumulation point }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-convergence consequence of vanishing global subproblem objective gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotically Exact Inner Solves
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive penalty subproblems are solved asymptotically exactly in objective value when the nonnegative gaps between the returned values and the corresponding global infima converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a nonempty set and, for each outer iteration \(k\), let \(P_k:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a penalty objective with finite infimum
\[
p_k^*=\inf_{x\in X}P_k(x)>-\infty.
\]
The inner solves are asymptotically exact in objective value if there exists a sequence \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\) with \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) such that the returned point \(x_{k+1}\in X\) satisfies
\[
P_k(x_{k+1})\leq p_k^*+\varepsilon_k
\]
for every outer iteration \(k\). Equivalently, the nonnegative global objective gaps converge to zero.
assumptions_latex: For every \(k\), the infimum \(p_k^*=\inf_{x\in X}P_k(x)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq P_k(x_{k+1})-p_k^*\leq\varepsilon_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing global objective-gap condition for successive penalty subproblems.

notation.meaning: penalty objective at outer iteration k
global infimum of the kth penalty subproblem

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be the penalty objective used at outer iteration \(k\), and let \(R_k(x)\geq0\) be an inner stationarity residual, such as \(\|\nabla P_k(x)\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sequential penalty methods. Exactness refers to the limiting inner optimality residual, not exact global minimization at every finite outer iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \(\{x_k\}\) consists of asymptotically exact inner solves if there is a nonnegative tolerance sequence \(\{\eta_k\}\) satisfying \[R_k(x_k)\leq\eta_k\quad\text{for every }k,\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty}\eta_k=0.\] For a smooth unconstrained subproblem, the canonical instance is \[\|\nabla P_k(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner solves are asymptotically exact when every returned point meets an explicit residual tolerance and those tolerances converge to zero. Individual subproblems may therefore be solved inexactly, while their stationarity errors vanish along the outer sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\leq R_k(x_k)\leq\eta_k\quad\text{and}\quad\eta_k\to0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The defining condition implies \(R_k(x_k)\to0\). The converse holds by choosing \(\eta_k=R_k(x_k)\), although an algorithm normally prescribes tolerances before termination.
special_cases_latex: For quadratic penalty subproblems, \(R_k(x)=\|\nabla_xQ(x;\mu_k)\|\).
For a closed convex retained set, a projected-gradient or normal-cone residual may replace the gradient norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: No fixed positive residual floor is permitted.
The definition allows slow, nonmonotone decay of \(\eta_k\), provided its limit is zero.
boundary_notes: Vanishing stationarity residual does not mean that \(x_k\) is a global minimizer of a nonconvex subproblem.
Additional assumptions are needed to infer feasibility or KKT convergence for the original problem.

notation.meaning: stationarity residual for the kth penalty subproblem

knowledge_statements.title: Generic Residual-Controlled Inner Accuracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Controlled inexactness bounds a declared subproblem stationarity residual by a prescribed or progress-coupled forcing tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For subproblem \(P_k\), let \(R_k(x)\geq0\) be a declared stationarity residual satisfying \(R_k(x)=0\) exactly at the selected first-order stationary points. A returned point \(x_{k+1}\) is residual-controlled at tolerance \(\eta_k\geq0\) when \[R_k(x_{k+1})\leq\eta_k.\] A progress-coupled regime additionally prescribes \(\eta_k\leq\phi_k\), where \(\phi_k\geq0\) is an explicitly defined outer- or inner-progress quantity. If \(\eta_k\to0\), then the returned stationarity residuals converge to zero.
assumptions_latex: Each \(R_k\) is a specified nonnegative stationarity residual with the declared zero set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_k(x_{k+1})\leq\eta_k\to0\Rightarrow R_k(x_{k+1})\to0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-independent residual forcing interface without committing to a particular violation-power schedule.

notation.meaning: declared stationarity residual for subproblem k

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Control Does Not Imply Global Objective Accuracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact first-order stationarity at a nonglobal local minimizer can coexist with a fixed positive global objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(x)=(x^2-1)^2+x\). This coercive smooth function has two strict local minimizers \(x_-<0<x_+\), with \(P(x_-)<P(x_+)\). The constant sequence \(x_k=x_+\) satisfies \(|P'(x_k)|=0\) for every \(k\), while \(P(x_k)-\inf_xP(x)=P(x_+)-P(x_-)>0\).
assumptions_latex: Accuracy is measured only by a first-order stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_k(x_{k+1})\to0\not\Rightarrow P_k(x_{k+1})-\inf P_k\to0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvex boundary separating residual-controlled and globally asymptotically exact solves.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P_k\) be the current penalty or augmented-Lagrangian subproblem, let \(R_k(x)\) be its stationarity residual, and let \(M_k\geq0\) be an outer progress measure, such as current infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional outer–inner schemes in which inner termination is deliberately tied to outer progress. Unlike asymptotically exact solves, vanishing tolerance is not part of the bare definition unless the controller forces it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A controlled inexact inner solve returns \(x_k\) when \[R_k(x_k)\leq\eta_k,\qquad \eta_k=\Psi_k(M_k,\mu_k,\mathcal H_k),\] where \(\Psi_k\geq0\) is a declared controller depending on current progress data and algorithmic history \(\mathcal H_k\). A residual-based controller may take \(\eta_k=\min\{\bar\eta,\kappa M_k^\alpha\}\) with \(\bar\eta,\kappa>0\) and \(\alpha>0\); a progress controller may tighten \(\eta_k\) after satisfactory feasibility reduction and leave it unchanged or alter the penalty parameter otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A controlled inexact solve stops at a nonzero residual tolerance chosen from current outer information. The inexactness is controlled because the tolerance is generated by a stated rule involving feasibility, the penalty parameter, or prior progress, rather than chosen arbitrarily.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[R_k(x_k)\leq\Psi_k(M_k,\mu_k,\mathcal H_k).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A relative criterion can use \(R_k(x_k)\leq\theta_kR_k(x_k^s)\) with \(0\leq\theta_k<1\), where \(x_k^s\) is the inner starting point.
special_cases_latex: If \(M_k\to0\) and \(\Psi_k(M_k,\mu_k,\mathcal H_k)\to0\), the controlled regime is also asymptotically exact.
An augmented-Lagrangian implementation may choose its tolerance as a function of the current infeasibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: The rule exposes the coupling between inner work and outer feasibility progress.
A fixed tolerance \(\eta_k\equiv\bar\eta>0\) is controlled only if explicitly permitted by the controller and the outer guarantees.
boundary_notes: The displayed power controller is a canonical formalization, not a uniquely prescribed source formula.
The definition alone supplies no convergence conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Controlled Inexact Inner Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual forcing rule coupling inner accuracy to current feasibility progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_k\) be the current differentiable penalty objective on a closed convex set \(X\), and define the projected-gradient residual
\[
r_k(x)=\bigl\|x-\Pi_X\bigl(x-\nabla P_k(x)\bigr)\bigr\|.
\]
An inner solution \(x_{k+1}\) is controlled inexact if
\[
r_k(x_{k+1})\leq\eta_k,
\qquad
\eta_k\leq\min\{\bar\eta,\,cV(x_k)^q\},
\]
for fixed \(\bar\eta>0\), \(c>0\), and \(q>0\). Consequently, whenever \(V(x_k)\to0\), the permitted stationarity residual also tends to zero. A nonsmooth implementation may replace \(r_k\) by a specified subdifferential or model-stationarity residual, provided the same forcing inequality is enforced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Terminate each inner solve when its stationarity residual is below a tolerance forced downward by the current constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is closed and convex, so \(\Pi_X\) is defined.
\(P_k\) is differentiable for the displayed residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x_k)\to0\) implies \(r_k(x_{k+1})\to0\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the retained set

knowledge_statements.title: Composition of Outer and Inner Iteration Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total inner and oracle complexity is the sum of per-subproblem work through the bounded outer iterations; uniform inner bounds yield a product bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an algorithm reaches its declared accuracy \(\varepsilon\) after at most \(K(\varepsilon)\) outer iterations, and outer iteration \(k\) uses at most \(T_k(\varepsilon)\) inner iterations. Then \[N_{\rm inner}(\varepsilon)\leq\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}T_k(\varepsilon).\] If \(T_k(\varepsilon)\leq T(\varepsilon)\) uniformly, then \[N_{\rm inner}(\varepsilon)\leq K(\varepsilon)T(\varepsilon).\] If every inner iteration uses at most \(a_r\) calls of type \(r\), then \[N_r(\varepsilon)\leq a_rN_{\rm inner}(\varepsilon)+\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}b_{r,k}.\]
assumptions_latex: The termination accuracy \(\varepsilon\) is explicitly defined.
\(T_k(\varepsilon)\) bounds inner iterations at outer iteration \(k\).
The per-inner call bound \(a_r\) and overheads \(b_{r,k}\) use the same declared operation type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\rm inner}(\varepsilon)\leq\sum_{k<K(\varepsilon)}T_k(\varepsilon)\leq K(\varepsilon)T(\varepsilon)\quad\text{under a uniform inner bound}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy-indexed complexity obtained by composing outer and per-subproblem bounds.

notation.meaning: total accuracy-indexed count of operation type r

knowledge_statements.title: Separated Outer–Inner Work Ledger
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track outer iterations, total inner iterations, each oracle type, and outer overhead separately, then sum work over completed subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(K\) outer iterations are completed and outer iteration \(k\) uses \(T_k\) inner iterations. Define \[N_{\mathrm{outer}}=K,\qquad N_{\mathrm{inner}}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}T_k.\] If inner iteration \((k,j)\) uses \(n_{k,j}^{(r)}\) calls of oracle type \(r\), and outer iteration \(k\) incurs \(b_{r,k}\) additional calls of that type, then \[N_r=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\left(b_{r,k}+\sum_{j=0}^{T_k-1}n_{k,j}^{(r)}\right).\] Complexity reports must state the termination accuracy and the counted operation types.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is the number of completed outer iterations.
\(T_k\) counts the inner iterations of subproblem \(k\).
Each counted call is assigned consistently to an inner iteration or to declared outer overhead.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{inner}}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}T_k\quad\text{and}\quad N_r=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\left(b_{r,k}+\sum_{j=0}^{T_k-1}n_{k,j}^{(r)}\right).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bookkeeping representation separating outer updates, subproblem iterations, oracle calls, and outer overhead.

notation.meaning: inner iterations used by outer subproblem k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disaggregated work ledger for a penalty algorithm
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: A sequential penalty algorithm performs outer parameter-management operations and, during each outer iteration \(k\), an inner solve that may evaluate functions, derivatives, and linear-algebra kernels.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An accounting definition independent of a particular machine model. Each primitive work unit must be fixed before algorithms are compared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An outer–inner work ledger through outer index \(K\) is the vector \[\mathcal W(K)=\left(N_{\rm out}(K),N_{\rm upd}(K),\sum_{k=0}^{K}N_{{\rm in},k},\sum_{k=0}^{K}N_{f,k},\sum_{k=0}^{K}N_{c,k},\sum_{k=0}^{K}N_{\nabla,k},\sum_{k=0}^{K}N_{H,k},\sum_{k=0}^{K}N_{{\rm lin},k}\right),\] where the components count, respectively, completed outer iterations, penalty-parameter updates, inner iterations, objective evaluations, constraint evaluations, first-derivative evaluations, second-derivative evaluations, and linear-system or subproblem solves. A scalar cost is defined only after weights \(\omega_i\geq0\) are declared: \(C_\omega(K)=\omega^T\mathcal W(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer–inner work accounting records parameter updates and inner effort separately, together with evaluation and linear-algebra counts. A single total cost is meaningful only after weights for these heterogeneous operations have been specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal W(K)=\bigl(\text{outer counts},\text{inner counts},\text{evaluation counts},\text{linear-algebra counts}\bigr),\qquad C_\omega(K)=\omega^T\mathcal W(K).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A per-iteration ledger \(w_k\) is equivalent via \(\mathcal W(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K}w_k\), with one-time initialization costs recorded separately.
special_cases_latex: A first-order oracle model may retain only \(N_f,N_c,N_\nabla\).
A factorization-dominated model may split \(N_{\rm lin}\) into factorizations and backsolves.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two methods with the same outer-iteration count can have different total work.
Repeated subproblem solves during a penalty update must be charged to inner or linear-algebra work rather than hidden in the update count.
boundary_notes: Wall-clock time is an empirical measurement, not an invariant work count.
No supplied source was found that states this complete ledger as a canonical definition.

notation.meaning: cumulative vector of declared work counts
inner iterations performed during outer iteration k
