Outer–Inner Work Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive accounting identity separating outer updates, inner iterations, and oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a penalty algorithm performs \(K\) completed outer iterations, and its \(k\)-th penalty subproblem uses \(T_k\) inner iterations. If inner iteration \((k,j)\) makes \(n^f_{k,j}\), \(n^c_{k,j}\), and \(n^d_{k,j}\) evaluations of objective values, constraint values, and derivative oracles, respectively, then the work through outer iteration \(K-1\) is
\[
N_{\mathrm{outer}}=K,\qquad N_{\mathrm{inner}}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}T_k,
\]
\[
N_f=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{j=0}^{T_k-1}n^f_{k,j},\quad N_c=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{j=0}^{T_k-1}n^c_{k,j},\quad N_d=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{j=0}^{T_k-1}n^d_{k,j}.
\]
Any reported complexity bound must specify which count is bounded and the feasibility-optimality accuracy defining termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report outer updates, total inner iterations, and each oracle count separately; aggregate complexity is the sum of work over all completed subproblems.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is the number of completed outer iterations.
Oracle calls are assigned to exactly one inner iteration or separately reported overhead.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{inner}}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}T_k\), with each oracle total obtained by the corresponding double sum.

notation.meaning: inner iterations used by outer subproblem k
objective, constraint, and derivative oracle counts

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scalar-merit globalization with elastic feasibility relaxation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a nonlinear program, let \(\Phi_\mu(x)=f(x)+\mu V(x)\) be a scalar merit function. At \(x_k\), let \(p\) be determined from a local objective model and linearized constraints that may be relaxed by nonnegative elastic variables \(e\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional line-search or trust-region globalization. Elastic variables ensure that the local step problem remains feasible while the merit function balances objective and feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A merit-elastic globalization method defines a step by a subproblem of the form \[\min_{p,e\geq0}\ m_k^f(p)+\mu_k\mathbf1^Te\quad\text{subject to relaxed linearized constraints and }p\in\mathcal P_k,\] and accepts the resulting trial point only through a scalar merit-reduction test, for example \[\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\leq\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_kD\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k;p_k),\qquad \sigma\in(0,1).\] The penalty parameter and elastic variables jointly control the balance between objective decrease and linearized feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit-elastic method relaxes potentially inconsistent linearized constraints with penalized nonnegative variables and globalizes the resulting step using decrease in one scalar merit function. The penalty weight affects both the value assigned to infeasibility and, when present in the step model, the computed direction itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(p_k,e_k)\text{ solves a penalized elastic model, and }x_k+\alpha_kp_k\text{ satisfies the declared merit-reduction test}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Positive and negative elastic variables may represent equality residuals, while one-sided slacks represent inequality residuals.
Eliminating elastic variables produces an \(\ell_1\) piecewise-linear violation term in the step model.
special_cases_latex: Elastic-mode SQP penalizes equality and inequality relaxation variables in a quadratic programming subproblem.
A restricted-step version replaces backtracking by a trust-region acceptance ratio based on actual and predicted merit reduction.
immediate_consequences_latex: The elastic subproblem can remain feasible even when the unrelaxed linearized constraints are inconsistent.
A sufficiently large feasibility weight discourages nonzero elastic variables but may degrade practical balance if chosen excessively large.
boundary_notes: Filter and funnel methods are outside this family when acceptance is not determined by a single scalar merit value.
Elastic relaxation does not make the original nonlinear constraints optional; it relaxes the local model or penalty formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scalar merit functions for constrained trial points
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Write \([z]^- =\max\{0,-z\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic nonlinear programming. The listed families scalarize objective value and constraint violation into a real-valued acceptance measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scalar merit function is a map \(\Phi_\mu:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) used to rank constrained trial points. Canonical penalty families include \[\Phi_{1,\mu}(x)=f(x)+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x)]^-,\] \[\Phi_{2,\mu}(x)=f(x)+\mu\|c(x)\|_2\quad\text{for equality constraints},\] and the quadratic family \[Q_\mu(x)=f(x)+\frac{\mu}{2}\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}c_i(x)^2+\frac{\mu}{2}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}([c_i(x)]^-)^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar merit function assigns one real number to a trial point by combining objective value with constraint violation. Standard families use an \(\ell_1\) violation, an unsquared \(\ell_2\) violation, or squared violations. The first two are generally nonsmooth and can be exact; the quadratic family is smoother but generally nonexact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Phi_\mu(x)=f(x)+\mu V(x),\qquad V(x)\geq0\text{ and }V(x)=0\text{ at feasible points}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing elastic variables converts the \(\ell_1\) violation terms into a linear objective over an epigraph formulation.
special_cases_latex: For feasible methods, \(V(x)=0\) at every iterate, so the objective itself can serve as the merit function.
For equality constraints only, \(V(x)=\|c(x)\|_2\) gives the exact unsquared \(\ell_2\) family.
immediate_consequences_latex: The parameter \(\mu>0\) sets the relative weight assigned to feasibility.
Squaring a norm changes both smoothness and exactness properties and is therefore not merely a notational variant.
boundary_notes: An augmented Lagrangian in \((x,\lambda)\) need not have a primal-dual solution as a minimizer and is not automatically a merit function in this strict sense.
Filter acceptance is not a scalar merit-function family.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.title: Ell-One Merit Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ell-one merit function adds to the objective a positive weight times the sum of absolute equality residuals and positive inequality violations. Its violation term is nonnegative and is zero exactly at feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:X\to\mathbb{R}^{m_E}\), and \(g:X\to\mathbb{R}^{m_I}\), with inequalities written as \(g_i(x)\leq0\). For a penalty parameter \(\rho>0\), the ell-one merit function is
\[
\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V_1(x),
\qquad
V_1(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m_E}|h_i(x)|+\sum_{i=1}^{m_I}\max\{0,g_i(x)\}.
\]
The violation function \(V_1\) is nonnegative and satisfies
\[
V_1(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h(x)=0\ \text{and}\ g(x)\leq0.
\]
Even when \(f\), \(h\), and \(g\) are smooth, \(\Phi_\rho\) is generally nonsmooth at zero equality residuals and at active inequality residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V_1(x)\) and \(V_1(x)=0\iff h(x)=0\text{ and }g(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard nonsmooth objective–violation scalarization for equality and inequality constraints.

notation.meaning: numbers of equality and inequality constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Wrong Fixed Multiplier Cannot Be Repaired by the Penalty
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular feasible KKT point the quadratic penalty has zero gradient, so no finite penalty compensates for an incorrect fixed multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^*\) be feasible and satisfy \(
abla f(x^*)+J_c(x^*)^{\mathsf T}\lambda^*=0\). If \(J_c(x^*)\) has full row rank, then for any fixed \(\lambda
eq\lambda^*\) and every finite \(ho>0\), \[
abla_x\mathcal L_ho(x^*,\lambda)=J_c(x^*)^{\mathsf T}(\lambda-\lambda^*)
eq0.\] Thus increasing \(ho\) cannot make the feasible KKT point stationary while the fixed multiplier remains incorrect.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla_x\mathcal L_\rho(x^*,\lambda)\neq0\quad\text{for every }\rho>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity boundary for a fixed multiplier estimate in an augmented-Lagrangian merit function.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier at the feasible point

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient and Effective-Multiplier Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented-Lagrangian gradient is an ordinary Lagrangian gradient with effective multiplier lambda plus rho times the constraint residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable, then \[
abla_x\mathcal L_ho(x,\lambda)=
abla f(x)+J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}(\lambda+ho c(x)).\] Thus the augmented gradient is the ordinary Lagrangian gradient with effective multiplier \(\widehat\lambda=\lambda+ho c(x)\). At a feasible point it reduces to \(
abla f(x)+J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla_x\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=\nabla f(x)+J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\lambda,\qquad \widehat\lambda=\lambda+\rho c(x).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differential representation of the equality-constrained quadratic augmented Lagrangian used as a merit function.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Lagrangian Merit Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented Lagrangian combines the objective, a multiplier-weighted residual, and a quadratic feasibility penalty into one scalar globalization function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem 
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x)=0,\]
with \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), the quadratic augmented Lagrangian merit function with multiplier estimate \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and penalty parameter \(\rho>0\) is
\[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert c(x)\rVert_2^2.\]
For fixed \((\lambda,\rho)\), globalization accepts steps by comparing scalar values or predicted and actual reductions of \(\mathcal L_\rho\). At every feasible point, \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert c(x)\rVert_2^2\), and feasibility implies \(\mathcal L_\rho=f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained quadratic augmented Lagrangian used as a scalar merit model.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Exact Merit Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth merit family is locally exact when one finite parameter threshold makes its nearby unconstrained local minimizers coincide with constrained local minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the constrained problem
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x)=0,\quad g(x)\leq 0,\]
with feasible set \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\), and let \(\{\Phi_\rho:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\}_{\rho>0}\) be a family of continuously differentiable functions. The family is locally smooth exact at a constrained local minimizer \(x^*\in F\) if there exist a finite \(\bar\rho>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) such that, for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\), \(x^*\) is a local minimizer of \(\Phi_\rho\), and every local minimizer of \(\Phi_\rho\) sufficiently near \(x^*\) is feasible and is a local minimizer of the constrained problem.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) are defined on a neighborhood of \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(\bar\rho<\infty\) such that, for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\), nearby local minimizers of \(\Phi_\rho\) and nearby constrained local minimizers coincide.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite-parameter exactness for differentiable scalar merit families.

children.title: Pure Feasibility Merit Functions
children.top_down_role: Scalar violation models used during feasibility-dominated phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Stationarity of Squared Violation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared feasibility merit function can have infeasible stationary points, so zero gradient is weaker than zero violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the scalar equality \(c(x)=x^2-1=0\), let \(V_2(x)=\tfrac12(x^2-1)^2\). Then \[V_2'(x)=2x(x^2-1),\qquad V_2'(0)=0,\qquad V_2(0)=\tfrac12>0.\] Thus \(x=0\) is stationary for the squared-violation merit function but infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V_2'(0)=0\quad\text{and}\quad c(0)=-1\neq0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity of a smooth pure-feasibility merit function is not a feasibility certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Squared-Violation Merit
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared equality and positive-inequality residual is a continuously differentiable pure-feasibility merit function with an explicit residual-Jacobian gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For continuously differentiable \(c\) and \(g\), define \[V_2(x)=\frac12\|c(x)\|_2^2+\frac12\|[g(x)]_+\|_2^2.\] Then \(V_2\) is continuously differentiable, \[\nabla V_2(x)=J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}c(x)+J_g(x)^{\mathsf T}[g(x)]_+,\] and \(V_2(x)=0\) if and only if \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V_2\in C^1,\qquad \nabla V_2=J_c^{\mathsf T}c+J_g^{\mathsf T}[g]_+,\qquad V_2=0\iff c=0,\ g\leq0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical differentiable objective-free alternative to the ell-one feasibility measure.

knowledge_statements.title: Pure Feasibility Merit Functions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pure feasibility merit function is nonnegative, vanishes exactly at feasible points, and measures only equality residuals and positive inequality violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For constraints \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), a pure feasibility merit function is any scalar \(V:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\) satisfying
\[V(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c(x)=0\ \text{and}\ g(x)\leq0.\]
A standard choice is
\[V_1(x)=\lVert c(x)\rVert_1+\lVert [g(x)]_+\rVert_1,\]
where \([g(x)]_{+,i}=\max\{g_i(x),0\}\). During a feasibility-dominated phase, a trial point is judged using reduction in \(V\), independently of objective reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_1(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) satisfies every equality and inequality constraint.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-free scalar violation measure for equality and inequality constraints.

notation.meaning: componentwise positive part of the inequality residual

children.title: Merit Descent-Parameter Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coordination of search directions, scalar models, and feasibility weights.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_\mu(x)=f(x)+\mu V(x)\) be directionally differentiable, let \(p_k(\mu)\) be a step computed from a model that may itself contain \(\mu\), and let \(D\Phi_\mu(x;p)\) denote the one-sided directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional line-search or trust-region methods using scalar merit decrease. The parameter may affect only acceptance or both the direction and acceptance model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Merit descent–parameter coupling is the requirement that \((p_k,\mu_k)\) be selected jointly so that \[D\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k;p_k)<0,\] or, in a quantified model form, \[\Delta q_k(\mu_k,p_k)\geq\sigma\mu_k\Delta V_k(p_k)>0\qquad(\sigma\in(0,1)),\] where \(\Delta q_k\) is predicted merit reduction and \(\Delta V_k\) is predicted violation reduction. When \(p_k=p_k(\mu_k)\), changing \(\mu_k\) changes both the scalarization and the step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merit descent–parameter coupling means choosing the search direction and feasibility weight as a compatible pair. The chosen weight must make the computed direction a descent direction, or must make predicted merit decrease dominate a fixed fraction of weighted feasibility improvement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(p_k,\mu_k)\text{ is compatible when }D\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k;p_k)<0\text{ or the declared quantified model-decrease condition holds}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(D\Phi_\mu(x_k;p_k)=a_k+\mu b_k\) with \(b_k<0\), compatibility is equivalent to \(\mu>-a_k/b_k\).
special_cases_latex: In standard SQP, the direction may be computed independently and \(\mu_k\) then enlarged until it is a merit descent direction.
In \(\ell_1\)-penalty QP methods, \(p_k\) depends on \(\mu_k\), requiring repeated step computations during parameter selection.
immediate_consequences_latex: A penalty parameter adequate for exactness near a solution need not automatically be adequate for descent far from the solution.
Excessively increasing \(\mu_k\) can overemphasize feasibility even when a smaller descent-compatible value exists.
boundary_notes: Descent compatibility is a local directional condition, not an acceptance condition for a finite step.
The strict inequality may be replaced by a safeguarded nonpositive bound in degenerate cases, but that variant is not included here.

notation.meaning: one-sided directional derivative of the merit function

children.title: Descent-Compatible Merit Parameters
children.top_down_role: Penalty choices making computed directions compatible with scalar decrease.

knowledge_statements.title: Descent-Compatible Merit Parameters
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit parameter is compatible when it makes the computed direction a strict merit-descent direction, preferably with a uniform predicted-decrease margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi_\rho\) be a scalar merit function, let \(x_k\) be the current iterate, and let \(d_k\neq0\) be a computed search direction. A parameter \(\rho_k>0\) is descent-compatible with \(d_k\) at \(x_k\) when the one-sided directional derivative satisfies
\[\Phi_{\rho_k}'(x_k;d_k)<0.\]
More quantitatively, given a predicted-decrease quantity \(\Delta_k>0\) and a constant \(\sigma\in(0,1]\), compatibility may be enforced by
\[\Phi_{\rho_k}'(x_k;d_k)\leq-\sigma\Delta_k.\]
This condition ensures that sufficiently small positive steps decrease the merit function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For a compatible \(\rho_k\), there exists \(\bar\alpha>0\) such that \(\Phi_{\rho_k}(x_k+\alpha d_k)<\Phi_{\rho_k}(x_k)\) whenever \(0<\alpha\leq\bar\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional-derivative condition coupling a computed step to its penalty parameter.

notation.meaning: one-sided directional derivative of the merit function

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Set of penalty weights compatible with a fixed direction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_\mu(x)=f(x)+\mu V(x)\) be directionally differentiable at \(x_k\), and let \(p_k\neq0\) be a computed direction. Assume its directional derivative is affine in \(\mu\): \(D\Phi_\mu(x_k;p_k)=a_k+\mu b_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional scalar merit globalization with a direction fixed while the parameter is tested. The common useful case has predicted feasibility decrease \(b_k<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The descent-compatible merit-parameter set for \((x_k,p_k)\) is \[\mathcal M_k^{\rm desc}=\{\mu>0:D\Phi_\mu(x_k;p_k)<0\}.\] If \(D\Phi_\mu(x_k;p_k)=a_k+\mu b_k\) and \(b_k<0\), then \[\mathcal M_k^{\rm desc}=\{\mu>0:\mu>a_k/(-b_k)\},\] with the threshold interpreted as zero when \(a_k\leq0\). A safeguarded choice uses \(D\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k;p_k)\leq-\rho\mu_k\delta_k\) for prescribed \(\rho\in(0,1)\) and predicted feasibility reduction \(\delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit parameter is descent-compatible with a given direction when that direction has a negative directional derivative for the resulting merit function. When the derivative is affine in the weight and the direction improves feasibility, the compatible weights form an interval above an explicit threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mu_k\in\mathcal M_k^{\rm desc}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad D\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k;p_k)<0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under the affine derivative formula with \(b_k<0\), compatibility is the scalar threshold inequality \(\mu_k>a_k/(-b_k)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(a_k<0\) and \(b_k\leq0\), every positive \(\mu\) is descent-compatible.
If \(b_k=0\), changing the feasibility weight cannot repair a non-descent direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: The compatible set can be empty when the direction does not improve the feasibility component and increases the objective component.
A margin condition places the selected parameter in the interior of the descent-compatible set.
boundary_notes: When the step depends on \(\mu\), this fixed-direction threshold must be recomputed with the resulting step and is no longer a one-shot formula.
Descent compatibility does not guarantee that a full step satisfies sufficient decrease.

notation.meaning: set of positive merit weights making p_k a descent direction

children.title: Adaptive Merit-Parameter Updates
children.top_down_role: Progress-sensitive adjustment of feasibility weighting.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Threshold Multiplicative Merit Update
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the merit parameter geometrically until compatibility holds. A persistent finite threshold guarantees termination and gives a logarithmic trial bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\rho_k>0\), \(\gamma>1\), and a test \(T_k(\rho)\), set \(\rho_{k,0}=\rho_k\) and \(\rho_{k,j}=\gamma^j\rho_k\). Return the first \(\rho_{k,j}\) satisfying \(T_k\). If there is a finite \(\bar\rho_k\) such that \(T_k(\rho)\) holds for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho_k\), then the update terminates after at most \[j_k=\max\!\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{\log(\bar\rho_k/\rho_k)}{\log\gamma}\right\rceil\right\}\] increases and returns a value no larger than \(\max\{\rho_k,\gamma\bar\rho_k\}\).
assumptions_latex: There exists \(\bar\rho_k<\infty\) for which \(T_k(\rho)\) holds for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update terminates in at most \(j_k\) increases at a parameter satisfying \(T_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reactive geometric increase until the current direction satisfies a persistent compatibility test.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated Success Does Not Ensure Geometric-Update Termination
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Existence of one successful parameter is insufficient: a geometric search can miss an isolated successful value forever.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_0=1\), \(\gamma=2\), and define \(T(\rho)\) to hold exactly when \(\rho=3\). Although \(T\) holds at a finite parameter above \(\rho_0\), the geometric samples are \(2^j\), so none satisfies \(T\) and the update does not terminate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(2^j)\) is false for every integer \(j\geq0\), despite \(T(3)\) being true.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a geometric parameter search when compatibility is not persistent above a threshold.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Progress-sensitive update of a merit feasibility weight
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q_\mu(p)=m_k^f(p)+\mu m_k^V(p)\) be a local merit model, let \(p(\mu)\) solve its step subproblem over \(\mathcal P_k\), and let \(p_k^F\) minimize the violation model \(m_k^V\) over the same set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional merit or exact-penalty methods in which the feasibility weight is selected from current model progress. The displayed rule is monotone nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive merit-parameter update selects \(\mu_k\geq\mu_{k-1}>0\) from current model data. A canonical progress-sensitive rule retains \(\mu_{k-1}\) if \(m_k^V(p(\mu_{k-1}))=0\); otherwise it increases trial values until \[m_k^V(0)-m_k^V(p(\mu_k))\geq\epsilon_1\bigl(m_k^V(0)-m_k^V(p_k^F)\bigr)\] and \[q_{\mu_k}(0)-q_{\mu_k}(p(\mu_k))\geq\epsilon_2\mu_k\bigl(m_k^V(0)-m_k^V(p(\mu_k))\bigr),\] where \(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive merit-parameter update uses the current step model to decide whether the previous feasibility weight is adequate. If not, it increases the weight until the resulting step achieves a fixed fraction of the best available feasibility reduction and sufficient total model reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mu_k\geq\mu_{k-1}\text{ is selected from current progress tests, with retention permitted when the existing weight is adequate}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update may be implemented by geometric trials \(\mu\leftarrow\gamma\mu\) with \(\gamma>1\) and repeated subproblem solves until both tests hold.
special_cases_latex: If the current step attains zero linearized violation, set \(\mu_k=\mu_{k-1}\).
If even the pure feasibility step has positive residual, require a prescribed fraction of its optimal reduction rather than zero residual.
immediate_consequences_latex: The rule avoids increasing the feasibility weight solely because it is below a predetermined schedule.
Repeated step solves used to locate \(\mu_k\) contribute to inner computational work.
boundary_notes: This update is distinct from stabilization, which concerns eventual constancy of \(\mu_k\).
A convention placing the objective weight, rather than feasibility weight, in the parameter reverses the direction of monotonic updates.

notation.meaning: step produced using merit weight mu

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Merit-Parameter Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone penalty increase until the current direction satisfies a descent test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), a direction \(d_k\), a current parameter \(\rho_k>0\), an increase factor \(\gamma>1\), and a descent test \(T_k(\rho)\), initialize \(j=0\) and set \(\widehat\rho=\rho_k\). While \(T_k(\widehat\rho)\) is false, update
\[\widehat\rho\leftarrow\gamma\widehat\rho,\qquad j\leftarrow j+1.\]
For example, use \(T_k(\rho)\equiv\Phi_\rho'(x_k;d_k)\leq-\sigma\Delta_k\), where \(\sigma\in(0,1]\) and \(\Delta_k>0\). Set \(\rho_{k+1}=\widehat\rho\), perform the merit acceptance test with this value, and terminate the update when the test first holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the feasibility weight geometrically until the current direction passes a prescribed merit-descent test, then use that weight for acceptance.
assumptions_latex: The test \(T_k(\rho)\) holds for some finite \(\rho\geq\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update returns a finite \(\rho_{k+1}\geq\rho_k\) satisfying \(T_k(\rho_{k+1})\).

children.title: Merit-Parameter Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Near-solution regimes in which merit parameters cease to obstruct local behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Parameter Stabilization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit parameter stabilizes when it becomes finite and constant after some iteration. This removes parameter variation but does not alone prove fast local convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A merit-parameter sequence \(\{\rho_k\}\) stabilizes if there exist \(K<\infty\) and \(\rho_*\in(0,\infty)\) such that \(\rho_k=\rho_*\) for every \(k\geq K\). Stabilization fixes the scalar merit model used by later iterations; by itself it does not guarantee full-step acceptance or a local convergence rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K<\infty,\rho_*>0:\ \rho_k=\rho_*\ \forall k\geq K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual finite constancy of the merit parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Compatibility Thresholds Prevent Finite Stabilization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every finite parameter eventually becomes incompatible, an update that repairs each failure cannot stabilize finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a retain-on-success, increase-on-failure update, suppose that for every finite \(R>0\) and every index \(K\), some \(k\geq K\) has \(T_k(R)\) false. Then no sequence that stabilizes at a finite value \(\rho_*\) can pass all sufficiently late tests. If the algorithm continues to repair every such failure by increasing the parameter, finite stabilization is impossible.
assumptions_latex: The parameter is retained after success and increased after each failed test.
Every finite candidate parameter fails at arbitrarily late iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite eventually constant parameter can satisfy all sufficiently late compatibility tests.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonstabilization when every retained finite parameter eventually fails.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Under a Uniform Persistent Threshold
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone multiplicative parameter update becomes constant when all later compatibility tests share one finite persistent threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\rho_k>0\) is changed only by multiplication by a fixed \(\gamma>1\) after a failed test \(T_k(\rho_k)\), and otherwise is retained. If there are \(K_0<\infty\) and \(\bar\rho<\infty\) such that \(T_k(\rho)\) holds for every \(k\geq K_0\) and every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\), then \(\{\rho_k\}\) stabilizes. After \(K_0\), at most \[\max\!\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{\log(\bar\rho/\rho_{K_0})}{\log\gamma}\right\rceil\right\}\] further increases can occur.
assumptions_latex: Updates retain \(\rho_k\) after success and replace it by \(\gamma\rho_k\) after failure, with \(\gamma>1\).
A common finite threshold passes every test from iteration \(K_0\) onward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(K<\infty\) and \(\rho_*<\infty\) such that \(\rho_k=\rho_*\) for all \(k\geq K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual constancy for monotone multiplicative updates with a uniform compatibility threshold.

notation.meaning: first iteration from which the uniform threshold applies

children.title: Merit Acceptance Globalization
children.top_down_role: Line-search and restricted-step acceptance families based on scalar merit reduction.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trial-step acceptance by scalar merit reduction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_{\mu_k}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be directionally differentiable, let \(p_k\) satisfy \(D\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k;p_k)<0\), and let \(x_k^+=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional line-search and restricted-step methods. Acceptance is governed by a single scalar merit function, unlike filter or funnel acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A merit-acceptance globalization rule accepts a line-search step when, for fixed \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), \[\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\leq\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_kD\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k;p_k).\] A restricted-step counterpart defines predicted reduction \(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\), actual reduction \(\operatorname{ared}_k=\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k)-\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k+p_k)\), and accepts when \[\rho_k=\operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k\geq\eta\] for a prescribed \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merit acceptance globalization accepts a trial point only when its scalar merit reduction is sufficient relative to a directional or model prediction. In a line search this is an Armijo-type inequality; in a restricted-step method it is a threshold on the ratio of actual to predicted merit decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_k^+\text{ is accepted exactly when the selected scalar merit sufficient-decrease test is satisfied}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Backtracking chooses the first element of \(\{1,\beta,\beta^2,\ldots\}\), with \(\beta\in(0,1)\), satisfying the line-search inequality.
special_cases_latex: For the \(\ell_1\) merit function, \(D\Phi\) is a one-sided directional derivative because the function is nonsmooth.
A second-order correction may be tested before backtracking when the full SQP step fails the merit condition.
immediate_consequences_latex: The acceptance test simultaneously compares objective and feasibility through the scalarization.
Descent of \(p_k\) is a direction-quality condition; sufficient decrease determines whether a particular finite step length is accepted.
boundary_notes: Nonmonotone watchdog variants permit temporary merit increases and require a modified reference value.
Filter acceptance cannot generally be rewritten as this single scalar test with a fixed parameter.

children.title: Monotone Merit Line Searches
children.top_down_role: Acceptance based on consistent scalar merit decrease.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Related Merit Backtracking Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly gradient-related directions and fixed-parameter Armijo backtracking yield gradient convergence and the standard inverse-square first-order iteration bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi\in C^1\) be bounded below by \(\Phi_{\inf}\) on the generated level set, and assume its gradient is \(L\)-Lipschitz on an open set containing all tested line segments. Let \(d_k=-B_k
abla\Phi(x_k)\), where \(mI\preceq B_k\preceq MI\), and apply Armijo backtracking with fixed \(\alpha_0>0\), \( eta,\eta\in(0,1)\). Define \[\underline\alpha=\min\left\{\alpha_0, rac{2 eta(1-\eta)m}{LM^2}ight\}.\] Then \(\alpha_k\geq\underline\alpha\), \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert
abla\Phi(x_k)Vert^2\leq rac{\Phi(x_0)-\Phi_{\inf}}{\eta m\underline\alpha},\] and for every \(N\geq1\), \[\min_{0\leq k<N}\lVert
abla\Phi(x_k)Vert\leq\sqrt{ rac{\Phi(x_0)-\Phi_{\inf}}{\eta m\underline\alpha N}}.\] Hence \(
abla\Phi(x_k)	o0\), and an \(\varepsilon\)-stationary iterate is obtained within \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) accepted iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is bounded below on the generated level set.
\(\nabla\Phi\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on a neighborhood containing every tested line segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla\Phi(x_k)\to0,\qquad \min_{0\leq k<N}\lVert\nabla\Phi(x_k)\rVert=O(N^{-1/2}).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity convergence and worst-case first-order bound for smooth fixed-merit Armijo backtracking.

notation.meaning: uniform lower bound on accepted step lengths

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Merit Decrease without Stationarity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict merit decrease can converge to a nonstationary point when the accepted decreases are summable and no quantitative descent safeguard is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi(x)=x\), \(x_0=0\), and \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\frac{1}{(k+1)^2}.\] Then \(\Phi(x_{k+1})<\Phi(x_k)\) for every \(k\), and \(x_k\to-\pi^2/6\), but \(\nabla\Phi(x_k)=1\) for all \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi(x_{k+1})<\Phi(x_k),\quad x_k\to-\pi^2/6,\quad\nabla\Phi(x_k)=1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of stationarity when monotonicity is used without quantitative descent safeguards.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination of Merit Backtracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Armijo backtracking accepts after finitely many contractions under the usual first-order directional expansion and strict descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\Phi(x+\alpha d)=\Phi(x)+\alpha\Phi'(x;d)+o(\alpha)\) as \(\alpha\downarrow0\), with \(\Phi'(x;d)<0\). For every \(\eta,\beta\in(0,1)\) and \(\alpha_0>0\), some finite \(j\geq0\) satisfies \[\Phi(x+\beta^j\alpha_0d)\leq\Phi(x)+\eta\beta^j\alpha_0\Phi'(x;d).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists j<\infty:\ \Phi(x+\beta^j\alpha_0d)\leq\Phi(x)+\eta\beta^j\alpha_0\Phi'(x;d).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-definedness of Armijo backtracking along a strict merit-descent direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Merit Line Searches
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack along a merit-descent direction until the Armijo inequality holds; every accepted nonzero step strictly lowers the same merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), a merit function \(\Phi\), a direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(\Phi'(x_k;d_k)<0\), an initial step \(\alpha_0>0\), a contraction \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\), choose the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) for which
\[\Phi(x_k+\beta^{j_k}\alpha_0d_k)\leq\Phi(x_k)+\eta\beta^{j_k}\alpha_0\Phi'(x_k;d_k).\]
Set \(\alpha_k=\beta^{j_k}\alpha_0\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Stop when the prescribed stationarity or feasibility tolerance is met; otherwise repeat. Every accepted nonzero step strictly decreases \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted iterate satisfies \(\Phi(x_{k+1})<\Phi(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking applied to a fixed scalar merit function.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi(\cdot;\mu):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be a scalar merit function for a nonlinear program, let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(p_k\) have finite directional derivative \(D\phi(x_k;\mu)[p_k]<0\). Fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\) and a backtracking factor \(\tau\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic line-search globalization, allowing a nonsmooth merit function with a directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A monotone merit line search chooses an integer \(j_k\geq0\), sets \(\alpha_k=\tau^{j_k}\), and accepts \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) only when \[\phi(x_k+\alpha_kp_k;\mu)\leq \phi(x_k;\mu)+\eta\alpha_kD\phi(x_k;\mu)[p_k].\] The accepted sequence is therefore monotone in the fixed merit function: because \(D\phi(x_k;\mu)[p_k]<0\), every nonzero accepted step satisfies \(\phi(x_{k+1};\mu)<\phi(x_k;\mu)\). Backtracking selects the first tested step length satisfying this inequality, typically from \(1,\tau,\tau^2,\ldots\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone merit line search fixes a scalar merit function and accepts a trial point only if its realized merit value is no greater than the current value plus a prescribed fraction of the negative first-order predicted change. Thus every accepted nonzero step strictly lowers the same merit function; rejected trial lengths are shortened until the condition holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k=\tau^{j_k}\) is accepted exactly when \(\phi(x_k+\alpha_kp_k;\mu)\leq\phi(x_k;\mu)+\eta\alpha_kD\phi(x_k;\mu)[p_k]\), implying \(\phi(x_{k+1};\mu)<\phi(x_k;\mu)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With predicted decrease \(\operatorname{pred}_k(\alpha)=-\alpha D\phi(x_k;\mu)[p_k]>0\), acceptance is equivalent to \(\phi(x_k;\mu)-\phi(x_k+\alpha p_k;\mu)\geq\eta\operatorname{pred}_k(\alpha)\).
special_cases_latex: For a differentiable merit function, \(D\phi(x_k;\mu)[p_k]=\nabla_x\phi(x_k;\mu)^Tp_k\), giving the usual Armijo condition.
immediate_consequences_latex: The merit values at accepted iterates form a strictly decreasing sequence unless the step is zero.
The definition uses one fixed scalar ordering and is distinct from filter acceptance, which retains objective and infeasibility separately.
boundary_notes: Changing \(\mu\) between the two sides of the acceptance test does not constitute decrease in one fixed merit function.
Nonmonotone reference values and watchdog steps belong to the relaxed merit-acceptance family.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be a merit function and let \(x_r\) be a reference iterate at which an ordinary sufficient-decrease test is available. Fix a finite relaxation horizon \(T\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic nonmonotone merit globalization with finite-duration relaxation and a mandatory recovery test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relaxed merit-acceptance mechanism is a rule that may accept one or more trial iterates without requiring \(\phi(x_{k+1})\leq\phi(x_k)\), but associates every relaxed episode with a reference point \(x_r\) and a finite horizon \(T\). Within at most \(T\) subsequent accepted trial steps, the mechanism must either obtain a point \(x_s\) satisfying a prescribed sufficient-decrease condition relative to \(x_r\), such as \[\phi(x_s)\leq\phi(x_r)+\eta D\phi(x_r)[x_s-x_r],\] when the displayed directional model is the chosen reference model, or discard the relaxed episode, return to \(x_r\), and perform an ordinary merit-decreasing globalization step. The penalty parameter is held fixed during a completed comparison cycle when the merit function depends on such a parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relaxed family permits temporary increases in a scalar merit function, but only inside a controlled episode. Each episode has a stored reference iterate and a finite deadline. By that deadline the algorithm must certify sufficient decrease relative to the stored reference or roll back and take a normal merit-decreasing step. Hence relaxation does not mean unrestricted acceptance of merit increases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Temporary merit increases are admissible only subject to finite-horizon recovery: within \(T\) steps sufficient decrease relative to \(x_r\) is obtained, or the method returns to \(x_r\) and forces an ordinary decrease.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A watchdog rule is the case in which a stored checkpoint controls a bounded sequence of relaxed steps and unsuccessful cycles are erased by returning to that checkpoint.
special_cases_latex: The one-step watchdog strategy uses \(T=1\): one merit-increasing step may be followed by a required successful comparison.
immediate_consequences_latex: The merit sequence need not be monotone at every accepted iterate.
Successful reference-cycle endpoints still provide a subsequence governed by sufficient merit reduction.
boundary_notes: A rule allowing indefinite merit increases without recovery or rollback is not a controlled relaxed merit-acceptance mechanism.
This definition does not prescribe how directions are generated or establish convergence.

notation.meaning: successful endpoint of a relaxed episode

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination of Nonmonotone Armijo Backtracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A descent direction guarantees finite nonmonotone Armijo backtracking whenever the finite reference is at least the current merit value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \Phi(x+\alpha d)=\Phi(x)+\alpha\Phi'(x;d)+o(\alpha) as \alpha\downarrow0, with \Phi'(x;d)<0. If R\geq\Phi(x) and \eta\in(0,1), then there exists \bar\alpha>0 such that every 0<\alpha\leq\bar\alpha satisfies \Phi(x+\alpha d)\leq R+\eta\alpha\Phi'(x;d). Consequently, geometric backtracking \alpha_j=\alpha_0\beta^j with \beta\in(0,1) terminates after finitely many reductions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists j<\infty:\ \Phi(x+\alpha_0\beta^jd)\leq R+\eta\alpha_0\beta^j\Phi'(x;d).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of an acceptable step for any finite reference not below the current merit value.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Merit Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory Armijo acceptance permitting controlled temporary merit increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a memory length \(M\geq1\). At iteration \(k\), define
\[R_k=\max_{\max\{0,k-M+1\}\leq i\leq k}\Phi(x_i).\]
Given a direction \(d_k\) with \(\Phi'(x_k;d_k)<0\), choose by backtracking an \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfying
\[\Phi(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq R_k+\eta\alpha_k\Phi'(x_k;d_k),\qquad \eta\in(0,1).\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). The new merit value may exceed \(\Phi(x_k)\), but it must decrease sufficiently relative to the finite-memory reference \(R_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a step against the largest recent merit value rather than only the current value, allowing bounded temporary increases while retaining sufficient decrease.
assumptions_latex: Backtracking is performed over positive trial step lengths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted point satisfies \(\Phi(x_{k+1})\leq R_k+\eta\alpha_k\Phi'(x_k;d_k)<R_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-memory maximum reference and nonmonotone Armijo inequality form a coherent algorithm and fit the terminal container, but no source is supplied. An authoritative locator is required to confirm the precise memory convention and acceptance variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Unlimited Unchecked Trials Provide No Merit Safeguard
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A watchdog with unlimited unchecked trials and no forced checkpoint test can admit a sequence whose merit diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \Phi(x)=x on \mathbb R and an underlying trial mechanism x_{k+1}=x_k+1. A purported watchdog rule that permits indefinitely many unchecked trials and never forces checkpoint progress or rollback admits this entire sequence, for which \Phi(x_k)=\Phi(x_0)+k\to+\infty. Thus such a rule alone provides no merit bound or convergence safeguard.
assumptions_latex: No finite bound is imposed on consecutive unchecked trials.
No checkpoint progress test or rollback is eventually forced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi(x_k)\to+\infty\quad\text{is compatible with the purported safeguard}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when neither a finite recovery horizon nor an eventual checkpoint test is imposed.

knowledge_statements.title: Checkpoint-Decrease Budget
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successful checkpoint decreases consume a finite merit budget, so a fixed positive decrease cannot occur indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let successful watchdog checkpoints satisfy \Phi(z_{j+1})\leq\Phi(z_j)-\delta_j with \delta_j>0. If \Phi(z_j)\geq\Phi_{\inf}>-\infty, then for every J, \sum_{j=0}^{J-1}\delta_j\leq\Phi(z_0)-\Phi_{\inf}. Hence \sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\delta_j<\infty. If \delta_j\geq\underline\delta>0, the number J of successful checkpoint transitions satisfies J\leq(\Phi(z_0)-\Phi_{\inf})/\underline\delta.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j=0}^{J-1}\delta_j\leq\Phi(z_0)-\Phi_{\inf}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Telescoping restriction on successful watchdog cycles.

knowledge_statements.title: Watchdog Merit Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trial steps without merit tests, followed by checkpoint recovery if progress fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a checkpoint \(z_j\), its merit value \(\Phi(z_j)\), and an integer horizon \(W\geq1\). Permit at most \(W\) consecutive trial iterates generated without imposing monotone merit decrease. If, before the horizon expires, an iterate \(x_k\) satisfies a prescribed checkpoint decrease test such as
\[\Phi(x_k)\leq\Phi(z_j)-\delta_j,\qquad \delta_j>0,\]
accept the trial sequence and set \(z_{j+1}=x_k\). Otherwise return to \(z_j\), compute a safeguarded merit-descent direction, and apply a monotone line search. Output the last accepted checkpoint or a point meeting the stopping tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allow a bounded sequence of unchecked trial steps; accept it after checkpoint progress, or roll back and recover with a monotone merit line search.
assumptions_latex: A safeguarded descent step can be computed at a restored checkpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each watchdog cycle either establishes \(\Phi(z_{j+1})\leq\Phi(z_j)-\delta_j\) or restores \(z_j\) and invokes monotone safeguarded acceptance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm captures the broad watchdog idea, but watchdog methods differ materially in checkpoint creation, trial acceptance, rollback, and recovery rules. With no source, the generic δ_j checkpoint test and claimed cycle outcome cannot be tied to a recognized variant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbounded Unchecked Horizons Nullify the Safeguard
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of a finite recovery horizon or an equivalent forced checkpoint test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a purported watchdog permits an unlimited sequence of trial iterates without a merit test and imposes neither a finite recovery horizon nor a forced checkpoint condition, then every sequence generated by the underlying trial mechanism is admissible, including sequences with \Phi(x_k)\to+\infty. Therefore merit boundedness or convergence cannot follow from such a watchdog rule alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a finite horizon or forced checkpoint recovery, the watchdog places no effective restriction on merit deterioration.
assumptions_latex: No finite bound is imposed on consecutive unchecked trials.
No checkpoint progress or rollback condition is eventually forced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{unlimited unchecked trials}\not\Rightarrow\text{merit control or convergence}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Unchecked Horizons Nullify the Safeguard
Uncontrolled Merit References Can Defeat Descent-Based Acceptance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unrestricted growing reference can accept a merit-divergent sequence even when every trial direction is locally descending.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi(x)=x-\sin(2\pi x)\), \(x_k=k\), \(d_k=1\), and \(\alpha_k=1\). Then \(\Phi(x_k)=k\to+\infty\), while \(\Phi'(x_k;d_k)=1-2\pi<0\). For any \(\eta\in(0,1)\), choose \(R_k=k+1+\eta(2\pi-1)\). Then \[\Phi(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)=k+1=R_k+\eta\alpha_k\Phi'(x_k;d_k).\] Thus every relaxed sufficient-decrease test is satisfied although the merit values diverge.
assumptions_latex: \(R_k\) is not bounded by a safeguarded function of current or historical merit values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi'(x_k;d_k)<0,\quad \Phi(x_k)\to+\infty,\quad \Phi(x_{k+1})\leq R_k+\eta\alpha_k\Phi'(x_k;d_k)\ \forall k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of relaxed sufficient decrease when reference growth is unrestricted, even with descent directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Recursively Weighted Merit Reference
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized recursive average gives a history-weighted reference with uniformly bounded total weight; acceptance below the old reference preserves a nonincreasing reference above the newest merit value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q_0=1, C_0=\Phi(x_0), and 0\leq\theta_k\leq\bar\theta<1. After accepting x_{k+1}, define Q_{k+1}=\theta_kQ_k+1 and C_{k+1}=(\theta_kQ_kC_k+\Phi(x_{k+1}))/Q_{k+1}. Then C_{k+1} is a convex combination of C_k and \Phi(x_{k+1}) and 1\leq Q_k\leq(1-\bar\theta)^{-1}. If acceptance ensures \Phi(x_{k+1})\leq C_k, then \Phi(x_{k+1})\leq C_{k+1}\leq C_k, so C_{k+1} remains an admissible reference for the new iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 1\leq Q_k\leq\frac{1}{1-\bar\theta},\qquad \Phi(x_{k+1})\leq C_{k+1}\leq C_k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized history-weighted reference and its admissibility invariant.

knowledge_statements.title: Current-Value and Finite-Window Merit References
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The monotone benchmark is the current merit value; a finite-memory benchmark is the largest of the most recent merit values, with memory one recovering the current benchmark.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For merit values \(\Phi(x_i)\), the current-value reference is \(R_k^{\mathrm{cur}}=\Phi(x_k)\). For an integer \(M\geq1\), the finite-window maximum reference is \[R_k^{\max}=\max_{\max\{0,k-M+1\}\leq i\leq k}\Phi(x_i).\] Both satisfy \(R_k\geq\Phi(x_k)\), and \(M=1\) makes the finite-window reference equal to the current-value reference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_k^{\max}\geq\Phi(x_k),\qquad M=1\Longrightarrow R_k^{\max}=R_k^{\mathrm{cur}}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical current and recent-maximum references, excluding the consuming line-search algorithm.

knowledge_statements.title: Merit Reference-Value Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified reference sequence for monotone and finite-memory merit acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A reference-value merit line search accepts \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) when
\[\Phi(x_{k+1})\leq R_k+\eta\alpha_k\Phi'(x_k;d_k),\qquad \eta\in(0,1),\]
where \(R_k\geq\Phi(x_k)\). The monotone regime is represented by \(R_k=\Phi(x_k)\). A finite-memory nonmonotone regime is represented by
\[R_k=\max_{\max\{0,k-M+1\}\leq i\leq k}\Phi(x_i),\qquad M\geq1.\]
More general relaxed regimes remain safeguarded when their update rule bounds \(R_k\) by controlled recent merit information and forces reference reduction after finitely many accepted steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One acceptance inequality covers monotone and relaxed searches: the reference is either the current merit value or a controlled summary of recent values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Choosing \(R_k=\Phi(x_k)\) yields monotone acceptance, while a recent maximum yields finite-memory nonmonotone acceptance.

notation.meaning: merit reference value used in acceptance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly unifies the monotone and finite-memory maximum-reference cases. However, the final claim about more general relaxed regimes uses undefined notions such as controlled recent information and forced reference reduction, so a precise sourced update regime is needed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A non-windowed reference-value regime based on a normalized weighted history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q_0=1, C_0=\Phi(x_0), and choose 0\leq\theta_k\leq\bar\theta<1. After accepting x_{k+1}, define Q_{k+1}=\theta_kQ_k+1 and C_{k+1}=(\theta_kQ_kC_k+\Phi(x_{k+1}))/Q_{k+1}. Then C_{k+1} is a convex combination of C_k and \Phi(x_{k+1}), while 1\leq Q_k\leq(1-\bar\theta)^{-1}. Thus C_k provides a bounded-memory-in-weight reference without storing a finite window of merit values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized exponentially weighted recurrence supplies a relaxed merit reference while keeping the total historical weight uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_{k+1}=\frac{\theta_kQ_k}{Q_{k+1}}C_k+\frac{1}{Q_{k+1}}\Phi(x_{k+1}),\qquad 1\leq Q_k\leq\frac{1}{1-\bar\theta}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponentially Weighted Merit Reference

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uncontrolled Merit References Can Make Acceptance Vacuous
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of relaxed sufficient decrease when the reference is allowed to grow without a safeguarding update rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi(x)=x\), \(x_k=k\), \(d_k=1\), \(\alpha_k=1\), and choose \(R_k=k+2\). For any \(\eta\in(0,1)\), \[\Phi(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)=k+1\leq k+2+\eta=R_k+\eta\alpha_k\Phi'(x_k;d_k),\] although \(\Phi(x_k)=k\to+\infty\). Hence the reference-value inequality alone supplies no descent or boundedness safeguard when \(R_k\) is uncontrolled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If references may grow arbitrarily, every step of a merit-divergent sequence can satisfy the relaxed acceptance inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(R_k\) is not constrained by current or historical merit values.
The acceptance rule imposes no independent descent-direction requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi(x_k)\to+\infty\quad\text{while every displayed relaxed acceptance test holds}.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Merit References Can Make Acceptance Vacuous

children.title: Trust-Region Merit Acceptance
children.top_down_role: Merit-based comparison of predicted and realized restricted-step progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Merit Acceptance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a restricted step when actual merit reduction is a sufficient fraction of predicted reduction, and update the radius according to model agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), trust-region radius \(\Delta_k>0\), merit function \(\Phi\), and local model \(m_k\) with \(m_k(0)=\Phi(x_k)\), compute a step \(s_k\) satisfying \(\lVert s_k\rVert\leq\Delta_k\) and positive predicted reduction
\[\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0.\]
Define
\[r_k=\frac{\Phi(x_k)-\Phi(x_k+s_k)}{\operatorname{pred}_k}.\]
For a threshold \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\), accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) if \(r_k\geq\eta_1\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Shrink \(\Delta_k\) after poor agreement and permit enlargement after sufficiently good agreement and a boundary-reaching step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(r_k\geq\eta_1\), the trial point is accepted and satisfies \(\Phi(x_k+s_k)<\Phi(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance by the ratio of actual to model-predicted merit reduction.

notation.meaning: local model of the merit function

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iterate \(x_k\), let \(p_k\) satisfy \(\|p_k\|\leq\Delta_k\). Let \(\phi(\cdot;\mu_k)\) be the merit function and \(q_k\) its trust-region model, with predicted reduction \(\operatorname{pred}_k=q_k(0)-q_k(p_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic trust-region globalization using a scalar merit function and a positive model reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Trust-region merit acceptance compares realized and model-predicted progress through \[\operatorname{ared}_k=\phi(x_k;\mu_k)-\phi(x_k+p_k;\mu_k),\qquad \rho_k=\frac{\operatorname{ared}_k}{\operatorname{pred}_k}.\] For an acceptance threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\), the trial step is accepted when \(\rho_k\geq\eta\), equivalently when \[\phi(x_k+p_k;\mu_k)\leq\phi(x_k;\mu_k)-\eta\bigl(q_k(0)-q_k(p_k)\bigr).\] An accepted step sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\) and permits a nondecreasing trust-region radius; a rejected step leaves \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and contracts the radius before recomputing a restricted step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region merit rule accepts a restricted trial step when the actual decrease in the scalar merit function is at least a fixed fraction of the decrease predicted by its local model. The actual-to-predicted reduction ratio performs this comparison. Failed steps are rejected and trigger a smaller region; successful steps update the iterate and may preserve or enlarge the region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step is accepted exactly under the rule \(\rho_k=\operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k\geq\eta\), with \(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The ratio test \(\rho_k\geq\eta\) is equivalent to the sufficient-decrease inequality \(\phi(x_k+p_k;\mu_k)\leq\phi(x_k;\mu_k)-\eta(q_k(0)-q_k(p_k))\).
special_cases_latex: For equality-constrained SQP with \(\phi_2(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu\|c(x)\|_2\), equation (18.48) uses the corresponding model \(q_\mu\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accepted step has positive actual merit reduction when \(\eta>0\).
The radius update couples acceptance to the assessed reliability of the local model.
boundary_notes: The ratio is undefined when the predicted reduction is nonpositive; such a trial requires a separate safeguard or model-improvement rule.
Filter trust-region acceptance replaces the single scalar ratio by a two-measure acceptability test.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elastic relaxation by penalized violation variables
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\), with \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and penalty weight \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonlinear programming; the relaxation addresses inconsistent nonlinear constraints or inconsistent local linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An elastic relaxation mechanism augments the decision vector with nonnegative violation variables \(v,w,t\) and replaces the original constraints by \[c_i(x)=v_i-w_i\quad(i\in\mathcal E),\qquad c_i(x)\geq-t_i\quad(i\in\mathcal I),\qquad v,w,t\geq0,\] while adding \[\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}(v_i+w_i)+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}t_i\] to the objective. The auxiliary variables explicitly absorb inconsistency: for any fixed \(x\), feasible elastic variables can be selected. Zero elasticity recovers satisfaction of the original constraints, whereas positive elasticity records and penalizes residual violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elastic mechanism makes constraint violation explicit. Each equality receives nonnegative positive and negative violation variables, and each inequality receives a nonnegative relaxation variable. Their weighted sum is added to the objective. The enlarged formulation remains feasible with respect to the relaxed constraints even when the unrelaxed constraint model is inconsistent, and zero violation variables recover the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic feasible set is defined by \(c_i(x)=v_i-w_i\), \(c_i(x)\geq-t_i\), and \(v,w,t\geq0\), with total elasticity penalized by \(\mu(\mathbf1^Tv+\mathbf1^Tw+\mathbf1^Tt)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eliminating \(v,w,t\) yields the nonsmooth penalty \(f(x)+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x)]^-\), where \([z]^- = \max\{0,-z\}\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, the relaxation is \(c(x)=v-w\) with \(v,w\geq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For every \(x\), choosing \(v_i=[c_i(x)]^+\), \(w_i=[c_i(x)]^-\), and \(t_i=[c_i(x)]^-\) as applicable gives feasible relaxed constraints.
The violation variables provide a direct diagnostic of which modeled constraints remain unsatisfied.
boundary_notes: Elastic feasibility does not imply feasibility of the original nonlinear program.
A sufficiently large penalty may promote zero elasticity under suitable regularity, but that exactness assertion is not part of this definition.

notation.meaning: nonnegative positive and negative elasticity for equality i

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic Penalties as Multiplier Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The elastic penalty weight becomes an infinity-norm bound on equality multipliers and an upper bound on nonnegative inequality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For elastic constraints \(r(d)=v^+-v^-\), \(s(d)\leq t\), and penalty \(\rho\mathbf1^T(v^++v^-+t)\), finiteness of the Lagrangian infimum over \(v^+,v^-,t\geq0\) requires and is ensured by \[-\rho\mathbf1\leq y\leq\rho\mathbf1,\qquad0\leq z\leq\rho\mathbf1,\] under the convention that \(z\geq0\) multiplies \(s(d)-t\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lVert y\rVert_\infty\leq\rho,\qquad0\leq z\leq\rho\mathbf1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual interpretation of a common componentwise elastic penalty.

notation.meaning: equality and inequality multipliers associated with the elastic constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination of Elastic Variables
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing out the elastic variables produces the sum of absolute equality residuals and positive inequality residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(d\), let \(r(d)=h+J_hd\) and \(s(d)=g+J_gd\). Then \[\min_{v^+,v^-,t\geq0}\left\{\mathbf1^T(v^++v^-+t):r(d)=v^+-v^-,\ s(d)\leq t\right\}=\lVert r(d)\rVert_1+\mathbf1^T[s(d)]_+.\] A minimizing choice is \(v^+=[r(d)]_+\), \(v^-=[-r(d)]_+\), and \(t=[s(d)]_+\).
assumptions_latex: The elastic variables are nonnegative and have equal positive objective weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{v^+,v^-,t}\mathbf1^T(v^++v^-+t)=\lVert r(d)\rVert_1+\mathbf1^T[s(d)]_+.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between explicit componentwise elastic variables and an ell-one penalty on affine residuals.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit elastic representation of constraint violation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(r_i(x)\) denote an equality residual and \(s_j(x)\) an inequality function required to satisfy \(s_j(x)\geq0\). All primal and elastic variables are finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural definition of the relaxed constraint set, independent of a particular step-acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An elastic constraint model replaces each equality \(r_i(x)=0\) by \[r_i(x)=v_i-w_i,\qquad v_i\geq0,\quad w_i\geq0,\] and each inequality \(s_j(x)\geq0\) by \[s_j(x)\geq-t_j,\qquad t_j\geq0.\] Its elasticity measure is \(E(v,w,t)=\sum_i(v_i+w_i)+\sum_jt_j\). At any minimum with fixed \(x\) and a strictly increasing penalty in \(E\), complementary positive and negative equality elasticities are not simultaneously needed, so the minimal equality elasticity equals \(|r_i(x)|\), while the minimal inequality elasticity equals \([s_j(x)]^-\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elastic constraint model represents equality residuals as the difference of two nonnegative variables and permits each inequality to be violated by a nonnegative slack on its adverse side. The sum of these variables measures modeled violation. For a fixed primal point, minimizing this sum reproduces absolute equality violation and the negative part of each inequality function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic constraint set is \(\{(x,v,w,t):r_i(x)=v_i-w_i,\ s_j(x)\geq-t_j,\ v,w,t\geq0\}\), with violation measure \(E=\mathbf1^Tv+\mathbf1^Tw+\mathbf1^Tt\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For fixed \(x\), \(\min\{v_i+w_i:r_i(x)=v_i-w_i,\ v_i,w_i\geq0\}=|r_i(x)|\).
For fixed \(x\), \(\min\{t_j:s_j(x)\geq-t_j,\ t_j\geq0\}=[s_j(x)]^-\).
special_cases_latex: A linearized SQP constraint model uses \(r_i(x_k)+\nabla r_i(x_k)^Tp=v_i-w_i\) and \(s_j(x_k)+\nabla s_j(x_k)^Tp\geq-t_j\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The relaxed constraint set has a feasible elastic completion for every primal point or step.
The condition \(E=0\) is equivalent to satisfaction of all original modeled constraints.
boundary_notes: Ordinary surplus variables that merely convert an already satisfied inequality to equality are not elastic violation variables.
Bounds or trust regions imposed on the primal step remain separate constraints and may require their own consistency conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic Constraint Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relaxation of linearized constraints using nonnegative violation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At an iterate \(x_k\), introduce nonnegative elastic variables \(u,v\in\mathbb{R}^m_+\) for the linearized equalities and \(w\in\mathbb{R}^p_+\) for the linearized inequalities. The elastic model is
\[c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)d-u+v=0,\qquad g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)d-w\leq0,\]
with model objective
\[q_k(d)+\rho\bigl(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}u+\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}v+\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}w\bigr),\qquad \rho>0.\]
For every step \(d\), feasible elastic variables exist by choosing them componentwise to cover the signed equality residuals and positive inequality residuals. Zero elastic variables recover satisfaction of the unrelaxed linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative elastic variables absorb linearized constraint violations and are penalized in the subproblem objective; zero elasticity means the original linearized constraints hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic constraints are feasible for every \(d\), and \(u=v=w=0\) exactly recovers the unrelaxed linearized constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elastic formulation is internally coherent for the convention g(x)≤0: nonnegative w can absorb any positive linearized inequality residual, and zero elastic variables recover the unrelaxed constraints. Nevertheless, no source is supplied to establish this particular sign convention, objective penalty, and representation as the intended elastic-model variant.

children.title: Elastic-Mode Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Always-solvable local subproblems formed through elastic relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Elastic-Subproblem KKT Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, stationarity, bounded multipliers, and the displayed complementarity relations certify global optimality of a convex elastic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be convex and \(q\) convex and differentiable. For \[\min_{d\in D,v^+,v^-,t\geq0}q(d)+\rho\mathbf1^T(v^++v^-+t)\] subject to \(h+J_hd-v^++v^-=0\) and \(g+J_gd-t\leq0\), a primal-feasible point is globally optimal if there exist \(y\), \(z\geq0\), and \(n_D\in N_D(d)\) such that \[\nabla q(d)+J_h^Ty+J_g^Tz+n_D=0,\quad -\rho\mathbf1\leq y\leq\rho\mathbf1,\quad0\leq z\leq\rho\mathbf1,\] \[z^T(g+J_gd-t)=0,\quad (\rho\mathbf1-y)^Tv^+=0,\quad(\rho\mathbf1+y)^Tv^-=0,\quad(\rho\mathbf1-z)^Tt=0.\]
assumptions_latex: The displayed primal and dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (d,v^+,v^-,t)\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{q(d)+\rho\mathbf1^T(v^++v^-+t)\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient global-optimality certificate for a convex elastic local subproblem.

notation.meaning: normal cone of the convex step set at d

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(c_i(x_k)+a_i^Tp\) be linearized constraints. Fix \(\mu>0\) and \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional SQP-type local modeling with an infinity-norm trust region and explicit elastic variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An elastic-mode subproblem is the quadratic program \[\min_{p,v,w,t}\ f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}(v_i+w_i)+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}t_i\] subject to \[c_i(x_k)+a_i^Tp=v_i-w_i\ (i\in\mathcal E),\quad c_i(x_k)+a_i^Tp\geq-t_i\ (i\in\mathcal I),\] \[v,w,t\geq0,\qquad\|p\|_\infty\leq\Delta_k.\] It is called elastic mode because violations of the linearized constraints are optimized rather than making the subproblem infeasible. The point \(p=0\), completed with sufficiently large nonnegative elastic variables, is always feasible; the bounded trust region also makes the feasible set in \(p\) compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elastic-mode subproblem is a local quadratic objective over a trust-region step together with nonnegative variables that absorb violations of every linearized constraint. Their weighted sum enters the objective. Since the zero step can always be completed by suitable elastic variables, inconsistent linearizations do not destroy subproblem feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic QP is defined by the displayed objective and constraints, and its feasible set is nonempty because \(p=0\) admits an elastic completion.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eliminating the elastic variables gives a trust-region problem with the piecewise-linear term \(\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x_k)+a_i^Tp|+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x_k)+a_i^Tp]^-\).
special_cases_latex: With \(B_k=0\), the model becomes a trust-region sequential linear-penalty subproblem.
With no inequalities, only the equality elasticities \(v,w\) remain.
immediate_consequences_latex: Indefiniteness of \(B_k\) does not affect feasibility, although it affects subproblem solution methods.
At any solution with zero elastic variables, the step satisfies the original linearized constraints.
boundary_notes: Nonempty feasibility does not by itself guarantee a unique minimizer.
If no trust-region or other coercive restriction is imposed, an indefinite quadratic model may be unbounded below despite elastic feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Mode Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An equality-and-inequality elastic quadratic subproblem with nonnegative violation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an iterate \(x\), objective model \(q(d)\), equalities \(h(x)=0\), and inequalities \(g(x)\leq 0\), an elastic-mode subproblem is
\[
\min_{d,v^+,v^-,t}\ q(d)+\rho\bigl(\mathbf 1^T v^++\mathbf 1^T v^-+\mathbf 1^Tt\bigr)
\]
subject to
\[
h(x)+J_h(x)d=v^+-v^-,\qquad g(x)+J_g(x)d\leq t,\qquad v^+,v^-,t\geq0,
\]
where \(\rho>0\). If the admissible step set contains \(d=0\), the problem is feasible because one may take \(v^+=[h(x)]_+\), \(v^-=[-h(x)]_+\), and \(t=[g(x)]_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic variables absorb linearized constraint violations, making the local subproblem feasible whenever the zero step is admissible.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are differentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic subproblem has a feasible point for every iterate \(x\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative equality and inequality elastic variables
componentwise positive part of a vector

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard elastic SQP construction and direct feasible initialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the elastic-subproblem container, introduces the principal variables, and the displayed feasible initialization has the correct signs. The always-solvable claim is mathematically direct under the stated zero-step assumption, but no inspectable source is supplied for the selected elastic formulation.

children.title: Elasticity Outcome Regimes
children.top_down_role: Vanishing-elasticity and persistent-elasticity outcome families.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x_k,e_k)\) be solutions or accepted iterates of elastic formulations, where \(e_k=(v_k,w_k,t_k)\geq0\) and \(E_k=\mathbf1^Tv_k+\mathbf1^Tw_k+\mathbf1^Tt_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of asymptotic outcomes of elastic nonlinear-programming models; it is not a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The vanishing-elasticity regime is the outcome \[E_k\to0,\] and exact zero elasticity at an index means \(v_k=w_k=t_k=0\), so the corresponding primal point satisfies the unrelaxed modeled constraints. The persistent-elasticity regime is the outcome \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}E_k>0,\] or, for a single solved elastic problem, an optimizer with \(E_*>0\). Persistent elasticity records that the penalized model selects residual violation rather than complete modeled feasibility. When the original nonlinear problem is infeasible and the penalty is sufficiently large, the associated elastic formulation is used to seek a stationary point of its infeasibility measure rather than a feasible nonlinear-program solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic outcomes separate into two principal regimes. In the vanishing regime, the total violation variables tend to zero and the unrelaxed modeled constraints are recovered asymptotically. In the persistent regime, a positive amount of optimized violation remains. Persistence is a model outcome indicating residual infeasibility or a penalty tradeoff; by itself it does not prove that the original nonlinear problem is globally infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Vanishing elasticity means \(E_k\to0\); persistent elasticity means \(\liminf_kE_k>0\) or \(E_*>0\) for a solved elastic model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because every component of \(e_k\) is nonnegative and the dimension is fixed, \(E_k\to0\) is equivalent to \(e_k\to0\) componentwise.
Exact zero elasticity is equivalent to satisfaction of all constraints represented by the elastic model.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, \(E_k=\mathbf1^T(v_k+w_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A zero-elasticity local step satisfies the corresponding unrelaxed linearization.
Positive limiting elasticity identifies constraints whose modeled violation remains active through positive components of \(e_k\).
boundary_notes: Persistent elasticity may result from an inadequate penalty weight or a local stationary point and therefore is not, without additional assumptions, a certificate of global infeasibility.
Vanishing elasticity of linearized subproblems does not alone establish convergence of the nonlinear iterates.

source_refs.locator: Section 18.3, paragraph following equations (18.12a)–(18.12d), beginning “The quadratic subproblem”
