knowledge_statements.title: Strictness of the Elastic Exactness Threshold
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At equality with the multiplier threshold, a zero-elastic minimizer may coexist with arbitrarily close infeasible minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min -x\) subject to \(x=0\). The equality multiplier has magnitude \(1\), and eliminating the elastic variables gives \(\phi_\rho(x)=-x+\rho|x|\). At \(\rho=1\), every \(x\geq0\) near zero satisfies \(\phi_1(x)=0=\phi_1(0)\). Thus the feasible point remains a penalty minimizer, but infeasible penalty minimizers occur arbitrarily near it. Strict inequality in the multiplier threshold is therefore needed for local identification of the zero-elastic solution set.
assumptions_latex: The objective is \(-x\), the equality constraint is \(x=0\), and \(\rho=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi_1(x)=0\ \text{for all }x\geq0,\quad\text{although only }x=0\text{ is feasible}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary behavior when the elastic penalty equals a KKT multiplier magnitude.

notation.meaning: elastic penalty after eliminating violation variables

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Elasticity Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness of an \(\ell_1\)-penalized elastic reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d^*\) be a local solution of a feasible smooth local subproblem, with KKT multipliers \(y^*\) for equalities and \(z^*\geq0\) for inequalities. Form its elastic reformulation by adding the penalty \(\rho(\mathbf1^Tv^++\mathbf1^Tv^-+\mathbf1^Tt)\). Under a constraint qualification and second-order sufficiency at \(d^*\), if
\[
\rho>\max\{\|y^*\|_\infty,\|z^*\|_\infty\},
\]
then \((d^*,0,0,0)\) is a locally exact solution of the elastic problem. Conversely, any local elastic solution with all elastic variables zero is feasible for the unrelaxed subproblem and has the same objective value there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently large elastic penalty reproduces a regular local solution with zero elasticity; zero-elastic solutions are feasible for the original subproblem.
assumptions_latex: The unrelaxed local subproblem has a KKT point \(d^*\) satisfying a constraint qualification.
A second-order sufficient condition holds at \(d^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\rho>\max\{\|y^*\|_\infty,\|z^*\|_\infty\}\), the elastic reformulation is locally exact at \((d^*,0,0,0)\).

notation.meaning: KKT multipliers of the unrelaxed subproblem

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical local exact-penalty multiplier threshold

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits vanishing-elasticity exactness and states the conventional strict multiplier threshold, but the precise local exactness result depends on the exact elastic formulation, constraint qualification, multiplier convention, and second-order hypotheses. An authoritative theorem or section locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Local Elasticity without Nonlinear Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible nonlinear problem can have an irreparably inconsistent linearization with positive minimum elasticity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(c(x)=x^2-1=0\), whose feasible points are \(x=\pm1\). At \(x_0=0\), the affine model is \[c(x_0)+c'(x_0)d=-1=0,\] which is inconsistent for every \(d\). Its minimum equality elasticity is therefore \(1\) on every nonempty step set. Positive or persistent elasticity of this local model consequently does not certify infeasibility of the nonlinear equation.
assumptions_latex: \(c(x)=x^2-1\) and the affine model is formed at \(x_0=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_d|c(0)+c'(0)d|=1\quad\text{while}\quad\{x:c(x)=0\}=\{-1,1\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between incompatibility of a local linearization and feasibility of the original nonlinear constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Elasticity Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation of positive limiting elasticity in a convergent sequence of solved elastic local models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(k\), let \(D_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(a_k:D_k\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(b_k:D_k\to\mathbb R^p\) be the equality and inequality residual maps of a local model, and let \(\rho_k>0\). Suppose \((d_k,v_k^+,v_k^-,t_k)\) globally minimizes an objective of the form \(q_k(d)+\rho_k\mathbf1^T(v^++v^-+t)\) subject to \(d\in D_k\), \(a_k(d)=v^+-v^-\), \(b_k(d)\leq t\), and \(v^+,v^-,t\geq0\). Assume \(d_k\to d_*\), \(v_k^+\to v_*^+\), \(v_k^-\to v_*^-\), \(t_k\to t_*\), \(a_k(d_k)\to a_*(d_*)\), and \(b_k(d_k)\to b_*(d_*)\). If \(\mathbf1^T(v_*^++v_*^-+t_*)>0\), then \(a_*(d_*)\neq0\) or at least one component of \(b_*(d_*)\) is positive. Thus the limiting step is infeasible for the limiting unrelaxed local model. This conclusion alone does not certify infeasibility of the original nonlinear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For explicitly specified convergent elastic models, positive limiting elasticity implies that the limiting step violates the limiting unrelaxed local constraints, but it does not by itself prove that the nonlinear program is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: Each elastic subproblem has the displayed positive-weight componentwise \(\ell_1\) formulation and is solved globally.
The steps, elastic variables, and residual values converge as stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limit satisfies \(a_*(d_*)\neq0\) or \(b_*(d_*)\not\leq0\).

notation.meaning: equality-residual vector of local model k
inequality-residual vector of local model k
nonnegative elastic variables of local model k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive-weight optimal elastic variables equal the componentwise residual violations

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Farkas Certificate from Elastic Duality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded multipliers with zero combined Jacobian coefficient and positive residual pairing certify affine-model infeasibility through a positive elastic dual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h+J_hd=0\) and \(g+J_gd\leq0\) with unrestricted \(d\), suppose \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(z\in\mathbb R^p\) satisfy \[J_h^Ty+J_g^Tz=0,\qquad\lVert y\rVert_\infty\leq1,\qquad0\leq z\leq\mathbf1,\qquad h^Ty+g^Tz>0.\] Then the affine system is infeasible. Moreover, \(h^Ty+g^Tz\) is a positive lower bound on \[\min_d\left(\lVert h+J_hd\rVert_1+\mathbf1^T[g+J_gd]_+\right).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{d:h+J_hd=0,\ g+J_gd\leq0\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual lower-bound certificate for infeasibility of an unrestricted affine local model.

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic Infeasibility Indications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A positive certified lower bound on minimum elastic violation over a prescribed local step set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(h\in\mathbb R^m\), \(g\in\mathbb R^p\), \(J_h\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(J_g\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and define
\[
\theta_D=\min_{\substack{d\in D,\ v^+,v^-\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ t\in\mathbb R_+^p}}\left\{\mathbf1^Tv^++\mathbf1^Tv^-+\mathbf1^Tt:\ h+J_hd=v^+-v^-,\ g+J_gd\leq t\right\}.
\]
If a globally valid lower bound \(L\) satisfies \(0<L\leq\theta_D\), then no \(d\in D\) satisfies \(h+J_hd=0\) and \(g+J_gd\leq0\). Consequently, a verified global optimum or valid global dual lower bound with positive value certifies infeasibility of the unrelaxed affine local constraints over \(D\), but not necessarily infeasibility of the original nonlinear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive certified lower bound on the minimum elastic violation proves that the unrelaxed affine local constraints have no feasible step in the prescribed region.
assumptions_latex: The affine residual data have the displayed compatible dimensions.
\(L\) is a globally valid lower bound satisfying \(0<L\leq\theta_D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{d\in D:h+J_hd=0,\ g+J_gd\leq0\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: minimum total elastic violation over D
certified global lower bound on the minimum elastic violation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: zero minimum elastic violation is equivalent to feasibility of the affine local constraints

children.title: Merit Globalization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failure modes and correction interfaces for scalar globalization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu h(x)\), where \(h(x)\geq0\) measures constraint violation. Let \(p_k\) be a proposed step and \(m_k\) a local merit model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Taxonomic definition of points at which a scalar merit acceptance mechanism needs parameter correction, direction correction, nonmonotonicity, or a higher-order step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The scalar-merit globalization boundary at \((x_k,p_k,\mu_k)\) is reached when the proposed local step cannot be represented as acceptable progress by the current scalar mechanism, specifically when at least one of the following holds: \[D\phi(x_k;\mu_k)[p_k]\geq0,\qquad m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\leq0,\] the penalty weight lies outside a range that balances objective and feasibility progress, or a locally fast full step fails the merit sufficient-decrease test because nonlinear constraint violation is of higher order than its linear model predicts. The corresponding interfaces are, respectively, direction or model modification, penalty-weight adjustment, controlled nonmonotone acceptance, filter/restoration globalization, or a second-order correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit-globalization boundary is a state where the current scalar merit function and its model no longer support acceptance of the proposed algorithmic step. It includes a non-descent direction, nonpositive predicted merit reduction, a badly balanced feasibility weight, and near-solution rejection caused by nonlinear constraint curvature. Crossing the boundary requires changing an interface of the globalization mechanism rather than merely restating the same scalar test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The boundary set contains states satisfying \(D\phi(x_k;\mu_k)[p_k]\geq0\), \(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\leq0\), an unacceptable penalty tradeoff, or curvature-induced rejection of an otherwise fast local step.
special_cases_latex: The Maratos boundary is the curvature-induced rejection of a step that would otherwise yield superlinear or quadratic local progress.
A direction boundary occurs before line-search backtracking when the directional derivative is nonnegative.
immediate_consequences_latex: Ordinary Armijo backtracking has no standard small-step guarantee when the proposed direction is not a merit descent direction.
A boundary diagnosis identifies which globalization component must be reconsidered.
boundary_notes: This definition classifies failure interfaces; it does not assert that every boundary event causes algorithmic failure.
Filter and restoration methods are neighboring correction architectures, not scalar merit functions.

children.title: Feasibility-Weight Tradeoff Boundary
children.top_down_role: Opposing failures caused by excessive or inadequate feasibility weighting.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu h(x)\) with \(h\geq0\), and suppose a step-generation model is \(q_\mu(p)=q_f(p)+\mu q_h(p)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar penalty or merit globalization in which the same feasibility weight influences step generation or acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proposed step \(p\), write \(\Delta_f=q_f(0)-q_f(p)\) and \(\Delta_h=q_h(0)-q_h(p)\), so the predicted merit reduction is \(\Delta_\phi(\mu)=\Delta_f+\mu\Delta_h\). The feasibility-weight tradeoff boundary is the set of \(\mu>0\) at which \(\Delta_\phi(\mu)=0\), together with the two adjacent failure regimes: an underweighted regime in which the chosen \(\mu\) permits objective improvement to dominate inadequate or adverse feasibility progress, and an overweighted regime in which the feasibility term dominates useful objective curvature and produces excessively conservative progress. A usable weight must yield positive predicted merit reduction and satisfy the algorithm's multiplier- or model-based lower bound without being unnecessarily large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasibility-weight boundary describes the opposing failures of a scalar objective-plus-violation model. If the weight is too small, objective decrease can conceal inadequate feasibility progress or lead away from a constrained solution. If it is excessively large, the model overemphasizes violation reduction and can make progress slow. Algebraically, the transition for a fixed step occurs where predicted objective reduction plus the weighted predicted feasibility reduction is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed modeled reductions, the algebraic boundary is \(\{\mu>0:\Delta_f+\mu\Delta_h=0\}\); acceptable weights require \(\Delta_f+\mu\Delta_h>0\) and the method's penalty lower bound.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\Delta_h\neq0\), the fixed-step boundary weight is \(\mu_b=-\Delta_f/\Delta_h\) whenever \(\mu_b>0\).
special_cases_latex: For exact \(\ell_1\) penalties near a regular solution, the customary lower threshold is tied to the magnitudes of the optimal Lagrange multipliers.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing \(\mu\) can change both the computed step and its acceptance when the penalty is embedded in the subproblem.
There is no universal finite upper weight that is best for all iterates and models.
boundary_notes: The phrase “too large” is an efficiency boundary, not a claim that exactness fails for all large weights.
The fixed-step equation does not by itself define an update algorithm because \(p\) may depend on \(\mu\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Penalty Conditioning Under Excessive Weight
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When penalty curvature acts outside a nontrivial constraint null space, excessive quadratic-penalty weight makes the penalized Hessian increasingly ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be nonzero with \(\ker A\neq\{0\}\). For \(B_\rho=H+\rho A^\top A\) and any unit \(z\in\ker A\), set \(M=z^\top Hz\). Then \[\kappa_2(B_\rho)\geq\frac{\rho\sigma_{\max}(A)^2+\lambda_{\min}(H)}{M},\] so \(\kappa_2(B_\rho)\) diverges at least linearly as \(\rho\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(H+\rho A^\top A)\to\infty\) at least linearly as \(\rho\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning growth when quadratic feasibility curvature vanishes on a nontrivial null space.

notation.meaning: largest singular value of the constraint matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Excessive Penalty Dominance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As the penalty diverges, minimizers first minimize violation and use the objective only to break ties among minimum-violation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be compact and let \(f,v:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous with \(v\geq0\). For \(\rho>0\), choose
\[
x_\rho\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho v(x)\}.
\]
If \(\rho_k\to\infty\) and \(x_{\rho_k}\to\bar x\), then
\[
v(\bar x)=\min_{x\in X}v(x).
\]
Among minimum-violation points, accumulation points minimize \(f\). Hence an excessively large feasibility weight makes reduction of \(v\) the primary ordering criterion; objective improvement affects selection only after minimum violation has been attained and may be numerically obscured for finite precision.
assumptions_latex: Each \(x_\rho\) is a global minimizer of \(f+\rho v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accumulation point of \(x_\rho\) as \(\rho\to\infty\) minimizes \(v\) over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic domination of objective quality by a diverging feasibility weight.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Exact-Penalty Failure Below the Multiplier Threshold
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the exact-penalty threshold, infeasible positive displacements reduce the merit function and the feasible solution is not locally preferred.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}-x\quad\text{subject to}\quad x=0.\] The unique feasible solution is \(x^*=0\), and the equality-multiplier magnitude is \(1\). For \(\phi_\rho(x)=-x+\rho|x|\) and \(0\leq\rho<1\), every \(x>0\) satisfies \(\phi_\rho(x)=(\rho-1)x<\phi_\rho(0)\); moreover, \(\phi_\rho(x)\to-\infty\) as \(x\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible solution \(x^*=0\) is not a local minimizer of \(\phi_\rho\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directly checkable equality-constrained example of inadequate feasibility weighting.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Threshold for Insufficient Feasibility Weight
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weight below the directional objective-to-violation tradeoff leaves an infeasible merit-descent direction; zero first-order violation growth cannot be repaired by any finite weight at first order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi_\rho=f+\rho v\), where \(v(x^*)=0\), and suppose the one-sided directional derivatives exist. If \(f'(x^*;d)<0\) and \(v'(x^*;d)>0\), then every \[0\leq\rho<-\frac{f'(x^*;d)}{v'(x^*;d)}\] satisfies \(\phi_\rho'(x^*;d)<0\), so \(x^*\) is not a local minimizer of \(\phi_\rho\). If \(v'(x^*;d)=0\) while \(f'(x^*;d)<0\), no finite \(\rho\) removes this first-order descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\rho v'(x^*;d)<-f'(x^*;d)\), then \(\phi_\rho'(x^*;d)<0\) and \(x^*\) is not a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order criterion for an infeasible objective-improving direction to defeat a merit penalty.

notation.meaning: directional minimum penalty threshold when the denominator is positive

knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Feasibility Weight
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar exact-penalty example below the multiplier threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R}-x\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad x=0.
\]
Its unique feasible solution is \(x^*=0\), with equality-multiplier magnitude \(1\). The \(\ell_1\) merit function is
\[
\phi_\rho(x)=-x+\rho|x|.
\]
For \(0\leq\rho<1\) and every \(x>0\), \(\phi_\rho(x)=(\rho-1)x<\phi_\rho(0)\); indeed, \(\phi_\rho(x)\to-\infty\) as \(x\to\infty\). Thus the constrained solution is not even a local minimizer of the merit function when the feasibility weight is below the multiplier threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the exact-penalty threshold, an infeasible direction can decrease the merit function, so the constrained solution need not be locally preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible solution \(x^*=0\) is not a local minimizer of \(\phi_\rho\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar calculation is correct, the multiplier magnitude is one under the displayed convention, and counterexample is the appropriate knowledge kind for this leaf. No inspectable source locator is supplied, however.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Threshold for Insufficient Feasibility Weight
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional criterion showing when an objective-improving infeasible displacement defeats a penalty merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi_\rho=f+\rho v\), where \(v(x^*)=0\), and suppose the one-sided directional derivatives at \(x^*\) exist. If for some direction d,
\[f'(x^*;d)<0,\qquad v'(x^*;d)>0,\]
then every
\[0\leq\rho<-\frac{f'(x^*;d)}{v'(x^*;d)}\]
satisfies \(\phi_\rho'(x^*;d)<0\), so \(x^*\) is not a local minimizer of \(\phi_\rho\). If instead \(v'(x^*;d)=0\) while \(f'(x^*;d)<0\), no finite \(\rho\) can remove this first-order descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility weight below the directional objective-to-violation tradeoff leaves an infeasible merit-descent direction; if violation has zero first-order growth, no finite weight repairs it at first order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\rho v'(x^*;d)<-f'(x^*;d)\), then \(\phi_\rho'(x^*;d)<0\) and \(x^*\) is not a local minimizer of \(\phi_\rho\).

notation.meaning: directional minimum penalty threshold when the denominator is positive

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Threshold for Insufficient Feasibility Weight
Monotone Comparative Statics of Feasibility Weight
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing feasibility weight cannot increase violation at a global penalized minimizer; objective values move oppositely, and the optimal scalarized value is concave and nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\neq\varnothing\), \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and \(v:X\to[0,\infty)\). If \(x_i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho_i v(x)\}\) for \(0\leq\rho_1<\rho_2\), then \[v(x_2)\leq v(x_1),\qquad f(x_1)\leq f(x_2).\] Moreover, \(q(\rho)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho v(x)\}\) is nondecreasing and concave on every interval where it is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(x_2)\leq v(x_1)\), \(f(x_1)\leq f(x_2)\), and \(q\) is concave and nondecreasing where finite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General ordering of global minimizers of objective-plus-violation scalarizations.

notation.meaning: optimal scalarized value at weight rho

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Weight Transition Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many candidates, penalty minimizers change only at pairwise tradeoff breakpoints, and increasing weight favors candidates with lower violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\) and define \(F_i(\rho)=f(x_i)+\rho v(x_i)\) for \(\rho\geq0\), where \(v(x_i)\geq0\). The minimizing index set
\[
I(\rho)=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{1\leq i\leq N}F_i(\rho)
\]
is constant on every open interval avoiding the finitely many nonnegative breakpoints
\[
\rho_{ij}=\frac{f(x_j)-f(x_i)}{v(x_i)-v(x_j)}
\]
for pairs with distinct violations. At a breakpoint, objective advantage and feasibility advantage balance exactly. Increasing \(\rho\) can only replace a uniquely selected candidate by one having no larger violation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite nonempty candidate set.
\(f(x_i)\) is finite and \(v(x_i)\geq0\) for every candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selection map \(I(\rho)\) is piecewise constant, with transitions only at nonnegative pairwise breakpoints \(\rho_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric transitions among minimizers of a scalar penalty model.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Directional Mismatch Obstructs Small Armijo Steps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive merit directional derivative makes every sufficiently small step increase the merit function and defeats an Armijo test demanding positive predicted decrease; a zero derivative is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\phi'(x;d)>0\), then there exists \(\bar\alpha>0\) such that \(\phi(x+\alpha d)>\phi(x)\) for every \(0<\alpha\leq\bar\alpha\). Consequently, no such \(\alpha\) satisfies \(\phi(x+\alpha d)\leq\phi(x)-\sigma\alpha\Delta\) when \(\sigma>0\) and \(\Delta>0\). By contrast, \(\phi'(x;d)=0\) alone does not determine acceptance.
assumptions_latex: The one-sided directional derivative \(\phi'(x;d)\) exists and is strictly positive.
The decrease test uses \(\sigma>0\) and predicted decrease \(\Delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar\alpha>0\;\forall\alpha\in(0,\bar\alpha]:\ \phi(x+\alpha d)>\phi(x),
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small-step rejection when the merit directional derivative is strictly positive, contrasted with the inconclusive zero-derivative case.

notation.meaning: radius of guaranteed local merit increase

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mismatch between a generated direction and scalar merit descent
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p_k\neq0\) be generated by a constrained local model at \(x_k\), and let \(\phi(\cdot;\mu_k)\) be the scalar merit function used for globalization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional compatibility at a fixed iterate and fixed penalty parameter; applicable to smooth or directionally differentiable merit functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A merit–direction mismatch occurs when the step-generation mechanism regards \(p_k\) as useful for its constrained model, but the acceptance merit function does not regard it as a descent direction: \[D\phi(x_k;\mu_k)[p_k]\geq0.\] In a trust-region formulation, the corresponding model mismatch is \[q_{\mu_k}(0)-q_{\mu_k}(p_k)\leq0.\] The first condition prevents the ordinary monotone Armijo test from having its standard descent interpretation, while the second makes an actual-to-predicted reduction test unusable as a positive-progress comparison. Compatibility is restored only after changing the direction, the merit model, or the penalty parameter so that the relevant predicted reduction becomes positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit–direction mismatch means that a direction produced as useful by the constrained subproblem is not descent for the scalar function used to accept it. For a line search this is a nonnegative directional derivative. For a trust-region merit model it is nonpositive predicted reduction. The mismatch concerns two algorithmic representations of progress and does not say that the direction is intrinsically poor for the constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mismatch is defined by \(D\phi(x_k;\mu_k)[p_k]\geq0\), or by \(q_{\mu_k}(0)-q_{\mu_k}(p_k)\leq0\) when acceptance uses a trust-region merit model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For differentiable \(\phi\), the line-search mismatch condition is \(\nabla\phi(x_k;\mu_k)^Tp_k\geq0\).
special_cases_latex: An SQP direction can satisfy its linearized constraints yet fail to descend an \(\ell_1\) merit function when the penalty weight is incompatible with the direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: Backtracking alone does not change the sign of the first-order directional merit prediction.
Penalty updates and direction modifications are distinct correction interfaces for the same mismatch.
boundary_notes: The Maratos effect is different: there the direction can have an appropriate first-order model but the full step is rejected because of nonlinear higher-order effects.
A non-descent condition is local and does not prove that every finite step increases the merit function.

notation.meaning: local model of the selected merit function
direction generated by the constrained step model

knowledge_statements.title: Merit–Direction Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A directional condition identifying incompatibility between a productive constrained-model step and scalar merit descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x,d\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(d\neq0\). Let a local constrained model assign the step a predicted reduction \(\Delta m(x;d)>0\), and let \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be the scalar merit function used for globalization. Assume the one-sided directional derivative
\[
\phi'(x;d)=\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}\frac{\phi(x+\alpha d)-\phi(x)}{\alpha}
\]
exists. A merit–direction mismatch occurs when \(\Delta m(x;d)>0\) but \(\phi'(x;d)\geq0\). In this case \(d\) is not a strict first-order descent direction for \(\phi\), so a descent line-search theory requiring \(\phi'(x;d)<0\) cannot be invoked. This condition alone does not imply that every sufficiently small trial step is rejected, because higher-order behavior and the precise acceptance test may still permit acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit–direction mismatch occurs when the constrained model predicts progress but the scalar merit function has a nonnegative directional derivative; this removes the usual strict first-order descent guarantee without proving universal step rejection.
assumptions_latex: The constrained local model predicts \(\Delta m(x;d)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\phi'(x;d)\geq0\), then \(d\) is not a strict first-order descent direction for \(\phi\).

notation.meaning: predicted reduction in the constrained local model
one-sided directional derivative of the scalar merit function

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonnegative directional derivative excludes strict first-order descent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order correction interface for Maratos rejection
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider equality constraints \(c(x)=0\), with \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), Jacobian \(A_k=A(x_k)\) of full row rank, and a primary step \(p_k\) satisfying \(A_kp_k+c(x_k)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained smooth nonlinear programming near a regular solution; the correction is used before backtracking a rejected full primary step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Maratos second-order correction associated with \(p_k\) is the minimum-norm vector \(\widehat p_k\) satisfying \[A_k\widehat p_k+c(x_k+p_k)=0.\] Under full row rank this vector is \[\widehat p_k=-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}c(x_k+p_k).\] The correction interface tests the full corrected trial point \(x_k+p_k+\widehat p_k\) when the uncorrected full step fails the merit sufficient-decrease condition because of constraint violation. It accepts the corrected point only if it satisfies the prescribed merit test; otherwise the correction is discarded and backtracking proceeds along the original direction \(p_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Maratos second-order correction is a minimum-norm auxiliary step computed from the nonlinear residual at the uncorrected trial point. It cancels that residual in the original constraint Jacobian model. The corrected full step is tried before shortening the primary direction, and it is retained only when it passes the merit acceptance test. This interface targets curvature-induced constraint violation that can cause rejection of an otherwise rapidly convergent local step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat p_k=-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}c(x_k+p_k)\) and \(A_k\widehat p_k+c(x_k+p_k)=0\); the corrected point is accepted only through the ordinary merit test.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\widehat p_k\) is the unique solution of \(\min_s\tfrac12\|s\|_2^2\) subject to \(A_ks=-c(x_k+p_k)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(c(x_k+p_k)=0\), then \(\widehat p_k=0\) and the corrected and uncorrected trial points coincide.
immediate_consequences_latex: The correction lies in \(\operatorname{range}(A_k^T)\), the normal space of the linearized constraints.
The interface requires an additional constraint evaluation at \(x_k+p_k\).
boundary_notes: The combined direction \(p_k+\widehat p_k\) need not itself be a merit descent direction, so standard implementations do not backtrack along it.
Rank-deficient Jacobians require a generalized inverse or a different correction definition.

notation.meaning: constraint Jacobian at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Circle Maratos Rejection Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the unit circle, the SQP tangent step lowers the objective but creates a quadratic constraint residual; any ell-one merit weight above one rejects the full step arbitrarily near the solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min f(x)=x_2\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=x_1^2+x_2^2-1=0\] with solution \(x^*=(0,-1)\). At \(x(\theta)=(\sin\theta,-\cos\theta)\), use the exact Lagrangian Hessian \(I\) corresponding to the solution multiplier \(1/2\). The equality-constrained SQP step is \[d(\theta)=-\sin\theta\,(\cos\theta,\sin\theta),\] which satisfies \(J_h(x(\theta))d(\theta)=0\). It gives \[f(x+d)-f(x)=-\sin^2\theta,\qquad h(x+d)=\sin^2\theta.\] Hence for \(\phi_\rho=f+\rho|h|\), \[\phi_\rho(x+d)-\phi_\rho(x)=(\rho-1)\sin^2\theta.\] Every \(\rho>1\) therefore makes the full step increase the merit function for all nonzero arbitrarily small \(\theta\), even though the SQP model predicts descent and enforces linearized feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The SQP model uses the exact solution Lagrangian Hessian \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi_\rho(x(\theta)+d(\theta))>\phi_\rho(x(\theta))\) for every nonzero sufficiently small \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit full-step rejection arbitrarily near a regular equality-constrained solution.

notation.meaning: feasible points approaching the solution along the unit circle

knowledge_statements.title: Maratos Acceptance Obstruction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order constraint curvature can make a locally fast SQP full step fail merit sufficient decrease and thereby obstruct superlinear behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality constraints \(h(x)=0\), suppose an SQP step \(d\) satisfies \(h(x)+J_h(x)d=0\). If \(h\) is twice continuously differentiable, then \[h(x+d)=\tfrac12h''(x)[d,d]+o(\!\|d\|^2).\] A Maratos acceptance obstruction occurs when this second-order residual, omitted by the linearized constraint model, makes an otherwise locally fast full step fail the scalar merit sufficient-decrease test. Repeated rejection of \(\alpha=1\) can prevent realization of the method's local superlinear rate.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is twice continuously differentiable near the iterate.
The SQP step satisfies the linearized equality constraints.
Acceptance uses a scalar merit sufficient-decrease test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The term \(\tfrac12h''(x)[d,d]+o(\|d\|^2)\) may cause rejection of the full step \(\alpha=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-step merit rejection caused by second-order constraint curvature near a regular solution.

notation.meaning: constraint Hessian applied twice to the step

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Correction Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order correction solves a normal linear system for the nonlinear residual, then tests the corrected trial point for acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x\) and an SQP step \(d\), form the nonlinear residual \(r=h(x+d)\). Compute a correction \(s\) by one of the systems
\[
J_h(x)s=-r,\qquad J_h(x+d)s=-r,
\]
or by a least-norm or trust-region-regularized solution of either system; active inequalities may be appended analogously. Test the corrected trial point \(x+d+s\) with the globalization rule and return it if accepted, otherwise revert to the ordinary line-search or trust-region step. Under full row rank of the selected Jacobian and \(r=O(\|d\|^2)\), a bounded right inverse gives \(s=O(\|d\|^2)\).
assumptions_latex: The selected constraint Jacobian has full row rank with a locally bounded right inverse.
The primary SQP step has already been computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm produces a corrected trial step \(d+s\), with \(s=O(\|d\|^2)\) when \(h(x+d)=O(\|d\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal corrections that cancel nonlinear residual left by an SQP trial step.

notation.meaning: nonlinear constraint residual at the uncorrected trial point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard SQP second-order correction systems

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role for this family leaf, and the displayed normal-correction variants and order estimate are coherent under the bounded-right-inverse assumption. A source is required for the algorithm family, treatment of active inequalities, and associated acceptance procedure.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Correction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The usual small-correction guarantee needs compatible residuals and uniformly controlled linear solves; rank loss only threatens that guarantee, while trust-region, bound, and acceptance constraints can independently make a computed correction unusable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider corrections \(s_k\) defined by
\[
J_h(\xi_k)s_k=-h(x_k+d_k),\qquad \xi_k\in\{x_k,x_k+d_k\}.
\]
The standard estimate \(\|s_k\|=O(\|d_k\|^2)\) follows when \(h(x_k+d_k)=O(\|d_k\|^2)\) and the selected linear systems admit solution operators whose norms are uniformly bounded. This standard guarantee cannot be invoked if the residual is outside \(\operatorname{range}(J_h(\xi_k))\), if no uniformly bounded solution operator is available, or if the chosen solutions cannot be bounded by a constant multiple of \(\|d_k\|^2\). Rank loss signals possible loss of the uniform guarantee but does not by itself prove that a particular correction is unsolvable or large. Even a small solvable correction must be modified or rejected if \(d_k+s_k\) violates a trust-region bound, bound constraints, or the globalization method's acceptance requirements.
assumptions_latex: The correction systems have the displayed form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The standard \(O(\|d_k\|^2)\) correction guarantee is unavailable without residual compatibility and uniform solution bounds, and admissibility must be checked separately.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a nonlinear program, let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be the objective and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) a constraint-violation measure. Let \(\mathcal F_k\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a finite archive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic nonlinear-programming globalization that keeps objective and infeasibility as separate measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter method globalizes trial steps using the map \(x\mapsto(f(x),h(x))\) without fixing a scalar weight between its components. The archive \(\mathcal F_k\) contains mutually nondominating pairs. A trial point \(x^+\) is filter-acceptable when no \((f_j,h_j)\in\mathcal F_k\) satisfies \[f_j\leq f(x^+)\quad\text{and}\quad h_j\leq h(x^+).\] Upon acceptance, \((f(x^+),h(x^+))\) may be inserted and all entries it dominates are removed. Practical filter methods strengthen bare nondominance with sufficient-progress margins and invoke restoration or radius/step-length reduction when repeated rejection makes ordinary step generation ineffective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter method treats objective reduction and constraint satisfaction as two separate goals. It stores previously accepted objective-infeasibility pairs that do not dominate one another. A trial point is acceptable if no stored pair is at least as good in both measures. Accepted pairs update the archive, while dominated old entries are deleted. No fixed penalty coefficient converts the two measures into a single scalar ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+\) is acceptable precisely when \(\nexists(f_j,h_j)\in\mathcal F_k\) with \(f_j\leq f(x^+)\) and \(h_j\leq h(x^+)\), subject to any stated sufficient-progress margin.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Bare acceptability is equivalent to \((f(x^+),h(x^+))\notin\bigcup_{(f_j,h_j)\in\mathcal F_k}[f_j,\infty)\times[h_j,\infty)\).
special_cases_latex: A trust-region filter method rejects an unacceptable trial point and reduces the trust-region radius before computing another step.
A line-search filter method backtracks along the trial direction after rejection.
immediate_consequences_latex: An acceptable point must improve at least one measure relative to every entry that is no worse in the other measure.
The archive remains an antichain after dominated entries are removed.
boundary_notes: Bare nondominance alone permits arbitrarily small improvements and is normally strengthened by margins.
Restoration is an auxiliary feasibility phase, not itself the filter archive.

notation.meaning: current archive of mutually nondominating pairs

children.title: Objective-Infeasibility Filter Geometry
children.top_down_role: Partial-order organization of objective and infeasibility measures.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Z=\mathbb R\times\mathbb R_+\) and map each primal point to \(z(x)=(f(x),h(x))\in Z\), where smaller values of both coordinates are preferred.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric representation of two-measure nonlinear-programming progress; objective values may be negative, while infeasibility is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Objective-infeasibility filter geometry equips \(Z\) with the componentwise preorder \[(f_1,h_1)\preceq(f_2,h_2)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f_1\leq f_2\ \text{and}\ h_1\leq h_2.\] A filter is an antichain under this order. Each entry \(z_j=(f_j,h_j)\) excludes its northeast orthant \(z_j+\mathbb R_+^2\); the union of these orthants is the bare forbidden region. Points outside the union are nondominated by the archive and hence geometrically acceptable before sufficient-progress margins or switching conditions are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The filter plane has objective value on one coordinate and infeasibility on the other, with smaller values preferred in both. Componentwise dominance gives only a partial ordering: two points may trade objective against feasibility and therefore be incomparable. Stored filter entries form an antichain. Each entry excludes the rectangle extending toward larger objective and larger infeasibility, and the union of these rectangles is the bare rejection region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order is componentwise, filter entries are mutually incomparable, and the forbidden region is \(\bigcup_{z_j\in\mathcal F}(z_j+\mathbb R_+^2)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A pair \(z^+\) is bare-filter acceptable iff for every \(z_j=(f_j,h_j)\in\mathcal F\), either \(f^+<f_j\) or \(h^+<h_j\).
special_cases_latex: When the archive has one entry, the forbidden region is one closed northeast rectangle.
A scalar merit contour \(f+\mu h=\text{constant}\) is a line in this plane and induces a different, total scalar comparison.
immediate_consequences_latex: Tradeoff points can both remain in the archive because neither dominates the other.
The lower-left boundary of the excluded union is a staircase determined by archive entries.
boundary_notes: Weak dominance includes equality in both coordinates; implementations may add strict margins around the rectangles.
The geometry alone does not prescribe archive initialization or restoration.

notation.meaning: nonnegative orthant in the filter plane

knowledge_statements.title: Nondominated Archive Update
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Insert an admitted pair and remove every old entry it strictly dominates; the resulting basic archive remains mutually nondominated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^+\) be a pair not weakly dominated by any member of a finite mutually nondominating filter \(\mathcal F\). Define \[\mathcal F^+=\bigl(\mathcal F\cup\{y^+\}\bigr)\setminus\{y\in\mathcal F:y^+\prec_D y\}.\] Then \(\mathcal F^+\) is finite and mutually nondominating. A rejected pair leaves the archive unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is finite and mutually nondominating.
No member of \(\mathcal F\) weakly dominates \(y^+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F^+\text{ is finite and mutually nondominating}.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic update of an objective–infeasibility filter after admission.

knowledge_statements.title: Non-Scalarized Tradeoff Principle
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter can retain incomparable objective–feasibility tradeoffs without selecting a fixed penalty weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Basic filter admissibility uses the componentwise order on \((\theta,f)\) and requires no fixed weight \(\rho>0\) forming \(f+\rho\theta\). Two incomparable pairs may therefore both remain archived, although a fixed scalarization orders them whenever their scalarized values are unequal.
assumptions_latex: Both objective value and violation are minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_1\parallel_D y_2\text{ permits }y_1,y_2\in\mathcal F\text{ independently of a scalarization weight}.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural distinction between a filter and a fixed scalar merit function.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For constraints \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in\mathcal E\), and \(c_i(x)\geq0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\), define \(h(x)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x)]^-\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical two-measure filter for finite-dimensional nonlinear programming with an ℓ1 infeasibility measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective–infeasibility filter is a finite set \[\mathcal F=\{(f_j,h_j):j\in J\}\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R_+\] satisfying, for every distinct \(i,j\in J\), neither \((f_i\leq f_j\ \text{and}\ h_i\leq h_j)\) nor \((f_j\leq f_i\ \text{and}\ h_j\leq h_i)\). A trial point \(x^+\) is acceptable when its pair is not dominated by any entry: \[\forall j\in J,\qquad f(x^+)<f_j\quad\text{or}\quad h(x^+)<h_j.\] After insertion of an acceptable pair, every old pair weakly dominated by it is deleted, restoring the antichain property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical filter stores objective values together with an ℓ1 measure of equality and inequality violation. No stored entry may be no worse than another in both coordinates. A trial point passes the bare filter exactly when, relative to each stored pair, it has either a smaller objective or smaller infeasibility. Insertion removes any entries dominated by the new pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is a finite antichain of \((f,h)\) pairs, and \(x^+\) is acceptable iff \(f(x^+)<f_j\) or \(h(x^+)<h_j\) for every \(j\in J\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Acceptability is equivalent to the absence of \(j\) satisfying \(f_j\leq f(x^+)\) and \(h_j\leq h(x^+)\).
special_cases_latex: At a feasible point, \(h(x)=0\); another pair can improve its feasibility coordinate only by also having zero infeasibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: All retained entries represent distinct objective-feasibility tradeoffs.
Archive pruning preserves every pair not dominated by the inserted point.
boundary_notes: Practical algorithms ordinarily replace strict bare improvement by sufficient-progress margins.
The filter set is an acceptance archive, not the feasible set of the nonlinear program.

notation.meaning: finite index set of filter entries

knowledge_statements.title: Objective–Infeasibility Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite filters on objective value and scalar constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and let \(\theta:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) measure constraint violation, with \(\theta(x)=0\) exactly at feasible points. An objective–infeasibility filter is a finite set
\[
\mathcal F\subset\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R
\]
of mutually nondominated pairs \((\theta_i,f_i)\). A pair \((\theta_a,f_a)\) dominates \((\theta_b,f_b)\) when \(\theta_a\leq\theta_b\) and \(f_a\leq f_b\). A trial point \(x^+\) is filter-admissible in the basic geometry when no \((\theta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F\) dominates \((\theta(x^+),f(x^+))\); practical filters strengthen this test by prescribed progress margins.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter stores mutually nondominated objective–violation pairs and admits a trial point not dominated by any stored pair.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite on evaluated trial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Filter admissibility is the absence of a stored pair simultaneously no worse in infeasibility and objective value.

notation.meaning: finite set of mutually nondominated filter entries

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical two-dimensional nonlinear-programming filter definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the classical objective–infeasibility filter container, uses consistent dominance geometry, and distinguishes the basic test from practical sufficient-progress margins. An inspectable filter-method definition or section locator is still required.

children.title: Filter Dominance-Exclusion Geometry
children.top_down_role: Partial-order and forbidden-region interpretations of filter entries.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dominance cones and filter exclusion region
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R_+\) be a finite filter and write each entry as \(z_j=(f_j,h_j)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic geometry of weak dominance and rejection in the two-dimensional filter plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dominance-exclusion region generated by an entry \(z_j\) is its closed upper cone \[C(z_j)=\{(f,h):f\geq f_j,\ h\geq h_j\}=[f_j,\infty)\times[h_j,\infty).\] The filter forbidden region is \[\mathcal D(\mathcal F)=\bigcup_{z_j\in\mathcal F}C(z_j).\] A candidate pair \(z^+=(f^+,h^+)\) is excluded exactly when \(z^+\in\mathcal D(\mathcal F)\), equivalently when some archive entry weakly dominates it. The bare acceptable region is the complement \((\mathbb R\times\mathbb R_+)\setminus\mathcal D(\mathcal F)\). Inserting an acceptable \(z^+\) removes each \(z_j\in C(z^+)\) and then adds \(z^+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every filter entry creates a closed northeast rectangle of pairs having no better objective and no better infeasibility. The union of these rectangles is the forbidden region. A trial pair is rejected by bare dominance precisely when it lies in that union. If an acceptable pair is inserted, any old entries inside the new pair's northeast rectangle are removed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal D(\mathcal F)=\bigcup_{(f_j,h_j)\in\mathcal F}[f_j,\infty)\times[h_j,\infty)\), and bare acceptability is membership in its complement.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(z^+\notin\mathcal D(\mathcal F)\) iff \(\forall z_j\in\mathcal F\), \(f^+<f_j\) or \(h^+<h_j\).
special_cases_latex: With two incomparable entries \(f_1<f_2\) and \(h_1>h_2\), the forbidden boundary has two staircase corners.
immediate_consequences_latex: Adding a nondominated entry can only enlarge the forbidden region before dominated entries are pruned.
Deleting entries dominated by the new pair does not change the union of excluded cones after the new cone is added.
boundary_notes: Sufficient-progress filters enlarge or shift these bare exclusion regions.
Dominance uses the orientation that smaller objective and infeasibility are preferable.

notation.meaning: upper dominance cone generated by entry j

source_refs.locator: Section 15.4, Definition 15.2 and paragraph following it describing the infinite rectangular regions in Figure 15.6

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance cones and filter exclusion region

source_witnesses.locator: Section 15.4, Definition 15.2 and paragraph following it describing the infinite rectangular regions in Figure 15.6

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Is a Partial Order
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Componentwise weak dominance is a partial order. Opposing objective and feasibility improvements produce incomparable pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(Y=\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\), define \((\theta_1,f_1)\preceq_D(\theta_2,f_2)\) iff \(\theta_1\le\theta_2\) and \(f_1\le f_2\). Then \(\preceq_D\) is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive. Its strict part is irreflexive and transitive but not total; two distinct pairs are incomparable exactly when one has smaller violation and the other has smaller objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\preceq_D\text{ is a partial order},\qquad y_1\parallel_D y_2\iff(\theta_1-\theta_2)(f_1-f_2)<0\text{ for distinct }y_1,y_2.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic structure of objective–infeasibility comparison.

notation.meaning: the pairs are incomparable under dominance

knowledge_statements.title: Nondominated Frontier Ordering
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sorting a finite filter by increasing violation sorts its objective values strictly downward; this staircase ordering characterizes mutual nondominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F=\{(\theta_i,f_i)\}_{i=1}^m\) have distinct, mutually nondominating entries. Indexing them by \(\theta_1<\cdots<\theta_m\) gives \(f_1>\cdots>f_m\). Conversely, any finite sequence satisfying these two strict coordinate orderings is mutually nondominating.
assumptions_latex: Entries are distinct and both coordinates are minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\text{ is mutually nondominating}\iff \theta_1<\cdots<\theta_m\text{ and }f_1>\cdots>f_m\text{ after sorting by }\theta.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate ordering of a finite mutually nondominated filter.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Dominance Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto dominance for objective–constraint-violation pairs in a minimization filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=\mathbb{R}_{+}\times\mathbb{R}\), where \(y=(\theta,f)\) records constraint violation and objective value. For \(y_1=(\theta_1,f_1)\) and \(y_2=(\theta_2,f_2)\), define \(y_1\preceq_D y_2\) when \(\theta_1\leq\theta_2\) and \(f_1\leq f_2\). Define strict dominance, \(y_1\prec_D y_2\), when \(y_1\preceq_D y_2\) and at least one inequality is strict. A filter is an archive \(\mathcal F\subset Y\) whose distinct entries are mutually nondominating under \(\prec_D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One filter pair dominates another when it is no worse in objective and infeasibility and strictly better in at least one; archived pairs are mutually nondominating.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta\geq0\) is an infeasibility measure to be minimized.
\(f\in\mathbb R\) is the objective value to be minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_1\prec_D y_2\iff \theta_1\leq\theta_2,\ f_1\leq f_2,\text{ and }y_1\neq y_2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the terminal container and are mathematically coherent, but the record has no citation. The standard-field rationale supports candidate status only; an inspectable filter-method source with a section, page, or definition locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Exclusion Generators
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generator is removable exactly when the other generators already cover its excluded set; under zero margins, a dominated entry is redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(j\in\mathcal F\), deletion of generator \(j\) leaves the total exclusion region unchanged exactly when \(E_j\subseteq\bigcup_{i\in\mathcal F\setminus\{j\}}E_i\). For zero-margin upper-orthant exclusion \(E_y=\{z:y\preceq_D z\}\), an entry weakly dominated by another entry is therefore redundant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(\mathcal F)=E(\mathcal F\setminus\{j\})\iff E_j\subseteq E(\mathcal F\setminus\{j\}).\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion for deleting an exclusion generator without changing admissibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Union Monotonicity of Exclusion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an exclusion generator enlarges the excluded union and shrinks its admissible complement; removing one has the reverse monotone effect.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For entry-generated exclusion sets \(E_i\), let \(E(\mathcal F)=\bigcup_{i\in\mathcal F}E_i\) and \(A(\mathcal F)=Y\setminus E(\mathcal F)\). If \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal G\), then \(E(\mathcal F)\subseteq E(\mathcal G)\) and \(A(\mathcal G)\subseteq A(\mathcal F)\).
assumptions_latex: Each archive entry determines a set \(E_i\subseteq Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal G\Longrightarrow E(\mathcal F)\subseteq E(\mathcal G),\quad A(\mathcal G)\subseteq A(\mathcal F).\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic behavior when exclusion generators are added or removed.

notation.meaning: complement of the total exclusion region

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Exclusion Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Margin-enlarged region rejected because one archived entry is insufficiently improved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix margins \(\gamma_\theta\in(0,1)\) and \(\gamma_f>0\). For an entry \(y_i=(\theta_i,f_i)\), define its exclusion region by \[E_i=\{(\theta,f)\in\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R:\ \theta>(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\ \text{and}\ f>f_i-\gamma_f\theta\}.\] For a finite filter \(\mathcal F\), the total exclusion region is \(E(\mathcal F)=\bigcup_{y_i\in\mathcal F}E_i\). A trial pair is filter-acceptable exactly when it lies outside \(E(\mathcal F)\), subject to any separate safeguards imposed by the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each archive entry excludes pairs that achieve neither the required relative infeasibility decrease nor the required objective decrease; the total rejected region is their union.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\theta,f)\notin E(\mathcal F)\iff \forall(\theta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F,\ \theta\leq(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\ \text{or}\ f\leq f_i-\gamma_f\theta\).

notation.meaning: exclusion region generated by entry i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches the exclusion-region container and the displayed complement is consistent with the stated open region. However, the particular relative-feasibility and objective-margin convention is algorithm-specific and has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Archive-Wide Acceptance Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full filter boundary is the union of the exposed, rather than hidden, pieces of the individual entry boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\), let a finite archive have open exclusion regions \(E_i\subset D\), let \(B_i=\partial_D E_i\), and define \(A_{\mathcal F}=D\setminus\bigcup_{i\in\mathcal F}E_i\). Then \[\partial_D A_{\mathcal F}=A_{\mathcal F}\cap\bigcup_{i\in\mathcal F}B_i.\] Hence only portions of the single-entry boundaries that remain outside every other exclusion region appear on the archive-wide boundary; portions covered by another entry's exclusion region are hidden.
assumptions_latex: Each \(E_i\) is open relative to \(D\) and has the margin geometry stated in the seed.
Boundary is taken relative to \(D=\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_D A_{\mathcal F}=A_{\mathcal F}\cap\bigcup_{i\in\mathcal F}B_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exposed acceptance boundary generated by a finite filter archive under the seed's margin convention.

notation.meaning: Open exclusion region generated by entry \(i\).
Boundary in the relative topology of \(D\).

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Acceptance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the margin-enlarged exclusion region generated by one filter entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y_i=(\theta_i,f_i)\), \(\gamma_\theta\in(0,1)\), and \(\gamma_f>0\), let \(E_i\) be the open exclusion region. Its acceptance boundary in \(\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\) is \[B_i=\{((1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i,f):f\geq f_i-\gamma_f(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\}\cup\{(\theta,f_i-\gamma_f\theta):\theta\geq(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\}.\] Thus the boundary consists of a vertical infeasibility-margin ray and an objective-margin ray. With non-strict acceptance tests, points on \(B_i\) satisfy the test associated with entry \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An entry's acceptance boundary comprises a vertical relative-infeasibility threshold and a sloped objective-decrease threshold meeting at one corner.
assumptions_latex: \(E_i\) uses strict inequalities in both exclusion conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_i=\partial E_i\) relative to \(\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: acceptance boundary generated by archive entry i
open exclusion region generated by entry i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Relative to the stated domain, the two rays correctly describe the boundary of the specified open exclusion region, and representation is the appropriate kind. A source is still required because the underlying margin convention and treatment of boundary equality are algorithm-dependent.

children.title: Filter Sufficient-Progress Margins
children.top_down_role: Strict separation mechanisms preventing arbitrarily weak tradeoff progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Objective-Separation Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective margin proportional to trial infeasibility is strict away from feasibility but supplies no uniform objective separation as violation tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the branch \(f^+\le f_i-\gamma_f\theta^+\), the guaranteed objective separation is \(f_i-f^+\ge\gamma_f\theta^+\). It is positive for \(\theta^+>0\), but tends to zero along any sequence with \(\theta^+\downarrow0\). Thus \(\gamma_f>0\) does not provide a uniform positive objective gap near feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The trial-scaled objective-margin convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_i-f^+\ge\gamma_f\theta^+,\qquad \inf_{\theta^+>0}\gamma_f\theta^+=0.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp limitation of an objective margin scaled by trial infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity in Progress Margins
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing either declared margin makes the progress test weakly stricter, so its admissible sets shrink.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the predicate \(\theta^+\le(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\) or \(f^+\le f_i-\gamma_f\theta^+\), suppose \(0<\gamma_\theta\le\widehat\gamma_\theta<1\) and \(0<\gamma_f\le\widehat\gamma_f\). Every pair acceptable under \((\widehat\gamma_\theta,\widehat\gamma_f)\) is acceptable under \((\gamma_\theta,\gamma_f)\), whereas the converse can fail.
assumptions_latex: The same filter archive is used for both parameter choices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(\widehat\gamma_\theta,\widehat\gamma_f)\subseteq A(\gamma_\theta,\gamma_f).\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nesting of admissible sets as the declared margins are strengthened.

notation.meaning: pairs satisfying the margin predicate against every filter entry

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) contain objective-infeasibility pairs \((f_j,h_j)\), let \((f^+,h^+)\) be a trial pair, and fix \(\beta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical sufficient-progress strengthening of bare filter nondominance for deterministic nonlinear-programming globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter sufficient-progress margin declares \((f^+,h^+)\) acceptable only if, for every \((f_j,h_j)\in\mathcal F\), \[f^+\leq f_j-\beta h_j\qquad\text{or}\qquad h^+\leq h_j-\beta h_j=(1-\beta)h_j.\] Thus a candidate must achieve a quantified objective improvement scaled by the stored infeasibility or a fixed relative reduction in infeasibility. A standard analytical variant replaces the first inequality by \[f^+\leq f_j-\beta h^+.\] These margins strictly separate accepted pairs from the archive's bare dominance boundary and prevent acceptance based on arbitrarily weak tradeoff progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficient-progress margin strengthens nondominance by requiring a definite improvement relative to every filter entry. The trial point must either reduce objective by an amount proportional to the stored infeasibility or reduce infeasibility by a fixed relative fraction. An analytical variant scales the objective margin by the trial infeasibility. The rule excludes pairs that are technically nondominated but arbitrarily close to an existing entry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \((f_j,h_j)\in\mathcal F\), acceptance requires \(f^+\leq f_j-\beta h_j\) or \(h^+\leq(1-\beta)h_j\), with \(\beta\in(0,1)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The margin-forbidden region generated by \((f_j,h_j)\) is \((f_j-\beta h_j,\infty)\times((1-\beta)h_j,\infty)\), with endpoint conventions determined by the non-strict acceptance inequalities.
special_cases_latex: If \(h_j=0\), the displayed rule reduces to \(f^+\leq f_j\) or \(h^+=0\); additional switching or merit conditions may be needed near feasibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: Whenever acceptance occurs through the feasibility alternative, \(h^+\leq(1-\beta)h_j<h_j\) for \(h_j>0\).
The margin rule implies bare nondominance except at equality conventions on the boundary.
boundary_notes: The margin parameter does not replace a restoration phase when step lengths or trust-region radii become too small.
Different filter algorithms use related but not identical margin and switching conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Sufficient-Progress Margins
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict objective-or-feasibility separation from every archived pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\subset\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\), \(\gamma_\theta\in(0,1)\), and \(\gamma_f>0\). A trial pair \((\theta^+,f^+)\) satisfies the filter sufficient-progress condition if \[\forall(\theta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F:\quad \theta^+\leq(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\quad\text{or}\quad f^+\leq f_i-\gamma_f\theta^+.\] Hence acceptance requires, relative to every entry, either a fixed fractional decrease in infeasibility or objective improvement proportional to the trial infeasibility. Positive margins exclude arbitrarily weak improvements approaching a dominated pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Against every archive entry, a trial must deliver either fractional infeasibility reduction or objective reduction proportional to its remaining infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\theta^+,f^+)\) is margin-acceptable precisely when the displayed disjunction holds for every filter entry.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the topic and its quantified disjunction is precise, but no source supports this particular filter-margin formula. The final claim about excluding arbitrarily weak improvements also needs qualification or source support, since the objective margin scales with trial infeasibility and can vanish as that infeasibility approaches zero.

children.title: Filter Acceptance-Archive Architecture
children.top_down_role: Trial-point classification, switching, and archive-maintenance families.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be the objective, and let \(h:X\to\mathbb R_+\) measure constraint violation, with \(h(x)=0\) exactly at feasible points. A filter archive is a finite subset \(\mathcal F\subset\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\) whose coordinates are ordered as \((h,f)\). Fix a margin parameter \(\gamma_h\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonlinear programming with a two-criterion objective-infeasibility filter and a margin-based acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter acceptance-archive architecture is the pair \((\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathcal F},\operatorname{Upd}_{\mathcal F})\) defined as follows. The archive satisfies \(\forall (h_i,f_i)\ne(h_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F:\ h_i<h_j\ \lor\ f_i<f_j\). A trial point \(x^+\in X\) is acceptable precisely when \[\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathcal F}(x^+)\iff \forall(h_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F,\quad h(x^+)<(1-\gamma_h)h_j\ \lor\ f(x^+)<f_j-\gamma_h h(x^+).\] If an acceptable pair \((h^+,f^+)=(h(x^+),f(x^+))\) is inserted, archive maintenance forms \[\operatorname{Upd}_{\mathcal F}(h^+,f^+)=\{(h_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F:h_j<(1-\gamma_h)h^+\ \lor\ f_j<f^+-\gamma_h h_j\}\cup\{(h^+,f^+)\}.\] Thus acceptance is a universally quantified comparison with the archived nondominated pairs, and insertion removes pairs excluded by the new pair's margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter acceptance-archive architecture consists of an archive of mutually nondominated infeasibility-objective pairs, a margin-based acceptance predicate, and an update operation. A trial point is acceptable only if, against every archived pair, it either reduces infeasibility by the prescribed relative margin or improves the objective by the prescribed infeasibility-scaled margin. When its pair is inserted, all archived pairs dominated within the corresponding margin are removed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is a margin-separated nondominated archive, \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathcal F}\) is the displayed universal disjunctive test, and \(\operatorname{Upd}_{\mathcal F}\) inserts an acceptable pair while deleting pairs that it excludes.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With zero margins, acceptance reduces to ordinary Pareto nondominance: no \((h_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F\) satisfies \(h_j\le h(x^+)\) and \(f_j\le f(x^+)\).
The unacceptable set is the union, over archived pairs, of their margin-enlarged upper-right dominated regions in the \((h,f)\)-plane.
special_cases_latex: For an empty archive, \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\varnothing}(x)=\mathrm{true}\) for every \(x\in X\).
Using \((f,h)\) instead of \((h,f)\) changes only coordinate order, not the partial-order construction.
immediate_consequences_latex: After every update, no retained old pair is excluded by the newly inserted pair's margin.
The acceptance decision does not require a penalty parameter combining \(f\) and \(h\).
boundary_notes: Practical algorithms may add a current-iterate test, an objective-decrease switching test, or restoration; those mechanisms are not part of this archive definition.
Strict versus non-strict inequalities and alternative objective margins occur in the literature and must be fixed consistently.
