children.title: Filter Progress-Type Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Classification by the progress measure credited for acceptance.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\) be a current iterate, \(s_k\) a trial step, \(h_k=h(x_k)\), and \(m_k\) a local objective model. Let \(\delta_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)\), with constants \(\kappa_h>0\) and \(\eta\in(0,1)\). Assume the trial point has passed the applicable filter test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of accepted trial steps by the progress test credited for acceptance; it does not classify the step-generation method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The filter progress type of an accepted trial step is defined by a switching predicate \(S_k\). In the standard trust-region SQP form, \[S_k\iff \delta_k\ge \kappa_h h_k^2.\] If \(S_k\) holds and the step is credited only after satisfying the objective agreement test \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{\delta_k}\ge\eta,\] the iteration is objective-type (or \(f\)-type). If \(S_k\) fails and acceptance is credited to sufficient reduction in the filter's infeasibility coordinate, the iteration is feasibility-type (or \(h\)-type). Restoration iterations form a separate class: they approximately minimize \(h\) because the ordinary step subproblem is incompatible or ordinary globalization has failed. Each accepted iteration receives the label corresponding to the decisive test, even if the other measure also improves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The progress taxonomy labels an accepted step according to the test that authorizes it. An objective-type step has enough predicted objective-model decrease to activate an actual-versus-predicted objective reduction test and passes that test. A feasibility-type step is accepted through the filter when the objective switching condition is not active and its credited progress is reduction of constraint violation. A restoration step is separate and is produced by a phase devoted to reducing violation after ordinary step generation or globalization fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_k\) and the decisive acceptance test partition credited progress into objective-type, feasibility-type, and restoration-type iterations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: An \(f\)-type step is one for which objective decrease is required in addition to filter acceptability; an \(h\)-type step is one for which filter progress supplies the decisive acceptance certificate.
special_cases_latex: At a feasible iterate \(h_k=0\), every positive predicted decrease satisfies \(S_k\), so the local regime is normally objective-type.
A restoration point can reduce \(h\) and be filter acceptable without being labeled an ordinary \(h\)-type SQP step.
immediate_consequences_latex: The taxonomy records why a point was accepted, not merely which coordinates decreased.
A single trial point may improve both \(f\) and \(h\), but its credited type is determined by the active branch.
boundary_notes: Different filter algorithms use different switching exponents, thresholds, or model-decrease measures.
The labels are not defined solely by the signs of \(f(x_k+s_k)-f(x_k)\) and \(h(x_k+s_k)-h_k\).

notation.meaning: Ratio of actual to predicted objective reduction.

source_refs.locator: Section 15.5.3, Algorithm 15.5.1, Steps 3–5, equations (15.5.8)–(15.5.9)

review_flags: Terminology such as “f-type” and “h-type” varies across filter implementations; the record fixes it by the decisive test in Algorithm 15.5.1.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Type and Feasibility-Type Filter Progress

source_witnesses.locator: Section 15.5.3, Algorithm 15.5.1, Steps 3–5, equations (15.5.8)–(15.5.9)

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Decrease Alone Does Not Determine Objective Type
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accepted trial may lower the objective without being objective-type; the declared objective certificate determines the label.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\) denote trial acceptance, \(D_k=[f(x_k+s_k)<f(x_k)]\), and \(O_k\) the method's complete objective-type certificate. In general, \(A_k\land D_k\not\Rightarrow O_k\): a trial may lower the objective while being accepted and classified through feasibility progress. Objective type is determined by \(O_k\), not by the sign of the objective change alone.
assumptions_latex: The method distinguishes trial acceptance from the certificate credited for its progress type.
\(O_k\) contains every switching and sufficient-decrease requirement used by the method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative objective change alone does not certify that iteration \(k\) is objective-type.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between observed objective reduction and classification through an objective certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Type Filter Iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification relative to an explicit switching test and objective decrease condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(x_k\) be the current point, \(s_k\) an accepted trial step, \(m_k\) a local objective model, and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\). The iteration is objective-type when the algorithm's switching predicate \(S_k\) is true and the accepted step satisfies the objective sufficient-decrease test \[f(x_k+s_k)\leq f(x_k)+\sigma\bigl(m_k(s_k)-m_k(0)\bigr),\qquad m_k(s_k)-m_k(0)<0.\] Its acceptance is therefore certified by objective-model decrease, whether or not the trial pair also satisfies the filter test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accepted iteration is objective-type when switching is active and actual objective decrease is sufficient relative to a negative predicted model change.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(m_k\) are finite at the tested points.
The algorithm specifies a Boolean switching predicate \(S_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_k\) together with the displayed decrease inequality classifies iteration \(k\) as objective-type.

notation.meaning: local objective model at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is an appropriate kind for the iteration class, but the switching predicate, model decrease test, and priority over simultaneous filter acceptance are algorithm-specific. No authoritative source or inspectable locator establishes this exact classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Type Filter Iterations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility-type iteration is accepted by the filter progress test rather than the switched objective-decrease test; its objective may still decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\theta_k^+,f_k^+)=(\theta(x_k+s_k),f(x_k+s_k))\) be an accepted trial pair and let \(\mathcal F_k\) be the current filter. Iteration \(k\) is feasibility-type when it is not accepted through the objective switching test and \[\forall(\theta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k:\quad \theta_k^+\leq(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\quad\text{or}\quad f_k^+\leq f_i-\gamma_f\theta_k^+.\] The name identifies the filter-based acceptance route; it does not require \(f_k^+\geq f(x_k)\) or strict reduction of \(\theta\) from the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_k\) is the filter before classifying the accepted trial.
The algorithm records which acceptance test certified the step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Filter certification without objective-switch certification classifies iteration \(k\) as feasibility-type.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by acceptance through objective–infeasibility filter progress.

notation.meaning: filter archive before acceptance at iteration k

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the feasibility-type iteration container and clearly distinguishes the certification route from actual objective or feasibility behavior. The classification rule and margin formula nevertheless require a cited algorithmic source with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlap Requires an Explicit Classification Convention
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping objective and feasibility certificates do not determine a unique iteration label without a tie convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O_k\) and \(F_k\) be objective-type and feasibility-type certification predicates for the same trial. If \(O_k\land F_k\) is satisfiable, these predicates alone do not define a single-valued type. A mutually exclusive classification requires a priority rule, a tie class, or disjoint refinements of the predicates. If \(O_k\land F_k\equiv\mathrm{false}\), no tie convention is required.
assumptions_latex: \(O_k\) and \(F_k\) are Boolean predicates evaluated on the same trial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O_k\land F_k\) being satisfiable implies that a single-valued two-type classification requires an additional convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary for assigning one progress type when objective and feasibility certificates overlap.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Iteration Classification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjoint classification rule when objective and filter acceptance tests overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(O_k\) denote satisfaction of both the objective switching predicate and its sufficient-decrease test, and let \(F_k\) denote satisfaction of the filter sufficient-progress test. Define the classification by \[\operatorname{type}(k)= egin{cases}\mathrm{objective},&O_k,\ \mathrm{feasibility},&
eg O_k\land F_k,\ \mathrm{rejected},&
eg O_k\land
eg F_k.\end{cases}\] The boundary between accepted types is therefore determined by \(O_k\), not merely by whether both tests happen to hold. This priority rule makes the classes mutually exclusive and exhaustive for every tested trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective certification has priority when both tests hold; otherwise filter certification gives feasibility type, and failure of both means rejection.
assumptions_latex: \(O_k\) and \(F_k\) are Boolean predicates evaluated on the same trial.
Objective certification is assigned priority in the overlap case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\mathrm{objective}\), \(\mathrm{feasibility}\), or \(\mathrm{rejected}\) is assigned to each trial.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the classification-boundary leaf, and the piecewise rule is internally exhaustive and disjoint under its assumptions. Objective priority in the overlap case is a chosen algorithmic convention, however, and no source supports that convention for the intended taxonomy node.

children.title: Filter Switching Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Transitions between partial-order acceptance and objective-oriented decrease tests.

knowledge_statements.title: Totality Conditions for a Filter Switch
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selector defines an executable switch only when its selected test and failure response are uniquely defined throughout the admissible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A switching tuple \((S_k,T_k^{\mathrm{obj}},T_k^{\mathrm{fil}},R_k)\) defines a total deterministic trial transition only if \(S_k\) is Boolean and defined for every admissible trial, the selected test is Boolean and defined on that trial, and \(R_k\) returns a unique permitted next state whenever the selected test fails. Otherwise an admissible trial may remain unclassified or have multiple successor states.
assumptions_latex: An admissible-trial domain and permitted state space are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Totality and determinism require a defined selector, a defined selected test, and a unique failure response on the entire admissible domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which an abstract switching tuple defines a deterministic transition for every admissible trial.

knowledge_statements.title: Identical Selectors Can Produce Different Acceptance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The switching predicate alone does not determine trial acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k=\mathrm{true}\), \(f(x_k)=0\), \(f(x_k+s_k)=-\tfrac12\), and \(\Delta m_k=1\). An objective-route test requiring actual reduction of at least \(0.1\Delta m_k\) accepts, whereas a test requiring at least \(0.75\Delta m_k\) rejects. Thus identical selectors and trial data can produce different decisions when the selected route tests differ.
assumptions_latex: Both mechanisms select the objective route.
Both use the same objective and model data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_k^{(1)}=S_k^{(2)}\ \not\Rightarrow\ \operatorname{accept}^{(1)}(s_k)=\operatorname{accept}^{(2)}(s_k).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete nonuniqueness example for an incompletely specified switch.

knowledge_statements.title: Components of a Filter Switching Mechanism
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A switch is not determined by its threshold alone; its two acceptance routes and failure response are also essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter switching mechanism may be represented by \((S_k,T_k^{\mathrm{obj}},T_k^{\mathrm{fil}},R_k)\), where \(S_k\) selects the objective-oriented regime, \(T_k^{\mathrm{obj}}\) and \(T_k^{\mathrm{fil}}\) are the route-specific acceptance tests, and \(R_k\) specifies the response to failure. A formula for \(S_k\) alone does not determine the mechanism: distinct tests or failure responses can generate different accepted iterates under the same selector.
assumptions_latex: The framework has distinct objective-oriented and filter-oriented acceptance routes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of selectors \(S_k\) does not imply equality of complete switching mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Framework-independent representation of the information needed to specify a switch between acceptance routes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(h_k\ge0\) be infeasibility, let \(m_k\) be a local objective model, let \(s_k\) be a trial step, and define \(\delta_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)\). Fix \(\kappa_h>0\) and \(0<\eta_1<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic switch between filter-based partial-order acceptance and an objective actual-versus-predicted decrease test in trust-region filter SQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter switching mechanism is a predicate \(S_k=S(h_k,m_k,s_k)\) together with two acceptance branches. For the canonical quadratic threshold, \[S_k\iff \delta_k\ge\kappa_h h_k^2.\] Every candidate must first be acceptable to the filter and current iterate. If \(S_k\) is true, define \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)]/\delta_k\) and require \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\); failure rejects the step and contracts the trust region. If \(S_k\) is false, the objective ratio is not the decisive condition and the filter-progress branch may accept the step; the current pair may then be inserted into the archive. Thus the switch prevents a trial with substantial predicted objective progress from being accepted solely because of bicriteria nondominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A switching mechanism evaluates predicted objective decrease relative to current infeasibility. When predicted decrease is at least a constant times squared infeasibility, the objective branch is active and the step must achieve a prescribed fraction of its predicted decrease. Otherwise the filter branch can credit feasibility-oriented progress. Filter acceptability remains a prerequisite in either branch in the stated trust-region construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate \(\delta_k\ge\kappa_h h_k^2\) selects between an objective-ratio test and filter-progress acceptance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The objective branch is active when \(h_k\le\sqrt{\delta_k/\kappa_h}\), provided \(\delta_k\ge0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(h_k=0\) and \(\delta_k>0\), the objective branch is necessarily active.
If \(\delta_k<\kappa_h h_k^2\), no conclusion about objective agreement is required by this switch alone.
immediate_consequences_latex: Near feasibility, steps with meaningful predicted objective decrease are tested like ordinary trust-region objective steps.
The mechanism separates archive admission from objective-model agreement.
boundary_notes: Line-search filters may use directional derivatives and step lengths instead of trust-region model reduction.
The switch does not itself define restoration triggers or archive deletion.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Switching Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic switch from filter acceptance to objective sufficient decrease near productive objective steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), trial step \(s_k\), filter \(\mathcal F_k\), objective model \(m_k\), thresholds \(\delta>0\), \(p>0\), and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), compute \(\Delta m_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\). Set \(S_k=[\Delta m_k>0\ \text{and}\ \Delta m_k\geq\delta\theta(x_k)^p]\). If \(S_k\) is true, accept only when \(f(x_k+s_k)\leq f(x_k)-\sigma\Delta m_k\). Otherwise apply the filter sufficient-progress test to \((\theta(x_k+s_k),f(x_k+s_k))\). Output the accepted trial and its objective- or feasibility-type label; reject it if the selected test fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A predicted-decrease threshold activates an objective Armijo test; otherwise acceptance uses the objective–infeasibility filter, with the selected route determining iteration type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The switching predicate selects exactly one primary acceptance test for the trial.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role for a switching mechanism, but the threshold involving predicted reduction and a power of infeasibility, as well as the rule that exactly one test is attempted, is framework-specific. An authoritative filter-method source is needed to determine the correct predicate, exponent restrictions, and fallback behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on transferring a numerical switching formula between filter methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter switching mechanism is determined by a tuple \((S_k,T_k^{\mathrm{obj}},T_k^{\mathrm{fil}},R_k)\), where \(S_k\) selects the objective-oriented regime, \(T_k^{\mathrm{obj}}\) and \(T_k^{\mathrm{fil}}\) are the corresponding acceptance tests, and \(R_k\) specifies behavior after failure. Specifying only a threshold formula for \(S_k\) does not determine the mechanism: different choices of acceptance test or failure route can produce different accepted iterates even when \(S_k\) is identical. Consequently, exponent restrictions, inequalities at equality, and fallback behavior cannot be inferred from the generic notion of a filter switch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A switching threshold alone does not define a filter switching mechanism; the selected tests and failure route are also essential.
assumptions_latex: The globalization framework admits distinct objective-oriented and filter-oriented acceptance routes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of switching predicates does not imply equality of switching mechanisms or generated accepted iterates.
knowledge_statements.title: No Framework-Independent Switching Threshold

children.title: Filter Archive Maintenance Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Initialization and dominance-based maintenance of the filter archive.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Filter Archive Initialization, Insertion, and Pruning
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z(x)=(h(x),f(x))\in\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\), and let \(\prec_\gamma\) denote the selected margin-dominance relation. Let \(\mathcal F_k\) be the archive at the start of iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifecycle of a finite two-dimensional filter archive under dominance-based maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The filter archive maintenance lifecycle is the recursion \[\mathcal F_0=\varnothing,\qquad \mathcal F_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\operatorname{Max}_{\prec_\gamma}(\mathcal F_k\cup\{z_k\}),&I_k=1,\\\mathcal F_k,&I_k=0,\end{cases}\] where \(I_k\in\{0,1\}\) is the algorithm's insertion decision and \(\operatorname{Max}_{\prec_\gamma}(A)=\{a\in A:\nexists b\in A\setminus\{a\}\text{ with }b\prec_\gamma a\}\). In the Conn–Gould–Toint margin rule, insertion of \(z_k=(h_k,f_k)\) deletes every \((h_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F_k\) satisfying \(h_j\ge(1-\gamma_h)h_k\) and \(f_j\ge f_k-\gamma_h h_j\). Initialization may instead include a sentinel \((h^{\max},-\infty)\) to impose \(h(x)<h^{\max}\) on all acceptable iterates. Rejected trials do not enter the archive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archive maintenance starts from an empty archive, or from a sentinel imposing a maximum violation. At iterations selected by the algorithm, a point's infeasibility-objective pair is inserted and all old pairs dominated under the chosen margin relation are removed. At other iterations the archive is unchanged. Consequently the archive always contains only pairs maximal with respect to the retained nondominance convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\) is obtained by conditional insertion followed by deletion of all margin-dominated entries.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Maintenance computes the nondominated frontier of the old archive together with the inserted pair, under the algorithm's margin relation.
special_cases_latex: With \(I_k=0\), \(\mathcal F_{k+1}=\mathcal F_k\).
With ordinary Pareto dominance, pruning removes every pair weakly worse in both coordinates.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every retained pair survives comparison with the newly inserted pair.
A rejected trial cannot enlarge the archive.
boundary_notes: The insertion decision need not coincide with acceptance of every successful step.
Data-structure compression and approximate pruning are implementation variants, not part of the exact lifecycle.

notation.meaning: Indicator that the selected iteration contributes an archive entry.
Removal of entries dominated under the fixed margin relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Archive Initialization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize with an empty archive or one artificial upper-bound entry, then ensure all retained objective–infeasibility pairs are mutually nondominating.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial point \(x_0\), bounds \(\theta_{\max}>\theta(x_0)\) and \(f_{\max}>f(x_0)\), initialize either \(\mathcal F_0=\varnothing\) or the guarded filter \(\mathcal F_0=\{(\theta_{\max},f_{\max})\}\), according to the algorithm's safeguard convention. Before the first trial, remove any entry dominated by another entry. Output a finite archive \(\mathcal F_0\subset\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\) of mutually nondominating pairs. The empty convention imposes no initial filter restriction; the guarded convention excludes trials simultaneously worse than the prescribed bounds.
assumptions_latex: Any guard pair is chosen strictly worse than the initial pair in both coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_0\) is finite and contains no two distinct entries related by strict dominance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization of a finite nondominated objective–infeasibility archive.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the initialization leaf, but the record blends empty-filter and artificial-guard conventions without identifying the algorithm to which either applies. The claimed rejection effect of the guard also depends on whether plain dominance or margin-enlarged acceptance is used. A source is required before selecting and stating the applicable initialization rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Order Independence of Pruned Batch Insertion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential insert-and-prune operations on eligible pairs produce the nondominated frontier of their union regardless of order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F be a finite nondominated archive and Y a finite set of insertion-eligible pairs. Insert the members of Y in any order and replace the archive after each insertion by its nondominated subset. The final archive is \operatorname{ND}(F\cup Y), independently of insertion order.
assumptions_latex: F\subset\mathbb R^2\text{ is finite and nondominated}.
The same coordinatewise dominance relation is used throughout.
Every member of Y is eligible for archival.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_{\mathrm{final}}=\operatorname{ND}(F\cup Y).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Final archive after inserting a finite collection of eligible pairs.

notation.meaning: Finite batch of eligible accepted pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Entry Insertion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Insertion of an accepted pair while preserving a nondominated archive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite nondominated filter \(\mathcal F_k\) and an accepted pair \(y^+=(\theta^+,f^+)\). If some \(y\in\mathcal F_k\) satisfies \(y\preceq_D y^+\), leave the archive unchanged. Otherwise form \[\mathcal F_{k+1}=\bigl(\mathcal F_k\setminus\{y\in\mathcal F_k:y^+\prec_D y\}\bigr)\cup\{y^+\}.\] If the algorithm archives only feasibility-type iterations, perform this update only for that class and set \(\mathcal F_{k+1}=\mathcal F_k\) after objective-type acceptance. The output archive remains finite and mutually nondominating.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Insert an eligible accepted pair, delete entries it dominates, and optionally restrict insertion to feasibility-type iterations; nondominance is preserved.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_k\) is finite and mutually nondominating.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated update produces a finite mutually nondominating \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nondominance-preserving insertion update is mathematically coherent and algorithm is the appropriate kind. The optional restriction to feasibility-type iterations blends distinct archive policies, so an authoritative source must identify the intended eligibility and insertion convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Idempotence and Coverage of Nondominance Pruning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pruning an already nondominated archive changes nothing, and every original entry is covered by a retained frontier entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite archive A\subset\mathbb R^2, let \operatorname{ND}(A) be its coordinatewise nondominated subset. Then \operatorname{ND}(\operatorname{ND}(A))=\operatorname{ND}(A), and every a\in A is weakly dominated by some z\in\operatorname{ND}(A).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{ND}(\operatorname{ND}(A))=\operatorname{ND}(A).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural invariants of pruning a finite archive by coordinatewise dominance.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance-Based Filter Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Removal of dominated archive entries without changing its nondominated frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite archive \(A\subset\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\), compute \[\operatorname{ND}(A)=\{y\in A:\nexists z\in A\setminus\{y\}\text{ with }z\preceq_D y\}.\] Replace the archive by \(\operatorname{ND}(A)\); if duplicate pairs occur, retain one representative. The output is mutually nondominating. Moreover, for every removed \(y\in A\setminus\operatorname{ND}(A)\), some retained \(z\in\operatorname{ND}(A)\) satisfies \(z\preceq_D y\), so removing \(y\) does not enlarge the set accepted by the unmarginized dominance filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pruning retains precisely the nondominated frontier, removes duplicates, and discards entries whose rejection effect is already implied by a retained entry.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a finite set of objective–infeasibility pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ND}(A)\) is mutually nondominating and dominates every removed entry.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pruning algorithm correctly identifies the nondominated subset of a finite set and fits the terminal container. The claim about preserving the accepted set is explicitly limited to an unmarginized dominance filter and does not automatically extend to margin-enlarged filters; a cited source and precise variant scope are required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic invariants of repeatedly pruning a finite filter archive by coordinatewise dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite archive A\subset\mathbb R^2, let \operatorname{ND}(A) be its set of coordinatewise nondominated elements. Then \operatorname{ND}(\operatorname{ND}(A))=\operatorname{ND}(A). Moreover, every element of A is weakly dominated by some element of \operatorname{ND}(A).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once an archive has been reduced to its nondominated frontier, pruning it again changes nothing, and every original entry is represented by a retained dominating frontier entry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{ND}(\operatorname{ND}(A))=\operatorname{ND}(A).
knowledge_statements.title: Idempotence of Nondominance Pruning

children.title: Filter Archive Rebuild Regimes
children.top_down_role: Archive rebuilding after material changes in scaling, barrier parameters, or local models.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Filter Archive Rebuild Under a Changed Progress Map
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P_k:X\to\mathbb R^2\) be the progress map used at iteration \(k\), for example \(P_k(x)=(h_k(x),f_k(x))\), and let \(\mathcal A_k\subset X\) be stored archive representatives. Let \(D_k\) be the dominance relation induced by \(P_k\) and its margins.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract definition for rebuilding after a material change in scaling, barrier parameter, or local progress model; no inspected source states a canonical rebuild rule at this scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter archive rebuild at an index \(k\) where \((P_k,D_k)\ne(P_{k-1},D_{k-1})\) is the operation \[\mathcal F_k:=\operatorname{ND}_{D_k}\{P_k(x):x\in\mathcal A_k\},\] where \(\operatorname{ND}_{D_k}\) removes all entries dominated under the new relation. A cold rebuild takes \(\mathcal A_k=\varnothing\), hence \(\mathcal F_k=\varnothing\). A retained-point rebuild reevaluates every stored representative under \(P_k\). A transformed rebuild is admissible only when a map \(T_k\) satisfies \(P_k(x)=T_k(P_{k-1}(x))\) for every retained representative and preserves the comparisons required by \(D_k\). Reusing numerical pairs without reevaluation is not a rebuild unless their meanings and dominance relation are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rebuild replaces the archive by the nondominated image of retained representative points under the new progress coordinates and margins. It may discard all entries, reevaluate retained points, or transform old entries through an exact comparison-preserving map. Merely carrying old numerical pairs across a change in their meaning is excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_k=\operatorname{ND}_{D_k}\{P_k(x):x\in\mathcal A_k\}\) defines the rebuilt archive under the changed progress map.
special_cases_latex: A change of barrier parameter replaces a barrier-objective coordinate \(\phi_{\mu_{k-1}}\) by \(\phi_{\mu_k}\).
A positive diagonal rescaling may permit an exact transformed rebuild when it preserves all relevant inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every rebuilt entry has a meaning consistent with the current progress map.
Dominance is recomputed under the current margin convention.
boundary_notes: The inspected sources support initialization and dominance pruning but do not identify a canonical taxonomy of rebuilds after scaling, barrier, or model changes.
Whether old representatives remain valid is algorithm-specific.
review_flags: No inspected authoritative source supports the exact three-regime rebuild taxonomy or its scope across scaling, barrier parameters, and local models.
A precise source locator is required before candidate review.
knowledge_statements.title: Filter Archive Rebuild Under a Changed Progress Map
Model-Change Filter Resets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a model change makes archived comparisons incompatible, discard and reinitialize the filter; compatible changes may retain a recomputed, pruned archive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose iteration \(k\) replaces model state \(M_k\) by \(M_{k+1}\), and let \(C(M_k,M_{k+1})\) be a declared compatibility predicate guaranteeing that stored filter pairs retain their interpretation and acceptance margins. If \(C(M_k,M_{k+1})\) is false, discard \(\mathcal F_k\), recompute \((\theta_{k+1},f_{k+1})\) under the new model state, and initialize \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\) using the prescribed empty or guarded convention. If compatibility holds, retain \(\mathcal F_k\) and prune it after any required pair recomputation. No unrecomputed entry measured under an incompatible model is used for acceptance.
assumptions_latex: The model state determines the meanings or evaluations of archived coordinates.
A compatibility predicate is specified before the update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every entry used after the update is valid under \(M_{k+1}\) and the current acceptance convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archive reset after a change invalidates model-dependent acceptance comparisons.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is a plausible kind for this reset leaf, but the compatibility predicate and reset/recompute policy are framework-specific abstractions rather than a sourced mathematical procedure. A precise source is needed to define which model changes invalidate archived coordinates and which entries may be retained or recomputed.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Change Filter Resets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After acceptance parameters change, recompute and prune all stored filter entries; clear the archive when its entries cannot be evaluated consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the filter coordinates under parameter vector \(q\) be \(M_q(x)=(\theta_q(x),\phi_q(x))\), and suppose the archive stores trial points \(X_{\mathcal F}\). When \(q^-\) changes to \(q^+\), reevaluate \(M_{q^+}(x)\) for every \(x\in X_{\mathcal F}\), discard entries violating the new domain or eligibility rules, and retain only pairs not dominated componentwise by another reevaluated pair. Thus \[\mathcal F^+=\operatorname{Min}_{\preceq}\{M_{q^+}(x):x\in X_{\mathcal F},\ x\text{ is eligible under }q^+\}.\] If the stored data do not permit reevaluation, set \(\mathcal F^+=\varnothing\). Subsequent acceptance uses only \(q^+\) and \(\mathcal F^+\).
assumptions_latex: \(M_q:X\to\mathbb R^2\) is defined for every eligible stored point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F^+\) is a nondominated archive expressed entirely under the new parameter vector \(q^+\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reinitialization when changed parameters alter filter coordinates, margins, or dominance.

notation.meaning: Parameters determining filter coordinates or acceptance margins.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the reset-regime leaf, and the notation is internally coherent. However, no citation supports the prescribed reevaluation, eligibility pruning, nondominance convention, or mandatory empty-archive fallback; these are implementation-specific choices rather than a source-independent theorem.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary-Dominance Rebuild Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite ordinary Pareto archive, retained pairs must be mutually nondominating and every omitted pair must be dominated by a retained pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subset\mathbb R^2\) be the finite set of distinct reevaluated filter-coordinate pairs and write \(u\prec v\) when \(u\le v\) componentwise and \(u
e v\). A subset \(F\subseteq S\) equals the ordinary nondominated set \(\operatorname{Min}_{\prec}(S)\) if and only if \[ orall u,v\in F,\ u
e v\Rightarrow u
ot\prec v,\qquad  orall w\in S\setminus F\ \exists u\in F:\ u\prec w.\]
assumptions_latex: Dominance is ordinary componentwise dominance for minimization; no filter margins are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F=\operatorname{Min}_{\prec}(S)\iff F\text{ is pairwise nondominating and dominates every element of }S\setminus F.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite certificate for a rebuilt coordinate-pair archive under ordinary componentwise dominance, excluding margin-based conventions.

notation.meaning: Distinct filter-coordinate pairs reevaluated under the new scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Coordinate Archive Rebuild Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With retained residual vectors, scaled violations take linear work in archive size and residual dimension, while Pareto pruning takes sorting time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(N\) stored points retain objective values and residual vectors in \(\mathbb R^m\). New diagonally scaled norm violations require \(O(Nm)\) arithmetic. Sorting one filter coordinate and scanning the best value of the other extracts the two-coordinate nondominated subset in \(O(N\log N)\) comparisons. Thus the retained-data rebuild requires \[O(Nm+N\log N)\] work and \(O(N)\) auxiliary storage.
assumptions_latex: All residual vectors and objective values are retained.
Dominance is componentwise in two scalar coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rebuild requires \(O(Nm+N\log N)\) work and \(O(N)\) auxiliary storage.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost of reevaluating scaled violations and extracting a nondominated filter archive.
review_flags: tie handling must match the chosen dominance convention

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Constraint Scaling Can Reverse Violation Order
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive nonuniform constraint scaling can reverse violation rankings, so rebuilding generally requires residual vectors or fresh evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(x)=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\), \(c(y)=(0,2)^{\mathsf T}\), and use the Euclidean norm. Initially \[\|c(x)\|_2=1<2=\|c(y)\|_2.\] For \(D=\operatorname{diag}(3,1)\), \[\|Dc(x)\|_2=3>2=\|Dc(y)\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonuniform positive constraint scaling need not preserve violation ordering.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Example showing why old scalar violations cannot generally be rescaled without residual vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Invariance Under Common Positive Coordinate Rescaling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive monotone rescaling of both scalar filter coordinates preserves ordinary dominance and archive membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For filter pairs \(u=(\theta_u,\phi_u)\), \(v=(\theta_v,\phi_v)\), define \[T(\theta,\phi)=(\rho\theta,a\phi+b),\qquad \rho>0,\ a>0.\] Under componentwise minimization, \[u\preceq v\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T(u)\preceq T(v),\] with strict dominance preserved. Therefore the ordinary nondominated subset is invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ordinary nondominated subset is invariant under \((\theta,\phi)\mapsto(\rho\theta,a\phi+b)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling changes that preserve all ordinary componentwise dominance relations.
review_flags: filter margins need not be invariant unless transformed consistently

knowledge_statements.title: Data Required to Reconstruct Rescaled Violations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual vectors support arbitrary scaling rebuilds, whereas an old scalar violation generally supports only a common positive rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta_D(x)=\|Dc(x)\|\). Retaining \(c(x)\) permits exact computation of \(\theta_{D^+}(x)\) for every new scaling \(D^+\). If only \(\theta_{D^-}(x)\) is retained, exact scalar reconstruction is guaranteed when \(D^+=\rho D^-\) with \(\rho>0\), because \(\theta_{D^+}(x)=\rho\theta_{D^-}(x)\). For a general nonuniform change, the old scalar violation is insufficient in general; the residual vector or a fresh constraint evaluation is required.
assumptions_latex: The same norm is used before and after the scaling change.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D^+=\rho D^-\Rightarrow\theta_{D^+}(x)=\rho\theta_{D^-}(x);\quad\text{otherwise }\theta_{D^-}(x)\text{ is not generally sufficient}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary for rebuilding violation coordinates without new constraint evaluations.

notation.meaning: old and new positive diagonal residual scalings

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Change Archive Rebuilds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archive reconstruction after changing objective or constraint scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive diagonal constraint scaling \(D\), positive objective scaling \(a\), and offset \(b\), define \(\theta_D(x)=\|Dc(x)\|\) and \(\phi_{a,b}(x)=a f(x)+b\). If \((D^-,a^-,b^-)\) changes to \((D^+,a^+,b^+)\), reevaluate every stored point and rebuild \[\mathcal F^+=\operatorname{Min}_{\preceq}\{(\theta_{D^+}(x),\phi_{a^+,b^+}(x)):x\in X_{\mathcal F}\}.\] Componentwise constraint rescaling can reverse the ordering of violation measures, so merely relabeling old pairs is not generally valid. If stored points or their constraint vectors are unavailable, the consistent rebuild is the empty archive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing scaling requires reevaluating stored points and recomputing the nondominated archive; old scalar filter pairs may no longer have the correct ordering.
assumptions_latex: \(D^+\) is diagonal with strictly positive diagonal entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F^+\) contains precisely the nondominated stored points under the new scaling.

notation.meaning: Diagonal scaling of the constraint residual.
Positive affine scaling of the objective.
Points represented by the old archive.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the archive-rebuild leaf. The ordering observation is mathematically plausible, but the exact coordinate definitions, rebuild rule, and empty-archive fallback have no supporting citation and may vary across filter implementations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed finite consistency check for one sufficient-progress filter convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\gamma_\theta\in(0,1)\) and \(\gamma_\phi>0\), and define acceptability relative to \(u_i=(\theta_i,\phi_i)\) by \[A(u;u_i)\iff \theta\le(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\quad\text{or}\quad \phi\le\phi_i-\gamma_\phi\theta_i.\] The proposal declares a rebuilt archive consistent when retained entries are pairwise acceptable and every omitted stored entry fails \(A\) relative to at least one retained entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal checks pairwise margin acceptability and exclusion of omitted entries.
assumptions_latex: All stored points have been reevaluated under the new scaling.
The displayed non-strict margin convention is used.

children.title: Filter Method Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Filter globalization attached to major constrained-optimization frameworks.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interface Contract for a Filter-Globalized Method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a constrained optimization framework maintain a state \(q_k\in Q\), a primal iterate \(x_k\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and an archive \(\mathcal F_k\). Let \(G\) generate trial states and let \(P:Q\to\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\) provide infeasibility and objective-like coordinates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract interface shared by SQP, line-search, trust-region, and barrier implementations of filter globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter-method interface is a tuple \(\mathfrak I=(G,P,A,U,R)\) with typed maps \[G:Q\rightrightarrows Q,\quad P:Q\to\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R,\quad A:Q\times Q\times2^{\mathbb R^2}\to\{0,1\},\] \[U:2^{\mathbb R^2}\times\mathbb R^2\to2^{\mathbb R^2},\quad R:Q\rightrightarrows Q.\] For each normal iteration, \(q^+\in G(q_k)\); acceptance requires filter acceptability of \(P(q^+)\), together with any framework-specific switching or model-agreement condition encoded by \(A\). If accepted, the state is committed and the archive is updated by \(U\); if rejected, the framework reduces a step length or trust-region radius and retries. If ordinary trial generation becomes incompatible or globalization falls below its safeguard, \(R\) produces a state intended to reduce the first coordinate of \(P\) and return an archive-compatible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface consists of a trial-state generator, a two-coordinate progress map, an acceptance predicate, an archive update, and a restoration map. The host method supplies its SQP, trust-region, line-search, or barrier state; the filter sees only progress coordinates plus the host's model-agreement conditions. Rejection returns control to the host's step-control mechanism, while incompatibility invokes restoration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak I=(G,P,A,U,R)\) is a filter globalization interface when its maps satisfy the stated generation, acceptance, update, rejection, and restoration contract.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The filter is a globalization module whose required inputs are a progress pair and host-specific acceptance metadata.
special_cases_latex: For trust-region SQP, \(q_k\) includes \((x_k,\Delta_k)\) and rejection contracts \(\Delta_k\).
For line-search SQP, \(q^+\) contains \(x_k+\alpha p_k\) and rejection reduces \(\alpha\).
For a barrier method, the second progress coordinate may be a barrier objective.
immediate_consequences_latex: The same archive semantics can be coupled to different step generators.
Framework-specific model tests remain distinct from Pareto filter acceptability.
boundary_notes: This interface definition does not assert convergence for every choice of its component maps.
Multiplier, slack, and trust-region updates remain properties of the host framework.

source_refs.locator: Section 15.4, discussion after equation (15.33) and Algorithm 15.1

children.title: Trust-Region SQP Filters
children.top_down_role: Filter acceptance for restricted composite or SQP steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Linearized-Feasibility Radius Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact linearized feasibility is compatible with the trust region exactly when the radius reaches the minimum required normal-step norm; smaller radii require relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J_kp+c_k=0\) and \(\|p\|_2\le\Delta_k\), define \[\delta_k=\inf\{\|p\|_2:J_kp+c_k=0\},\] with \(\delta_k=+\infty\) if the affine equation is inconsistent. The combined constraints are feasible if and only if \(\delta_k\le\Delta_k\). If \(J_k\) has full row rank, the minimum-norm solution is \(p_k^N=-J_k^T(J_kJ_k^T)^{-1}c_k\), so \(\delta_k=\|p_k^N\|_2\). Contracting the radius below \(\delta_k\) makes the exact SQP subproblem infeasible; a relaxed or composite-step formulation must permit incomplete linearized feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The explicit minimum-norm formula assumes that \(J_k\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{p:J_kp+c_k=0,\ \|p\|_2\le\Delta_k\}\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\delta_k\le\Delta_k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating exact equality-constrained trust-region SQP from relaxed composite-step formulations.

notation.meaning: Minimum norm required for exact linearized feasibility.
Minimum-norm normal step under full row rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal–Tangential Composite-Step Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite-step trust-region SQP combines a normal feasibility step with a Jacobian-null tangential objective step and couples their radii.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A composite SQP step may be written \(p_k=n_k+t_k\), where \(n_k\) approximately reduces \(\|c_k+J_kn\|\) subject to \(\|n\|\le\Delta_k^N\), and \(t_k\) satisfies \(J_kt_k=0\) while reducing the objective model subject to \(\|n_k+t_k\|\le\Delta_k\). Then \(c_k+J_kp_k=c_k+J_kn_k\). Separate bounds imply the full-radius constraint whenever \(\Delta_k^N+\Delta_k^T\le\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c_k+J_kp_k=c_k+J_kn_k,\qquad \|n_k\|+\|t_k\|\le\Delta_k\Longrightarrow\|p_k\|\le\Delta_k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic decomposition used when exact linearized feasibility is incompatible with the trust-region radius.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider smooth constrained optimization on \(\mathbb R^n\). At \(x_k\), let \(m_k\) be a quadratic Lagrangian model, \(\Delta_k>0\) a trust-region radius, and \(h(x)\) a constraint-violation measure. Let \(\mathcal F_k\) be a filter archive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite-step trust-region SQP with filter acceptance and a feasibility-restoration phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region SQP filter method generates a normal step \(n_k\) reducing linearized infeasibility and a tangential step \(t_k\) reducing \(m_k\) without destroying the normal-step feasibility gain, with \(s_k=n_k+t_k\) and \(\|s_k\|\le\Delta_k\). The trial \(x_k+s_k\) must be acceptable for \(\mathcal F_k\cup\{(h_k,f_k)\}\). When the predicted model decrease \(\delta_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)\) satisfies \(\delta_k\ge\kappa_hh_k^2\), it must also satisfy \([f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)]/\delta_k\ge\eta_1\). Rejection leaves \(x_k\) unchanged and chooses \(\Delta_{k+1}<\Delta_k\); acceptance sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) and does not shrink the radius under the successful-step rule. If the trust-region SQP subproblem is incompatible, restoration seeks an acceptable point from which a compatible normal step exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region SQP filter combines a normal feasibility step and a tangential objective-model step inside a trust region. The resulting point must pass the filter; when predicted objective decrease is sufficiently large relative to infeasibility, it must also pass an actual-versus-predicted reduction test. Rejected steps shrink the radius. An incompatible subproblem sends the method to restoration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed composite-step generation, filter and ratio tests, radius update, and compatibility restoration define a trust-region SQP filter method.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A single-step SQP variant may replace the normal-tangential decomposition by one step satisfying an appropriate criticality-decrease condition.
special_cases_latex: At a feasible iterate, the normal step may be zero and the construction reduces locally to a tangential trust-region step with objective agreement testing.
immediate_consequences_latex: Filter rejection is handled by recomputing a step in a smaller trust region.
Restoration is triggered by incompatibility rather than by assigning an arbitrarily large penalty parameter.
boundary_notes: The definition does not specify a unique approximate solver for either step.
Global convergence additionally requires smoothness, boundedness, model-quality, and restoration hypotheses.

notation.meaning: Normal and tangential SQP step components.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region SQP Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generic equality-constrained trust-region SQP and filter interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and archive \(\mathcal F_k\), compute an SQP trial step \(p_k\) from a quadratic model subject to \(J_kp_k+c_k=0\) and \(\|p_k\|\le\Delta_k\), or from a compatible composite-step relaxation. The pair \((\theta(x_k+p_k),f(x_k+p_k))\) is filter acceptable when, for every \((\theta_i,\phi_i)\in\mathcal F_k\), \[\theta(x_k+p_k)\le(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\quad\text{or}\quad f(x_k+p_k)\le\phi_i-\gamma_\phi\theta(x_k+p_k).\] Accept only if this condition and the prescribed model-agreement test hold; otherwise reduce \(\Delta_k\), recompute the step, or invoke restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region SQP step must satisfy its radius, filter dominance margins, and the applicable model-agreement test before acceptance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\) only after filter and trust-region acceptance; otherwise the radius contracts or restoration begins.

notation.meaning: Constraint-violation measure, typically a norm of the residual.
Current archive of nondominated filter pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Local Filter Acceptability Ensures Finite Backtracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuity guarantees finite filter backtracking when the zero-step pair is strictly inside the acceptable region; boundary membership and extra decrease tests require additional analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) be the acceptable set induced by a fixed filter and fixed margins. Suppose \(\alpha\mapsto(\theta(x_k+\alpha p_k),f(x_k+\alpha p_k))\) is continuous at \(0\) and \((\theta(x_k),f(x_k))\in\operatorname{int}A\). Then some \(\bar\alpha>0\) makes every \(0\le\alpha\le\bar\alpha\) filter acceptable. Hence geometric backtracking \(\alpha_j=\beta^j\), \(0<\beta<1\), finds a filter-acceptable trial after finitely many reductions. If the current pair is not interior to \(A\), continuity alone gives no such conclusion; switching and sufficient-decrease tests must also be verified separately.
assumptions_latex: The filter and its margins remain fixed during backtracking.
The trial filter coordinates are continuous at zero step length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists j<\infty:\ (\theta(x_k+\beta^jp_k),f(x_k+\beta^jp_k))\in A.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for termination of geometric backtracking at the filter-acceptance layer.

notation.meaning: Acceptable region induced by the current filter and margins.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Acceptability Does Not Replace Directional Decrease
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An archive may accept every trial along an ascent direction while every positive step fails objective sufficient decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x\), \(\theta(x)=0\), \(x_k=0\), and \(p_k=1\). If the current filter imposes no restriction on these trial pairs, every \(x_k+\alpha p_k\) is filter acceptable. For \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), however, the Armijo condition becomes \(\alpha\le\sigma\alpha\), which fails for every \(\alpha>0\).
assumptions_latex: The current filter does not reject the displayed trial pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{filter acceptable for all }\alpha>0\quad\not\Rightarrow\quad\text{Armijo acceptable for any }\alpha>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between archive acceptability and objective sufficient decrease in line-search SQP.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p_k\) be an SQP direction at \(x_k\), let \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), and let \(x_k^+(\alpha)=x_k+\alpha p_k\). Let \(\mathcal F_k\) archive objective-infeasibility pairs and fix a minimum safeguarded step length \(\alpha_{\min}>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking line-search SQP in which a filter replaces a penalty merit function for primary step-length acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search SQP filter method selects \(\alpha_k\) from a decreasing backtracking sequence and accepts the first trial \(x_k^+(\alpha_k)\) that is acceptable to \(\mathcal F_k\), subject to any active objective switching condition. If the trial is rejected, \(\alpha\) is reduced and the same SQP direction is retested. If backtracking would produce \(\alpha<\alpha_{\min}\), ordinary line search terminates and a feasibility-restoration phase is invoked to seek a filter-compatible point with reduced constraint violation. On acceptance, \(x_{k+1}=x_k+lpha_kp_k\), and archive insertion and dominance deletion are performed according to the method's insertion rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A line-search SQP filter computes an SQP direction and backtracks along it until the trial point passes the filter and any active objective-decrease test. If the step length falls below a safeguard, the method stops backtracking and invokes feasibility restoration. Accepted points become new iterates and may update the archive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Filter acceptability determines the accepted backtracking step length, while \(\alpha<\alpha_{\min}\) triggers restoration.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The filter replaces the merit-function sufficient-decrease test in the inner SQP backtracking loop.
special_cases_latex: If \(\alpha_k=1\) is acceptable, the full SQP step is taken.
If no safeguarded step is acceptable, restoration replaces indefinite continuation of backtracking.
immediate_consequences_latex: The direction computation and the globalization acceptance test remain separate.
The safeguard rules out acceptance only at arbitrarily small step lengths without a phase change.
boundary_notes: The exact backtracking factor and switching condition are implementation-dependent.
A second-order correction may be attempted before backtracking but is not intrinsic to this definition.

notation.meaning: Safeguard below which restoration is invoked.

source_refs.locator: Section 15.4, paragraphs following equation (15.33), including the line-search backtracking and minimum-step restoration safeguard
Section 18.4, paragraph stating that a filter may be used in the inner line-search loop and restoration is invoked below the step-length threshold

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search SQP Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking SQP globalization using filter acceptance and a switching test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an SQP direction \(p_k\), choose \(0<\beta<1\) and test \(\alpha_j=\beta^j\), starting with \(j=0\). For \(x_{k,j}=x_k+\alpha_jp_k\), require that every \((\theta_i,\phi_i)\in\mathcal F_k\) satisfy \[\theta(x_{k,j})\le(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\quad\text{or}\quad f(x_{k,j})\le\phi_i-\gamma_\phi\theta(x_{k,j}).\] If the switching rule classifies the trial as objective-driven, also require the selected sufficient-decrease condition for \(f\) or the SQP model. Accept the first qualifying \(\alpha_j\); otherwise continue backtracking and invoke restoration if no admissible step is obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking selects the first SQP step length satisfying filter margins and, for objective-driven trials, a sufficient-decrease test.
assumptions_latex: \(p_k\) is an SQP search direction defined at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_jp_k\) for the first accepted index \(j\), or control passes to restoration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the line-search interface leaf. The backtracking structure is coherent, but the switching rule, sufficient-decrease condition, filter margins, and restoration trigger are method-dependent and are not supported by a cited filter-SQP source.

children.title: Interior-Point Filter Methods
children.top_down_role: Filter globalization for primal-dual barrier subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Filter Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual barrier step preserves positive slacks and must pass a feasibility–barrier-objective filter before acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For slack variables \(s>0\) and barrier parameter \(\mu>0\), define \(\phi_\mu(x,s)=f(x)-\mu\sum_i\log s_i\) and let \(\theta(x,s)\) measure primal equality residuals. Compute a primal-dual Newton direction \((p_x,p_s,p_y)\), then choose a fraction-to-boundary step \(\alpha\) satisfying \(s+\alpha p_s\ge(1-\tau)s\) componentwise for some \(0<\tau<1\). Accept the trial only when \((\theta(x+\alpha p_x,s+\alpha p_s),\phi_\mu(x+\alpha p_x,s+\alpha p_s))\) is acceptable to the current filter and any switching test holds. Otherwise shorten \(\alpha\) or enter restoration; rebuild the archive when \(\mu\) changes if its coordinates depend on \(\mu\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and the primal residual mapping are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted iterate has positive slacks and is acceptable in the filter coordinates associated with the current \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filter globalization for a fixed positive barrier parameter.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the interior-point filter leaf. The fixed-barrier description is plausible, but the primal residual map, switching test, restoration rule, and archive treatment when the barrier parameter changes depend on the particular method and require a specific source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For slack variables \(s\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\) and barrier parameter \(\mu>0\), define \(\phi_\mu(x,s)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log s_i\) and \(h(x,s)=\|(c_E(x),c_I(x)-s)\|\). Let \((p_x,p_s,p_y,p_z)\) be a primal-dual search direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filter globalization of a fixed-parameter primal-dual barrier subproblem with strictly positive slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An interior-point filter method forms its archive from pairs \((h(x,s),\phi_\mu(x,s))\). It selects primal and dual step lengths \(\alpha_s\in(0,\alpha_s^{\max}]\) and \(\alpha_z\in(0,\alpha_z^{\max}]\), maintaining positivity, and proposes \[x^+=x+lpha_sp_x,\quad s^+=s+lpha_sp_s,\quad y^+=y+lpha_zp_y,\quad z^+=z+lpha_zp_z.\] The primal trial is accepted only if \((h(x^+,s^+),\phi_\mu(x^+,s^+))\) is not excluded by the filter and satisfies any active switching test. Rejection reduces the primal step length or invokes restoration under the method's safeguard. When \(\mu\) changes, the barrier-objective coordinate changes and archive handling must be specified by the implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interior-point filter uses the barrier objective and primal residual norm as its two progress coordinates. Fraction-to-the-boundary limits keep slacks and dual variables positive, while a backtracking step is accepted only if its new progress pair passes the filter and any switching test. Repeated rejection may invoke restoration. Because changing the barrier parameter changes one filter coordinate, archive treatment across barrier subproblems must be explicit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((h,\phi_\mu)\), positivity-preserving primal-dual step, and filter test define the fixed-parameter interior-point filter interface.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The construction applies an objective-infeasibility filter to the equality-constrained slack formulation of the barrier subproblem.
special_cases_latex: With fixed \(\mu\), archive comparisons use a common barrier objective.
If the filter is inactive locally, the method accepts the primal-dual steps according to its local barrier algorithm.
immediate_consequences_latex: Objective progress is measured by \(\phi_\mu\), not by the original objective \(f\) alone.
Constraint violation includes both equality residuals and slack-form inequality residuals.
boundary_notes: The source does not prescribe a unique archive rebuild when \(\mu\) changes.
Centrality and complementarity safeguards are additional to filter acceptability.

notation.meaning: Norm of equality and slack-form inequality residuals.

source_refs.locator: Section 19.4, equations (19.27)–(19.28) and the following paragraph defining filter pairs from the barrier function and constraint violations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barrier Residual Certificate and Original-KKT Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual test distinguishing solution of a fixed-barrier subproblem from approximate KKT satisfaction for the original NLP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(r_p=(c(x),g(x)+s)\), \(r_d=\nabla f(x)+J_c(x)^Ty+J_g(x)^Tz\), and \(r_c=Sz-\mu e\). With \(s>0\) and \(z>0\), \(r_p=r_d=r_c=0\) certifies satisfaction of the primal-dual KKT equations for the barrier parameter \(\mu\). It does not certify complementary slackness for the original NLP when \(\mu>0\), because then \(s_i z_i=\mu\). An approximate original-KKT test must additionally require \(\mu\) or \(\|Sz\|\) to be small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero primal, dual, and perturbed-complementarity residuals solve the fixed-barrier equations; original-NLP KKT accuracy additionally requires small complementarity or a small barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_p=r_d=r_c=0\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{fixed-barrier KKT},\qquad \mu>0\ \Longrightarrow\ Sz\ne0.
knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Residual Certificate and Original-KKT Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-independent primal-dual equations underlying a filter-globalized logarithmic-barrier step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)+s=0\) with \(s>0\), the logarithmic-barrier subproblem with parameter \(\mu>0\) has primal-dual equations \[\nabla f(x)+J_c(x)^Ty+J_g(x)^Tz=0,\qquad c(x)=0,\qquad g(x)+s=0,\qquad Sz=\mu e,\qquad s>0,\ z>0.\] Newton linearization gives \[\begin{bmatrix}H&J_c^T&J_g^T&0\\J_c&0&0&0\\J_g&0&0&I\\0&0&S&Z\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p_x\\p_y\\p_z\\p_s\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}r_d\\c\\g+s\\Sz-\mu e\end{bmatrix},\] where \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2(f+y^Tc+z^Tg)\). A filter globalizes the primal trial generated from this system; it does not replace these barrier KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interior-point filters globalize Newton steps for the fixed-barrier primal-dual KKT equations coupling stationarity, primal feasibility, positivity, and perturbed complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c,g\) are twice continuously differentiable at the linearization point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The displayed block system is the Newton linearization of the fixed-}\mu\text{ primal-dual barrier equations}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Barrier Primal-Dual KKT System

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global and Local Filter Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\{x_k\}\) be generated by a filter-globalized constrained method, let \(h_k=h(x_k)\), and let \(\chi_k\ge0\) be a first-order criticality measure satisfying \(h(x_*)=0\) and \(\chi(x_*)=0\) exactly at feasible first-order critical points within the stated regularity regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Taxonomy of convergence regimes; it distinguishes global subsequential alternatives from eventual local inactivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convergence regime of a filter run is classified as follows. It is a feasible-stationary global regime if there exists \(k_j\to\infty\) with \(h_{k_j}\to0\), \(\chi_{k_j}\to0\), and \(x_{k_j}\to x_*\). It is a restoration-failure regime if restoration terminates at an infeasible first-order stationary point of \(\min h(x)\). It is an eventual-inactivity regime if there exists \(K\) such that no iteration \(k\ge K\) inserts a pair into the filter and every sufficiently local trial accepted by the underlying method also passes the filter. It is a fast-local regime when eventual inactivity holds and the underlying SQP or primal-dual iteration retains its stated superlinear or quadratic local rate. These labels concern logically distinct conclusions and require their respective algorithmic hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter run may have a subsequence approaching feasible first-order stationarity, may terminate restoration at an infeasible stationary point of the violation measure, or may eventually stop using the archive as an active restriction. In the last case, a fast local rate belongs to the underlying constrained method and is retained only when its local assumptions and eventual acceptance conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family comprises feasible-stationary, restoration-failure, eventual-inactivity, and fast-local regimes defined by the stated quantified sequence properties.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eventual archive inactivity means that the set of later insertion indices is finite.
special_cases_latex: An infinite subsequence of archive insertions may itself satisfy \(h_{k_j}\to0\) and \(\chi_{k_j}\to0\).
If only finitely many points enter the archive, restoration iterations are finite in the cited trust-region SQP framework.
immediate_consequences_latex: Global subsequential convergence does not by itself assert convergence of the full sequence.
A filter globalization does not automatically supply a local convergence rate.
boundary_notes: The local fast-rate regime needs regularity, accurate Hessian information, and often second-order correction.
Failure of restoration is an allowed global alternative, not a feasible-stationary conclusion.

notation.meaning: Index after which the filter is inactive.

children.title: Feasible Stationary Filter Limits
children.top_down_role: Filter convergence toward constrained stationary points.

knowledge_statements.title: A Feasible Limit Need Not Be Stationary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence to feasibility alone does not imply stationarity; a criticality or stationarity residual must also vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2} x\) subject to \(y=0\). The constant sequence \((x_k,y_k)=(0,0)\) is feasible and converges to \((0,0)\), but no multiplier \(\lambda\) satisfies \((1,0)+\lambda(0,1)=(0,0)\). Hence its limit is feasible but not a KKT point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(x_k,y_k)=0\ \forall k\quad\not\Rightarrow\quad (0,0)\text{ is a KKT point}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary showing that feasibility convergence alone cannot establish the stationary-filter-limit conclusion.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)\ge0\). Let \(h(x)\ge0\) vanish exactly on the feasible set, and let \(\chi(x)\ge0\) be a continuous first-order criticality measure appropriate to the constraint qualification used by the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the limit object appearing in global convergence results for finite-dimensional smooth filter SQP methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A point \(x_*\in\mathbb R^n\) is a feasible stationary filter limit of a sequence \(\{x_k\}\) if there exists an infinite index sequence \(k_j	o\infty\) such that \[x_{k_j}	o x_*,\qquad h(x_{k_j})	o0,\qquad \chi(x_{k_j})	o0.\] Consequently \(h(x_*)=0\), and \(\chi(x_*)=0\) expresses first-order criticality. Under a constraint qualification admitting KKT multipliers, this means that there exist multipliers \((\lambda_*,
u_*)\) with \[
abla f(x_*)-J_E(x_*)^T\lambda_*-J_I(x_*)^T
u_*=0,\quad c_E(x_*)=0,\quad c_I(x_*)\ge0,\quad 
u_*\ge0,\quad 
u_{*,i}c_{I,i}(x_*)=0.\] The term “limit” is subsequential unless full-sequence convergence is separately established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible stationary filter limit is an accumulation point reached along a subsequence on which constraint violation and a first-order criticality measure both vanish. With an appropriate constraint qualification, the point satisfies the KKT feasibility, stationarity, dual-feasibility, and complementarity conditions. The definition does not claim that every iterate converges to that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_*\) is a feasible stationary filter limit exactly when it is the limit of a subsequence with \(h_{k_j}\to0\) and \(\chi_{k_j}\to0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under the stated multiplier qualification, the limiting conditions are equivalent to the displayed KKT system.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, the complementarity and sign conditions disappear.
If \(\chi(x)=\|\nabla_xL(x,y^{\mathrm{LS}}(x))\|\), vanishing \(\chi\) gives Lagrangian stationarity with least-squares multipliers.
immediate_consequences_latex: The limit is feasible because \(h\) is continuous and vanishes only on the feasible set.
Subsequential stationarity permits other accumulation points unless further hypotheses exclude them.
boundary_notes: Without a constraint qualification, first-order criticality need not admit the displayed KKT multipliers.
Restoration may instead converge to an infeasible stationary point of \(h\).

source_refs.locator: Section 15.5.4, Theorem 15.5.13 and preceding limits for infeasibility and criticality; Section 15.5.5, Theorem 15.5.14

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Stationary Filter Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract KKT limit statement for equality-constrained filter iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(f,c\) continuously differentiable. Let a bounded filter-generated sequence \(\{x_k\}\) satisfy \(\|c(x_k)\|\to0\), and suppose there are multipliers \(\lambda_k\) such that \[\|\nabla f(x_k)+J(x_k)^\mathsf T\lambda_k\|\to0.\] If \(x_{k_j}\to x_*\), the multipliers \(\lambda_{k_j}\) are bounded, and \(J(x_*)\) has full row rank, then every convergent multiplier subsequence \(\lambda_{k_{j_\ell}}\to\lambda_*\) satisfies \[c(x_*)=0,\qquad \nabla f(x_*)+J(x_*)^\mathsf T\lambda_*=0.\] Hence \(x_*\) is a feasible first-order stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing infeasibility and Lagrangian-gradient residuals imply that every regular accumulation point is a feasible KKT point.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c\in C^1\) near the bounded iterate sequence.
\(\|c(x_k)\|\to0\) and the Lagrangian-gradient residual tends to zero.
\(J(x_*)\) has full row rank and the relevant multipliers are bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(x_*)=0\) and \(\nabla f(x_*)+J(x_*)^\mathsf T\lambda_*=0\).

notation.meaning: Accumulation point of the filter-generated iterates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the convergence-limit leaf, and the stated limiting KKT implication is mathematically sound under the explicit residual and subsequence assumptions. Nevertheless, those assumptions are simply imposed rather than derived from a filter method, and no cited filter-convergence result supports the claimed local context.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inequality-Constrained KKT Limit from Vanishing Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic continuity passage from assumed residual convergence to the KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\), a convergent primal-multiplier subsequence with nonnegative inequality multipliers and vanishing feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity residuals has a KKT limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assumed convergence of all KKT residuals passes to the KKT equations at a finite limit.
assumptions_latex: The primal and multiplier subsequence converges finitely.
The KKT residuals vanish and inequality multipliers are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x_*,\lambda_*,\mu_*)\text{ satisfies the KKT conditions}.
knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Constrained KKT Limit from Vanishing Residuals

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns filter-specific guarantees that feasible accumulation points are stationary and the assumptions delimiting that conclusion. The accepted counterexample supplies the feasibility-only boundary. Generic KKT continuity arguments are deferred as belonging to general KKT-limit theory; restoration failure, archive inactivity, and correction mechanisms are excluded to sibling scopes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalized Fritz–John Alternative at a Filter Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic abnormal-multiplier limit statement proposed for a filter-limit leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k_j}\to x_*\), \(c(x_{k_j})\to0\), and suppose normalized pairs satisfy \(\alpha_j\ge0\), \(\alpha_j^2+\|\lambda_j\|^2=1\), and \(\alpha_j\nabla f(x_{k_j})+J(x_{k_j})^{\mathsf T}\lambda_j\to0\). Any convergent multiplier subsequence has a nonzero Fritz–John limit. Full row rank rules out \(\alpha_*=0\) and yields KKT stationarity after normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized residual convergence gives a generic Fritz–John limit, with regularity recovering KKT stationarity.
assumptions_latex: The normalized residual converges to zero.
A convergent normalized multiplier subsequence is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limit is Fritz–John stationary; full row rank implies KKT stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Fritz–John Alternative at a Filter Limit
