knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Evaluation-Complexity Tuple
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative order alone does not define a restoration complexity class; target criticality, tolerances, oracle accounting, outcomes, and total count must also be fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restoration evaluation-complexity claim may be indexed by (p,q,\varepsilon,\mathcal O,\mathcal S,N): derivatives through order p are admitted, order-q criticality is requested, \varepsilon gives tolerances, \mathcal O declares counted exact or approximate oracle calls, \mathcal S declares successful-feasibility and stationary-violation outcomes, and N bounds all counted calls through termination. Claims with different \mathcal O or \mathcal S are not directly comparable.
assumptions_latex: The restoration objective and termination predicates are defined.
Approximate or stochastic oracle requirements are included in \mathcal O.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathfrak C=(p,q,\varepsilon,\mathcal O,\mathcal S,N).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Taxonomy separating information order, target, oracle, outcomes, and count.

knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Evaluation-Complexity Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-based classification of restoration evaluation guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the restoration problem \\(\min_x v(x)\\), an evaluation-complexity family is indexed by an order \\(q\ge1\\), a tolerance vector \\(\varepsilon\\), an oracle specification, and a worst-case bound \\(N_q(\varepsilon)\\). Membership means that, after at most \\(N_q(\varepsilon)\\) permitted evaluations of \\(v\\) and its derivatives through order \\(q\\), the method returns either an accepted feasibility outcome or a point satisfying its stated order-\\(q\\) stationarity test. First-order families use values and gradients; second- and higher-order families additionally use Hessians or higher derivatives, Hessian-vector products, or approved approximations. Bounds from different oracle models or termination predicates are not directly interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration complexity is classified by derivative order, oracle, termination tolerance, and worst-case evaluation bound; counts are comparable only when oracle and outcome conventions agree.
assumptions_latex: The restoration objective and its admissible oracle are explicitly specified.
The termination predicate is computable from the allowed evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A complexity claim is identified by the tuple \\((q,\varepsilon,\text{oracle},N_q)\\), not by derivative order alone.

notation.meaning: Highest derivative order used by the family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation appropriately describes a classification leaf, but the asserted evaluation-complexity family conventions lack a source. The meanings of order-q stationarity, permitted approximations, evaluation counting, and accepted feasibility outcomes must be tied to a specific complexity framework.

children.title: Restoration Variant-Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Information regimes, scale regimes, and characteristic restoration failures.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c_E:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_E}\), and \(c_I:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_I}\) define a nonlinear program with \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)\ge 0\). Let \(h(x)=\|c_E(x)\|+\|[c_I(x)]_-\|\). A restoration phase seeks a trial point \(z\) having smaller \(h\) than its reference point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional restoration phases are classified by information and computational regime, separately from the mathematical obstruction encountered. This is a candidate formalization because the inspected source supports restoration but not the complete taxonomy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restoration episode is represented by \(R=(x,\mathcal O,\mathcal M,\tau,z,s)\), where \(\mathcal O\) is the available function/derivative oracle, \(\mathcal M\) is the restoration model, \(\tau\) is its termination tolerance, \(z\) is its output, and \(s\) is its termination status. Its variant label is \(V(R)\subseteq\{\mathrm{imperfect\ information},\mathrm{large\ scale},\mathrm{inexact\ solve}\}\). Its failure label is \(F(R)\subseteq\{\mathrm{rank\ deficient},\mathrm{model\ inconsistent},\mathrm{insufficient\ progress},\mathrm{positive\ residual\ stationary}\}\), with membership defined respectively by unavailable or inaccurate oracle data; matrix-free, sparse, or residual-terminated solution of \(\mathcal M\); deficient rank of the restoration linearization; infeasibility of the local restoration model; failure of \(h(z)\le h(x)-\sigma\Delta_h\) for the required \(\sigma\in(0,1)\); or termination at \(h(z)>0\) with an applicable first-order residual at most \(\tau\). The taxonomy is the pair \(\mathfrak T(R)=(V(R),F(R))\), so a computational variant and a failure class may occur simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restoration episode consists of its reference point, available oracle, local feasibility model, stopping tolerance, output, and status. Its variant labels record imperfect information, large-scale structure, or an inexact solve. Its failure labels record rank deficiency, inconsistency of the local model, failure of the prescribed violation decrease, or termination at a positive stationary residual. The taxonomy is the ordered pair of these label sets, allowing one episode to have both a regime label and a failure label.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) vanishes exactly at feasible points.
\(\Delta_h\ge0\) denotes the progress predicted or required by the restoration mechanism.
A stationarity residual is included only when the selected restoration model supplies a well-defined first-order condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak T(R)=(V(R),F(R))\in 2^{\mathcal V}\times2^{\mathcal F}\), with variant and failure labels assigned by the stated oracle, scale, model-geometry, progress, and stationarity conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The taxonomy may be viewed as a product classification \(\mathcal R\to2^{\mathcal V}\times2^{\mathcal F}\), rather than as mutually exclusive branches.
special_cases_latex: With exact derivatives and an accurately solved dense model, \(V(R)=\varnothing\), although \(F(R)\) may still be nonempty.
If \(h(z)=0\), neither insufficient-progress nor positive-residual-stationary failure applies.
immediate_consequences_latex: A positive stationary residual is not, by definition alone, a certificate that the original nonlinear constraint system is globally infeasible.
Rank deficiency and model inconsistency are geometry failures; inexact computation alone is a regime label.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe a particular restoration objective, norm, or step-acceptance test.
No inspected source was found that canonically presents this complete product taxonomy.
review_flags: The inspected restoration source supports violation minimization and restoration triggers but not this complete variant–failure taxonomy.
A precise authoritative locator for the taxonomy is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Variant–Failure Taxonomy

children.title: Imperfect-Information Restoration Family
children.top_down_role: Restoration under unavailable, noisy, or controllably inaccurate derivative information.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) measure constraint violation. At restoration iteration \(j\), only approximations \(\widetilde h_j\), \(\widetilde c_j\), and an approximate Jacobian action \(\widetilde J_jv\) may be available.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic or conditionally deterministic restoration with unavailable, noisy, derivative-free, or controllably inaccurate information. Stochastic distributional guarantees are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restoration method belongs to the imperfect-information family if, for every restoration iteration \(j\), its model \(m_j(s)\) and acceptance test are constructed from an oracle \(\mathcal O_j\) satisfying stated error bounds \(|\widetilde h_j(x)-h(x)|\le\delta^h_j\), \(\|\widetilde c_j(x)-c(x)\|\le\delta^c_j\), and, when derivative information is used, \(\|\widetilde J_jv-J(x_j)v\|\le\delta^J_j\|v\|\) on the trial region. A trial step \(s_j\) is admissible only if its computed decrease exceeds the uncertainty margin, for example \(\widetilde h_j(x_j)-\widetilde h_j(x_j+s_j)>2\delta^h_j\), or if an equivalent certified error-aware test holds. The information is controllably inaccurate when the method can request tolerances with \(\delta^h_j,\delta^c_j,\delta^J_j\downarrow0\) as its restoration tolerance decreases. Derivative-free restoration is the special case in which \(\widetilde J_j\) is absent and the model is built solely from evaluated constraint residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An imperfect-information restoration method builds its feasibility model and acceptance decision from approximate values or derivative actions with explicit error bounds. A computed decrease is credited only when it is larger than the uncertainty that could reverse its sign, or when another certified error-aware test is used. Information is controllably inaccurate if the algorithm can tighten its requested errors toward zero. Derivative-free restoration is included by omitting Jacobian information entirely.
assumptions_latex: Every oracle quantity used by the acceptance test has a declared deterministic error bound on the relevant trial region.
If errors are controllable, requested tolerances can be reduced without changing the constraint system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family consists precisely of restoration procedures whose models and acceptance decisions use bounded imperfect oracle data and whose credited progress is certified relative to those bounds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a value-only test, \(\widetilde h_j(x_j+s_j)+\delta^h_j<\widetilde h_j(x_j)-\delta^h_j\) is equivalent to strict worst-case decrease under the symmetric error bound.
special_cases_latex: A finite-difference restoration model has \(\delta^J_j\) determined by differencing and evaluation errors.
A derivative-free interpolation model belongs to the family when its residual-model error is bounded on the trust region.
immediate_consequences_latex: An apparent decrease smaller than the uncertainty margin cannot by itself certify true feasibility progress.
Exact-information restoration is recovered when all error bounds vanish.
boundary_notes: Unbiased stochastic estimates without deterministic or high-probability error certification are not covered.
No inspected source supplied an exact locator for this restoration-specific definition.
review_flags: The available derivative-free and inexact-solve hints did not establish this restoration-specific family.
A source supporting the error-aware acceptance scope is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Imperfect-Information Restoration Method
Positive-Spanning Poll Restoration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct-search restoration polls a uniformly well-spread direction set for sufficient violation decrease and shrinks the scale after an unsuccessful poll.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given x_k, \alpha_k>0, and a finite positive-spanning set D_k, poll points x_k+\alpha_kd until finding v(x_k+\alpha_kd)\le v(x_k)-c\alpha_k^2. On success accept such a point and update \alpha_k by the declared success rule; if no direction succeeds, retain x_k and contract \alpha_k. Stop at the feasibility tolerance or the declared polling criticality scale.
assumptions_latex: Violation values are available without derivative evaluations.
The cosine measures of D_k are uniformly positive.
The step-size update factors and stopping rule are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{successful poll}\Rightarrow v(x_{k+1})\le v(x_k)-c\alpha_k^2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-search restoration branch using exact violation values.

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Linear Violation-Model Accuracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully linear derivative-free violation model has quadratic value error and linear gradient error throughout its trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A differentiable model \(m_k\) of a differentiable violation function \(v\) is fully linear on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\) if uniform constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g\) satisfy \(|v(x_k+s)-m_k(s)|\le\kappa_f\Delta_k^2\) and \(\|\nabla v(x_k+s)-\nabla m_k(s)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k\) for every \(\|s\|\le\Delta_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(v\) and \(m_k\) are differentiable on the trust region.
The constants are uniform over modeled iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |v-m_k|=O(\Delta_k^2),\qquad\|\nabla v-\nabla m_k\|=O(\Delta_k)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy condition for model-based derivative-free restoration.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional First-Order Derivative-Free Restoration Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform epsilon-squared decrease yields an order epsilon-to-the-minus-two successful-iteration bound, but not automatically an evaluation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every successful noncritical iteration with \|\nabla v(x_k)\|>\varepsilon decreases v by at least \kappa\varepsilon^2 and v\ge v_{\inf}, then the number of such successful iterations is at most \lceil(v(x_0)-v_{\inf})/(\kappa\varepsilon^2)\rceil. An evaluation bound additionally requires explicit bounds for polling, model construction, geometry repair, and unsuccessful iterations.
assumptions_latex: v is bounded below on the generated level set.
Evaluation claims separately account for all sampled and rejected trials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{succ}}(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^{-2}).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional successful-iteration bound for a smooth violation objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Unpoised Samples Do Not Determine a Reliable Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular sample geometry prevents values from determining a unique restoration model or direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the polynomial interpolation matrix for the sample set is singular, distinct coefficient vectors interpolate the same values. Consequently the local violation model, its gradient, and a model-minimizing restoration direction are not uniquely determined by those samples.
assumptions_latex: The model is constructed by polynomial interpolation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}M_k<\dim(M_k)\Rightarrow\text{nonunique interpolation coefficients}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry failure for interpolation-based derivative-free restoration.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Free Restoration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-based restoration using constraint values but no derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \\(x_k\\), radius \\(\Delta_k>0\\), and sampled values of \\(c\\), construct a derivative-free model \\(m_k(s)\\) of \\(v(x_k+s)=\tfrac12\|c(x_k+s)\|^2\\) on \\(\|s\|\le\Delta_k\\). Approximately minimize \\(m_k\\) over that ball to obtain \\(s_k\\), evaluate \\(v(x_k+s_k)\\), and compute the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio. Accept \\(x_k+s_k\\) when the ratio exceeds a prescribed threshold; otherwise retain \\(x_k\\). Update \\(\Delta_k\\) by the trust-region agreement rule and improve the sample geometry whenever the model's poisedness condition fails. Stop at feasibility tolerance or a derivative-free model-stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a local violation model from constraint values, minimize it in a trust region, accept by reduction agreement, and repair sample geometry when the interpolation set is inadequate.
assumptions_latex: Constraint values can be sampled, but derivatives are unavailable or intentionally unused.
The sample set supports the stipulated interpolation or regression model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restoration iteration uses no derivative evaluations and globalizes progress through model agreement and radius control.

A derivative-free trust-region or derivative-free constrained-restoration source with a specific locator is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder-proposed theorem combining model-based and polling frameworks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The builder asserts a common liminf or full-gradient convergence result for fully linear trust-region models and positive-spanning polling under broad framework descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two branches have different algorithms and safeguards; a single generic theorem without precise update and criticality conditions is not validated.
assumptions_latex: The model-based and polling algorithms, criticality safeguards, and unsuccessful-iteration rules are not fully specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Claim deferred pending separate framework-specific convergence theorems.}
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Free Restoration Criticality

intermediate_metadata.reason: Locally owned content is fully linear value-based modeling, interpolation geometry, positive-spanning polling, the singular-geometry failure, and a conditional successful-iteration count. The combined convergence theorem is deferred. Noisy and controllably inexact evaluation regimes are excluded as siblings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: True-gradient bound obtained from an unsuccessful sufficient-decrease poll.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\nabla v\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz near \(x\), every \(d\in D\) has \(\|d\|=1\), and \(D\) has cosine measure \(\mu>0\): for every nonzero \(g\), some \(d\in D\) satisfies \(g^Td\le-\mu\|g\|\). If no poll point satisfies \(v(x+\alpha d)\le v(x)-c\alpha^2\), then \[\|\nabla v(x)\|<\frac{c+L/2}{\mu}\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure of every well-spread poll direction to achieve quadratic sufficient decrease certifies first-order violation criticality at the polling scale.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla v\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on every tested segment.
\(D\) consists of unit directions with cosine measure at least \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall d\in D:\ v(x+\alpha d)>v(x)-c\alpha^2\Rightarrow\|\nabla v(x)\|<\mu^{-1}(c+L/2)\alpha.

notation.meaning: cosine measure of the polling set

knowledge_statements.title: Unsuccessful Positive-Spanning Poll Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of model criticality to true violation criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(m_k\) is fully linear for differentiable \(v\) on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\), so that \(\|
abla v(x_k)-
abla m_k(0)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k\), then \[\|
abla v(x_k)\|\le\|
abla m_k(0)\|+\kappa_g\Delta_k.\] Hence \(\|
abla m_k(0)\|\le\varepsilon_m\) and \(\kappa_g\Delta_k\le\varepsilon-\varepsilon_m\) certify \(\|
abla v(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small model gradient certifies a small true violation gradient only when the fully linear modeling error is also small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\nabla m_k(0)\|\le\varepsilon_m\ \land\ \kappa_g\Delta_k\le\varepsilon-\varepsilon_m\Rightarrow\|\nabla v(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Fully Linear Model-Gradient Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle definition and principal derivative-free restoration branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivative-free restoration method decreases a declared violation function \(v\) using value evaluations but no supplied derivatives of \(v\) or the constraints. Two principal subclasses are model-based restoration, which constructs value-based local models satisfying declared accuracy conditions, and direct-search restoration, which tests directions from a uniformly well-spread polling set at a controlled scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative-free restoration uses violation values without supplied derivatives; prominent realizations use accurate value-based models or well-spread direct-search polls.
assumptions_latex: Violation values are available at admissible trial points.
No derivative oracle is used by the restoration step generator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal R_{\mathrm{model}}\cup\mathcal R_{\mathrm{poll}}\subseteq\mathcal R_{\mathrm{DF}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Free Restoration Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-evaluation order for smooth criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the smoothness, uniform fully-linear-model or positive-spanning geometry, sufficient-decrease, and unsuccessful-iteration accounting assumptions of the selected framework, a derivative-free restoration method reaches \(\|\nabla v(x)\|\le\varepsilon\) after \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) successful iterations. If each iteration uses a uniformly bounded number of violation evaluations, the same order holds for evaluations; interpolation methods must additionally count geometry-repair samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth derivative-free restoration has the standard epsilon-to-the-minus-two first-order iteration order, with evaluation counts depending on polling or model-repair cost.
assumptions_latex: The conditions of the derivative-free criticality theorem hold.
Successful iterations yield decrease proportional to the squared criticality scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{succ}}(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^{-2}).
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Derivative-Free Restoration Bound
Interval-Certified Acceptance and Rejection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceptance or rejection is certified only when the entire possible true-reduction interval lies on one side of the threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=v(x_k)-v(x_k+s_k)\), \(\widetilde A=\widetilde v(x_k)-\widetilde v(x_k+s_k)\), and \(E=e(x_k)+e(x_k+s_k)\). Then \(A\in[\widetilde A-E,\widetilde A+E]\). For predicted reduction \(P_k>0\) and threshold \(\eta\), acceptance is certified if \(\widetilde A-E\ge\eta P_k\), rejection if \(\widetilde A+E<\eta P_k\), and neither otherwise.
assumptions_latex: Both endpoint error bounds are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\in[\widetilde A-E,\widetilde A+E]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decision certificate for a ratio test with bounded evaluation errors.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Inexact Violation Evaluation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact violation value is accompanied by a valid deterministic error bound, optionally reducible on request.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact violation evaluation is a pair \((\widetilde v(z),e(z))\) satisfying \(|\widetilde v(z)-v(z)|\le e(z)\), where the algorithm may request a smaller bound when the oracle supports refinement.
assumptions_latex: The reported error bounds are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(z)\in[\widetilde v(z)-e(z),\widetilde v(z)+e(z)]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic, certifiably bounded evaluation regime for restoration.

knowledge_statements.title: Irreducible Error Creates a Decision Dead Zone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero error floor creates an unresolved band around the acceptance threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the smallest attainable combined error is \(E_{\min}>0\), then \(|\widetilde A-\eta P_k|\le E_{\min}\) leaves the true reduction interval intersecting the acceptance boundary, so the bounded-error test certifies neither acceptance nor rejection.
assumptions_latex: Only the stated deterministic bounds are available.
The combined error cannot be reduced below \(E_{\min}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\widetilde A-\eta P_k|\le E_{\min}\Rightarrow\text{decision unresolved}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary when evaluation accuracy cannot be refined.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Evaluation Restoration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy condition ensuring reliable restoration acceptance decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(\widetilde v_k(x)\\) be an inexact evaluation of \\(v(x)\\), with a computable bound \\(e_k(x)\\) satisfying \\( |\widetilde v_k(x)-v(x)|\le e_k(x)\\). For a trial step \\(s_k\\) with predicted decrease \\(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\\), the evaluation accuracy is acceptance-compatible when \\[e_k(x_k)+e_k(x_k+s_k)\le\omega\operatorname{pred}_k\] for a fixed \\(\omega\\) smaller than the separation between the acceptance threshold and the relevant ratio boundary. Under this condition, lower and upper bounds on the true actual reduction can determine acceptance or rejection; if the bounds straddle the threshold, evaluations must be refined before deciding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluation errors must be small relative to predicted progress. If certified error intervals cannot resolve the acceptance test, the constraint evaluations must be refined.
assumptions_latex: Each inexact violation value has a valid computable absolute-error bound.
The trial has strictly positive predicted violation decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed relative-error condition prevents evaluation uncertainty from dominating the restoration ratio test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct kind, but the required bound on omega is expressed through an undefined acceptance-threshold separation and therefore cannot be checked from the record. A specific inexact-evaluation ratio test and source are needed to determine the correct constant and hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Irreducible Evaluation Error Creates an Acceptance Dead Zone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for restoration decisions when evaluation accuracy cannot be refined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the smallest attainable endpoint-error sum is \(E_{\min}>0\), then any trial satisfying \(|\widetilde A-\eta P_k|\le E_{\min}\) cannot be certified as accepted or rejected by the bounded-error ratio test. Therefore arbitrarily small predicted reductions cannot in general support reliable decisions under a fixed nonzero error floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero evaluation-error floor leaves a band around the acceptance threshold in which the restoration decision is intrinsically unresolved.
assumptions_latex: Only the stated deterministic error bounds are available.
The error floor cannot be reduced below \(E_{\min}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\widetilde A-\eta P_k|\le E_{\min}\Rightarrow\text{decision unresolved}.
knowledge_statements.title: Irreducible Evaluation Error Creates an Acceptance Dead Zone
Fixed-Trial Sub-Gaussian Reduction Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sub-Gaussian sample means give a high-probability interval for expected violation reduction at a fixed trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose independent sample means \(\bar V_0,\bar V_1\), using \(N_0,N_1\) conditionally \(\sigma^2\)-sub-Gaussian observations, estimate expected violations \(V_0,V_1\). For a trial fixed relative to these samples, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[| (\bar V_0-\bar V_1)-(V_0-V_1)|\le\sigma\sqrt{2\log(4/\delta)}(N_0^{-1/2}+N_1^{-1/2}).\]
assumptions_latex: Endpoint samples are independent or conditionally independent.
The trial is fixed relative to the certificate samples.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr\{|\widehat A-A|\le w_{N_0,N_1,\delta}\}\ge1-\delta
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Confidence certificate for one nonadaptively selected noisy restoration trial.

knowledge_statements.title: Anytime-Valid Restoration Reduction Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A summable allocation of conditional error probabilities gives intervals valid at every adaptive sampling stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At sampling stage n, let I_n be conditionally valid for the true reduction A with conditional failure probability at most \delta_n, where \sum_{n\ge1}\delta_n\le\delta. Then \Pr\{A\in I_n\text{ for every }n\}\ge1-\delta. A trial may be accepted when \inf I_n\ge\eta P_k, rejected when \sup I_n<\eta P_k, and sampled further otherwise.
assumptions_latex: Each I_n is conditionally valid given all earlier decisions.
The predicted reduction P_k is measurable before the certificate decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr\{\forall n:A\in I_n\}\ge1-\delta.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Union-bound confidence sequence valid under adaptive stopping.

notation.meaning: stage-n interval for true expected reduction

knowledge_statements.title: Sub-Gaussian Sampling Cost to Resolve a Reduction Margin
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy acceptance costs inversely with the squared distance from its decision boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For conditionally independent \sigma^2-sub-Gaussian endpoint observations and true margin g=|A-\eta P_k|>0, balanced sampling resolves the sign of A-\eta P_k with error probability at most \delta using O(\sigma^2g^{-2}\log(1/\delta)) samples. No finite bound is uniform as g\downarrow0 without an indifference zone or indeterminate outcome.
assumptions_latex: The declared conditional sub-Gaussian law and concentration inequality hold.
The true decision margin g is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N=O\!\left(\sigma^2g^{-2}\log(1/\delta)\right).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-decision sample complexity away from the acceptance boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Indistinguishable Opposite Acceptance Instances
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent bounded noise can make an acceptable and an unacceptable trial observationally identical.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Y=A+E with |E|\le w and acceptance boundary zero. The instances A_+=w/2 and A_-=-w/2 can both produce Y=0 using errors -w/2 and w/2. Any decision based only on Y is therefore wrong for one instance.
assumptions_latex: w>0 and no additional information distinguishes the instances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y_+=Y_-=0,\qquad\operatorname{sign}(A_+)\ne\operatorname{sign}(A_-).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit persistent bounded-noise resolution failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Restoration Information Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy restoration regimes differ by bias, dependence, tails, and whether repeated sampling can remove uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relative to a filtration (\mathcal G_k), observations of expected violation V(x) may be conditionally unbiased with a declared tail law, biased with a conditional bias bound, dependent with a declared martingale or conditional concentration law, or adversarially bounded. Noise is reducible when replication drives a valid uncertainty radius to zero and persistent otherwise.
assumptions_latex: The filtration contains prior adaptive trials and sampling decisions.
All bias or concentration claims hold conditionally on that filtration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Acceptance and convergence guarantees must match the declared noise regime}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by conditional bias, dependence, tail law, and reducibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Noise Imposes a Restoration Resolution Floor
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent uncertainty creates a resolution floor below which restoration progress cannot be certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every admissible confidence interval for actual expected reduction has half-width at least \(w>0\), trials whose reduction lies within \(w\) of the acceptance boundary cannot be uniformly classified from the available observations. Arbitrarily fine progress therefore cannot be certified unless uncertainty is reduced correspondingly.
assumptions_latex: The observation scheme has irreducible confidence half-width \(w>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |A-\eta P_k|<w\Rightarrow\text{no uniform classification from the available data}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information limit under finite sampling or irreducible uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable Decision Errors Imply Eventual Correct Classification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditionally valid decisions with summable error budgets are eventually all correct almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G_{k-1}\) contain all information preceding restoration decision \(k\), and let \(E_k\in\mathcal G_k\) be the event that its resolved accept-or-reject classification is incorrect. If \(\Pr(E_k\mid\mathcal G_{k-1})\leq\delta_k\) almost surely and \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\delta_k<\infty\), then \(\Pr(E_k\ \mathrm{i.o.})=0\). Thus almost surely only finitely many resolved restoration decisions are misclassified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(E_k\ \mathrm{i.o.})=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence-level reliability of adaptively sampled noisy-restoration decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Noisy-Information Restoration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restoration with stochastic constraint or violation observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \\(x_k\\), obtain random observations used to construct an estimator \\(\widehat m_k(s)\\) of a local violation model and choose \\(s_k\\) with \\(\|s_k\|\le\Delta_k\\). Draw independent or conditionally valid samples at \\(x_k\\) and \\(x_k+s_k\\) until confidence intervals for their expected violation values are narrow enough to resolve the prescribed actual-to-predicted reduction test with confidence at least \\(1-\delta_k\\). Accept or reject the trial according to the resolved test, update \\(\Delta_k\\), and output the accepted point. If the test remains unresolved at the sampling budget, report an indeterminate restoration outcome rather than declaring success.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate violation reduction from noisy samples, sample until confidence intervals resolve the acceptance test, and report indeterminacy when the sampling budget is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The observation model admits valid conditional confidence intervals for expected violation.
\\(\delta_k\in(0,1)\\) and a finite sampling budget are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each resolved acceptance decision has its stipulated confidence level; exhausted unresolved tests do not certify restoration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the noisy-information leaf, but validity under adaptive sampling requires a specified observation model and confidence construction, such as conditionally valid or time-uniform intervals. The current assumptions and absent citation do not establish the claimed per-decision confidence guarantee.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-trial confidence certificate for noisy violation reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose independent sample means \(\bar V_0,\bar V_1\), based on \(N_0,N_1\) observations at the current and trial points, estimate means \(V_0,V_1\), and each observation is conditionally \(\sigma^2\)-sub-Gaussian. Then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[|(\bar V_0-\bar V_1)-(V_0-V_1)|\le \sigma\sqrt{2\log(4/\delta)}\left(N_0^{-1/2}+N_1^{-1/2}\right).\] Comparing this confidence interval with \(\eta P_k\) certifies a fixed-trial acceptance or rejection decision at confidence \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sub-Gaussian sample means provide an explicit high-probability interval for the expected violation reduction.
assumptions_latex: Samples used at the two points are independent or conditionally independent.
The stated sub-Gaussian scale is valid.
The trial is fixed relative to the samples used for this certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_0-V_1\) lies in the displayed confidence interval with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sub-Gaussian Reduction Confidence Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Noise Prevents Arbitrarily Fine Restoration Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information limit caused by a finite sampling budget or nonvanishing uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every admissible estimator of the actual violation reduction has confidence half-width at least \(w>0\), then trials with \(|A-\eta P_k|<w\) cannot be uniformly classified relative to the acceptance boundary using that information. In particular, a method cannot certify arbitrarily small feasibility improvements unless uncertainty is reduced accordingly or the stopping tolerance remains above the noise resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent uncertainty creates a resolution floor below which noisy restoration progress cannot be certified.
assumptions_latex: The available observation scheme has an irreducible confidence half-width \(w>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |A-\eta P_k|<w\Rightarrow\text{no uniform acceptance classification from the available data}.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Noise Prevents Arbitrarily Fine Restoration Certification

children.title: Large-Scale Restoration
children.top_down_role: Sparse, matrix-free, and partially solved restoration models.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Direct Trust-Region Restoration Variant
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the regularized restoration trust-region model through sparse augmented QR and a trust-region multiplier search, then globalize the trial by actual versus predicted violation reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), define \(q_k(s)=\tfrac12\|c(x_k)+J_ks\|_2^2+\tfrac{\lambda_k}{2}\|s\|_2^2\) with \(\|s\|_2\leq\Delta_k\). Determine a trust-region multiplier \(\tau_k\geq0\) by a safeguarded secular search and solve \[(J_k^TJ_k+(\lambda_k+\tau_k)I)s_k=-J_k^Tc(x_k)\] using sparse QR of \(\begin{bmatrix}J_k\\\sqrt{\lambda_k+\tau_k}I\end{bmatrix}\), with rank-revealing treatment when \(\tau_k=\lambda_k=0\), until \(\|s_k\|_2\leq\Delta_k\), \(\tau_k(\Delta_k-\|s_k\|_2)=0\), and the prescribed inner residual tolerance hold. Accept the trial only when its positive predicted reduction and actual-to-predicted violation-reduction ratio pass the declared threshold; contract the radius after rejection and expand it only after a sufficiently successful boundary-active trial. Stop at the declared feasibility and model-criticality tolerances.
assumptions_latex: Sparse access to \(J_k\) and a fill-reducing ordering are available.
The secular search and sparse solves meet declared residual and complementarity tolerances.
The agreement ratio is formed only for positive predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|s_k\|_2\leq\Delta_k,\qquad \tau_k\geq0,\qquad \tau_k(\Delta_k-\|s_k\|_2)=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse orthogonal-factorization solution of a regularized linearized least-squares restoration model.

notation.meaning: trust-region multiplier used by the sparse-direct solve

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Inner Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive regularization makes the matrix-free normal residual an inner-solve accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\lambda>0\), the quadratic \(q\) is \(\lambda\)-strongly convex with unique minimizer \(s_*\), and every \(s\) satisfies \(\|s-s_*\|_2\le\lambda^{-1}\|J^T(c+Js)+\lambda s\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|s-s_*\|_2\le\lambda^{-1}\|\nabla q(s)\|_2
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori termination test for the unconstrained regularized inner model.

knowledge_statements.title: Cauchy-Fraction Certificate for Constrained Inner Solves
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible approximate inner step is adequate when it captures a fixed fraction of Cauchy model decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For q_k(s)=q_k(0)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks on \|s\|\le\Delta_k, let s_k^C minimize q_k(-\alpha g_k) over 0\le\alpha\le\Delta_k/\|g_k\|. An approximate step is adequate when \|s_k\|\le\Delta_k and q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\ge\kappa_C[q_k(0)-q_k(s_k^C)] with \kappa_C\in(0,1].
assumptions_latex: g_k\ne0; otherwise the method applies its declared stationarity or curvature test.
Candidate and Cauchy model values are computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|s_k\|\le\Delta_k,\quad\operatorname{pred}_k(s_k)\ge\kappa_C\operatorname{pred}_k(s_k^C).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-decrease test for an approximate trust-region restoration step.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Equations Square Spectral Conditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal equations square the Jacobian condition number, and matrix-free access alone does not cure it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For full-column-rank \(J\), \(\kappa_2(J^TJ)=\kappa_2(J)^2\). Matrix-free application avoids forming the normal matrix but does not itself remove this spectral conditioning.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) has full column rank for the finite condition-number identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(J^TJ)=\kappa_2(J)^2
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical boundary for large-scale least-squares restoration.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Normal-Operator Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regularized restoration model can be processed with Jacobian and adjoint-Jacobian products alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(s)=\tfrac12\|c+Js\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|s\|_2^2\), \(\nabla q(s)=J^T(c+Js)+\lambda s\) and \(\nabla^2q=J^TJ+\lambda I\). These actions require only products with \(J\) and \(J^T\), not formation of \(J^TJ\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla q(s)=J^T(c+Js)+\lambda s
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator form of a regularized linearized least-squares restoration model.

knowledge_statements.title: Large-Scale Restoration Solver Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse direct, matrix-free Krylov, preconditioned Krylov, and decomposition methods are the principal scale-oriented realizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Large-scale restoration may realize its local model through sparse-direct factorization, matrix-free Krylov iteration using Jp and J^Tr, preconditioned Krylov iteration, or block and Schur-complement decomposition. Each realization must declare a computable inner residual, model-decrease, or trust-region termination certificate.
assumptions_latex: The selected realization preserves the declared restoration model.
Its inner stopping quantity is computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{realization}\in\{\text{sparse direct, Krylov, preconditioned Krylov, decomposition}\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementation partition for large restoration models.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(h(x)=\|c(x)\|\) for equality constraints, and let \(J(x)\) denote the constraint Jacobian. A local restoration model may be \(\min_s\|c(x)+J(x)s\|\) subject to \(\|s\|\le\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional problems whose dimension or sparsity makes dense Jacobian formation, dense factorization, or exact subproblem solution unsuitable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restoration method is large-scale if each local feasibility model is represented through sparse operators or matrix-free products \(v\mapsto J(x_j)v\) and \(w\mapsto J(x_j)^Tw\), and its trial step \(s_j\) may be obtained by a truncated iterative solve rather than an exact factorization. If \(M_j(s)\) is the restoration model and \(r_j\) is an applicable first-order model residual, the partial solve must satisfy a declared condition such as \(\|r_j(s_j)\|\le\eta_j\|r_j(0)\|\) with \(0\le\eta_j<1\), or a certified fraction-of-Cauchy decrease \(M_j(0)-M_j(s_j)\ge\kappa_C\Delta M_j^C\) with \(\kappa_C\in(0,1]\). Storage is limited to sparse problem data and at most \(O(qn+qm)\) working vectors for a prescribed iteration or memory budget \(q\), rather than dense \(n\times n\) or \(m\times n\) arrays. Restoration acceptance remains based on actual violation reduction, not merely on termination of the inner linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large-scale restoration represents Jacobians sparsely or through matrix–vector products and permits iterative, partially solved feasibility models. The inner solve must meet an explicit residual-reduction or fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease condition. Its storage uses a bounded number of work vectors plus sparse data instead of dense matrices. Completing the inner iteration is not enough: the outer restoration mechanism still checks actual constraint-violation progress.
assumptions_latex: Jacobian and transpose-Jacobian products, or equivalent sparse actions, are available.
The restoration model has a computable residual or a computable reference decrease.
The outer algorithm can evaluate or certify the violation measure at a trial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large-scale restoration is characterized by sparse or matrix-free model representation, quantitatively controlled partial solution, limited working memory, and an outer test of actual feasibility progress.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A Krylov solution stopped by relative normal-equation residual is a residual-controlled partial restoration solve.
A truncated method satisfying a uniform fraction of Cauchy decrease is a model-decrease-controlled partial solve.
special_cases_latex: Limited-memory quasi-Newton curvature may supplement matrix-free Jacobian products.
A sparse direct solve can qualify when it avoids dense storage and respects the stated scale regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact solution of every restoration model is not required by the definition.
Matrix-free computation does not remove the need for an outer feasibility acceptance condition.
boundary_notes: The asymptotic storage expression is a structural criterion, not an evaluation-complexity theorem.
No inspected source directly supported the combined sparse, matrix-free, and partial-solve definition.

Stop the inner solve when its residual or achieved model reduction meets a forcing tolerance tied to the outer restoration accuracy. Evaluate the true violation at the trial, accept by an actual-to-predicted reduction test, and update \\(\Delta_k\\). The inner model need not be solved exactly.

assumptions_latex: Products with \\(J_k\\) and \\(J_k^\top\\), or equivalent sparse operations, are available.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), the quadratic \(q(s)=\tfrac12\|c+Js\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|s\|_2^2\) is \(\lambda\)-strongly convex with unique minimizer \(s_*\). Any computed \(s\) satisfies \[\|s-s_*\|_2\le \lambda^{-1}\|J^T(c+Js)+\lambda s\|_2.\] Thus the matrix-free normal residual is an a posteriori inner-solve accuracy certificate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale restoration using sparse orthogonal factorization rather than normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), form the sparse augmented least-squares model \[\min_{\|s\|_2\leq\Delta_k}\left\|\begin{bmatrix}J_k\\ \sqrt{\lambda_k}I\end{bmatrix}s+\begin{bmatrix}c(x_k)\\0\end{bmatrix}\right\|_2^2.\] Compute a trial step by sparse QR or an equivalent orthogonal-factorization method, stopping only after the step is trust-region feasible and attains a prescribed fraction \(\kappa_C\in(0,1]\) of Cauchy model decrease. Evaluate the true violation, accept when the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio is at least \(\eta_1\), contract the radius after rejection, and permit expansion only after a sufficiently successful boundary-active step. Stop when the declared feasibility and model-criticality tolerances hold.

The predicted reduction is positive before forming its agreement ratio.

children.top_down_role: Rank deficiency and inconsistent local models obstructing reliable feasibility directions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At a restoration point \(x\), let \(c(x)=0\) denote equality constraints, let \(J=J(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and consider the linearized feasibility equation \(Js=-c(x)\), possibly with \(s\in\mathcal S\) for a trust region, bounds, or other local restrictions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local first-order restoration geometry for finite-dimensional smooth constraints. The labels describe the local model and do not by themselves establish global infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The restoration geometry at \(x\) is rank-deficient when \(\operatorname{rank}J<\min\{m,n\}\), or, relative to a required full-row-rank condition, when \(\operatorname{rank}J<m\). It is linearly inconsistent when \(-c(x)\notin J\mathcal S:=\{Js:s\in\mathcal S\}\); without step restrictions this is equivalent to \(-c(x)\notin\operatorname{Range}(J)\). It is ill-conditioned at level \(\kappa_{\max}\) when the smallest relevant nonzero singular value satisfies \(\sigma_{\min}^+(J)>0\) and \(\sigma_{\\max}(J)/\sigma_{
min}^+(J)>\kappa_{\max}\). A reliable first-order feasibility direction fails to exist when the prescribed local model has no admissible step attaining its required predicted decrease. The geometry-failure label is the set \(G(x)\) of all applicable conditions; rank deficiency, inconsistency, and ill-conditioning are therefore distinct and may overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration geometry is rank-deficient when the constraint Jacobian lacks the rank required by the method. It is inconsistent when the negative residual cannot be produced by any admissible linearized step. It is ill-conditioned when the ratio of the largest to the smallest relevant nonzero singular value exceeds a declared threshold. Reliable-direction failure occurs when no admissible local-model step achieves the required predicted decrease. These are separate labels and may occur together.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the explicitly declared set of admissible restoration steps.
Any condition-number label specifies the singular subspace and threshold being used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(x)\subseteq\{\mathrm{rank\ deficient},\mathrm{inconsistent},\mathrm{ill\ conditioned},\mathrm{no\ reliable\ direction}\}\) is determined by the stated rank, range, singular-value, and model-decrease conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\mathcal S=\mathbb R^n\), linearized consistency is equivalent to \((I-JJ^\dagger)c(x)=0\).
Unrestricted inconsistency is equivalent to \(\min_s\|Js+c(x)\|>0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m\le n\) and \(J\) has full row rank, the unrestricted equality linearization is consistent for every residual.
Trust-region restrictions can make \(Js=-c(x)\) inconsistent even when the unrestricted equation is consistent.
immediate_consequences_latex: Rank deficiency does not logically imply inconsistency for the current residual.
Local linearized inconsistency does not certify that the nonlinear constraint set is empty.
boundary_notes: Inequalities require an explicitly selected active-set or complementarity linearization.
The inspected source mentions safeguards for rank-deficient Jacobians but does not state this complete classification.
review_flags: The complete rank/inconsistency/conditioning taxonomy lacks an exact inspected source.
The formula should be source-checked, including the method-relative meaning of required rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Geometry Failure Classes
Descent Despite Singular Restoration Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency alone does not prevent feasibility descent. First-order progress is blocked exactly when the residual is orthogonal to the Jacobian range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v(x)=	frac12\|c(x)\|_2^2\), where \(c\) is differentiable and \(J(x)=
abla c(x)\). Then \(
abla v(x)=J(x)^Tc(x)\). Even if \(\operatorname{rank}J(x)<m\), the direction \(d=-J(x)^Tc(x)\) strictly decreases \(v\) to first order whenever \(J(x)^Tc(x)
e0\). Conversely, \(J(x)^Tc(x)=0\) holds exactly when no direction has negative first-order change in \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[J(x)^Tc(x)\ne0\Longrightarrow \nabla v(x)^T[-J(x)^Tc(x)]=-\|J(x)^Tc(x)\|_2^2<0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates Jacobian rank deficiency from first-order stationarity of squared violation.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Restoration Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-deficient equality-constraint geometry in a linearized restoration model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable, fix \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and define \(r=c(x)\) and \(J=\nabla c(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). Consider minimizing \(\|r+Jd\|_2\) over \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Singular restoration geometry occurs when \(\operatorname{rank}J<m\). Then \(JJ^{\mathsf T}\) is singular, so a restoration formula using \((JJ^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\) is undefined. Moreover, \(r+J(d+z)=r+Jd\) for every \(z\in\ker J\). Consequently, if \(d_*\) is a least-squares minimizer, then the full minimizer set is \(d_*+\ker J\), and the direction is nonunique exactly when \(\ker J\ne\{0\}\); row-rank deficiency alone does not imply this latter condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row-rank loss makes the restoration matrix JJᵀ singular and invalidates inverse-based formulas. Least-squares directions are nonunique only when the Jacobian also has a nontrivial null space.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable at the restoration iterate \(x\).
The restoration model minimizes the Euclidean norm of the affine equality residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}J<m\Longrightarrow JJ^{\mathsf T}\text{ is singular}\), and \(r+J(d+z)=r+Jd\) for every \(z\in\ker J\); direction nonuniqueness occurs exactly when \(\ker J\ne\{0\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Local Inconsistency Does Not Establish Global Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible nonlinear problem can have an inconsistent restoration linearization at the current point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c(x)=x^2-1\), feasible points \(x=\pm1\) exist, but at \(x=0\), \(c(0)+c'(0)d=-1\) for every \(d\), so the local affine restoration equation is inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:c(x)=0\}\ne\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad\{d:c(0)+c'(0)d=0\}=\varnothing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates one affine-model failure from nonlinear infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Model Consistency Characterization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearized equality model is inconsistent exactly when the residual has a nonzero component orthogonal to the Jacobian range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine equation \(Jd=-c\) is inconsistent iff \(-c\notin\operatorname{Range}J\), equivalently iff some \(y\in\operatorname{Null}(J^T)\) satisfies \(y^Tc\ne0\). Moreover, \(\min_d\|c+Jd\|_2=\|P_{\operatorname{Null}(J^T)}c\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -c\notin\operatorname{Range}J\iff\exists y\in\operatorname{Null}(J^T):y^Tc\ne0
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact characterization of inconsistent linearized equality restoration.

knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Alternative for Mixed Affine Restoration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed affine restoration model is feasible or has a Farkas multiplier certificate of inconsistency, but not both.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ad=b\), \(Cd\le q\), exactly one holds: either a feasible \(d\) exists, or there are \(y\) and \(z\ge0\) such that \(A^Ty+C^Tz=0\) and \(b^Ty+q^Tz<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists d:Ad=b,\ Cd\le q\iff\exists(y,z\ge0):A^Ty+C^Tz=0,\ b^Ty+q^Tz<0
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier certificate for inconsistent affine equality and inequality models.

notation.meaning: equality and nonnegative inequality alternative multipliers

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Local Restoration Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inconsistency of the linearized equality-restoration equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an equality residual \(c(x)\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and Jacobian \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), the exact linearized restoration equation \(c(x)+Jd=0\) is consistent if and only if \(-c(x)\in\operatorname{range}J\). It is inconsistent precisely when \(P_{\ker J^{\mathsf T}}c(x)\ne0\). In that case every direction satisfies \[\|c(x)+Jd\|_2\ge \|P_{\ker J^{\mathsf T}}c(x)\|_2>0,\] so the local linear model cannot predict exact feasibility, even when the original nonlinear constraints may have feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local restoration model is inconsistent when the negative residual lies outside the Jacobian range; its least achievable linearized residual is then strictly positive.
assumptions_latex: The restoration model is the affine equality model \(c(x)+Jd\).
Orthogonal projections and residuals use the Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(x)+Jd=0\text{ has no solution}\Longleftrightarrow P_{\ker J^{\mathsf T}}c(x)\ne0.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Farkas Alternative for Linearized Inequality Restoration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact alternative characterizing incompatibility of affine equality and inequality restoration constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the affine system \(Ad=b\), \(Cd\le q\), exactly one of the following holds: (i) there exists \(d\) satisfying the system; (ii) there exist multipliers \(y\) and \(z\ge0\) such that \(A^Ty+C^Tz=0\) and \(b^Ty+q^Tz<0\). The second alternative certifies inconsistency of the local restoration model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine restoration system is either feasible or has a Farkas multiplier certificate of inconsistency, but never both.
assumptions_latex: All matrices and vectors are finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists d:Ad=b,\ Cd\le q\iff\exists(y,z\ge0):A^Ty+C^Tz=0,\ b^Ty+q^Tz<0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Alternative for Linearized Inequality Restoration
Uniformly Reliable Linearized Restoration Direction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform positive smallest singular value gives a well-defined, bounded minimum-norm restoration direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(J(x)J(x)^T\succeq\sigma^2I\) with \(\sigma>0\), then \(d_R=-J(x)^T(J(x)J(x)^T)^{-1}c(x)\) is the unique minimum-norm solution of \(J(x)d=-c(x)\) and satisfies \(\|d_R\|_2\le\sigma^{-1}\|c(x)\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J(x)d_R=-c(x),\qquad\|d_R\|_2\le\sigma^{-1}\|c(x)\|_2
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform regularity condition for equality-restoration directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Residual-to-Direction Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reciprocal smallest singular value is the exact worst-case amplification from residual error to direction error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For full-row-rank \(J\), \(\|J^\dagger\|_2=1/\sigma_{\min}(J)\). Thus \(\|\delta d\|_2\le\|\delta c\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(J)\), and the worst-case factor is attained along a left singular vector for \(\sigma_{\min}(J)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{\delta c\ne0}\frac{\|J^\dagger\delta c\|_2}{\|\delta c\|_2}=\frac1{\sigma_{\min}(J)}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact perturbation boundary for minimum-norm restoration directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Residual Contraction under Uniform Regularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform Jacobian regularity and Lipschitz variation yield quadratic one-step residual contraction for the exact linearized direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(J\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \([x,x+d_R]\) and \(J(x)J(x)^T\succeq\sigma^2I\), then \(\|c(x+d_R)\|_2\le(L/2)\|d_R\|_2^2\le L\|c(x)\|_2^2/(2\sigma^2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step nonlinear reliability of the exact linearized direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Reliable Restoration-Direction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform regularity conditions delimiting reliable linearized restoration directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), \(m\le n\), be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood \(U\), and suppose \(J(x)J(x)^T\succeq \sigma^2I\) for every \(x\in U\), with \(\sigma>0\). The minimum-norm linearized restoration direction is \(d_R(x)=-J(x)^T(J(x)J(x)^T)^{-1}c(x)\). It is well defined and satisfies \(J(x)d_R(x)=-c(x)\) and \(\|d_R(x)\|_2\le \sigma^{-1}\|c(x)\|_2\). Reliability reaches its regularity boundary when the smallest singular value of \(J(x)\) approaches zero; then this uniform step bound and stable dependence on residual perturbations can be lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly positive smallest Jacobian singular value guarantees a bounded exact linearized restoration direction; reliability can fail as that singular value vanishes.

notation.meaning: uniform lower bound on the constraint Jacobian's singular values

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The full-row-rank condition, minimum-norm right-inverse formula, and norm bound are correct, and condition is appropriate for this boundary leaf. An inspectable restoration or constrained-optimization source is still required for the reliability-boundary interpretation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small Singular Values Amplify Residual Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp sensitivity boundary for minimum-norm linearized restoration directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a full-row-rank matrix \(J\), the map from an equality residual \(c\) to the minimum-norm correction \(d=-J^\dagger c\) has operator norm \(\|J^\dagger\|_2=1/\sigma_{\min}(J)\). Hence a residual perturbation \(\delta c\) can cause \(\|\delta d\|_2\le\|\delta c\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(J)\), and this worst-case amplification factor is attained along a left singular vector associated with \(\sigma_{\min}(J)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reciprocal smallest singular value is the exact worst-case residual-to-direction sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\delta c\ne0}\|J^\dagger\delta c\|_2/\|\delta c\|_2=1/\sigma_{\min}(J)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Small Singular Values Amplify Residual Perturbations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Residual Contraction from a Regular Restoration Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local nonlinear reliability obtained from a uniformly bounded right inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz Jacobian near \(x\), and suppose \(J(x)J(x)^T\succeq\sigma^2I\) with \(\sigma>0\). For \(d=-J(x)^T(J(x)J(x)^T)^{-1}c(x)\), \[\|c(x+d)\|_2\le\frac L2\|d\|_2^2\le\frac{L}{2\sigma^2}\|c(x)\|_2^2,\] provided the segment \([x,x+d]\) remains in the Lipschitz neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform Jacobian regularity and Lipschitz variation make the exact linearized restoration direction reduce the nonlinear residual quadratically when the current residual is small.

notation.meaning: lower singular-value bound for the equality Jacobian

children.title: Restoration Progress Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Weak violation progress or local residual minima that do not establish global infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) be a locally Lipschitz violation measure, let \(x\) be the restoration reference point, and let \(z\) be the point returned by a restoration phase. Let \(\Delta_h\ge0\) be its predicted or required violation decrease.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local deterministic restoration outcomes. The definition separates unsuccessful progress and local residual stationarity from a global certificate of infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constants \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon_F\ge0\), and stationarity tolerance \(\varepsilon_S\ge0\), restoration progress fails at \((x,z)\) when \(h(z)>\varepsilon_F\) and \(h(z)>h(x)-\sigma\Delta_h\). A positive-residual stationary termination occurs when \(h(z)>\varepsilon_F\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial h(z)+N_X(z))\le\varepsilon_S\), where \(X\) contains any simple constraints imposed during restoration. The progress-failure boundary is the union of these conditions. Neither condition is a global infeasibility certificate unless an additional valid lower bound \(L\) for the global residual problem satisfies \(L>\varepsilon_F\), where \(L\le\inf_{y\in X}h(y)\). Thus local failure establishes only failure of the chosen progress test or approximate stationarity of the residual problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progress fails when the returned point remains above the feasibility tolerance and does not attain the required fraction of predicted violation decrease. A positive-residual stationary outcome occurs when violation remains positive while the first-order residual for minimizing violation over the restoration domain is small. Their union is the progress-failure boundary. Neither event proves global infeasibility unless an independently valid global lower bound on minimum violation is itself positive.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is locally Lipschitz on the restoration domain \(X\).
\(\partial h\) is a declared generalized subdifferential appropriate to the adopted stationarity condition.
\(N_X(z)\) is the corresponding normal cone to the restoration domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The boundary distinguishes insufficient credited decrease and positive-residual local stationarity, while reserving global infeasibility for outcomes accompanied by a valid positive global lower bound.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For smooth \(h\) and \(X=\mathbb R^n\), the stationarity test reduces to \(\|\nabla h(z)\|\le\varepsilon_S\).
Exact positive-residual stationarity is \(h(z)>0\) and \(0\in\partial h(z)+N_X(z)\).
special_cases_latex: A strict local minimizer of \(h\) with positive value lies on the stationary-failure side of the boundary.
If \(h(z)\le\varepsilon_F\), the episode is restoration-successful under the stated feasibility tolerance.
immediate_consequences_latex: Convergence to an infeasible stationary point is weaker than establishing that the original constraints are globally infeasible.
Changing \(\sigma\), \(\varepsilon_F\), or \(\varepsilon_S\) changes the operational boundary.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert that every restoration algorithm can compute a global residual lower bound.
No inspected source precisely supported this local-versus-global failure boundary.

notation.meaning: Selected generalized subdifferential of the violation measure.
Normal cone to the restoration domain.

review_flags: A precise source is needed for the stated boundary and global-lower-bound distinction.
knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Progress Failure Boundary
Restoration Stagnation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration stagnates when violation converges to a positive level while successive reductions vanish; uniform fractional decrease excludes this behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\) be a continuous violation measure and let \(\{x_k\}_{k\in\mathcal R}\) be restoration iterates with \(v_{k+1}\le v_k\), where \(v_k=v(x_k)\). Restoration stagnation occurs when \(v_k\to\bar v>0\) while the achieved decreases vanish: \(v_k-v_{k+1}\to0\). If acceptance requires \(v_{k+1}\le(1-\eta)v_k\) for a fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), then stagnation at positive violation is impossible for infinitely many accepted restoration steps. Hence observed positive-limit stagnation marks failure of uniform fractional decrease, termination of accepted restoration progress, or mismatch between predicted and actual violation reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v_k\to\bar v>0\ \text{and}\ v_k-v_{k+1}\to0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \inf_k\frac{v_k-v_{k+1}}{v_k}=0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic failure to reduce constraint violation during restoration.

notation.meaning: constraint violation at restoration iterate k

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The monotone-sequence implication is correct, but the proposed meaning of restoration stagnation is uncited. In addition, writing both an index set \(\mathcal R\) and transitions from \(k\) to \(k+1\) implicitly assumes consecutive restoration indices; a source or explicit reindexing of the restoration subsequence is needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Separation Required for a Residual Infeasibility Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact search set, a continuous exact residual certifies infeasibility through a positive global minimum. Without attainment, an infeasible system can have residual infimum zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\ne\varnothing\) and let \(\theta:X\to\mathbb R_+\) vanish exactly at feasible points. If \(X\) is compact and \(\theta\) is continuous, then the system is infeasible if and only if \(\min_{x\in X}\theta(x)>0\). Without attainment, infeasibility need not imply positive residual separation: on \(X=\mathbb R\), the equation \(e^{-x}=0\) is infeasible although \(\inf_{x\in X}e^{-x}=0\). Thus local stationarity, local-model failure, positive violation at one point, or failure of one restoration run is not a global infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: Compactness of \(X\) and continuity of \(\theta\) are assumed for the attained-minimum equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[X\ \text{compact}\Longrightarrow\bigl[\mathcal F=\varnothing\iff\min_{x\in X}\theta(x)>0\bigr],\qquad \mathcal F_{e^{-x}}=\varnothing,\quad\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}e^{-x}=0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when residual separation certifies infeasibility and why local or nonattained signals do not.

knowledge_statements.title: False Infeasibility Signals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that local restoration failure does not certify global infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the feasible equality constraint \(c(x)=x^2-1=0\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), with violation \(v(x)=\tfrac12c(x)^2\). At \(x=0\), \(c(0)=-1\) and \(J(0)=c'(0)=0\), so the linearized restoration equation \(c(0)+J(0)d=0\) is inconsistent for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}\). Moreover, \(v'(0)=J(0)c(0)=0\), although feasible points \(x=\pm1\) exist. Therefore failure of a local linearized restoration model, or stationarity of this smooth residual merit function at positive violation, is not by itself a certificate that the original nonlinear constraint is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible equation x²−1=0 has an inconsistent restoration linearization and a stationary positive residual at zero, so either local signal can falsely suggest infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The original feasibility problem is the scalar equality \(c(x)=0\) on \(\mathbb{R}\).
The putative infeasibility signal uses only local linearization failure or positive-violation stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[c(\pm1)=0,\qquad c(0)+J(0)d=-1\ne0\ \text{for every }d\in\mathbb{R},\qquad v'(0)=0.\]

notation.meaning: derivative of the scalar constraint residual

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible System with a Strict Positive Residual Trap
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible equation 1+x²−x⁴=0 has a strict positive local minimum of its squared residual at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the scalar equality \(c(x)=1+x^2-x^4=0\), let \(v(x)=\tfrac12c(x)^2\). At \(x=0\), \(c(0)=1\), \(v'(0)=0\), and \(v''(0)=2>0\), so \(0\) is a strict local minimizer of \(v\) with positive violation. Nevertheless, \(c\) vanishes at \(x=\pm\sqrt{(1+\sqrt5)/2}\). Thus a strict positive residual trap neither implies infeasibility nor excludes zero residual elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v(0)=\tfrac12>0,\quad v'(0)=0,\quad v''(0)=2>0,\quad c\!\left(\pm\sqrt{\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}}\right)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demonstrates that a strict positive local residual minimum can coexist with feasible points.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Residual-Minimum Traps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive local minima of residual violation that trap descent restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality constraints \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), define \(v(x)=\tfrac12\|c(x)\|_2^2\). A local residual-minimum trap is a point \(\bar x\) with \(c(\bar x)\ne0\) for which \(v(x)\ge v(\bar x)\) throughout some neighborhood of \(\bar x\). If \(c\) is differentiable, then \(J(\bar x)^Tc(\bar x)=0\); if \(c\) is twice differentiable, a necessary second-order condition is \(J(\bar x)^TJ(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m c_i(\bar x)\nabla^2c_i(\bar x)\succeq0\). A restoration method accepting only local decrease of \(v\) cannot leave a strict such trap without a nonlocal or model-altering mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive local minimum of squared constraint residual is stationary and can trap any restoration method restricted to local residual decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is differentiable near \(\bar x\); twice differentiable for the second-order condition.
Restoration accepts only steps that locally decrease \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[c(\bar x)\ne0,\quad \bar x\ \text{locally minimizes}\ v\quad\Longrightarrow\quad J(\bar x)^Tc(\bar x)=0.\]

notation.meaning: half the squared equality-constraint residual norm

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The first- and second-order necessary conditions are correct under the stated differentiability assumptions, and failure_boundary is defensible for the terminal failure-class container. The named trap and the claim about restoration methods require an inspectable restoration-specific source, especially because the escape limitation depends on what counts as a local step.

children.title: Funnel and Hybrid Globalization
children.top_down_role: Envelope-based and hybrid globalization structures connecting penalties, filters, and restoration.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: Gould and Toint, A Trust-Funnel Method for Equality-Constrained Optimization

locator_traceability.matched_excerpt: - 11.7 Trust Regions p. 285

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: Curtis, Robinson, and Samadi, Complexity Analysis of a Trust Funnel Algorithm for Equality Constrained Optimization

locator_traceability.matched_excerpt: - 11.7 Trust Regions p. 285

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be the objective, \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) a violation measure, and \(v_k>0\) an iteration-dependent feasibility envelope.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-dimensional architectures combining a feasibility funnel with at least one penalty, merit, filter, trust-region, line-search, or restoration mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A funnel–hybrid globalization architecture is a tuple \(\mathcal A=(\{v_k\},\mathcal G,\chi,U)\). The funnel invariant requires every accepted iterate to satisfy \(h(x_k)\le v_k\), with \(v_{k+1}\le v_k\). The set \(\mathcal G\) contains at least two step-control mechanisms and includes the funnel mechanism; its other members may be a scalar merit or penalty test, a nondominance filter, or a restoration phase. The selector \(\chi_k\) maps the current algorithmic state and trial data to an active mechanism in \(\mathcal G\). The update map \(U\) accepts or rejects the trial and updates \(v_k\) and the auxiliary mechanism states. An accepted objective-oriented step may leave \(v_k\) unchanged but must remain inside the funnel; a feasibility-oriented step must satisfy a declared sufficient violation reduction and may contract the envelope. Restoration is invoked only by a declared trigger and must return a point satisfying the architecture's re-entry condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A funnel–hybrid architecture consists of a nonincreasing upper bound on accepted constraint violation, at least one additional globalization mechanism, a rule selecting the active mechanism, and a joint state-update rule. Every accepted iterate remains inside the envelope. Objective steps may retain the envelope, feasibility steps may contract it, and restoration must meet an explicit condition for re-entering normal operation.
assumptions_latex: The selector \(\chi_k\) is determined from available algorithmic state rather than future iterates.
Every component mechanism supplies a declared acceptance and state-update rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is funnel–hybrid exactly when it preserves the funnel invariant while switching or combining it with at least one distinct globalization mechanism under explicit selector and update maps.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The architecture can be represented as a state machine whose state contains \((x_k,v_k)\) and the states of the auxiliary globalization mechanisms.
special_cases_latex: A funnel with restoration re-entry is a two-mechanism hybrid.
A funnel whose objective steps are additionally accepted by an exact-penalty merit test is a funnel–merit hybrid.
immediate_consequences_latex: Membership in an auxiliary filter or decrease of a merit function cannot override the funnel bound unless the architecture explicitly relaxes that bound.
A pure funnel with no distinct secondary mechanism is excluded.
boundary_notes: This definition does not impose a universal switching rule or convergence theorem.
No inspected source provided an exact canonical definition of the complete architecture class.

notation.meaning: Current upper envelope on accepted infeasibility.

review_flags: The inspected merit/filter/restoration source does not support the funnel component or the complete hybrid tuple.
A funnel-specific authoritative locator is required.
