children.title: Feasibility Funnel Geometry
children.top_down_role: Globalization through an adaptive upper envelope on constraint violation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the algorithmic domain and let \(h:X\to\mathbb R_+\) be a constraint-violation measure satisfying \(h(x)=0\) exactly on the feasible set \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric definition of envelope-based feasibility control; it does not specify how trial steps are generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a positive scalar \(v\), the feasibility-funnel section is \(\mathcal U(v)=\{x\in X:h(x)\le v\}\). A feasibility funnel is a sequence \(\{\mathcal U(v_k)\}_{k\ge0}\) generated by envelope values satisfying \(0<v_{k+1}\le v_k\) and the acceptance invariant \(x_k\in\mathcal U(v_k)\) for every accepted iterate. An envelope contraction at iteration \(k\) is any update satisfying \(h(x_{k+1})\le v_{k+1}<v_k\); an envelope-preserving update has \(v_{k+1}=v_k\) while retaining \(h(x_{k+1})\le v_k\). If \(v_k\downarrow0\), then the sections form nested neighborhoods whose intersection is \(\mathcal F\), provided \(h\) is lower semicontinuous and \(\mathcal F=\{h=0\}\). The term funnel refers to the nested geometry in the product of iteration and violation level, not to monotonicity of the accepted values \(h(x_k)\) themselves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At envelope value v, the funnel section is the set of points whose violation is at most v. A feasibility funnel is a nested sequence of such sections with nonincreasing envelope values, and every accepted iterate must lie in its current section. The envelope may stay fixed even if accepted violation rises, so the funnel controls an upper bound rather than requiring monotone violation. If the envelope tends to zero under the stated regularity, the nested sections close down onto the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: Only accepted iterates are required to satisfy the funnel invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U(v_{k+1})\subseteq\mathcal U(v_k)\), \(x_k\in\mathcal U(v_k)\), and, when \(v_k\downarrow0\), \(\bigcap_k\mathcal U(v_k)=\mathcal F\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The acceptance invariant is equivalently \(h(x_k)\le v_k\) for every accepted index \(k\).
The funnel is a nested sublevel-set family of the violation measure.
special_cases_latex: For equalities, \(h(x)=\|c(x)\|\) produces norm tubes around \(c^{-1}(0)\).
For equalities and inequalities, \(h(x)=\|c_E(x)\|+\|[c_I(x)]_-\|\) yields a mixed-residual funnel.
immediate_consequences_latex: Accepted violation values need not be monotone when the envelope is unchanged.
Strict envelope contraction produces a strictly smaller admissible section whenever the corresponding sublevel sets differ.
boundary_notes: The definition alone gives no rate at which \(v_k\) approaches zero.
No inspected source directly supported this funnel geometry.

notation.meaning: Violation sublevel set at envelope value \(v\).

review_flags: A precise funnel-method source is required for the envelope definition and terminology.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Funnel Geometry

children.title: Monotone Feasibility Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Decreasing upper bounds on accepted infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Accepted Violation Need Not Be Monotone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepted infeasibility can rise between iterations even while a strictly decreasing funnel bound contains every accepted point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_k=1/(k+1)\), with \(v(x_{2j})=0\) and \(v(x_{2j+1})=V_{2j+1}\). Then \(0\le v(x_k)\le V_k\) and \(V_{k+1}<V_k\) for every \(k\), but \(v(x_{2j+1})>v(x_{2j})\) for every \(j\).
assumptions_latex: Only envelope containment and monotonicity are imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_{k+1}<V_k\not\Rightarrow v(x_{k+1})\le v(x_k).\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between monotonicity of the envelope and of accepted infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Limit Envelope Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone funnel may stagnate at positive width, so containment alone does not guarantee asymptotic feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conditions \(0\le v(x_k)\le V_k\) and \(V_{k+1}\le V_k\) do not force \(v(x_k)\to0\). For example, \(V_k\equiv1\) and \(v(x_k)\equiv1/2\) satisfy both conditions while violation remains positive. A separate mechanism forcing \(V_\infty=0\), or directly forcing violation reduction, is necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_k\downarrow V_\infty>0\text{ permits }\inf_k v(x_k)>0.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: What monotone envelope containment alone cannot guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Limit and Violation Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative monotone envelope has a limit; accepted violation is asymptotically bounded by it, and a vanishing envelope forces violation to vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(0\le v(x_k)\le V_k\) and \(V_{k+1}\le V_k\), then \(V_k\) converges to some \(V_\infty\ge0\) and \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}v(x_k)\le V_\infty\). In particular, \(V_k\to0\) implies \(v(x_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_k\downarrow V_\infty\ge0,\quad \limsup_k v(x_k)\le V_\infty;\quad V_\infty=0\Rightarrow v(x_k)\to0.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence consequences of a monotone nonnegative feasibility envelope.

notation.meaning: limit of the monotone feasibility envelope

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h:X\to\mathbb R_+\) measure violation and let \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb N\) index accepted iterates \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The envelope is monotone; accepted violation values need not be monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \(\{v_k\}_{k\ge0}\subset(0,\infty)\) is a monotone feasibility envelope for \(\{x_k\}_{k\in\mathcal A}\) if \(h(x_k)\le v_k\) for every \(k\in\mathcal A\) and \(v_{k+1}\le v_k\) for every update. It is contracting on an index set \(\mathcal C\) if for each \(k\in\mathcal C\), \(v_{k+1}\le(1-\gamma_k)v_k\) with \(\gamma_k\in(0,1)\); it is uniformly contracting when \(\inf_{k\in\mathcal C}\gamma_k>0\). It is asymptotically feasible when \(v_k\to0\). A valid update map must choose \(v_{k+1}\) in the nonempty interval \([h(x_{k+1}),v_k]\) after accepting \(x_{k+1}\). Thus monotonicity belongs to the bound \(v_k\), while the only pointwise requirement on accepted infeasibility is domination by that bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone feasibility envelope is a positive, nonincreasing sequence that upper-bounds every accepted iterate's constraint violation. It contracts on selected iterations when the next bound is smaller by a declared relative factor, and it is asymptotically feasible when it tends to zero. After accepting a point, a valid new bound lies between that point's violation and the previous bound. The actual accepted violation may rise while remaining under an unchanged envelope.
assumptions_latex: Envelope updates occur after acceptance or use a trial point already certified to satisfy the proposed bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h(x_k)\le v_k\) and \(v_{k+1}\le v_k\); valid post-acceptance updates satisfy \(v_{k+1}\in[h(x_{k+1}),v_k]\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The sublevel sets \(\{h\le v_k\}\) form a nested sequence containing the corresponding accepted iterates.
special_cases_latex: The update \(v_{k+1}=v_k\) preserves the current envelope.
The update \(v_{k+1}=\max\{h(x_{k+1}),\rho v_k\}\), when it does not exceed \(v_k\), gives contraction controlled by \(\rho\in(0,1)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(v_k\to0\), then \(h(x_k)\to0\) along accepted indices.
Envelope monotonicity alone does not imply strict progress at every iteration.
boundary_notes: A positive limiting envelope permits persistent nonzero infeasibility.
No inspected source supplied the precise envelope-update definition.
review_flags: A funnel-specific source supporting monotone envelope updates is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Feasibility Envelope
Monotone Feasibility Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decreasing upper bounds governing accepted constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\) measure constraint violation. A monotone feasibility envelope is a sequence \(\{V_k\}_{k\ge0}\) satisfying \(V_k\ge0\), \(V_{k+1}\le V_k\), and \(v(x_k)\le V_k\) for every accepted iterate \(x_k\). An update is strict whenever prescribed feasibility progress occurs, for example \(V_{k+1}\le V_k-\gamma\bigl(V_k-v(x_{k+1})\bigr)\) with \(\gamma\in(0,1]\); otherwise \(V_{k+1}=V_k\) may retain the current envelope. Thus accepted infeasibility need not decrease at every iteration, but it never exceeds the current nonincreasing bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone feasibility envelope is a nonincreasing sequence of bounds containing the violation of every accepted iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(v(x)\ge0\) for every point in the algorithmic domain.
Only accepted iterates are indexed by \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\le v(x_k)\le V_k\quad\text{and}\quad V_{k+1}\le V_k\quad\text{for all }k.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The core nonincreasing-envelope definition matches the node role, and definition is the appropriate kind. The optional update formula is a framework-specific choice rather than a source-independent consequence, so a precise funnel-method citation is required before selecting this formulation.

children.title: Tolerance-Tube Interpretations
children.top_down_role: Feasibility envelopes viewed as neighborhoods of the constraint set.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Tube Error-Bound Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local residual error bound converts a residual tolerance tube into a metric neighborhood; local Lipschitz continuity supplies the reverse comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C=\{x:c(x)=0\}. If, on a neighborhood U of C, \operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le \kappa\|c(x)\|, then for every V\ge0, \{x\in U:\|c(x)\|\le V\}\subseteq\{x\in U:\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa V\}. If c is locally L-Lipschitz, then also \|c(x)\|\le L\operatorname{dist}(x,C), giving a local two-sided comparison.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa\|c(x)\| on a neighborhood U of C.
For the reverse inclusion, c is L-Lipschitz on U.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{\|c\|\le V\}\cap U\subseteq\{\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,C)\le\kappa V\}\cap U.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which residual tubes are contained in metric neighborhoods of the feasible set.

notation.meaning: neighborhood on which the error bound holds

knowledge_statements.title: Hölder Metric-Tube Conversion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hölder residual error bound converts a residual tube of radius V into a metric tube of radius proportional to V raised to alpha.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=r^{-1}(0)\) and \(T(V)=\{x:\|r(x)\|\le V\}\). If, on a neighborhood \(U\) of \(C\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa\|r(x)\|^\alpha\) for constants \(\kappa>0\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), then \[T(V)\cap U\subseteq\{x\in U:\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa V^\alpha\}.\]
assumptions_latex: The stated Hölder error bound holds on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(V)\cap U\subseteq\{x\in U:\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa V^\alpha\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric interpretation under a Hölder residual error bound.

notation.meaning: Residual tolerance tube of radius V.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Radius Need Not Control Distance Linearly
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the constraint x squared equals zero, residual tolerance V permits distance of order square root of V, so linear residual-to-distance control fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For c(x)=x^2 on \mathbb R, C=\{0\} and \{x:|c(x)|\le V\}=[-\sqrt V,\sqrt V]. Hence no fixed \kappa satisfies \operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa|c(x)| near 0, and the residual tube of radius V is not contained in a metric tube of radius O(V).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{|c(x)|\le V}\operatorname{dist}(x,C)=\sqrt V\not=O(V).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of metric-tube interpretation without an error bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Constraint Residual Tubes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality residuals and positive inequality violations form one residual tube whose zero-radius member is the feasible set and whose radii are nested.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\le0\}\), define \(r(x)=(h(x),[g(x)]_+)\) and \(T(V)=\{x:\|r(x)\|\le V\}\). Then \(C=T(0)\), \(T(V_1)\subseteq T(V_2)\) whenever \(0\le V_1\le V_2\), and a point satisfies the declared mixed-constraint feasibility tolerance \(V\) exactly when it belongs to \(T(V)\).
assumptions_latex: A fixed norm is used on the combined residual space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C=T(0),\qquad 0\le V_1\le V_2\Rightarrow T(V_1)\subseteq T(V_2).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-tube representation for equality and inequality feasibility residuals.

notation.meaning: Componentwise positive part of the inequality residual.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tolerance-Tube Interpretation of a Feasibility Envelope
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(C:X\to Y\) map into a normed residual space \(Y\), and let the feasible set be \(\mathcal F=C^{-1}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-space tubes are defined exactly; their equivalence to distance neighborhoods requires an error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerance \(v\ge0\), the residual tolerance tube is \(T_C(v)=\{x\in X:\|C(x)\|_Y\le v\}\). A feasibility envelope \(v_k\) therefore defines the nested tubes \(T_C(v_k)\). If a local error bound holds on a neighborhood \(U\), namely \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal F)\le\kappa\|C(x)\|_Y\) for all \(x\in U\), then \(T_C(v)\cap U\subseteq\{x\in U:\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal F)\le\kappa v\}\). If, additionally, \(C\) is Lipschitz on \(U\) with constant \(L\) and vanishes on \(\mathcal F\), then \(\{x\in U:\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal F)\le v/L\}\subseteq T_C(v)\cap U\). Hence an envelope can be interpreted as a geometric distance tube only under the corresponding error-bound and Lipschitz hypotheses; without them it remains a residual sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tolerance tube of radius v is the set of points whose constraint residual norm is at most v. A funnel envelope produces nested residual tubes. Under a local error bound, such a tube lies inside a distance neighborhood of the feasible set. Under Lipschitz continuity, an appropriate distance neighborhood lies inside the residual tube. Without these regularity properties, residual tolerance and geometric distance are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: The distance comparison is asserted only on the neighborhood where the stated error bound or Lipschitz condition holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(v)=C^{-1}(\overline B_Y(0,v))\), with distance-tube inclusions available precisely under the stated error-bound and Lipschitz conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The residual tube is the inverse image under \(C\) of the closed radius-\(v\) ball centered at zero.
special_cases_latex: For linear equalities \(C(x)=Ax-b\), Hoffman-type error bounds can relate residual and distance tubes.
For mixed constraints, \(C\) may concatenate equality residuals and negative parts of inequality residuals.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(v_k\downarrow0\), residual tubes contract toward \(\mathcal F\).
Small residual need not imply proportionally small distance when no error bound holds.
boundary_notes: The tube need not be convex when \(C\) is nonlinear.
No inspected source directly supported this funnel-specific interpretation.
review_flags: A source is required for the intended tolerance-tube interpretation and its regularity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Tube Interpretation of a Feasibility Envelope
Tolerance-Tube Interpretations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric interpretation of funnel bounds as residual neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c(x)=0\}\) and let \(v(x)=\|c(x)\|\). For a funnel bound \(V_k\ge0\), the admissible region is the residual tolerance tube \(T_k=\{x:v(x)\le V_k\}=c^{-1}(B(0,V_k))\). Hence the funnel acceptance condition \(v(x_{k+1})\le V_k\) is exactly membership \(x_{k+1}\in T_k\). If \(V_{k+1}\le V_k\), then \(C\subseteq T_{k+1}\subseteq T_k\). This is a residual-space tube; equivalence to a metric neighborhood \(\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa V_k\}\) requires an additional local error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each funnel bound defines a residual tube around the feasible set; decreasing bounds produce nested tubes, while metric-distance equivalence requires an error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[T_k=c^{-1}(B(0,V_k)),\qquad C\subseteq T_{k+1}\subseteq T_k.\]

notation.meaning: residual tolerance tube at iteration k
closed residual-space ball of radius V_k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-image representation, nesting relation, and qualification concerning metric error bounds are mathematically correct, and representation fits the interpretation leaf. No inspectable source supports the use of this geometry as a feasibility-funnel interpretation.

children.title: Funnel Progress Iteration Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Iteration classes distinguished by their credited form of progress.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\) be the current iterate, \(y_k\) an accepted trial point, \(h\) a violation measure, \(v_k\) the current envelope, and \(f\) the objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted iterations are classified by the form of progress credited by the globalization mechanism; unsuccessful trials are excluded from the progress classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix constants \(\gamma_h,\gamma_f\in(0,1)\) and model-predicted decreases \(\Delta h_k^{\mathrm{pred}},\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\ge0\). An accepted iteration is an \(h\)-iteration if \(h(y_k)\le h(x_k)-\gamma_h\Delta h_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\) and the envelope is optionally contracted to some \(v_{k+1}\in[h(y_k),v_k]\). It is an \(f\)-iteration if \(h(y_k)\le v_k\) and \(f(y_k)\le f(x_k)-\gamma_f\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\), with no required contraction of \(v_k\). It is a restoration iteration if it is generated by a separately declared feasibility-restoration phase and satisfies that phase's re-entry condition. If several tests hold, a deterministic precedence rule assigns the credited class; without such a rule the iteration has a set of applicable labels. A rejected trial belongs to none of these progress classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An h-iteration is credited for sufficient constraint-violation decrease and may tighten the envelope. An f-iteration is credited for sufficient objective decrease while remaining inside the current envelope. A restoration iteration is generated by a distinct feasibility phase and must satisfy its re-entry condition. When multiple tests hold, the algorithm either applies a declared precedence rule or retains multiple labels. Rejected trials receive no progress label.
assumptions_latex: Predicted decreases are nonnegative and are computed by the active local model.
Every accepted trial satisfies the applicable funnel bound.
The restoration re-entry condition and any label precedence are declared by the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted iterations are classified by credited feasibility progress, objective progress within the funnel, or restoration re-entry according to the stated inequalities and phase identity.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The taxonomy is a labeling map from accepted transition data to \(2^{\{h,f,R\}}\), reduced to a single label when a precedence rule is imposed.
special_cases_latex: An accepted point may satisfy both sufficient objective and feasibility decrease.
An envelope-contraction iteration is normally an \(h\)-iteration, but contraction alone is insufficient unless the required feasibility-decrease test also holds.
immediate_consequences_latex: An \(f\)-iteration may increase \(h\) provided the new point remains below \(v_k\).
A restoration iteration is distinguished by its generating phase, not solely by observing a decrease in \(h\).
boundary_notes: The constants and predicted-decrease models are method-specific.
No inspected source supplied an exact funnel iteration taxonomy.
review_flags: A precise funnel-method source is required for the h-, f-, and restoration-iteration labels.
knowledge_statements.title: Funnel Progress Iteration Taxonomy
Feasibility-Type Funnel Iterations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility-type iteration accepts a funnel-admissible trial point that achieves a prescribed fraction of predicted violation reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_k=v(x_k)\le V_k\), and let a trial point \(x_k^+\) have predicted violation reduction \(\Delta v_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0\). A feasibility-type funnel iteration accepts the trial point when \(v(x_k^+)\le V_k\) and \(v_k-v(x_k^+)\ge\eta_v\Delta v_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\), where \(\eta_v\in(0,1)\). After acceptance set \(x_{k+1}=x_k^+\) and choose \(V_{k+1}\) so that \(v(x_{k+1})\le V_{k+1}\le V_k\), with a strict reduction of \(V_k\) whenever the method's feasibility-progress rule requires it. Rejection leaves the accepted iterate unchanged and may contract the step-control parameter.
assumptions_latex: The current accepted point satisfies \(v_k\le V_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v(x_k^+)\le V_k\ \text{and}\ v_k-v(x_k^+)\ge\eta_v\Delta v_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{k+1}=x_k^+.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance regime driven by sufficient constraint-violation reduction.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Condition is a plausible role for an iteration acceptance regime, but the sufficient-reduction test is only a generic proposed variant. The violation model from which \(\Delta v_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\) is computed is not defined, and no source identifies these tests and envelope updates as a particular funnel method.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Type Funnel Iterations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimality-type iteration accepts sufficient objective decrease only when the trial point remains inside the current feasibility funnel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(v(x_k)\le V_k\), and suppose a trial point \(x_k^+\) has predicted objective reduction \(\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0\). An optimality-type funnel iteration accepts the trial point when \(v(x_k^+)\le V_k\) and \(f(x_k)-f(x_k^+)\ge\eta_f\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\), with \(\eta_f\in(0,1)\). It then sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k^+\) and selects \(V_{k+1}\) satisfying \(v(x_{k+1})\le V_{k+1}\le V_k\). Thus objective improvement is credited only inside the current feasibility envelope; failure of either test causes rejection or switching to feasibility-oriented progress.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v(x_k^+)\le V_k\ \text{and}\ f(x_k)-f(x_k^+)\ge\eta_f\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{k+1}=x_k^+.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-progress regime constrained by funnel admissibility.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The statement describes a coherent possible optimality-type acceptance condition, and condition fits the terminal regime. Nevertheless, the objective model defining \(\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\), the envelope update, and the rejection-or-switching behavior are method-dependent and lack a supporting locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Funnel Iteration Switching Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A switching rule selects objective progress when predicted feasibility disturbance is sufficiently small; otherwise it invokes feasibility progress, always enforcing funnel admissibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), funnel bound \(V_k\), predicted reductions \(\Delta v_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\) and \(\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\), and constants \(\tau>0\), \(p\ge1\), classify iteration \(k\) as optimality-type when \(\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0\) and \(\Delta v_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\le\tau(\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}})^p\); otherwise classify it as feasibility-type. Apply the corresponding sufficient-reduction test, always requiring \(v(x_k^+)\le V_k\). If accepted, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k^+\) and choose \(v(x_{k+1})\le V_{k+1}\le V_k\); if rejected, retain \(x_k\) and reduce the step-control radius. Stop when prescribed feasibility and stationarity tolerances both hold.
assumptions_latex: Both objective and violation models provide predicted reductions.
Trial steps are controlled by a radius or comparable size parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0\ \text{and}\ \Delta v_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\le\tau(\Delta f_k^{\mathrm{pred}})^p\Rightarrow\text{optimality-type};\quad\text{otherwise feasibility-type}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-based switching between feasibility and optimality progress tests.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is acceptable as a role for a complete switching procedure, but the displayed power-law rule is explicitly generic and cannot be treated as a canonical funnel switching regime without a precise source. Its scaling also depends on the units and normalization of the two predicted reductions.

children.title: Funnel Method Families
children.top_down_role: Major step-control and information variants of feasibility funnels.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a funnel method maintain \(h(x_k)\le v_k\), where \(h\) is constraint violation and \(v_k\) is a nonincreasing envelope.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by step-control mechanism and information regime, not by convergence rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family signature of a funnel method is \(\Sigma=(S,I,R)\). The step-control component satisfies \(S\in\{\mathrm{line\ search},\mathrm{trust\ region},\mathrm{regularization}\}\), according as trial size is controlled by a scalar step length, a region constraint \(\|s\|\le\Delta_k\), or an explicit regularization term. The information component is a subset \(I\subseteq\{\mathrm{exact\ derivatives},\mathrm{inexact\ derivatives},\mathrm{derivative\ free},\mathrm{stochastic}\}\), determined by the oracle used to construct and assess trial steps. The recovery component satisfies \(R\in\{\mathrm{none},\mathrm{restoration},\mathrm{penalty\ fallback},\mathrm{filter\ fallback}\}\). Every member must retain the defining funnel invariant and must specify acceptance, envelope update, and unsuccessful-trial update rules. Two methods are in the same family only when their signatures agree; differing numerical parameter choices alone do not create a new family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A funnel method family is identified by its step-control mechanism, information regime, and recovery mechanism. Step control may use line search, trust regions, or regularization. Information may be exact, inexact, derivative-free, or stochastic. Recovery may be absent or use restoration, penalty, or filter fallback. Every method still has to state how trials are accepted, how the envelope changes, and how unsuccessful trials alter the control state. Parameter changes alone do not define a different family.
assumptions_latex: The method maintains a nonincreasing feasibility envelope on accepted iterates.
Exactly one principal step-control category is selected; multiple information labels may apply.
Any stochastic information label requires an explicitly stated probabilistic acceptance regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma=(S,I,R)\) gives the method-family classification while preserving the common funnel invariant and explicit state-update rules.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The family space is a product of step-control, information, and recovery categories.
special_cases_latex: A trust-region funnel with exact derivatives and restoration has signature \((\mathrm{trust\ region},\{\mathrm{exact\ derivatives}\},\mathrm{restoration})\).
A derivative-free regularization funnel without recovery has signature \((\mathrm{regularization},\{\mathrm{derivative\ free}\},\mathrm{none})\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Methods with the same funnel geometry can belong to different families because their trial-size or information mechanisms differ.
A method that drops the envelope invariant is not a funnel method under this definition.
boundary_notes: Hybrid methods with simultaneously active step-control mechanisms require a set-valued extension of \(S\).
No inspected source canonically supports this complete family classification.
review_flags: A funnel literature source is required for the proposed method-family categories.

children.title: Trust-Region Funnel Methods
children.top_down_role: Feasibility envelopes coupled to restricted composite-step models.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal–Tangential Sufficient-Decrease Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite step is adequate when its normal and tangential components attain declared fractions of method-specific reference decreases and their sum obeys the trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let s_k=n_k+t_k satisfy \|s_k\|\le\Delta_k. Given declared nonnegative reference decreases D_k^n,D_k^t, the step satisfies a fixed-fraction model-decrease certificate when m_k^v(0)-m_k^v(n_k)\ge\kappa_nD_k^n and m_k^o(n_k)-m_k^o(n_k+t_k)\ge\kappa_tD_k^t, where \kappa_n,\kappa_t\in(0,1], and t_k satisfies the declared linearized-feasibility safeguard.
assumptions_latex: D_k^n,D_k^t\ge0 are explicitly defined and computable.
The tangential safeguard and joint trust-region constraint are enforced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{pred}_k^v\ge\kappa_nD_k^n,\quad\operatorname{pred}_k^o\ge\kappa_tD_k^t,\quad\|n_k+t_k\|\le\Delta_k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract adequacy test for an approximate composite step; reference decreases remain method-specific.

notation.meaning: method-specific reference normal and tangential decreases

knowledge_statements.title: Separate Component Bounds Do Not Ensure Composite Feasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two individually admissible step components can sum to a step outside the trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In one dimension, let n=\Delta and t=\Delta. Then |n|\le\Delta and |t|\le\Delta, but |n+t|=2\Delta>\Delta. Thus independently bounding normal and tangential components does not enforce the trust-region constraint on the composite step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |n|,|t|\le\Delta\not\Rightarrow|n+t|\le\Delta.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of independently imposed radius bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Step Trust-Region Funnel Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family couples a jointly bounded normal–tangential step with funnel screening and feasibility- or optimality-specific model agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region funnel method forms a trial step s_k=n_k+t_k within a joint trust region \|s_k\|\le\Delta_k. The normal component targets a local constraint-violation model; the tangential component targets objective or Lagrangian reduction while preserving the achieved linearized-feasibility progress. An evaluated trial is accepted only if it lies within the current feasibility envelope and satisfies the iteration-type model-agreement test.
assumptions_latex: Smooth derivative-based local models are available.
The combined step, rather than merely each component, satisfies the trust-region constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_k=n_k+t_k,\quad\|s_k\|\le\Delta_k,\quad\text{acceptance}\Rightarrow v(x_k+s_k)\le V_k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining structure of derivative-based trust-region funnel methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Funnel Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite-step trust-region method with funnel-constrained acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\), \(V_0\ge v(x_0)\), and \(\Delta_0>0\), at iteration \(k\) compute a composite step \(s_k=n_k+t_k\) satisfying \(\|s_k\|\le\Delta_k\), where \(n_k\) targets reduction of a local violation model and \(t_k\) targets objective or Lagrangian reduction subject to the normal-step linearization. Form \(x_k^+=x_k+s_k\). Accept only if \(v(x_k^+)\le V_k\) and the designated feasibility- or optimality-type actual-to-predicted reduction test holds. On acceptance set \(x_{k+1}=x_k^+\) and \(v(x_{k+1})\le V_{k+1}\le V_k\); on rejection set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and contract \(\Delta_k\). Stop at the prescribed feasibility and stationarity tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region funnel method computes a bounded composite step and accepts it only when funnel feasibility and the selected model-reduction test both pass.
assumptions_latex: Smooth local models of objective and constraint violation are available.
The composite step obeys the trust-region bound \(\|n_k+t_k\|\le\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\quad\text{only if}\quad v(x_k+s_k)\le V_k\ \text{and the selected reduction test succeeds}.\]

notation.meaning: normal and tangential components of the trial step

children.title: Funnel–Restoration Methods
children.top_down_role: Feasibility envelopes supplemented by explicit restoration phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Can Stop at Positive Violation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration can terminate at a positive-violation stationary point; smoothness alone cannot guarantee a compatible return.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c(x)=x^2+1\) and \(h(x)=|c(x)|=x^2+1\), the feasible set is empty and \(x=0\) is a stationary global minimizer of \(h\) with \(h(0)=1\). Therefore restoration cannot be guaranteed to produce arbitrarily small violation or a point below an arbitrary funnel bound without feasibility and descent assumptions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Obstruction to unconditional restoration success.

knowledge_statements.title: Funnel–Restoration Phase Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family is characterized by a separate feasibility phase triggered by main-phase failure and an explicit compatibility test before returning to the funnel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A funnel–restoration method enters a restoration phase when the main phase cannot produce an acceptable trial under its step-control rules. Restoration seeks reduction of a declared violation measure h independently of objective progress. Return to the main phase requires a restoration output satisfying the current method's funnel-compatibility test; otherwise restoration may terminate at a stationary point of h or report failure.
assumptions_latex: h(x)\ge0 and h(x)=0 exactly at feasible points.
The main-phase trigger and restoration-return test are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{main failure}\to\text{restoration}\to\{\text{compatible return, violation stationarity, or failure}\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining interface between a funnel main phase and explicit feasibility restoration.

knowledge_statements.title: Funnel–Restoration Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic funnel globalization with an explicit feasibility-restoration phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given continuously differentiable \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), set \(h(x)=\lVert c(x)\rVert\), choose \(x_0\), and initialize \(H_0>h(x_0)\). At iteration \(k\), compute a trial step \(s_k\). Accept \(x_k+s_k\) only if \(h(x_k+s_k)\le H_k\) and the prescribed feasibility or objective decrease test holds; then choose \(H_{k+1}\in[h(x_{k+1}),H_k]\). If no acceptable step is produced, enter restoration and compute \(x_k^R\) satisfying \(h(x_k^R)<H_k\). Resume the main phase from \(x_k^R\); terminate at a stated feasibility and first-order optimality tolerance, or report restoration stationarity or failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a decreasing feasibility envelope; accept productive steps inside it, and invoke a separate feasibility-reduction phase when the main phase cannot produce an acceptable step.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable on an open set containing the iterates.
Each accepted or restored point satisfies the current funnel bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{k+1}\le H_k\), and every resumed main-phase iterate satisfies \(h(x_{k+1})\le H_k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic funnel–restoration architecture determined by the node role
A funnel-specific authoritative algorithm and acceptance test are required

children.title: Derivative-Free Funnel Methods
children.top_down_role: Funnel globalization using interpolation or other derivative-free models.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Free Funnel Model Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family uses value-based local models, a feasibility funnel, and explicit sample-geometry management; merely replacing derivatives by uncontrolled differences is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A model-based derivative-free funnel method constructs local models of f and the constraint residuals from sampled function values, not supplied derivatives, and screens evaluated trial points by a feasibility envelope together with a model-progress test. Geometry management maintains sample sets accurate enough on the current sampling region for the selected model class.
assumptions_latex: Objective and constraint values can be evaluated at sampled points.
A declared model class and sampling region are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{information input}=(f(x_i),c(x_i))\text{ values, with no required derivative oracle}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical information boundary for model-based derivative-free funnel methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Linear and Fully Quadratic Derivative-Free Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fully linear and fully quadratic models approximate values and derivatives uniformly over the sampling region with the standard trust-region orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On B(x_k,\Delta_k), a differentiable scalar model m is fully linear for q if constants \kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg}>0, uniform over the model sequence, satisfy |q(x_k+s)-m(x_k+s)|\le\kappa_{ef}\Delta_k^2 and \|\nabla q(x_k+s)-\nabla m(x_k+s)\|\le\kappa_{eg}\Delta_k for every \|s\|\le\Delta_k. A twice-differentiable model is fully quadratic if uniform constants bound the function, gradient, and Hessian errors by \kappa_{ef}\Delta_k^3, \kappa_{eg}\Delta_k^2, and \kappa_{eh}\Delta_k, respectively. A derivative-free funnel analysis must impose the selected class on the objective and relevant scalar constraint models.
assumptions_latex: The function and model possess the derivatives appearing in the selected accuracy definition.
The accuracy constants are uniform over the model sequence and sampling regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
ext{fully linear}: (|q-m|,\|

abla m\|)=O(\Delta_k^2,\Delta_k);\quad 	ext{fully quadratic}: (|q-m|,\|
abla q-
abla m\|,\|
abla^2q-
abla^2m\|)=O(\Delta_k^3,\Delta_k^2,\Delta_k).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative accuracy classes required by interpolation-based derivative-free funnel models.

knowledge_statements.title: Poisedness Is Necessary for Interpolation Accuracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerate sample geometry cannot identify local derivatives or guarantee accurate models, even when all sampled values agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the interpolation matrix for the selected polynomial basis is singular, sampled values do not determine a unique interpolation model. Distinct smooth functions can agree at every sample point while having different gradients at the center; consequently no uniform fully-linear gradient bound follows from those samples alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{singular geometry}\Rightarrow\text{model nonuniqueness and no sample-only gradient guarantee}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability failure for degenerate derivative-free sample geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Sample Geometry Does Not Identify an Interpolation Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerate sample geometry cannot uniquely determine the local interpolation model or support the usual model-accuracy guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the interpolation matrix for the selected polynomial basis is singular, the sampled values do not determine unique model coefficients. Consequently, those samples alone cannot guarantee a uniform fully-linear gradient-accuracy bound for an arbitrarily selected interpolant.
assumptions_latex: The interpolation matrix for the selected basis and sample set is singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{singular interpolation geometry}\Rightarrow\text{model nonuniqueness and no sample-only fully-linear guarantee}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability failure for degenerate derivative-free sample geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Free Funnel Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-based derivative-free funnel method for smooth equality-constrained optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), initialize \(x_0\), radius \(\Delta_0>0\), funnel bound \(H_0>\lVert c(x_0)\rVert\), and a poised sample set. At iteration \(k\), construct interpolation models \(m_k^f\) and \(m_k^c\) using only sampled values of \(f\) and \(c\). Compute \(s_k\) with \(\lVert s_k\rVert\le\Delta_k\). Accept it only if the evaluated point satisfies \(\lVert c(x_k+s_k)\rVert\le H_k\) and an actual-versus-predicted feasibility or objective decrease test; otherwise shrink \(\Delta_k\) or improve poisedness. Update \(H_k\) monotonically after acceptance and stop when model-based feasibility and criticality measures meet prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build interpolation models from function values, restrict trial steps by a radius, and accept evaluated points only when they satisfy the funnel and model-agreement tests.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are smooth on a neighborhood of the sampled level set.
Sample sets are maintained sufficiently poised for the selected interpolation models.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure uses no derivative evaluations and preserves \(\lVert c(x_{k+1})\rVert\le H_k\) at every accepted iteration.

children.title: Funnel Convergence-Complexity Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Global convergence and work classifications for funnel frameworks.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: Curtis, Robinson, and Samadi, Complexity Analysis of a Trust Funnel Algorithm for Equality Constrained Optimization

locator_traceability.matched_excerpt: - 12 Analysis of Convergence p. 291

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be a funnel algorithm generating accepted iterates \(x_k\), violation envelopes \(v_k\), and a stationarity measure \(\chi(x_k)\ge0\). Let \(W_k\) count a declared unit of work.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This slot defines how a funnel guarantee is recorded; it does not assert that every funnel method satisfies such a guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A funnel convergence–complexity guarantee is a tuple \(G=(\mathcal H,\mathcal C,W,N)\). The hypothesis set \(\mathcal H\) states the smoothness, boundedness, model-accuracy, acceptance, and subproblem-solution conditions. The convergence component \(\mathcal C\) specifies an explicit alternative, such as finite termination at \(h(x_k)\le\varepsilon_h\) and \(\chi(x_k)\le\varepsilon_s\), or asymptotic relations \(h(x_k)\to0\) and \(\liminf_k\chi(x_k)=0\). The work measure \(W\) identifies whether iterations, objective evaluations, constraint evaluations, derivative evaluations, or linear-algebra operations are counted. The complexity map \(N(\varepsilon_h,\varepsilon_s)\) is a bound such that some index with both residuals below their tolerances occurs by work count \(N\). A claim lacking either its work unit or its accuracy criterion is a convergence statement, not an evaluation-complexity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A funnel convergence–complexity guarantee records four items: its hypotheses, its exact convergence alternative, the unit of work being counted, and a tolerance-dependent work bound. Convergence may mean finite approximate termination or an asymptotic feasibility and stationarity statement. Complexity requires an explicit count such as iterations or evaluations and an explicit target accuracy. Without both, the claim is only a convergence guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(\chi\) are the explicitly declared feasibility and stationarity measures.
\(W_k\) is nondecreasing and counts a specified work unit.

children.title: Funnel Global Convergence Families
children.top_down_role: Global alternatives induced by feasibility envelopes and step control.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Monotonicity Alone Gives No Stationarity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonincreasing feasible envelope does not force feasibility or optimality progress; sufficient-decrease and step-control hypotheses are essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conditions \(0\le h(x_k)\le H_k\) and \(H_{k+1}\le H_k\) alone imply neither \(h(x_k)\to0\) nor first-order stationarity. For the unconstrained problem \(\min_x x\), let \(h\equiv0\), \(x_k=0\), and \(H_k=0\). Both envelope conditions hold, but the iterates are not stationary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(h(x_k)\le H_k,\ H_{k+1}\le H_k\bigr)\not\Rightarrow\text{stationarity}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for funnel global-convergence claims.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Limit Need Not Admit KKT Multipliers Without a Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible funnel limit can be constrained-optimal yet fail the KKT multiplier equation when the constraint gradient is degenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}f(x)=x\) subject to \(c(x)=x^2=0\). The feasible set is \(\{0\}\), so \(x^*=0\) is globally constrained-optimal. Nevertheless, \(f'(0)=1\) and \(c'(0)=0\), so no \(\lambda\) satisfies \(f'(0)+\lambda c'(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*=0\text{ is globally feasible-optimal},\qquad \nexists\lambda:\ f'(0)+\lambda c'(0)=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-qualification boundary for interpreting feasible funnel limits as KKT-stationary.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\{x_k\}\) be accepted iterates of a funnel method, \(h(x_k)\le v_k\), and let \(\chi(x_k)\) be a nonnegative stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of the logical strength of global conclusions, not a theorem asserting those conclusions for a particular algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A funnel global-convergence claim is feasibility-global if every infinite generated sequence satisfies \(\liminf_k h(x_k)=0\), and strongly feasibility-global if \(h(x_k)\to0\). It is subsequential first-order global if every generated sequence has an accumulation subsequence \(K\) with \(h(x_k)\to0\) and \(\chi(x_k)\to0\) for \(k\in K\). It is full-sequence first-order global if \(h(x_k)\to0\) and \(\chi(x_k)\to0\) along the entire accepted sequence. It is alternative-global if its conclusion explicitly allows finitely many outcomes, for example approximate first-order termination, restoration termination at a stationary residual point, or divergence of a declared control state. A claim belongs to exactly the strongest family whose quantified conclusion it establishes; statements about \(\liminf\), subsequences, and full-sequence limits are not identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Funnel convergence claims are classified by their quantified strength. Feasibility-global claims force violation arbitrarily close to zero; strong feasibility claims force violation to converge to zero. Subsequential first-order claims provide a feasible stationary subsequence, while full-sequence claims make both residuals converge along all accepted iterates. Alternative-global claims state a finite list of possible outcomes. A claim is assigned to the strongest class actually established, and these quantifier patterns are kept distinct.
assumptions_latex: The generated sequence and the indexing of accepted iterates are explicit.
\(h\) and \(\chi\) are fixed throughout the claim.
Any alternative outcome is mathematically defined rather than described informally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family label is determined by whether the conclusion uses \(\liminf\), full feasibility convergence, a stationary subsequence, full-sequence first-order convergence, or an explicit global alternative.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Subsequential first-order global convergence may be written \(\liminf_k\max\{h(x_k),\chi(x_k)\}=0\) when a common subsequence realizes both residual limits.
special_cases_latex: Finite termination at \(h\le\varepsilon_h\) and \(\chi\le\varepsilon_s\) is an approximate alternative rather than an asymptotic full-sequence statement.
A claim that every accumulation point is feasible and stationary is distinct from merely asserting existence of one such accumulation point.
immediate_consequences_latex: Full-sequence first-order global convergence implies subsequential convergence whenever an infinite subsequence exists.
Feasibility-global convergence alone does not imply optimality stationarity.
boundary_notes: The definition does not address local rates or evaluation complexity.
No inspected source established this exact funnel-specific hierarchy.

Funnel Global Convergence Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract convergence alternative shared by monotone-envelope funnel methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_k\ge0\) be constraint violation and \(H_k\) a nonincreasing funnel bound with \(h_k\le H_k\). Suppose every nonstationary accepted iteration yields a uniformly quantified decrease in either violation or an optimality measure, unsuccessful step control drives the model radius to zero, and the models are first-order consistent on a compact set containing the iterates. Then every infinite run has the funnel alternative: either \(h_k\to0\) and every accumulation point is first-order stationary for the constrained problem, or a subsequence generated by feasibility or restoration iterations converges to a stationary point of the violation problem with positive violation. A finite run terminates at one of the corresponding certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under consistent models and sufficient decrease, an infinite funnel run approaches constrained stationarity or exposes positive-violation stationarity of the feasibility problem.
assumptions_latex: Iterates remain in a compact set and local models are first-order consistent.
Accepted steps give sufficient decrease; rejected-step radii tend to zero when rejection persists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(h_k\to0\) with constrained-stationary accumulation points, or \(\liminf_k h_k>0\) along a subsequence converging to violation stationarity.
review_flags: Exact stationarity measures and constraint qualifications vary among funnel convergence theorems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is theorem-like rather than a principle: it asserts a global convergence alternative. No source is supplied, and phrases such as “uniformly quantified decrease,” “first-order consistent,” and “first-order stationary” do not define the applicable stationarity measures, problem class, constraint qualifications, or precise iteration subsequences. The stronger claim that every accumulation point is constrained-stationary is not justified by the listed abstract assumptions.

children.title: Funnel Evaluation-Complexity Families
children.top_down_role: Work classifications for feasibility and optimality phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Phase-Partition Evaluation Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate phase bounds yield a total evaluation bound only when every oracle call is counted once and all overhead is controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every oracle request through termination is assigned exactly once to feasibility work, optimality work, or overhead, with counts \(N_F,N_O,N_R\). Then \(N_{\mathrm{eval}}=N_F+N_O+N_R\). If \(N_F\le C_F\epsilon_f^{-p}\), \(N_O\le C_O\epsilon_o^{-q}\), and \(N_R\le C_R(\epsilon_f^{-p}+\epsilon_o^{-q})+C_0\), then \(N_{\mathrm{eval}}\le(C_F+C_R)\epsilon_f^{-p}+(C_O+C_R)\epsilon_o^{-q}+C_0\).
assumptions_latex: Oracle calls are partitioned disjointly and exhaustively into \(N_F,N_O,N_R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{eval}}=O(\epsilon_f^{-p}+\epsilon_o^{-q}).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional aggregation of feasibility, optimality, and overhead oracle counts.

notation.meaning: Rejected-trial, restoration, repair, and other overhead count.

knowledge_statements.title: Funnel Evaluation-Oracle Accounting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Funnel evaluation complexity must count each declared oracle separately through a precise stopping certificate, including rejected, restoration, and model-repair work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a declared stopping time \tau(\epsilon_f,\epsilon_o), report separate counts N_f,N_c,N_g,N_J,N_H through \tau for objective, constraint, gradient, Jacobian, and Hessian-information requests. Counts include unsuccessful trials, restoration, model repair, and termination checks. A weighted total \sum_i w_iN_i is meaningful only when fixed weights and the treatment of cached or simultaneous calls are declared.
assumptions_latex: The stopping time and oracle interface are declared before counting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\rm eval}\text{ is well defined only relative to the declared oracle vector and stopping time.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counting convention for evaluation-complexity claims about funnel methods.

notation.meaning: first stopping index meeting the declared feasibility and optimality tests

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Bounds Do Not Automatically Bound Evaluations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepted-iteration complexity is not evaluation complexity unless all intervening oracle work is controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bound on accepted or outer iterations implies an evaluation bound only if the number of rejected trials, restoration evaluations, and model-repair evaluations charged between counted iterations is uniformly bounded or separately summed. Without such control, finitely many accepted iterations may coexist with arbitrarily many evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\rm accepted}=O(B)\not\Rightarrow N_{\rm eval}=O(B).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between successful-iteration complexity and oracle complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Funnel Evaluation-Complexity Families

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N_f(\epsilon_f)\) count evaluations required to obtain \(h(x)\le\epsilon_f\), and let \(N_o(\epsilon_f,\epsilon_o)\) count additional evaluations required, while maintaining the funnel, to obtain an optimality measure \(\chi(x)\le\epsilon_o\). A funnel evaluation-complexity family with exponents \(p,q>0\) and evaluation cost \(
u\) satisfies \[N_{\mathrm{eval}}(\epsilon_f,\epsilon_o)\le 
u igl(C_f\epsilon_f^{-p}+C_o\epsilon_o^{-q}+C_0 igr)\] for all sufficiently small positive tolerances, where the constants are tolerance-independent. Evaluations spent on rejected trials, model improvement, and restoration must be included in \(N_{\mathrm{eval}}\); derivative orders counted by \(
u\) must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complexity is classified by separate feasibility and optimality tolerance exponents, while counting all trial, model-improvement, and restoration evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(\epsilon_f>0\) and \(\epsilon_o>0\) are prescribed feasibility and optimality tolerances.
All constants in the bound are independent of \(\epsilon_f\) and \(\epsilon_o\).

children.title: Hybrid Globalization Architectures
children.top_down_role: Frameworks switching or combining penalty, filter, funnel, merit, and restoration mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q_k\) denote the complete state of a constrained optimization algorithm, including its iterate, penalty parameters, filter entries, funnel envelope, trust-region radius, and restoration status when applicable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic architecture combining or switching among penalty, merit, filter, funnel, and restoration mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hybrid globalization architecture is a state-transition system \(\mathcal H=(Q,\mathcal G,\chi,A,U)\), where \(Q\) is the state space, \(\mathcal G\) contains at least two distinct globalization mechanisms, \(\chi:Q\times D\to2^{\mathcal G}\setminus\{\varnothing\}\) selects the mechanism or mechanisms applied to trial data \(D\), \(A\) is the resulting acceptance predicate, and \(U\) updates all component states after acceptance or rejection. Distinct mechanisms include scalar merit or penalty decrease, filter nondominance, funnel containment, and restoration generation. The selector and update maps must specify entry, exit, and re-entry conditions whenever control switches. A sequential hybrid has \(|\chi(q,d)|=1\); a conjunctive hybrid requires all selected acceptance predicates; a fallback hybrid activates a secondary mechanism after failure of a declared primary test. Merely changing parameters within one acceptance predicate is not a hybrid architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid globalization architecture is a state machine containing at least two genuinely different acceptance or recovery mechanisms. It defines which mechanisms are active for each state and trial, how their acceptance tests combine, and how every component's state changes after acceptance or rejection. Sequential hybrids select one mechanism, conjunctive hybrids require several tests, and fallback hybrids activate a secondary mechanism after a declared failure. Parameter changes within a single mechanism do not constitute hybridity.
assumptions_latex: All component mechanisms have well-defined acceptance predicates and state variables.
Switching decisions depend on available state and trial data.
Updates preserve every invariant required by mechanisms that remain active.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is hybrid exactly when \(|\mathcal G|\ge2\) for distinct globalization mechanisms and explicit selection, acceptance-combination, and joint-update maps are supplied.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The architecture may be represented by a labeled directed graph whose nodes are mechanism states and whose edges carry trigger and update conditions.
special_cases_latex: A filter method invoking restoration after repeated rejection is a fallback hybrid.
A trial required to satisfy both a funnel bound and merit decrease is a conjunctive hybrid.
immediate_consequences_latex: Unspecified switching cannot define a reproducible hybrid algorithm.
Inactive mechanism states may still require updates if they affect later re-entry.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert convergence of arbitrary switching policies.
The inspected source supports merit, filter, and restoration mechanisms but not this complete architecture-level definition.

notation.meaning: Combined acceptance predicate and joint state-update map.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Phases Replacing Restoration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace restoration by descent on an always-defined exact-penalty objective, returning once compatibility or sufficient penalty decrease is achieved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality constraints \(c(x)=0\), define \(\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\lVert c(x)\rVert_1\) with \(\rho>0\). When the main globalization phase cannot compute or accept a trial step, start a penalty phase at the current point and apply a globally defined descent procedure to \(\Phi_\rho\). Accept an iterate \(x^+\) once it either satisfies the main phase's compatibility test or achieves prescribed sufficient decrease in \(\Phi_\rho\); otherwise continue the penalty phase and, when its test requires, increase \(\rho\). Return \(x^+\) to the main phase. Terminate if feasibility and constrained stationarity tolerances hold, or if a declared stationary certificate for \(\Phi_\rho\) is obtained.
assumptions_latex: The penalty-phase descent method is well defined from every admitted iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every penalty-phase return satisfies its declared compatibility condition or a verified decrease condition for \(\Phi_\rho\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-penalty fallback phase used instead of a separate restoration subproblem.

notation.meaning: point returned by the penalty phase

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a quadratic or local nonlinear-programming model with objective \(q(s)\), equality residuals \(a_i(s)\), \(i\in E\), and inequality residuals \(b_i(s)\ge0\), \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elastic exact-penalty phases whose auxiliary formulation is feasible for every base trial and which replace a separate feasibility-restoration subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty phase replaces restoration when it solves an elastic problem \(\min_{s,u,v,w}\;q(s)+M\bigl(\mathbf1^T(u+v)+\mathbf1^Tw\bigr)\) subject to \(a_i(s)+u_i-v_i=0\) for \(i\in E\), \(b_i(s)+w_i\ge0\) for \(i\in I\), and \(u,v,w\ge0\). For every \(s\), choosing \(u_i=[-a_i(s)]_+\), \(v_i=[a_i(s)]_+\), and \(w_i=[-b_i(s)]_+\) makes the elastic constraints feasible, so the phase has no infeasible-start obstruction. It is an exact-penalty replacement when there exists \(M_*<\infty\) such that, for \(M>M_*\), any relevant local solution associated with a feasible solution of the unelastic model has \(u=v=w=0\). Positive elastic variables measure residual infeasibility and may trigger an increase of \(M\), rather than invocation of a distinct restoration phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restoration-replacing penalty phase introduces nonnegative elastic variables into equality and inequality constraints and penalizes their sum with weight M. Suitable elastic variables make the subproblem feasible for any proposed primal step. The phase is exact when, above a finite penalty threshold, solutions corresponding to feasible solutions have zero elastic variables. If elastic variables remain positive, the penalty weight can be increased instead of launching a separate restoration problem.
assumptions_latex: The elastic objective is bounded below or otherwise solved within a bounded step region.
The exactness statement is restricted to points satisfying the constraint qualification and multiplier conditions required by exact-penalty theory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic formulation is always feasible in its auxiliary variables and replaces dedicated restoration when exactness forces zero elasticity for sufficiently large \(M\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A single scalar \(\eta\ge0\) with \(|a_i(s)|\le\eta\) and \(-b_i(s)\le\eta\), penalized by \(M\eta\), gives an \(\ell_\infty\)-elastic variant.
Separate \(u,v,w\) variables yield an \(\ell_1\)-elastic variant.
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic program, the scalar-elastic big-\(M\) problem is feasible by choosing \(\eta\) sufficiently large.
When the unelastic model is feasible and exactness applies, the optimal elastic variables vanish.
immediate_consequences_latex: Subproblem infeasibility caused solely by the linearized constraints is removed by elasticity.
Always-feasible refers to the elastic formulation, not to feasibility of the original nonlinear constraints.
boundary_notes: A finite exactness threshold requires additional regularity and multiplier hypotheses.
The cited source treats quadratic-programming Phase I replacement; extension to arbitrary nonlinear local models requires separate support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infeasible Stationarity at an Insufficient Penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp warning that a stationary or minimizing penalty-phase point need not be feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min (x-1)^2\) subject to \(x=0\), with \(\Phi_\rho(x)=(x-1)^2+\rho|x|\). For every \(0<\rho<2\), \(x_\rho=1-\rho/2>0\) is the unique global minimizer of \(\Phi_\rho\), hence is stationary for the penalty problem but infeasible for the constraint. At \(\rho=2\), the constrained point \(x=0\) becomes a penalty minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact-penalty fallback can terminate at an infeasible global minimizer when its penalty is below the exactness threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_\rho=1-\rho/2\neq0\quad\text{and}\quad x_\rho\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R}\Phi_\rho(x).

notation.meaning: global minimizer of the penalized problem

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Solvability of a Penalty Replacement Phase
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence conditions behind the claim that a penalty fallback phase is always solvable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\neq\varnothing\) be compact and let \(f\) and \(c\) be continuous on \(D\). For every finite \(\rho>0\), the exact-penalty problem
\[\min_{x\in D}\ \Phi_\rho(x):=f(x)+\rho\lVert c(x)\rVert_1\]
has a global minimizer. Without compactness, coercivity, or another level-boundedness condition, finiteness and continuity of \(\Phi_\rho\) do not imply attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty replacement phase is guaranteed to have a solution on a compact admitted set, but being defined everywhere does not by itself make the phase solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}\Phi_\rho(x)\neq\varnothing.

notation.meaning: admitted domain of the penalty phase

children.title: Filter Methods with Merit Fallback
children.top_down_role: Partial-order acceptance supplemented by scalar decrease mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Hybrid Acceptance Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter mode checks every archive entry; merit mode requires a fixed fraction of positive predicted scalar decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trial y has a filter certificate when, for every (h_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k, h(y)\le(1-\gamma_h)h_i or f(y)\le f_i-\gamma_fh(y). In merit mode it has a fallback certificate when M_{\rho_k}(x_k)-M_{\rho_k}(y)\ge\sigma\operatorname{pred}_k with \sigma\in(0,1) and \operatorname{pred}_k>0. Acceptance requires the certificate of the active mode.
assumptions_latex: The active mode is selected before the trial is tested.
The chosen filter convention and merit prediction are explicitly defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{accept}(y)\Rightarrow C_F(y)\lor C_M(y).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mode-specific filter or scalar-merit acceptance test.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Acceptance with Scalar Merit Fallback
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hybrid uses filter acceptance in its normal mode and a fully specified scalar merit decrease test in fallback mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter-with-merit-fallback method normally accepts trials through a declared margin-modified nondominance test in the pair (h,f). When a declared trigger disables or fails that mechanism, it switches to a scalar merit function M_\rho and accepts only a trial satisfying the fallback's sufficient-decrease test. The algorithm must declare the trigger, penalty update, return condition, and archive insertion and pruning rules.
assumptions_latex: h(x)\ge0 is a declared violation measure.
The filter margins, switching rule, merit function, and penalty update are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{accepted trial}\Rightarrow\text{filter certificate or merit-decrease certificate}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical switching interface between partial-order and scalar acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Switching Does Not Inherit Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two sound globalization modes can lose their guarantees when combined without a controlled switching rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Global convergence of a filter mode and global convergence of a merit mode do not imply convergence under arbitrary switching between them. A hybrid theorem additionally requires switching safeguards that preserve a common progress argument or bound nonproductive transitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{convergence of each mode}\not\Rightarrow\text{convergence under arbitrary switching}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for combining two individually valid acceptance mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter–Merit Hybrid State Transition System
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The iterate, archive, penalty, active mode, switching predicates, and update rules comprise the hybrid state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter–merit hybrid may be represented by (x_k,\mathcal F_k,\rho_k,z_k), with z_k\in\{\mathrm{filter},\mathrm{merit}\}. Archive insertion and pruning, penalty updates, and transitions between modes are governed by declared rules; rejected trials leave x_k unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Archive, switching, penalty, and fallback-return rules are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x_{k+1},\mathcal F_{k+1},\rho_{k+1},z_{k+1})=\mathcal T(x_k,\mathcal F_k,\rho_k,z_k;\text{trial outcome}).

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Methods with Merit Fallback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filter acceptance augmented by scalar merit-function descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x)\ge0\) measure infeasibility and let \(\mathcal F_k\) be an archive of pairs \((h_i,f_i)\). A trial point \(y\) is filter-acceptable when, for every \((h_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k\), it satisfies \(h(y)\le(1-\gamma_h)h_i\) or \(f(y)\le f_i-\gamma_f h(y)\), with \(\gamma_h,\gamma_f>0\). If this test or the step-generation mechanism fails, invoke a fallback using \(M_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho h(x)\), accepting only a step with prescribed sufficient decrease in \(M_\rho\). Update the archive after filter acceptance and update \(\rho\) according to the declared penalty rule after merit fallback; stop at feasibility and first-order stationarity tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use nondominance-style filter acceptance normally, but require scalar merit decrease when the filter or step mechanism cannot safely progress.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and the chosen violation measure \(h\) are defined at every trial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted trial is certified either by filter acceptability against every archive entry or by sufficient decrease of \(M_\rho\).

children.top_down_role: Restoration outputs governed by compatibility with a filter archive.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter-Screened Restoration Cycle
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration seeks feasibility, while successful return additionally requires compatibility with the existing filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a declared main-phase failure, generate restoration iterates for a declared violation objective. Return a candidate only after it satisfies both the restoration progress or accuracy test and the filter-compatibility test against every archive entry; then perform the declared archive update and rebuild the main-phase model. A stationary-restoration or unresolved-failure status does not authorize return.
assumptions_latex: The trigger, restoration objective, accuracy test, filter convention, archive update, and exit statuses are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{successful return}\Rightarrow C_R(x^R)\land C_F(x^R;\mathcal F_k).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family-level cycle whose restoration objective and numerical rules must be instantiated.

notation.meaning: declared restoration progress or accuracy test

knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Exit Status Partition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified compatible success, stationary violation, and unresolved failure are distinct statuses once their precedence is declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restoration call may assign mutually exclusive statuses by declared priority: compatible success when its verified return tests hold; otherwise stationary violation when \chi_{v_R}(x^R)\le\varepsilon_v; otherwise unresolved failure. Only compatible success authorizes return to the main phase.
assumptions_latex: The return and restoration-criticality tests are computable.
Status precedence is declared so overlapping inequalities cannot produce multiple statuses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{return}\iff\operatorname{status}=\mathrm{compatible\ success}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority-defined partition of successful, stationary, and unresolved outcomes.

notation.meaning: criticality measure for the selected restoration objective

knowledge_statements.title: Violation Reduction Need Not Give Filter Compatibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restoration point can improve violation relative to the current iterate while remaining dominated by an older filter entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under ordinary Pareto nondominance, let the current pair be (h,f)=(2,10), let the archive contain (1,0), and let restoration return (h_R,f_R)=(1.5,10). Then h_R<h, but the archive entry has both smaller violation and smaller objective, so the restored pair is dominated and cannot be returned as filter-compatible.
assumptions_latex: Filter acceptability excludes points Pareto-dominated by an archive entry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h_R<h\quad\not\Rightarrow\quad(h_R,f_R)\text{ is filter-compatible}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of restoration progress from archive admissibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter-Compatible Restoration Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration candidates are screened against the existing filter before return, and lower violation alone need not establish archive compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter–restoration hybrid invokes a feasibility-oriented restoration phase after a declared main-phase failure. A restoration candidate may return to the main phase only if it belongs to the archive-induced acceptable region under the method's filter margins; accepted insertion removes archive entries dominated by the new pair. Violation decrease from the current iterate and archive compatibility are logically distinct tests unless the specified filter rule makes one imply the other.
assumptions_latex: A filter archive of objective–violation pairs and its margin rule are declared.
A restoration trigger and return test are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{successful return}\Rightarrow\text{filter-compatible restoration output}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining interface for restoration outputs screened by a filter archive.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter–Restoration Hybrids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restoration phase whose output must remain compatible with the filter archive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a filter \(\mathcal F_k\) of infeasibility-objective pairs. If the main phase cannot generate a filter-acceptable step from \(x_k\), solve a restoration problem aimed at reducing \(h(x)\), producing \(x_k^R\). Return to the main phase only if \(h(x_k^R)<h(x_k)\) and, for every \((h_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k\), \(h(x_k^R)\le(1-\gamma_h)h_i\) or \(f(x_k^R)\le f_i-\gamma_f h(x_k^R)\). Insert the accepted pair after removing entries it dominates. Terminate at constrained first-order tolerances, or report restoration stationarity or failure when no compatible restoration output can be obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invoke feasibility restoration after main-phase failure, but return only a feasibility-improving point acceptable to the existing filter archive.
assumptions_latex: \(h(x)\ge0\) is zero exactly at feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every successful restoration return strictly reduces violation and is acceptable relative to all entries of \(\mathcal F_k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable outcomes required from the restoration subsolver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerances \(\varepsilon_R,\varepsilon_v>0\), a restoration call returns exactly one declared status: (i) compatible success, with \(C_F(x^R;\mathcal F_k)\) and \(v_R(x^R)\le\varepsilon_R\) or the required relative decrease; (ii) stationary violation, with \(\chi_{v_R}(x^R)\le\varepsilon_v\) but no compatible success; or (iii) unresolved failure, with neither certificate. Only status (i) authorizes main-phase return.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successful return, stationary violation, and unresolved failure are distinct restoration outcomes.

The statuses are assigned from verified inequalities.
