children.top_down_role: Restoration coordinated by scalar feasibility–optimality merit models.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Merit Compatibility of a Restoration Return
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restoration point that strictly reduces violation passes the scalar merit return test exactly when the penalty exceeds its objective-increase-to-feasibility-decrease ratio plus the required margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho h(x)\), \(\Delta h=h(x)-h(x^R)>0\), and \(\sigma\geq0\). Then \[M_\rho(x^R)\leq M_\rho(x)-\sigma\Delta h\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \rho\geq\sigma+\frac{f(x^R)-f(x)}{\Delta h}.\] Thus, if both objective values are finite, every strictly feasibility-improving restoration point admits a finite merit-compatible penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_\rho(x^R)\leq M_\rho(x)-\sigma\Delta h\iff \rho\geq\sigma+(f(x^R)-f(x))/\Delta h.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar-merit test for returning a strictly feasibility-improving restoration point.

notation.meaning: required merit decrease per unit feasibility improvement

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) measure violation, and let \(\phi(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu h(x)\) or another declared scalar feasibility–optimality merit function.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-search or trust-region algorithms that normally globalize with a scalar merit function and invoke a separate feasibility-restoration phase after a declared failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A merit–restoration hybrid has a normal mode and a restoration mode. In normal mode, a trial \(y_k\) is accepted only if it satisfies a sufficient merit-decrease test, such as \(\phi(y_k;\mu_k)\le\phi(x_k;\mu_k)+\eta\alpha_kD\phi(x_k;\mu_k;p_k)\) with \(\eta\in(0,1)\) and negative predicted directional change. Restoration mode is entered when a declared normal-mode failure occurs, such as \(\alpha_k<\alpha_{\min}\), an infeasible step-generation subproblem, or repeated rejection. Restoration computes \(z_k\) primarily by reducing \(h\), and normal mode is resumed only if \(h(z_k)\le h(x_k)-\sigma\Delta h_k\) or another explicit re-entry condition holds. The penalty parameter and other merit state must be updated explicitly across both modes. A method is not a merit–restoration hybrid if feasibility repair is only an undeclared side effect of the normal merit step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit–restoration hybrid uses a scalar merit function for ordinary acceptance and a distinct restoration mode after a specified failure such as an excessively short line-search step, an infeasible subproblem, or repeated rejection. Restoration focuses on reducing constraint violation and must satisfy an explicit condition before normal merit-based operation resumes. Penalty parameters and other merit state are updated across both modes. Incidental feasibility improvement during a merit step does not by itself create a hybrid.
assumptions_latex: The merit function has a computable predicted or directional decrease.
The restoration phase uses a nonnegative violation measure that vanishes at feasible points.
Entry and re-entry triggers are fully declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The architecture is a merit–restoration hybrid exactly when scalar merit acceptance governs normal steps and a distinct violation-reduction phase is entered and exited under explicit failure and re-entry conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In a trust-region variant, sufficient reduction in a merit model replaces the directional-derivative line-search inequality.
special_cases_latex: An \(\ell_1\)-merit SQP method may invoke restoration when backtracking produces \(\alpha_k<\alpha_{\min}\).
A trust-region merit method may invoke restoration when its normal step-generation model becomes infeasible.
immediate_consequences_latex: Restoration acceptance need not reduce the original objective if its declared purpose is feasibility recovery.
A restoration trigger prevents endless normal-mode contraction without a recovery transition.

knowledge_statements.title: Merit–Restoration Hybrids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restoration coordinated with a scalar feasibility–optimality merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho h(x)\), where \(h(x)\ge0\) measures constraint violation. From \(x_k\), first attempt a main-phase step satisfying the declared sufficient-decrease test for \(M_\rho\). If no such step is generated or the local constraint model is incompatible, invoke restoration to compute \(x_k^R\) with \(h(x_k^R)<h(x_k)\). Return from restoration only when \(x_k^R\) satisfies a stated merit-compatibility test, increasing \(\rho\) if necessary under a bounded update rule. Resume the main phase from the returned point. Terminate at feasibility and first-order optimality tolerances, or report stationary failure of the restoration problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use scalar merit decrease in the main phase and invoke feasibility restoration when that phase fails, screening restoration outputs through merit compatibility.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(h\) are defined on all admitted trial and restoration points.
\(\rho>0\), and the restoration phase is invoked only under a declared failure condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted main-phase step decreases \(M_\rho\), while every successful restoration return decreases \(h\) and satisfies the merit-compatibility rule.
